body:
Restack b178 (octnov, row2-svc-discord). Mich's #4375 is three Mind Wipe loop commits stacked on #4132 (superseded in b177). Its own range was read as merge-base..head; nothing of its head was merged, because its LoopVoice and MindWipePlayer are older than the trunk's (no master gain, no one-shot generation guard, no pausable loop).

- includes #4375 port(mind-wipe): prepare loop voice ahead of overlap - HAND-PORTED, one slice:
  - Taken ("stop safely during first loop build"): StartLoop carries a loop generation that StopLoop advances (so Stop and CoreEngine.Stop / panic too). A voice whose build finishes after a stop or a newer StartLoop is disposed, never published as the loop. Before this, a panic during the loop build left that loop playing after the stop. WPF MindWipeService.cs:553-563 arbitrates the same way.
  - Not taken, prepare-ahead: LibVLC creates Media and MediaPlayer cheaply and only opens the input at Play, so building the next copy off-thread gains nothing like WPF's NAudio prebuild (AudioFileReader index plus waveOutOpen). FOLLOWUPS candidate if a measured gap at the 120 ms overlap shows up.
  - Not taken, retry: retrying a failed copy every 100 ms for as long as the loop runs. The trunk ends a dead loop on purpose (`A_loop_that_dies_stops_reporting_looping_and_pays_no_clean_slate`), and a broken file would rebuild a player 10 times a second. WPF self-repairs on its crossfade tick instead. Owner or Mich call.
  - App.axaml.cs PlayVoice -> CreateVoice and MindWipeLoopPreparationTests belong to the parts left out.

Review: no polls, no network, no new windows, startup untouched. Panic only gets stricter in the sense that matches WPF (a late voice is disposed).

Ledger: `svc-discord-rich-presence` (where b105 noted the Mind Wipe one-shot guard) names #4375, what was taken and what was not. Only that row changed.

Tests (Release): new MindWipeTests.Stop_during_loop_start_disposes_the_late_voice (stop, panic) and Newer_loop_start_wins_over_an_older_one_that_finishes_later; all three fail with the generation check removed. ## O que muda

No `.github/workflows/fundamentos.yml`, a coleta semanal dos fundamentos passa a gravar na branch `dados`:

- o padrão do campo `branch` do `workflow_dispatch` muda de `dados-teste` para `dados`;
- o valor usado na execução agendada (`BRANCH_DE_DADOS`) muda de `dados-teste` para `dados`.

O campo `branch` continua existindo: numa execução manual dá para informar outra branch e ensaiar sem mexer na `dados`.

README e CHANGELOG atualizados para dizer isso.

## Por quê

A primeira execução real (#37, PR #61) foi feita em `dados-teste` e aprovada. O build do workflow de 15 minutos lê da `dados`, então é a partir desta troca que as fichas das companhias passam a sair em `dist/fundamentos/dados/`.

## O que esperar depois do merge

- A branch `dados` só recebe a pasta `fundamentos/` (64 arquivos e o índice, 47 MB) na primeira coleta: no domingo às 09:23 de Brasília ou numa execução manual.
- Os extratos em cache foram criados na branch do PR #61, e o cache do Actions não passa de uma branch para a `main`. Por isso a primeira coleta na `main` baixa os 229 MB de novo (cerca de 2 minutos e meio); as seguintes usam o cache.
- A branch `dados-teste` continua no repositório. Não apaguei.

## Testes

Só configuração e documentação: nenhum código mudou. A suíte continua com 889 testes passando, e o YAML do workflow foi validado.

body:
## What was wrong
Lin Wei's card says he opens the story knowing **Sun Breath Sword Art** and **Azure Meridian Method**. The writer is given that correctly, so its end-of-chapter list was right. The Codex check list was the problem. It built its checks from the chapter-only holdings, which count only what chapters have tagged, so it flagged his starting techniques in every chapter (`closing-untagged`). His ring got through only because Chapter 1 happened to tag it.

The chapter-only view is deliberate: it keeps a card hidden from the reader until the story reaches it. The check list should not have borrowed it.

## The fix
- `deriveStoryCodex` (`shared/storyCodex.ts`) now builds the check list from the full record, Chapter 0 included (`worldAtChapterZero`). That is the same record the writer and the Holdings fixer already read.
- What the reader sees in the Codex is unchanged.
- No words any model reads change, and nothing new is stored.

## Tests
- New tests in `codexAtChapterZero.test.ts`:
  - nothing the hero opened with is flagged, in any chapter
  - starting cards stay hidden until a chapter reaches them
  - a closing-list item that neither the world nor a tag gave is still flagged
- Without the fix, the first and third of those tests fail.
- `test:harness-generation`: 758 tests pass. Typecheck is clean.
- README History has a new entry.

author: litree-ceo
body:
## Why

Run #25 (the #419 proof run, Actions run 43533213013) failed at `payment_success_redirect` again — but the PR #956 name/ZIP fix worked: both fields were filled and read back. The run #25 diagnosis found the failure had moved into the submit path itself:

1. The submit search was context-major: the top document was swept through all candidates before any frame was tried, so candidate-2 (anchored text, ANY element) clicked the order summary's "Subscribe to <product>" text node — visible from page load, trivially "enabled", and a no-op — before the real button inside the payment frame was ever reached. No confirmation was ever triggered: no processing state and no navigation in ~110s of observation.
2. The Link save-info uncheck and phone fill were page-scoped, but both controls now render inside the paymentForm iframe, so the uncheck silently no-opped and Link's phone validation stayed armed.
3. The script's network summary filter (`/api/`) can never see Stripe's `payment_pages` confirm call, so "did the click start a payment" was unobservable — runs #24 and #25 recorded no-op clicks as submitted and let Step 6 time out blind.

## What this PR does

One file: `scripts/final-acceptance/stripe-test-checkout.mjs` (+76/−20).

1. **Link/phone frame-scoping:** the Link uncheck and phone fill run through the same `orderedContexts()` sweep as the name/ZIP fill, so they execute in whichever context actually renders them.
2. **Candidate-major submit targeting:** `role="button"` and `button[type="submit"]` candidates are exhausted across ALL contexts before the text-anchored fallback is tried anywhere, and the fallback is scoped to actual button elements only — never a bare text node in the order summary.
3. **Honest submit verification:** the script watches page requests for Stripe's `payment_pages` confirm call (URL contains `payment_pages` and `/confirm`). If a click produces no confirmation traffic, no navigation, and no processing state within the existing 20s probe, `stripe_checkout_submitted` now FAILS with that evidence instead of passing and letting `payment_success_redirect` time out blind.

No waits, timeouts, verdict logic, or the `payment_success_redirect` pass condition were changed. No step was weakened. `node --check` passes.

## Proof path

Merge on green, then run #26 of staging-stripe-e2e is dispatched from the main chat. Issue #419 closes only on a full PASS.

## Separate flag (not in this PR)

The diagnosis also noted that `success_url` is built from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`APP_URL` with a production fallback (`src/app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts`, `getAppUrl()`). Verified in code on main. The staging env value itself is not readable from the connector — if staging lacked that variable, even a successful payment would redirect to the production origin and Step 6 could not pass. Worth a Railway-side check before run #26.

## Branch note

This PR replaces #958 (closed unmerged). The original `agent/stripe-e2e-submit-fix` branch turned out to be an older branch forked before PR #956, so its PR conflicted with main and could not be updated; per the #955 precedent the identical change was republished as one clean snapshot on this branch, based exactly on current main (004561c2). The change content is byte-identical.

author: kent746
body:
Three bugs from the 2026-11-13 Studio review, each reproduced before the fix.

## A run in flight landed on a different design's element
`ContentStep` keyed the panel on `{#key el.id}` only, and element ids repeat across designs (every artwork-only design's logo is `e1`). Press Auto Digitize in design A, open design B from My designs before it ends: A's panel stayed mounted and A's stitches, review and `appliedConfig` were saved onto B's `e1`, with Download unlocked.

- The panel is keyed by design + element (`App` passes `currentId` down as `projectId`).
- `DigitizePanel` and `TextStep` fix the design, element and art at submit and drop a result if any of them changed; the landing patch carries `projectId`, and `ContentStep.relayRun` refuses a patch for a design that is no longer open.
- The sessionStorage resume mark was keyed by the bare element id too, so a mark left by design A auto-ran a digitize on design B's `e1` that nobody pressed. It is now keyed by design + element. `TextStep.runLettering` had the same hazard and gets the same fix.

## Replace file while a run was in flight
Nothing stopped the run and the landing never checked the art, so art A's stitches landed under art B's name, read as current, and downloaded. Loading new art now cancels the run through the existing `cancelDigitize()`, and the landing drops a result whose art (stored original's key + preview) is no longer on the element.

## Replace file kept the old art's settings
The new-art patch carried `forced_class` ("Sew as flat art") through and never reset `textConversions`, `preflight`, `stats`, `priorRun` or `appliedBase`. A photo replacing a flat logo was sent as flat art, and a surviving conversion entry could make converted lettering sew twice. Those are reset now.

**Kept on purpose** (choices about the design, not the old art): every other param, a typed width and `widthTyped`, placement and garment, and text elements already converted from the old art.

## Trade-offs
- "Sew as flat art" must be re-picked after a Replace.
- A resume mark written under the old key is not resumed after a reload: one lost resume, once.
- `relayRun` has no direct test: with the new key the old panel is torn down and drops its own result first, so no test reaches it.

## Tests
8 new tests in `ContentStep.projectSwitch.spec.js` and `DigitizePanel.replaceArt.spec.js`, all red on main (8 failed) and green here. Full `npm test`: 2471 passed, 0 failed. e2e not run locally.

body:
## Summary

C12: the Vista sweep, verification and node-hour scripts. **Stacked on #65.** The base is `mikail/megakernel`, so this diff shows only C12. Merge #65 first; GitHub then retargets this PR to `dev`.

- **`scripts/tacc/sweep.py`** (`plan`, `run`, `merge`): the BENCHMARKING "Sweeps" rows as presets around the baseline (`bench_1m`, 1080p, lbvh, mega, B = R = max), using the Vista or laptop thread lists.
  - Presets: `cpu-threads`, `gpu-build-threads`, `size` (includes the 1-core baseline at each size), `bvh`, `resolution`, `tapp`. `g2` is the first T_app / T_br / T_frame at 3 sizes, `core` is all of them, and `smoke` is the known scene.
  - Prepared points run `rt_render --mode prepared`. T_app points run 5 fresh processes through Arek's `run_tapp.py`. Every file is validated against schema v2.
  - Before measuring, it records machine identity (nvidia-smi, lscpu, gcc, nvcc, modules, ldd, env). It also refuses to run without `OMP_PROC_BIND=close OMP_PLACES=cores` and checks that `rt_render` loads GCC's libgomp.
  - `merge` writes `sweep.csv`: one row per point and quantity, with the components of the median run, plus spread and dirty-build warnings.
  - Finished points are skipped, so a job that hit its time limit can be resubmitted.
- **`scripts/tacc/verify.sh`**: the G2 correctness checks on one node. It runs ctest, checks the `scenes-v1` hashes against `scenes/manifest.json`, compares CPU vs CUDA with `rt_compare` on the known scenes and `bench_10k/100k/1m`, checks byte equality, and repeats the CUDA run.
- **`sweep.sbatch`** (`gh-dev` by default, `PRESET=verify|g2|core|...`), **`env.sh`** (modules and pinning), **`build_vista.sh`** (fails on warnings or a wrong OpenMP runtime), and **`node_hours.sh`** (turns `sacct` records into rows for the node-hour log).
- The light-count dimension isn't automated. `rt_render` has no light override, so it needs scene variants; this is noted in BENCHMARKING.

## Tests

- New `sweep_py` (18 cases): preset contents against BENCHMARKING, the libgomp and pinning checks, and a real CPU sweep through `rt_render` (CSV rows, identity files, resume, merge, missing-scene and failure paths). It runs in CPU-only CI.
- Laptop:
  - `verify.sh` passes: ctest 305/305, manifest hashes, all CPU/CUDA pairs byte-identical.
  - The `g2` preset completes in 1.5 min (18 points, 27 CSV rows).
  - The CPU-only build passes `sweep_py` too.

**Run on Vista (Nov 13):** smoke job 1142824, then the `g2` preset with `verify.sh` (1142829) and the `core` preset (1142842) on `gh-dev`, allocation `TRA25006`. `verify.sh` passes: ctest 306/306, hashes match the manifest, CPU and CUDA byte-identical on all scenes. The results, ratios and what limits them are in docs/RESULTS.md (added here), with the sweep data in docs/data/. 1M primitives, T_br: 1 core / best CPU 29.8x, best CPU / GPU 1.46x, 1 core / GPU 43x; T_frame GPU 5.7 ms vs 29.1 ms. A 72-job build on a login node hit the process limit, so `build_vista.sh` now defaults to `-j 8` (`RT_JOBS`). Also adds `scripts/tacc/ratios.py`.

body:
## Why
Effect files could push particles with gravity, drag and turbulence, but nothing made them circle. Tornado funnels, dust devils, whirlpools and swirling portals had to be faked with spinning meshes or many rotated emitters.

## What
- **`function/plugins/render3d/effects.ts`, `core/ports/render3d.ts`:** a new optional effect block, `"vortex": {"spin": <deg/s>, "pull": <m/s²>}`.
  - `spin` defaults to 90 and is counter-clockwise seen from above (negative: clockwise).
  - `pull` defaults to 0 and draws particles toward the line (negative flings them out).
- **`function/plugins/render3d/particles.ts`:** each step turns live particles' positions and velocities about the vertical line through the emitter and applies the pull, never past the line in one step. The line follows a moving emitter. Effects without the block are unchanged; 2D ignores it.
- **`docs/concepts/visuals.md`, `sdk/parallax/__init__.pyi`:** documented; `docs/reference` regenerated.

```json
{ "rate": 200, "lifetime": 3, "speed": [1, 2], "direction": 90, "spread": 20,
  "vortex": { "spin": 240, "pull": 3 } }
```

## Verified
- New test in `vfx.test.ts`: a particle on the line stays there; a particle 2 m from a continuous emitter's line turns 90° in one second at `spin: 90`, about the emitter's new position after it moves; pull draws particles inward without overshoot.
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/runtime typecheck` clean.
- `npx vitest run src/function/plugins/render3d src/function/plugins/render2d src/function/plugins/visuals`: 20 files, 436 passed; `packages/check` vitest: 129 passed.

author: pokeehokee
body:
**Stacked on #23** (base is `ccr-84fdac1e-xs8evp`, so this diff is only the live path). Merge #23 first.

**Nothing is armed by this PR.** `LIVE` still needs the mode switch, the screen lock, credentials, a passing preflight and the acceptance notes. The point of a separate PR is that the order code can be read before it ever has capital behind it.

`:core:test` (210) and `:app:testDebugUnitTest` pass.

---

## Why the invariant moved

`PaperRangeLongshot` refused `LIVE` by construction — *"a candidate from the pool search is forward-tested in paper before anything else, and LIVE is not offered."* That was right while the paper book was the only evidence. It is **not** what decided this:

| evidence | losses | close-dates | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the paper book | ~6 | **7** | cannot resolve anything |
| settled history, 12 series @60m | **29** vs 135.0 implied | **49** | ratio 0.21, +3.88c [+3.47, +4.22], 48/49 days positive |

Count the **losses**, not the fills — the same rule the deep-ITM band correction turned on, and the reason the paper book's own band splits (0–3 losses each) were never actionable.

So the gate moved rather than opening:

- the base class is live-capable only where a subclass implements **every** venue hook **and** sets `liveCapable`;
- a **variant is never live**, whatever its base can do;
- `kalshi_commodity_longshot` is the only opt-in. **`polymarket_temperature_longshot` stays paper-only** and is untouched.

## The order path is the ladder's, not a new one

`KalshiBtcLadder` has 1,500+ live positions behind it. Four things reused rather than rediscovered:

- **The shard.** Commodities route to the same non-default `exchange_index` as the crypto ladder, and Kalshi does not fund a shard automatically. The shard is read off each market, carried on orders and fill reads, and preflight fails when that shard has no cash.
- **Live size comes from the exchange or is not taken.** `liveEquity` reads the shard's own cash; an unreadable balance **aborts the pass** (`balance unreadable`) rather than falling back to a local number. The budget subtracts only collateral behind orders still **resting** — the exchange has already taken a filled position's out of cash, and subtracting both under-deploys by the size of the book (the mirror of weatherbot's 2026-09-08 double-count).
- **A withdrawal is a cancel at the exchange, never a result.** Cancel at Kalshi, re-read the fill after (a cancel races a fill), hand the row to the settlement pass with no result written. This is the August TTL sweep that wrote 28 quotes off as expired without checking fills — 18 of them real filled positions.
- **Live P&L is the exchange's figure or nothing.** The three-tier chain (settlements → `positions?settlement_status=settled` → `/historical/positions`); a filled row no store has a figure for is left **ungraded and reported**, never derived. Only the venue's own fill record reading zero grades a row unfilled.

## What the acceptance notes say out loud

The go-live checklist now carries two notes that cannot be ticked away by a passing backtest:

- the verdict needs **losses**, not fills, which is why the first live lot should be small;
- **a paper fill never sat in the real book.** It is modelled from the public tape behind our queue position, so it cannot be lifted by flow reacting to it. On the weather book that selection took a population loss ratio of 0.73 to **0.96 on fills** — most of an edge.

## How to start it

Lot 1, the shipped 0.02–0.25 band, the whole pool (~56 markets/day, ~$50/day of collateral), `$10` brake unchanged — one market can lose ~$0.95, so the brake stops the day well before a second. The verdict depends on the number of losses, not the lot, so take the markets and not the size. Then watch the **live loss ratio against the population's 0.21** and size up on that number.

## Tests

`core/src/test/kotlin/com/marketbot/core/CommodityLiveTest.kt` (8) freezes: the post-only order on the market's own shard, the aborted pass on an unreadable balance, cancel-before-withdraw with no result written, grading from the settlement payload rather than local arithmetic, ungraded-not-guessed, never-filled reconciliation when the order endpoint disagrees with the fill record, and that live and paper books never mix. `SearchCandidatesTest`'s blanket paper-only assertion now states the narrower invariant it was really protecting; two pass summaries gained reason codes.

author: phantoslayer21
body:
Model L (#89): the D3D12 port of Model L's C = 32 Swin block, byte for byte against its merged HIP kernel
(`l_swin_block_c32_nc` of `l_swin.co`, #102).

- **`clean/dx12/kernels/l_swin.hlsl`** (new): instantiates `swin_block.hlsl` as `l_swin_block_c32_nc`:
  - C = 32, 2 heads, MLP 128;
  - HIP's transcendental GELU chain (`SW_GELU=0`) and HIP's MLP unit cut (`SW_HPU=8`);
  - the `_nc` form, as Model M's ports.
- **`clean/dx12/kernels/swin_block.hlsl`**: the RMS-norm scale had only the C = 64 and 96 cases. This adds `SW_C == 32`
  (scale 1/32). Without it, most output bytes differed. `fused_swin.hlsl`, generated from it, gets the same two lines
  (`fused_swin_gen.py --check`: up to date). **Model M's DXILs are unchanged** (below).
- **`clean/dx12/vgpr_limits.json`**: `l_swin_block_c32_nc` bounded at 96 VGPRs. **`clean/dx12/build_dx12.py`** checks
  `l_swin_*` kernels too.
- **`clean/dx12/tests/kernel_replay.cpp`** (new): runs single kernels on the native D3D12 device (the project's Device
  API) from a case file of modules, a launch and its arguments.
- **`clean/l/runner/l_d3d12_check.py`** (new): the harness. `--prepare` (CPU) builds the HIP code objects, the D3D12
  ports and `kernel_replay.exe`. `--run` (one GPU slot) runs each case on HIP, then the same inputs through
  `kernel_replay` on D3D12, and compares the whole output buffers with `bytes ==`. Counts only, no timing.

What "byte for byte" is checked on:
- the same synthetic token map (FP8, seeded), window offsets, grid size and packed weight blob (`packing.pack_block` at
  C = 32, heads 2, MLP 128) on both back ends;
- the **raw downloaded bytes** of both outputs compared, the full FP8 output map, with no tolerance. Nothing is decoded
  and encoded again, so for example the two FP8 NaN codes stay distinct;
- **each output buffer filled beforehand with its own non-zero sentinel**: HIP 0xA5, D3D12 0x5A (`kernel_replay`'s
  `arg out` takes a fill byte). A byte that either path, or both, leaves unwritten therefore differs;
- a **negative control**: one case again on D3D12 with half its workgroups, which the comparison must catch;
- Model M's `swin_block_c96_nc` (HIP `swin.co` against its existing D3D12 port) as a control on the same harness, so the
  harness itself is proven too.

Refs #89

## Tested

Local, Windows, Radeon RX 9000 series card, main cf8e8ac plus this commit:

- **GPU (one GPU slot, 12.5 s), `l_d3d12_check.py --run --seeds 6`, raw bytes and sentinels (after the review):**
  - `l_swin_block_c32_nc`: **48 of 48 cases identical** (6 seeds x 8 grid / offset cases; 23,911,488 output bytes in
    all; 0 differing bytes in every case);
  - the Model M control `swin_block_c96_nc`: **48 of 48 identical** (71,734,464 bytes, 0 differing);
  - since the two sentinels differ, identical outputs mean every byte was written by both back ends;
  - the **negative control** (half grid) was caught: 1,248 differing bytes, all of them still the D3D12 sentinel;
  - `kernel_replay`: 0 cases failed.

  The first run, before the review fixes, decoded and re-encoded the HIP output and zero-filled both outputs: also 48 of
  48 and 48 of 48.
- **`--prepare` (CPU):** builds clean. VGPR check: `l_swin_block_c32_nc` 95 / 96, `swin_block_c96_nc` 192 / 192.
- **Model M's DXILs unchanged:** the 9 Swin kernels of `swin_block.hlsl`, `swin_c64w2.hlsl` and `fused_swin.hlsl`
  (`swin_block_c96_nc`, `swin_block_c96_add_ex_nc`, `swin_block_c64_nc`, `swin_block_c96_pm_nc`,
  `swin_block_c96_pm_rev_nc`, `swin_block_c96_add_xe_rev_nc`, `swin_block_c96_add_xe_nc`, `swin_block_c96_add_xe_xo_nc`,
  `swin_block_c96_add_xe_xd_nc`) were built from main and from this branch under the same output names
  (`build_dx12.py --only ... -j 1`). **DXIL SHA-256: 9 of 9 identical** (for example `swin_block_c96_nc`
  0d8bea45c7803504..., `swin_block_c64_nc` 9f7c47f23ff1174c..., `swin_block_c96_add_xe_xd_nc` 2767e993c6ca1d46...).
- `python tools/ci/check_line_endings.py`: 0 problems. Public gates (secrets, personal data, licence, chunks) pass.

## Not tested

- Whole-frame `compare.py` for Model L (waits for the L runtime frame).
- The FP16-input form of the block (comes with its HIP kernel, then its port).
- `kernel_replay.exe` is not built by CI (it needs a GPU to be useful).

Two holes in how the system lets a ticket go while it is still waiting. Ticket: https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-11514/396

HTPR-8207 ended a run on 13 Nov with the note "In Progress (PR 3476 checks running; recheck after 2026-11-13T23:54Z)". That note names neither AI Review nor QA, so the wait gate did not treat it as a wait. The open PR list was stale, so nothing looked changed, and runner 2 took the ticket again at 23:35:29, 19 minutes before the recheck time. Now a BUILDING end note that names a PR with running or pending checks, or a recheck time, counts as a built PR end. If it states a recheck time, the gate holds the ticket until that time even when the PR list says nothing. A ticket edit or a changed PR still releases it first.

HTPR-8737 came back 14 times on runner 6 from 5 to 7 Nov. Its end notes said it was blocked on a CI repair, and the note was read as a plain wait. A line that says blocked by, blocked on or awaiting another ticket key is now a wait on that ticket, which the park step turns into a hold until that ticket closes. Notes that name no ticket stay plain waits.

Checks run: fleet/pick --self-test and fleet/runner-state.py --self-test pass. New asserts: the exact HTPR-8207 row is held at 23:35:29 and free at its recheck time, an ordinary BUILDING end is not held, a ticket edit frees it, and "blocked by HYCI-140" parks on HYCI-140 while "awaiting CI repair" stays a plain wait. No CI was run on this VPS.

body:
`ChromaticAberration` extracts the unchanged green channel and merges it with the distorted red and blue planes using `cv2.merge`. `ImageCompression` uses `cv2.merge` for JPEG output with more than three channels up to the OpenCV runtime limit. WebP and higher channel counts use `np.dstack`. The WebP probe changed median Compose latency by less than 1% on either host. [Codec comparison](https://github.com/albumentations-team/AlbumentationsX/actions/runs/43533656327)

## Compose latency

`Compose([RandomCrop, transform])` on seeded synthetic images, with JPEG quality fixed at 75. Values are paired medians in microseconds per image, `main` (`2fa2d18`) → this PR (`992c86b`). Each host used one CPU thread, Python 3.11.15, Albucore 0.3.8, NumPy 2.4.6, and OpenCV 5.0.0.93. Mac ran on Apple M4 Max. The Linux runners were AMD EPYC 9V74 for ChromaticAberration and AMD EPYC 7763 for JPEG. [ChromaticAberration run](https://github.com/albumentations-team/AlbumentationsX/actions/runs/43535239564), [ImageCompression run](https://github.com/albumentations-team/AlbumentationsX/actions/runs/43534752839)

- The JPEG channel limit and the first count above it (128 and 129 with OpenCV 5) matched the baseline on both platforms. Regression tests compare channel assembly against the previous NumPy path. Optimize chromatic aberration and multichannel JPEG channel assembly with OpenCV while preserving existing output behavior.

author: vvonchain
body:
## Summary

A drop in keploy's own unit coverage now fails `gate`, so it blocks the merge. Each night the native-Linux record/replay lanes are merged into that measurement, and every `Fuzz*` target searches for ten minutes. Tests added for the untested packages also fix three defects: a cut-short MySQL OK or EOF packet returns an error instead of panicking, a gRPC test case is left out of a Postman export instead of becoming a `null` item, and a Go coverage file whose functions are empty reports `0.00%` instead of `NaN%`.

The unit floor in [`.github/coverage-floor.yaml`](https://github.com/vvonchain/keploy/blob/coverage-floor-nightly-fuzz/.github/coverage-floor.yaml) starts at 80.0. A local `linux/arm64` run of `go test -cover ./...` measured 83.70% without `pkg/service/replay` (those tests are killed in that container and pass on CI), so the first `unit_coverage` run should clear 80. Raise the floor to that run's number, rounded down to one decimal. The merged floor stays 0 until the first nightly run prints a number worth keeping. The two numbers are not comparable: unit leaves out packages with no test file, and the merged binary counts every package linked into keploy, so merged can come out lower.

## Decisions

- `unit_coverage` is its own job and feeds `gate`, still the only required check. It sets no private parsers and none of the lane-only `KEPLOY_TEST_*` variables, so a fork and an internal PR measure the same tests. Rows that need MySQL, Docker, or user namespaces still run only in `go-test.yaml`.
- A floor can only go up. The ratchet also fails when a tolerance is raised far enough that a later run could pass at 0%, and when a tolerance is removed.
- A pull-request run of `coverage-nightly.yml` covers one lane. It skips only a below-floor result (exit 3). A measurement or floor file it cannot read still fails.
- The agent is the same binary, started by the CLI under plain sudo, which drops `GOCOVERDIR`. Each lane adds `Defaults env_keep += "GOCOVERDIR"` on the runner, and the data directory is mode 1777. A lane fails unless the proxy's start function, which only the agent runs, has coverage.
- A fuzz crash uploads its input and opens or comments on one public issue labelled `nightly-failure`. Proxy-parser crashes may belong in the private path in `SECURITY.md` instead; this PR leaves that call to the maintainers, and the workflow header says the input is public.
- `coverage_stage.yml` is removed. No workflow called it, and it measured the gin-mongo sample, not keploy.

## Test plan

- [x] On this branch, before the rebase onto `fa981c0`: `go test` for the changed packages, `-race` on `pkg/platform/telemetry` and `pkg/service/export`, the three script suites (`coverage-floor`, `fuzz-targets`, `covdata-assert`), ShellCheck, actionlint, and golangci-lint `--new-from-merge-base=origin/main` (0 issues). The rebase shares no files with `fa981c0` (`pkg/agent/routes`, `pkg/service/agent/claimer.go`).
- [ ] `unit_coverage` on this pull request is the first GitHub run of the floor. Confirm it clears 80.0, then raise the floor in a follow-up.
- [ ] `coverage-nightly.yml` and `fuzz-nightly.yml` run in their short form on this pull request (one lane, one target for 30 seconds, no issue). The full nightly jobs run on `main` after merge.

author: circle-ron
body:
# Description
Splits the Segment snippet in `ui/src/partials/head-scripts.hbs`. The stub and the `dd_docs_page` track call stay as they are. `analytics.load()` moves into its own `<script type="text/plain" data-cookieconsent="marketing">` tag inside the same `{{#with site.keys.segmentWrite}}` block. Cookiebot stays in auto mode. No other files change.

Calls made before consent (`dd_docs_page`, the unguarded `analytics.track` in `404.hbs`, copy-code, search, page vote) wait in the stub's queue and are sent once Marketing consent is given. The stub sets no cookies and makes no network requests.

**Analytics:** affected. Segment now loads only after Marketing consent. No events or properties are added or renamed.
**Risk:** low. One template line moves; no logic changes.

# Reasons
- Docs leaves Segment's consent handling to Cookiebot's automatic blocking, so whether Segment waits for consent changes with each circleci.com scan. Docs pageviews in Segment flipped four times between Oct 4 and Nov 2 (WBCT-1507). A scan that skips docs pages would undo the current behavior.
- Compliance policy requires opt-in for GDPR countries, Brazil, Quebec, and Mexico. Docs shares the circleci.com Cookiebot domain group, so the policy applies.
- Marketing is the right category. Our Cookiebot declaration (scan 2026-10-29) puts `ajs_user_id` in Marketing, `ajs_anonymous_id` in Statistics, and `ajs_group_*` in Preferences, so the strictest category applies. Segment on docs also sends to AdWords.
- circleci.com already uses this pattern (`morph/base/segment.html`), so both sites count the same visitors.

Linear: [WBCT-1563](https://linear.app/circleci/issue/WBCT-1563/gate-segment-on-marketing-consent-on-the-docs-site)

# Not in this PR
Other docs trackers load before consent. Facts from the WBCT-1420 trace, listed for reference only: gtag, HubSpot, LinkedIn Insight, Reddit, 6sense, ZoomInfo, Qualified, Reo, OpenAI `oaiq`, Hotjar, Google Ads `viewthroughconversion`. `js-cookie` stays ungated (it only reads cookies).

# How to test
Feature-branch builds have no Segment key, so the CI preview artifact will not show this change. Check it locally.

**1. Build with placeholder keys** (from the repo root):

```
SEGMENT_WRITE_KEY=PLACEHOLDERKEY COOKIEBOT=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 npm run build:docs
```

The build should finish without errors. A `go: command not found` message from the LLM-markdown step is unrelated and the build continues.

**2. Check the built pages.** Run this for `build/index.html` and `build/404.html`:

```
grep -o '<script type="text/plain" data-cookieconsent="[a-z]*">[^<]*</script>' build/index.html
grep -o 'analytics.load("[^"]*")' build/index.html
```

Expected for each file:
- The first command prints exactly one line: `<script type="text/plain" data-cookieconsent="marketing">analytics.load("PLACEHOLDERKEY");</script>`
- The second command prints exactly one `analytics.load("PLACEHOLDERKEY")`, which is the one inside that gated tag. The ungated Segment script no longer calls it.
- `grep -c 'data-blockingmode="auto"' build/index.html` prints `1`, so Cookiebot is still in auto mode.
- The `analytics.track("dd_docs_page"` call is still in the inline script.

**3. Consent behavior** (needs a real Segment key and the circleci.com Cookiebot, so it runs on production after merge):
- No consent: no requests to `cdn.segment.com` or `api.segment.io`, and no `ajs_*` cookies.
- Accept Marketing: `analytics.min.js` loads and the queued `dd_docs_page` is sent to `api.segment.io`.
- Statistics only: Segment stays off.
- 404 page with no consent: no console `ReferenceError`.

I will post the production results on WBCT-1563.

# Content checks
N/A. Template-only change, no docs content touched.

author: seathatflowsinourveins
body:
M2's pacer is wired into the Alpaca gateway, so `connect` no longer refuses for lack of an order budget. The values it runs on are the owner's: they come from an owner-held file outside the public repository, and this pull request adds none.

## What it changes

- `meridian/alpaca/pacing.py` (new): `load_controls()` reads the 16 control rows from the file named by the new `order_budget_rows_path` setting and builds M2's `Controls` through its unchanged validation; `build_pacer()` builds M2's `AccountPacer` and starts it empty, so the first request leaves one full interval after a connect and a reconnect adds no burst. `meridian/order_budget/` is untouched.
- `production_wiring()` in `factories.py` passes that pacer factory to the gateway (it passed `None`).
- Refusals carry no value: no setting or an unreadable file gives `order budget rows file unavailable`; a file that is not a list of rows, a missing row, a malformed row or a fixture-scope row gives `order budget rows invalid` (a fixture row still refuses in M2's own validation, as before). The validation's exception is dropped before the fixed one is raised, so no row value, path or exception chain leaves the module.
- `deploy/alpaca-order-budget.template.json` (new): the 16 row names with every field null, for the owner to copy, fill in and review. `.gitignore` gains `local/` as a place for that copy; a test checks the suggested file name and a backup of it are ignored.
- `docs/m3-alpaca.md` section 5 and the `budget.py` and `factories.py` docstrings say what is now true; one row in `UPSTREAM.md`. Markdown is 5 lines longer (1,869 of 1,900), config 19 (411 of 450).

Decision behind it (the landing session's, under the owner's delegation): an owner-held rows file outside the public repository; no fixture or Sextant value goes into the tree as a production value.

## How it was checked

16 new test cases in `tests/test_alpaca_production_budget.py`, on fakes (fake keys, venue, stream and clock) with the real production wiring and M2's real pacer; the worker ran them before the change and all 16 failed. They cover: ten kinds of missing or invalid file, none disclosing a value; a reviewed file connects, and connects empty again on reconnect; connect still refuses without commission evidence; a simulated minute of requests leaves at the paced interval and within the budget; a 429 pauses; a refusal is not sent; the template has every name and no value. The tests promote the public fixture rows to reviewed scope in `tmp_path` at run time only.

The head `f37a382` trial-merged onto `origin/main` (`e3f06f2`) gives the head's own tree, `86d7985`. On it, by the lead:

- `uv run ruff check .`: `All checks passed!`
- `uv run ruff format --check .`: `73 files already formatted`
- `uv run pyright`: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`
- `uv run pytest`: `1039 passed in 140.01s (0:02:20)`
- `gitleaks git --redact --no-banner .` (8.30.1): `no leaks found`

Written by a Codex worker (`gpt-6-astra`) in its own Orca worktree. Reviewed by the lead, a different model family; its record is in a comment.

## Not done

- The owner's rows file: 16 reviewed rows, written by the owner. Until it exists the lane refuses.
- `connect` still refuses without commission evidence (its own pull request), and there is no lane entry point or market-data wiring yet, so nothing can connect.
- Tested on fakes only: no socket was opened and no real rows or keys were read.
- A recovery-read defect on main (coverage marked complete before the engine has applied the read) is being fixed in its own pull request and must land before any attended order.

body:
## What

- **Remote**: the server detects the `package.json` / `composer.json` run configurations (`run/manifests`), so they are listed in remote mode. The native server downloads ripgrep over https (`--enable-url-protocols=https`) and the remote bundle (`tools/remote-bundle.sh`) is the GraalVM build with ripgrep bundled; it copies its result to `~/.kotlin-editor/bundles/`.
- **Home**: the welcome screen is the IDE frame (toolbar, burger menu with Remote Development and Settings, status bar). The toolbar centers the search, with Run, Deploy and the mode switch at the right. A settings gear sits at the bottom of the tool strip, with the Git branches button just above it.
- **Find in Files**:
  - several globs with exclusions (`*.kt, !*.xml, !build/`, `FileGlobs`), several directories (one ripgrep path each; nested or repeated ones searched once; the built-in engine follows the same rules; `scopes` in the protocol, the old `scope` is still read);
  - a directory dropdown with a filter, Select all and Clear; crosses on the fields;
  - extension and exclusion suggestions computed by the server (`search/facets`), so they work in remote mode;
  - icons for the options; the previous results stay on screen (dimmed, "Searching…") while a new search runs; typing is debounced to 250 ms, option changes are immediate.
- **XML**: `.xml`, `.xsd`, `.xsl`, `.svg`, `.plist`, `.csproj`... are colored by tree-sitter with the HTML grammar (bonede/tree-sitter-ng has no XML grammar).
- **Language Servers window**: one column (settings on one line, servers, then the IDE resources as a Memory / CPU table) instead of two.

## Tests

- `./lint` passes. Run per module: `syntax`, `protocol`, `server`, `tree-client`, `shared`, `language-servers-client`, `remote` (all green at the time of their last run).
- New e2e: Find in Files globs, suggestions, several directories, select all / clear, results kept while searching (chaos, slow link), toolbar and tool strip layout, Language Servers layout. New unit tests: `FileGlobsTest`, `SearchFacetsTest`, `FindOptionsCodecTest`, `RunManifestsTest`, ripgrep arguments, XML highlighting.
- Not run: the full `./run-tests` (one run was interrupted) and `./ci`. No performance test was added for the Find in Files filters: their cost does not depend on the number of directories ticked.

author: pcomans
body:
### Summary

A renderer that posts eve's completed Slack reply can't edit that reply later, for example to add a footer once the turn settles, because `postCompletedSlackReply` returns nothing. To learn the message's `ts`, an app has to wrap eve's thread API. This PR makes `postCompletedSlackReply` return the message it posts.

### Changes

- `postCompletedSlackReply` (`eve/channels/slack`) returns `Promise<SlackPostedMessage | undefined>`: the posted message for your blocks or your Markdown, and `undefined` when eve uploads a snippet or drops a reply to a deleted thread. The return type widens from `void`, so existing callers keep working.
- eve's default renderer ignores the returned message.

author: popmechanic
body:
Stage 5, the last, of taking Kata out of the run path (operator's decision, 2026-11-13). It also carries the readings stages 3 and 4 left unread.

`49 files changed, 319 insertions(+), 5113 deletions(-)`

## What changed

**Deleted (13 files):** `fleet/kata-client.mjs`, `kata-file.mjs`, `kata-hub.mjs`, `kata-hub-setup.sh`, `kata.service`, `board-read.mjs`, `policy.json`; `factory/board.mjs`, `factory/flock/kata_mirror.mjs`, `factory/audit.mjs`; the sims `test_board_read.mjs` and `test_factory_board.mjs`; the probe `probe_kata_facts.mjs`.

**The engine and boot** write to no service. A run's `events.jsonl` holds no `kata:mirror`, `board:close`, `board:mark` or `run:audit` row, and the boot's end is the status page, one commit, the tag and the removal request.
- `factory/audit.mjs` went with it: its one row listed the hub closes a run had missed, so without a hub it could only say "none". No reader of that row exists in the repository.

**The launcher** opens no hub, and a plan commit is `plan.md` and its gate record. The duplicate-launch guard stays, reworded: two runs of one plan now only build the same change twice.

**The janitor and the hub's VM remover** read the evidence record and nothing else. Both switches back to Kata are removed with the code they switched to (`janitor.record.source`, `launch.kata.mode` and `REAPER_RECORD`), and `fleet/policy.json` with its last cells. The remover's journal line is again `reap caller=… run=… status=…`, plus `vm=… removed=…` on a 202.

**The doctor** has ten rows; the `kata` row and its section of `first-run.md` are gone. The `reaper` row still finds the hub VM by its name, `kata-hub`, which it keeps.

**Docs:** `fleet/CONTRACT.md` (a short "The hub VM" section replaces the Kata hub paragraph and the 26-row `Kata facts (measured)` list; the one exe.dev fact in that list moved to the exe.dev facts), `fleet/RUNBOOK.md`, both rules files, `CLAUDE.md`, the skill, the README and `first-run.md`.

**The way back** is a launch from a checkout made before this change, with `kata.service` started and its two integrations re-created. It is the rule the retired factory has.

## Changed outside the repository, each on the operator's yes (2026-11-13)

- `kata-hub` VM: `kata.service` stopped and disabled (4:31 PM Pacific). Its data is left at `/var/lib/kata` (103 MB), and `/etc/kata/kata.env` and the program are untouched.
- `kata-hub` VM: this branch's `reaper.py` and `reaper.service` installed and restarted; the unit no longer loads Kata's env file or waits on its service. **The hub runs this branch's remover ahead of the merge.**
- exe.dev: the integrations `kata` and `kata-sync` removed. Left on the hub VM: `evidence-read` and `lobby-rm`; `reaper` stays on `tag:fleet`.
- **The ultraviz viewer VM is now dark**, on the operator's pick: its server tails the Kata daemon. Nothing on that VM was changed. Rebuilding it on the evidence record (`projectRun` in `fleet/run-read.mjs`) is not in this PR.
- `popmechanic/flock-baseline`: run 48 merged on purpose (popmechanic/flock-baseline#47) and was reverted by hand (popmechanic/flock-baseline#48). Main is `5683eb2a`, the same tree as the wrong-plans base `d668b2e7`, two commits on; the fixture's README says so.

## Readings

Gate: `239 passed, 13 skipped in 175.49s (0:02:55)` (`python3 -m pytest`, 2026-11-13, the final tree).

**The items stages 3 and 4 left unread** (n=1 run each, flock-baseline, 2026-11-13, 3:17 to 3:22 PM Pacific, engine `0157bce9`, account `marcus.e-gmail.com`):

- *A parked run with Kata off:* run 46 (the contradiction plan, held) ended `parked` with a draft pull request. Its record held 0 `kata:mirror` rows and one `board:mark` row, `skipped: no kata.json to read`. Janitor: `rm fleet-r46-2611132317-574a  run=46 parked since 2026-11-13T23:18:38.436Z`.
- *A failed run with Kata off:* run 47 (control, held), its unit killed by hand with SIGKILL while `running`. The VM wrote its own death: `failed`, error `unit signal (killed KILL) while the record said running`, with `journal.txt` and its tag. Janitor: `rm fleet-r47-2611132317-6e40  run=47 failed since 2026-11-13T23:18:00.940Z`.
- *The remover refuses both:* asked on the hub for runs 46 and 47, it answered `status=409` twice.
- *A merged run asking by itself:* run 48 (control, not held) merged at 23:21:18Z, and six seconds later the journal read `reap caller=fleet-r48-2611132320-bf71 run=48 status=202 record=evidence vm=fleet-r48-2611132320-bf71 removed=True`. The fleet listing was empty after it.
- *The janitor removing a VM for real:* read three times (runs 45, 46, 47).

**This change** (n=1, flock-baseline run 49, held, 2026-11-13, 4:32 to 4:33 PM Pacific, engine `863a607a`, launched from this branch after the hub changes above):

```
== following (every 10 s; ! lines flag trouble)
  00:32:36Z run-49 run        main moved to 5683eb2 (start), 0 files taken in
  00:32:36Z run-49 task 1     claimed by A
  00:32:48Z run-49 task 1     done by A
  00:32:48Z run-49 task 2     claimed by A
  00:32:59Z run-49 run        settled green at dc422eabbc
  00:32:59Z run-49 run        ended ready: settled green
  00:33:01Z run-49 task 2     done by A
  00:33:10Z run-49 run        pull request opened: https://github.com/popmechanic/flock-baseline/pull/49
== run-49 done: the pull request is open  https://github.com/popmechanic/flock-baseline/pull/49
```

- Its record: 38 rows, none of kind `kata:*`, `board:*` or `run:audit`; the boot log has 0 lines naming Kata or a board; the run ended `done` and was tagged.
- The remover, asked from the run's own VM with Kata stopped: `reap caller=fleet-r49-2611140032-8de7 run=49 status=202 vm=fleet-r49-2611140032-8de7 removed=True`.
- The doctor from this branch: 10 rows, all `ok`; `reaper`: `the key hub-reaper-2026-11b is good until 2027-11-13 (364 days); the remover answered from the hub`.
- The first line of the watch also reads the fixture's moved main: a run launched at the old base took main in with 0 files changed.

Cleanup: popmechanic/flock-baseline#46 and popmechanic/flock-baseline#49 closed unmerged and their branches deleted by the janitor, no fleet VM listed, no live branch left.

## Not read

- **Either way back to Kata, live.** On the operator's pick they were not run before being deleted; they were in sims only.
- **A parked or failed run on this engine.** Runs 46 and 47 ran on `0157bce9`, where the boot still called the board script and skipped. On `863a607a` the call is gone; that path is read in `test_factory_boot.mjs` (legs c and h) and not on a run.
- **A merged run on this engine asking by itself.** Run 49 was held, so its request was sent by hand from its VM. Run 48 read that path on the engine before.
- **A run with several builders or a conflict on this engine.** The control plan is two tasks and one builder; the mirror's removal is exercised only that far live.
- **A fresh operator with no hub VM.** The runbook's hand `new` for one was not run.
- `--follow` over a long run, and its cost against GitHub's rate limit, are still unread (stage 4's list).

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

- The ultraviz viewer needs rebuilding on the evidence record, or retiring.
- Kata's data, env file and program are still on the hub VM, and `~/.ultrapowers/kata-hub.env`, `kata-hub.vmtoken.json` and `kata.curlrc` are still on the laptop; no tool reads them.
- The doctor does not check that the hub can read the evidence repository (`evidence-read`).
- `~/.ultrapowers/fleet.json` still names the expired account `marcus-fireproof.storage`; a launch needs `--account`.
- `skills/ultrawrite/SKILL.md` and `tests/test_plan_parse.py` use `grep -q 'kata 0.17.2' fleet/CONTRACT.md` as an example probe line; it is an example of the grammar and no longer matches the contract.

When starting a sync failed for a reason of bilan's own (the sync model answering 500, a D1 error, a request that expired before admission), the endpoint answered 500 with the error's message as is. That text can quote another Worker's reply, a SQL error, or an internal id, and the page showed it to whoever clicked.

The cause now goes to the Worker's log, and the client gets "The sync could not start. Try again in a moment." The answers that mean something to the viewer (401, 404, 409, 429, 503) are unchanged.

author: philipphoeninger
body:
**Task:** S5-11 (sprint 05) · **Requirements:** SPEC §7.6, SD13 (base of R-AUTH-01, R-AUTH-02, R-AUTH-04, R-ORG-02) · **Invariants:** PRV-11 → `active` (integration part; E2E part with S5-12/S5-14) · ARC-01 – ARC-03 green
**Owner decisions:** 1 (A) plain text + HTML · 2a texts in Platform, the four message types of sprint 05 · 3a legacy mails through the new sender · 4a strict settings · Mailpit approved

## Summary
- **`IEmailSender` in Platform** (`Platform.Contracts/Email`): `AddressConfirmationEmail`, `PasswordResetEmail`, `AlreadyRegisteredEmail`, `OrganisationInvitationEmail`. Sends synchronously with one retry, then throws `EmailDeliveryException` (which carries no cause).
- **Rendering:** the texts are the UX copy's `email.*` keys, held in Platform's embedded `Email/Texts/de.json` (third target of `check-i18n.mjs`). Each mail is `multipart/alternative`: plain text plus an HTML part built from the same text, with the message's own link as the only link and no image, style or script. Values are escaped, and values with control characters are refused.
- **Logs:** the message type above `Debug`; the recipient and the SMTP error only at `Debug`.
- **Settings:** `Email:Smtp:Host/Port/Username/Password/Security`, `Email:From`, `Email:DisplayName`. Only Development and E2E may send without credentials or TLS; every other environment stops at startup. The `catalog`/`roles` command hosts don't register e-mail.
- **#302:** the legacy sign-up and reset mails now go to the user's own address. The legacy mail service, templates and settings are removed.
- **Mailpit** (MIT, pinned by tag and digest) catches all mail in `docker-compose.dev.yml` (UI at http://localhost:8025) and `docker-compose.e2e.yml`.
- **Docs:** TESTING_v59 (V184–V187), ARCHITECTURE_v52 (C138), SPEC v2.20, CLAUDE.md, protocol `docs/sprints/sprint_05/S5-11_email_sender.md`.

No EF migration.

## Checks
- `dotnet build -warnaserror` and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`: clean.
- `dotnet test --solution`: 1001 passed, including a Mailpit Testcontainer round trip for every message type and a server refusal.
- Invariant gate, i18n (three targets), Figma links, API notices and `reuse lint`: green.
- Real app: the branch API ran with `dotnet run` against a throwaway PostgreSQL and Mailpit. Sign-up → mail to the real address; confirmation link → 200; reset mail to the same address; unknown address → 200 and no mail.
- E2E was not run locally because the disk was full; no client or E2E file changed. CI runs the five projects on the stack that now includes Mailpit.
- **TD-12:** the `compose.log` artefact holds no secrets. The only E2E secret is the random DB password, and Mailpit logs no recipients.

## Review findings
| Finding | Sorting |
|---|---|
| An address Identity accepts but MimeKit can't parse caused a 500 after the account was stored | fixed: counts as a failed send |
| The exception constructor with an inner exception could carry an SMTP text that quotes the address | fixed: removed |
| MailKit's default timeout is 2 min per operation, so with the retry a request can hang for minutes | follow-up: needs a 🔧 value (`Email:Smtp:Timeout`) |
| forgot-password answers slower for a known address than an unknown one | follow-up: S5-13 |
| Umlauts appear as numeric entities in the HTML | won't fix: valid HTML |

## Open points (protocol §5)
1. **Owner, before staging sends mail (#236):**
   - set `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` (the API won't start without them)
   - make sure Lettermint open/click tracking is off
   - set `App__BaseUrl` to staging's HTTPS origin (the default is `http://procureaccess.tech:4200`)
2. PRV-11 E2E part with S5-12/S5-14.
3. SMTP timeout setting (proposed issue).
4. Timing of forgot-password (S5-13).
5. `email.confirm.body` hard-codes „24 Stunden“ (UX copy, S5-12).
6. The legacy reset link carries the address (S5-13).

Closes #302

Give this list's value column a 200px preferred width, allowing it to shrink within narrow rows, and use zero-minimum grid tracks through the environment page, tab panel and list so intrinsic content cannot widen the container. The existing 400px floating editor continues to wrap long and multiline values and clamp to the list width.

Only `web/app.css` changes. The fixed value-column rule applies to Secrets; Variables retain their proportional value column. Other settings and card lists are unaffected.

Validation:
- Chromium and WebKit using the real `createEnvPage` module and production CSS in an isolated browser fixture with synthetic data and mocked persistence (no real vault access).
- Three rows covering short, approximately 28KB unbroken, and multiline values; hidden and revealed editor states; 1280px, 760px and 480px viewports. Value cells stay 200px at normal width and shrink in narrow rows; list and editor dimensions do not depend on value length. Existing editor stays at 400px or less. Baseline note: on current main, secret values already render as a constant number of dots and the floating editor already has a 400px cap, so the original report of value length alone widening the list was not reproducible in these browsers. This change enforces the requested fixed list value width and addresses the grid/flex constraints, including a value cell exceeding the inner row width at very narrow sizes.

author: mogita
body:
## Problem

The Stream API key is an identifier, yet CI reads it from a repository secret. A secret cannot be read back, so nobody can see which test app CI runs against.

## Solution

The workflows read the key from the `STREAM_API_KEY` Actions variable. The API secret stays a repository secret.

## How to verify

1. The CI run on this PR passes with the key coming from the variable.
2. After merge, the scheduled test workflow passes on the default branch and the `STREAM_API_KEY` repository secret is deleted.

author: musharna
body:
## Outcome

- `phylokit-mcp --root DIR` (repeatable, or `PHYLOKIT_ROOTS`) confines every path a tool is given: `fasta_path` and `trees_path` must be files inside a root, and `out_path` creates its file only inside one.
- Off by default. Without the flag or the variable the server behaves exactly as before.
- A path outside the roots is refused with the roots named. The refusal is the same whether or not the outside file exists.

## Why

Audit finding K-M3 (2026-11-10): `fasta_path="../outside/..."` is read, and `out_path` through `../` or a symlinked directory writes outside the working directory. #117 made `SECURITY.md` say so; it also said "there is no option yet to confine paths to a directory". The owner chose an opt-in root over leaving it documented or confining to the working directory by default (which breaks clients that pass absolute paths).

## How

- `roots.py` holds the policy: roots are resolved once, when set.
- `inputs.py` applies it, judging each path twice, because a name can be re-pointed between a check and an open:
  - by name (`realpath`, so `..` and symlinks are followed) before anything is opened or stat'ed;
  - on the descriptor that was opened, asking the kernel where it lives. A read opens first, checks the descriptor, and only then looks at the file's kind and size. A write opens the directory, checks that descriptor, and creates the file relative to it with `O_EXCL`.
- On a platform that cannot locate an open descriptor (neither `/proc` nor `F_GETPATH`), a server with roots set refuses the path; it does not skip the check.

## Acceptance check

```
uv run pytest -q tests/test_roots.py
uv run python benchmarks/perf/ratchet.py
uv run mypy src
```

- `tests/test_roots.py`: 10 passed. Reads and writes by every route (absolute, `..`, symlinked file, symlinked directory, a dangling symlink at the new file's name, a working directory outside the roots), each beside a legitimate path in the same test; nothing appears in the outside directory; a path swapped after the name check is refused at the descriptor, for a read, a read re-pointed at a directory, and a write; environment variable, several roots, flag over environment; the refusal through the server's tool layer.
- Real execution: two real server processes over stdio, one started with `--root` (inside path answered, absolute and `..` paths refused with the roots named) and one without (the same outside file is read), so the refusal is the flag's doing.
- Seen to fail through `mutate-run`, 13 of 13 killed: each name check, each descriptor check, the descriptor check moved after `fstat`, the blocking open (killed by timeout on the FIFO), the size check, read or write not routed, the flag ignored, the environment ignored, `inside` always true, an unlocatable descriptor skipped.
- Work counts equal the baseline (no gated workload reads a path); `mypy src` clean.

## Constraints

- No change with roots unset: same code path for reads and writes, same messages.
- New public surface: the `--root` flag, `PHYLOKIT_ROOTS`, and `PathOutsideRootsError` (an `InputFileError`). This wants a minor version (0.10.0) at the next release; no version is bumped here.
- Roots cover the paths a caller passes. MAFFT's private temporary directory is the server's own and is not inside them.
- Not run: macOS (`F_GETPATH` branch) and Windows. CI is Linux only.

## Risk and revert

- A client that sets roots and passes a path outside them now gets a refusal; that is the feature. Revert is `git revert`; nothing on disk changes format.

author: doriancollier
body:
## What this adds

One **Remote access** switch at the top of Settings → Remote access (DOR-3650, the off-switch item only).

- **Off disconnects other devices at once, and refuses them after.**
  - Refused at the server: `middleware/remote-access-switch.ts` runs in the `/api` chain right after the managed-host guard, ahead of sign-in, webhooks, the app's files and every route; the upgrade router refuses WebSockets the same way. "Another device" is the request classifier's answer: the own tunnel, managed remote access, Wi-Fi, a proxy's forwarding headers, a non-loopback peer or `Host`, a foreign page, the relay. The refusal is a 403 with code `REMOTE_ACCESS_OFF`.
  - Cut on the flip (Security M1): every connection on the three listeners only other devices reach (own tunnel, managed, Wi-Fi) is cut through each one's own socket set, whatever credential opened it. Every remote event stream, streamed MCP or A2A answer and WebSocket on the main listener (a proxy, a non-loopback route) is closed too.
  - Chat from the web (Security M2): the session relay's pin reads as none while off, and the live relay closes on the flip.
- **Never locks the person out.** This computer is never refused, and neither is a container's own published port (`isContainerPortClass`). Hubs and agent computers keep their own gates. A request from this computer never reads the setting.
- **Not affected:** Telegram (polling) and Slack (Socket Mode) dial out, so they keep working, as do local A2A calls. Two things have their own ports and are not covered: the preview port, and Telegram's own webhook listener when that mode is chosen. Settings and the docs say so.
- **Stays off after a restart.** New top-level setting `remoteAccess.enabled`, default on so an upgrade closes nothing. A whole top-level section, so conf writes it and no migration is needed (pinned by an on-disk upgrade test).
- **Only a person turns it on.** Owner-only front-door setting in the reach stake, so `PATCH /api/config` runs the cookie, agent and front-door bars. An agent may write only `false` (`SAFEST_VALUES`). `config_patch` never writes `true`, not even after a person's yes on a card (`NEVER_RAISED_BY_AN_AGENT`, pinned at the tool call site too).
- Carried across a config wipe when off; shown to `config_get`; `GET /api/config` reports `remoteAccess.enabled`.
- **Settings**, with @designer's copy: on reads "Your other devices can reach DorkOS with an API key.", off reads "Off. Only this computer can reach DorkOS.", right after switching off "Off. Other devices are disconnected now." Under the switch, in every state: "Telegram, Slack and preview links aren't affected." No confirm on off. Turning on with nothing set up opens the existing tunnel setup. The ways in are hidden while it is off.
- Docs: `docs/getting-started/configuration.mdx` and `contributing/configuration.md`. Changelog fragment included. Dev Playground: the real tab, on and off-with-nothing-set-up, at `/dev/settings`.

## Not in this PR

- Slowing down bad keys (Should, after launch).
- A write from another process (`dorkos config set`) fires no change listener here: open streams then end at their next reconnect, which is refused.

## Tests

- `http/__tests__/remote-access-off.test.ts` (real config, real config route, real chain): off refuses the own tunnel, managed, Wi-Fi and a proxy on the next request, and before sign-in, `/mcp`, the app files and health; this computer still works; it stays off after a restart (read from disk); the person turns it back on; an agent caller's `PATCH` to turn it on is a 403. An event stream each of those holds is closed on the flip; one from this computer stays open; another setting closes nothing; each registered listener is cut once.
- `own-tunnel-ingress`, `managed-ingress` and `lan-access` tests: `dropConnections` cuts a kept-alive connection (and, on managed, an event stream and a forwarded socket) and keeps listening.
- `upgrade-router.test.ts`: off refuses a tunnel, managed or Wi-Fi WebSocket before any route runs; a remote socket already open closes with 4403 on the flip; this computer's stays open.
- `session-relay-flag.test.ts`: no pin while off; the flip closes the live relay; other settings don't.
- `middleware/__tests__/remote-access-switch.test.ts`: the relayed class is refused while off; a Docker install's own port is never refused; the same request without the container flag, or behind a proxy, is.
- `config-patch-cloud-owner.test.ts` (the tool itself) and `operator-only-tightening.test.ts`: never on, even with a card; off on a card and at Full.
- `RemoteAccessTab.test.tsx`: the switch's states and copy, an older server reads as on, off hides the ways in, no confirm, the just-off line, on with nothing set up opens setup.
- Config guards updated: write policy, disclosure, default verdicts (permissive cap 23 → 24, reason recorded), wipe carryover, config schema, config-manager upgrade test.
- Fail-first: before wiring, 10 of 11 chain cases and 7 of 8 client cases failed. With the stream wiring put back to the first commit, 6 stream and socket cases fail. Emptying each listener's `dropConnections`, removing the relay checks, or dropping the rule at the `config_patch` call site turns those 6 tests red.
- Ran locally: every server test under `services/core`, `services/session`, `routes`, `http`, `middleware`, `startup` and the server root, plus the client settings tests; `@dorkos/shared`, `@dorkos/server` and `@dorkos/client` typecheck, eslint on touched files, prettier, `check:max-lines`, `check:copy-length`, the vocab and banned-word gates. `docs:export-api` shows no change.

Refs DOR-3650

## Summary

The Codex public contract now records `codex --help` and `codex app-server --help`, as the Claude contract records `claude --help`. A new `codex` subcommand (a native ACP mode, for one), a changed `app-server --listen` transport list, or an added or removed `daemon` or `proxy` subcommand now fails the pinned and latest-contract drift jobs instead of passing unnoticed.

Fixes #367
Fixes #363

## Changes

- mea: `mea capture --harness codex` runs the two help probes next to `--version` and the schema generator, writes `help.txt` and `app-server-help.txt` verbatim, and lists both probes in the manifest. A named-fake test (`public_codex_capture_records_both_help_surfaces_with_digests`) covers the probe order, the written text, the manifest probes and the digests.
- fixtures: `fixtures/codex/contract/` gains the two help files and their manifest digests, captured at the pinned `codex-cli 0.167.1` through `scripts/install-vendor-cli.sh`. Two consecutive captures match the committed files through `scripts/check-vendor-contract.sh`; the schemas and version are unchanged.
- docs: `docs/vendor-drift.md` and `docs/harness-codex.md` describe the probes and what now fails the drift jobs.

## Compliance impact

- [x] No vendor surface changes, or the change stays on a documented surface (cite it below)
- [x] No login handling was added; no credential is read, stored or forwarded
- [x] `docs/compliance.md` and `docs/harness-<vendor>.md` updated if the posture moved

Vendor document followed: the `--help` output of the official `codex` CLI. The probes are read-only, need no login, and spawn only the host-supplied binary.

## Test Plan

- [x] `scripts/check.sh` passes
- [x] Fixtures re-captured with `mea capture` where a vendor dialect changed
- [x] Additive on the public API, or the minor was bumped (0.x semver)

## Notes

The help text is stored verbatim, not parsed into a surface file. The Claude capture does the same for `help.txt`; a parsed `cli-surface.json` for Codex can follow if the diffs prove noisy.

Help output is not wrapped to a terminal width, because the CLI is not attached to one. The pinned job reproduces it on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; the capture here ran on Linux x64 only.

author: marianna-13
body:
## Historia

**US-020 · E8 Calidad y no funcionales (NFR-02)**
Como equipo queremos que el desarrollo y las conclusiones acepten textos muy largos, para no truncar el relato de la reunión.

> Nota del backlog: «Límite real de caracteres a validar en diseño de base de datos».

## Límite elegido: 50.000 caracteres por campo

- Equivale a unas 15 páginas carta. Alcanza para el relato de una reunión larga y deja un techo para la página y el PDF.
- El número está en un solo lugar del código, `aportes.MAX_LARGO_APORTE`, y la base de datos repite el mismo valor en un `CHECK`. Si cambia uno, hay que cambiar el otro (los dos archivos lo advierten).
- Se cuentan caracteres, no bytes: una tilde, una eñe o un emoji valen 1, tanto en Python (`len`) como en PostgreSQL (`char_length`).
- El navegador envía los saltos de línea como `\r\n`. Se normalizan a `\n` **antes** de contar, para que el contador de la página y el servidor den la misma cifra.

## Qué cambia

- **`db/migraciones/US-020_aporte_textos_largos.sql`**
  - Pasa `acta_participantes.desarrollo` y `conclusiones` a `TEXT`, con un `CHECK` de 50.000 caracteres.
  - Agrega `aporte_actualizado_en`.
  - Es idempotente: sirve si las columnas no existen, si son `VARCHAR(n)` o si ya son `TEXT`.
- **`aporte_texto.py`** (nuevo): normalización, validación y el límite.
  - Quita espacios solo al inicio y al final.
  - Elimina el carácter nulo, que PostgreSQL no admite.
  - Un campo vacío se guarda como `NULL`.
- **`app.py`**: `MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE = 2 MB`. Flask corta los formularios normales en 500 KB con un 413 y se pierde lo escrito. El peor caso del aporte es 1,2 MB (el cálculo está en `aporte_texto.py`).
- **`aportes.py`** (de `main`) y **`actas.py`**
  - La ruta `POST /actas/<id>/aporte` (`aportes.guardar_aporte`) ahora usa la validación de 50.000 caracteres.
  - Responde 404 si el acta no existe y 403 si la persona no es participante, antes de validar el texto.
  - Bloquea el acta con `FOR SHARE` mientras guarda, para que no se cierre a mitad del guardado.
  - Si hay un error de validación **no redirige**: la página vuelve con el texto escrito y el mensaje con el conteo, p. ej. «El desarrollo tiene 50.001 caracteres; el máximo es 50.000.».
  - La consulta de `ver` se movió a `contexto_ver()` para reutilizarla, sin cambios de comportamiento.
- **`templates/ver_acta.html`** y **`static/css/actas.css`**
  - Sección **Mi aporte** con dos campos, solo para participantes y con el acta abierta.
  - Cada campo tiene un contador «1.234 / 50.000 caracteres» que avisa al llegar al tope.
  - Si se pega un texto que no cabe, un aviso dice cuánto quedó por fuera. El navegador no lo corta en silencio.
  - Pregunta antes de salir si hay cambios sin guardar.
  - Los aportes completos se muestran en el acta conservando los saltos de línea.

## Para probar

1. **Obligatorio antes de usar la rama:** correr en pgAdmin `db/migraciones/US-013_aportes_compromisos_firma.sql` (ya está en `main`) y después `db/migraciones/US-020_aporte_textos_largos.sql`. Se puede correr más de una vez. Sin esa migración, ver acta responde 503 porque falta la columna `aporte_actualizado_en`.
2. Entrar como un participante del acta, ir al acta, llenar **Mi aporte** y guardar.
3. Pegar un texto de más de 50.000 caracteres. Debe avisar cuánto no cupo.

## Pruebas

`python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Son 23 pruebas, no necesitan base de datos ni dependencias nuevas:
- normalización de `\r\n`;
- límite exacto, y un carácter de más;
- tildes y emoji;
- un formulario de 1,2 MB sin 413;
- avisos dentro de Mi aporte.

Además se probó contra PostgreSQL 16:
- la migración corrida 2 veces;
- guardar 50.000 caracteres y rechazar 50.001;
- 403 para quien no participa.

La pantalla se revisó a 1440 y 390 px.

## Integración con el commit «PDF» de `main` (c1994ed)

`main` ya traía su propio aporte (máx. 5.000 caracteres), compromisos, «Mi firma» con imagen y la descarga en PDF. Esta rama ya trae `main` integrado, sin conflictos:
- **Una sola ruta para guardar el aporte:** `aportes.guardar_aporte`, con el límite de 50.000 caracteres, la normalización y el bloqueo de US-020. Reemplaza la validación de 5.000.
- **Validación en su propio archivo:** el texto se valida en `aporte_texto.py`, para no importar `aportes.py` desde `actas.py`, que habría sido un import circular.
- **Lo que se conserva de `main`:** compromisos, «Mi firma» con imagen y la descarga en PDF, sin cambios.
- **`ver_acta.html`:** queda un solo formulario «Mi aporte», el de US-020 con contador.

## Notas

- Si la base real tiene vistas sobre `acta_participantes.desarrollo` o `conclusiones`, el `ALTER TYPE` fallará. Habría que recrear esas vistas, porque el esquema base (`db/init`) no está en el repo y no se pudo comprobar.
- Este PR trae lo mínimo de **Mi aporte** que se necesita para probar textos largos. La firma y el cierre del acta van en el PR de US-013, que se apoya en este. **Este PR se fusiona primero.**

author: jhihyangwu
body:
## Why
`SurfaceFx` can flash, dissolve, glow and scroll a surface, but cannot move it. Living or floating surfaces (a breathing creature, a heaving ship deck, a wobbling jelly, a pulsing membrane) needed per-frame mesh rewriting from game code, which is slow and does not reach the GPU's vertex stage.

## What
- **`SurfaceFx.ripple`** (peak height in metres, 0..4, default 0 = off), **`ripple_scale`** (main wavelength in metres, default 2) and **`ripple_speed`** (crest speed in m/s, default 0.5; negative reverses):
  - **`function/plugins/visuals/render_schemas.ts`, `core/ports/render3d.ts`, `function/plugins/render3d/surface_fx.ts`:** fields, port and pass-through.
  - **`platform/browser/render3d/layout.ts`:** packed in the material block's spare `fxLines.yzw` slots, so the block keeps its size.
  - **`platform/browser/render3d/material_fx_shaders.ts`, `shaders.ts`:** `fxRipple()` sums travelling waves over world space; the mesh vertex stage moves each vertex along its normal and tilts the normal against the wave slope (WGSL and GLSL). A dense mesh visibly undulates; a coarse one still shades as if it did. Shadows are cast from the still surface.
- **`sdk/parallax/__init__.pyi`, `docs/concepts/visuals.md`:** documented; `docs/reference` regenerated.

```python
blob.add(SurfaceFx(ripple=0.05, ripple_scale=0.6, ripple_speed=0.3))
```

## Verified
- New tests in `surface_fx.test.ts`: the fields reach the shape's material effects and turn effects on; height, wavelength and speed are packed after the hologram lines with the effects flag and time set.
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/runtime typecheck` clean.

author: scala-steward
rubys
body:
The follow-up that #2127 deferred. This makes the fixpoint's library setup incremental and trims three harvest scans. The work is @tobi's, from his compile-time work on a large app, adapted onto the per-round caches `main` already has (`BodySurveys`, from 3601e3eec). The emitted output is byte-identical.

## What

**Library setup reads only the classes a pass rewrote.** Every fixpoint pass walked every library class's method bodies twice:
- `mailer_templates::looking_up_mailers`, to find which classes pass `mail` a `template_name:` or `template_path:`;
- the `module_ivars` loop, for each module's instance-method ivar writes.

Both answers are now kept per class in `BodySurveys::library` and refreshed under the rule the body surveys already use: `stale = retyped_since_survey ∪ dirty`.
- A module declared more than once is walked again in declaration order, because `extract_ivar_assignments` merges into the map the earlier declarations left, widening against it.
- In debug builds, every kept read is compared with a fresh one, and a mismatch panics with `kept library setup reads of … are stale`.
- `lookup_dirs` splits into `looking_up_mailers_with` and `lookup_dirs_of`, so the kept answers feed the same code.

**Harvest:**
- **Block values:** a method can return its block's value only if it has a block parameter or a `yield` in its body, so other methods aren't asked. This is a pre-filter: `returns_block_value` is unchanged.
- **View context:** `registry::view::InstanceHelpers` walks the helper owners once and answers every `helper_method` name. Before, every library class and controller was scanned once per helper.
- **Concern fold:** the AR catalog test is a set and the same-name declaration test an index, instead of a linear scan per method.

**Timing spans:** `typing: library setup`, `harvest: returns`, `harvest: block values` and `harvest: folds`, under `ROUNDHOUSE_TIMINGS=1`.

## Why

On the large app, library setup took about 11–12 s summed over the compile's passes. With these changes it took about 3 s. Block values fell from about 2.2 s to 1.6 s.

## Behavior changes to review

None intended, and the emitted output is byte-identical (see Verification). The risk is a kept read going stale. A class whose bodies changed without landing in `stale` would keep its old template options or ivar writes. Debug builds check for that on every pass, and `library_reads_tests::a_rewritten_class_left_out_of_the_stale_set_fails_the_check` pins that the check fires.

## Verification

**Emitted output.** I emitted 7 fixtures (real-blog, store, tiny-blog, tiny-api, tiny-blog-uuid, roda-blog, gem-capabilities) to 13 targets with a `main` binary and a binary from this branch.
- 45 trees are byte-identical.
- 46 runs are refused by both binaries with the same diagnostics.
- No run's diagnostics differ.

**Timing.** I used a synthetic 1,000-model app from `scripts/synth-app` (25,003 `.rb` files) with `--target ruby` and release builds. The runs were interleaved, and the `main` binary carried the same spans. Each number sums the 37 passes' spans in one run, and the trees are identical.

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| typing: library setup | 1.48, 1.45 s | 0.77, 0.46 s |
| harvest: returns | 1.31, 1.36 s | 1.39, 1.32 s |
| harvest: block values | 0.38, 0.38 s | 0.38, 0.38 s |
| harvest: folds | 0.77, 0.76 s | 0.76, 0.76 s |
| wall | 68.9, 65.4 s | 67.6, 63.0 s |

The synthetic app has few helpers, block-taking methods or concerns, so only library setup moves there.

Peak RSS varied from 4,256 to 4,718 MB, and that spread is already there at `ingest: compact`, before any changed code runs (1,643–2,101 MB). Growth after that point overlaps: 2,610–2,773 MB on `main` and 2,507–2,966 MB on this branch.

**Tests.**
- `bin/rh verify --all` on macOS ran 10,451 tests, with 44 failures. Those are the same environmental failures as on `main` in #2127:
  - 40 `emit_and_run` tests need gems this machine lacks;
  - 3 CI-policy tests call `nproc`;
  - 1 runs `scripts/campfire-suite` under macOS's bash 3, which has no `mapfile`.
- New tests: `analyze::library_reads_tests`.

## Left out

On the fork, each class's kept results hang off a per-class print of its typed trees, and `main` doesn't have that print. Three parts depend on it and aren't ported:
- the kept per-model method returns and `readonly_attr_types`;
- the kept "which bodies yield" answers;
- reading an includer's own defs once per concern fold, which builds on fork-only own-defs logic.
