author: rbrtbn
body:
## Summary

**Posted and edited times per question.** The question header in the workspace now shows something like `Posted 13 Nov 22:10 · edited 23:41`. The date is left out of the edited time when it falls on the same day as the posted time. No new table: `snapshot()` works out `questionTimes` in the pass over the grill's events that it already makes.
- Posted is the first `loaded` event whose `questions.added` lists the question. Loads from before question diffs were recorded have no `questions` field, so for those the grill's first load stands in.
- Edited is whichever is later: the last load whose `questions.changed` lists the question, or the last `revised` rewrite of its step. Comments don't count. It is left out when the question was never edited.
- Squad pages key each member's times by the shared question id (`server/squad.ts`).
- `Snapshot.questionTimes` is an `optionalKey`, so a page served by an older server shows no times.

**No more silent 4,000-character truncation.** Notes, own answers, asks and the send message used to be cut short on the server without warning. Now the server answers 400 with, for example, "The note is 4,005 characters; the limit is 4,000. Shorten it and try again." The limit lives in one constant, `TEXT_LIMIT` in `src/domain.ts`, which both server and client use.
- In the composers, a character count appears from 3,600 characters and turns red over the limit.
  - Workspace: own answer, note, Review message, discussion box and quote reply.
  - Legacy page: Send dialog, Talk composer and the thread box.
- Send and Ask are disabled while the text is over the limit.
- An over-limit ask is no longer posted, and its draft is kept. Before, the draft was cleared before the server had accepted the ask.
- An over-limit note or own answer still posts when the box loses focus. The server's message then shows in the existing save-error banner, and the error clears once the text is shortened and the box loses focus again.
- The counters only read the drafts the Model already gets from input events. No textarea is bound to the Model.

**Not in this PR: keeping drafts through the build reload.** This was item 2 of the plan and was dropped from this PR. #13 (`fix/wispr-dictation`) already makes the build reload keep box text, the Review message and focus. These changes sit next to #13's textareas in `src/view.ts` and `src/workspaceView.ts`, so expect small merge conflicts there. They only add sibling counter elements and `Disabled` conditions.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:server`: clean.
- `bun run test`: vitest 43 files, 298 tests pass; bun 285 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run lint`: the same 24 errors as `origin/main`, compared as sorted lists without line numbers.
- New tests:
  - `server/store.test.ts`: posted and edited from added and changed loads; rewrite versus comment; legacy loads with no question diff; squad shared ids.
  - `server/routing.test.ts`: over HTTP, all four kinds of text are refused with 400 and nothing is recorded; text exactly at the limit is kept whole.
  - `src/questionTimes.scene.test.ts`: the three label shapes, and no label when the server sends no times.
  - `src/textLimit.scene.test.ts`: counters, and Send/Ask disabled while over the limit.
  - `src/textLimit.story.test.ts`: an over-limit ask keeps its draft and posts nothing.
- Browser check on an isolated server (port 4391, temporary database, `GF_POLL_*=0`) with Playwright:
  - The header showed `Posted 14 Nov 01:35 · edited 01:36` after a reload changed the question's title.
  - The Review and note counters showed.
  - The note's 400 appeared in the save banner and cleared once the note was shortened.

## Size

Code +233 −23 (including 18 lines of CSS), tests +349 −2.

## What changed

Add opt-in `.ts-prose` styling for authored articles: heading rhythm, nested lists, quotes, underlined links with focus outlines, and literal code that can wrap. The rules use existing semantic tokens and logical inline sides. Add a standalone synthetic HTML example and a small Jekyll post layout that wraps rendered content while preserving the existing document shell and permalink.

## Why

The planned blog pilot needs article typography beyond dashboard cards. The expanded disposable Markdown fixture now exercises native prose and escaped code through the pinned Jekyll stack.

## Behaviour changes

- New typography applies only beneath `.ts-prose`; existing document-wide selectors are unchanged.
- Code preserves source whitespace and can wrap rather than creating a horizontal scroll region. Print rules permit long quotes/code to split.
- The fixture verifier now checks the post article boundary, headings, nested list, quote, internal fragment link, escaped inline/fenced code and rule.
- JSON models still accept plain text only. This is not an HTML/URL sanitizer or syntax-highlighting palette. No new dependencies, framework adapters or CI workflow.

- `npm test`: 58 passed on local Node 26, including existing bounds/escaping, CSS token contrast, new scoped-source contracts and verifier corruption cases.
- `npm run build:examples`: rebuilt assets; all 18 generated HTML pages differ only by the new scoped CSS block.
- Six fresh synthetic builds passed: full/minimal/empty at root and `/synthetic-preview`, Jekyll 3.10.0 / Liquid 4.0.4 / Ruby 4.0.5. Used the existing isolated bundle, resolved locally and installed no gems. The final verifier passed all six outputs.

## What

## Why
The test assumes no other row falls on the days the sweep rebuilds. CI runs other suites against the
same database with the real clock, so from 2026-11-14 UTC their runs landed on those days and the sweep
reported 4 rows instead of 1 (`expected { days: 2, rows: 4 } to deeply equal { days: 2, rows: 1 }`).

`publish` jobs: no images were published for #743's merge commit.

- typecheck, `yarn biome check` on the file, `docs:check` and `invariants:check` pass.

body:
O painel do aquecimento apresentava o botão circular demasiado grande e os estados dos termóstatos ultrapassavam o mostrador. O Diagnóstico abria sem registos e mostrava uma ação de guardar/reiniciar sem configurações para editar.

- Reduz o botão circular para 96 px no computador (76 px no telemóvel) e adapta os indicadores ao espaço interior.
- Mostra o nome de rede configurado na barra lateral. Retira a legenda permanente, preservando o espaço até ao menu e as mensagens de falha/comando pendente.
- Ajusta os textos dentro dos termóstatos, preservando os cartões e os comandos existentes.
- Carrega os registos ao abrir Diagnóstico, incluindo acesso direto após autenticação; Atualizar volta a consultá-los. Oculta Guardar configurações e reiniciar apenas nesse separador.
- Identifica o firmware como 0.3.23-orbit-ntp-ota.

Validação: compilação ESP32 local concluída; test_web_ui_minimal.cjs, test_orbit_controls.cjs e test_web_ui.cjs passaram (Node 24.22.1, jsdom 30.1.3). Verificação no navegador com dados simulados a 1440, 390 e 320 px: texto contido, temas, navegação entre separadores/voltar, registos após login e mensagens de erro/pendente. Sem erros JavaScript observados. Revisão independente sem regressões identificadas.

Âmbito: apenas este firmware. Não altera a lógica de aquecimento, KNX, rede, NTP ou validação OTA. Não foi instalado no equipamento. Aguardar revisão e aprovação antes de integrar.

author: billmal071
body:
## What

In Checkers (move, resign, expire-turn) and Whot draw, a request that lost the `updated_at` optimistic-lock race returned `{}`, which the route turned into a 200 success. State stayed correct, but a client or bot trusting the 200 would show a move or draw that never happened (found by playtesting: 4 concurrent identical Checkers moves all returned 200; 4 concurrent Whot draws returned 200 x3 while the hand grew by one card).

## Fix

The four `if (!won) return {}` sites now return `{ error: 'Another action already updated this turn — try again' }`, the same wording Rummy uses. The routes already map process errors to 400, so no route changes. The winning request is unchanged.

## Tests

New `src/lib/lost-race.test.ts`: a fake client makes the conditional update match 0 rows; asserts the error and that no hand write or `markGameFinished` follows. Existing `checkers.test.ts` passes; eslint, prettier and tsc clean.

## Not included

`processWhotPlay` has the same pattern (~L1152) and the empty-draw-pile branch of `processWhotDraw` ignores the `persistSession` result; both are left for a follow-up. No migrations.

---

author: andre-atkinson
body:
Closes #24

## What changed

**Self-care while charging (always on, no toggle, no new NVS key).** Plugged into USB, with the PMU answering, and untouched for 10 minutes, the pet looks after itself up to half: once a minute the first need under 40, in the order food, hygiene (which also clears the poops), energy, joy, goes back up to 50.

- `Pet::setCharger(pmuOk, usb, idleMs)` (new): the sketch calls it on every loop pass, before `pet.update()`, with `batBegin()`'s result (now kept as `pmuReady`), the cached `usbPresent()` and `idleSince(now, lastInteract)`. It only sets a RAM flag.
- `Pet::selfCare()` (new, private) runs from `Pet::tick()`, after the minute's drain and before the slip-up and run-away checks. Its position is the guard: the early returns above it keep it off during a ceremony, the starter or egg choice, as an egg and asleep. `syncClock()` (the powered-off catch-up) never runs `tick()`.
- It is not the player's care: no `registerCare()` (streak), no `addBond()`, no medal of its own, no heart, no eating state. (Because a need it lifts that minute is not a slip-up, a pet left on the charger can still earn IN SHAPE at level 5: owner decision 3, documented after R2-1.) A visible event would wake the screen and restart the idle time that keeps self-care on, so it is silent. No `save()` of its own: `tick()`'s periodic save covers it. Each top-up logs one serial line, `self-care: food 14->50`.
- **USB unknown counts as unplugged.** `usbPresent()`/`usbPresentNow()` return `true` when the AXP2101 never answered at boot. Self-care ANDs in `pmuReady`, so that case is off. `rtcbat.cpp` and every existing caller of `usbPresent*()` are unchanged. A failed I2C read after boot already reads as unplugged (XPowersLib's `getRegisterBit()` returns false on error).
- **"Ready to evolve" chime at most once per level for each form** (`EvoChime` in `pet.h`, used in `loop()`). The needs now keep coming back over 40 on the charger, so the evolve button came and went several times an hour and each return chimed. The chime still needs the button to appear (as before), and now also a level it hasn't chimed at for this form. A new form (an evolution, or a new pet, which is always an egg first) starts over.
- **Simulator:** `pmu ok|none` boot step. `none` makes the fake PMU behave like `rtcbat.cpp` without the AXP2101: `batBegin()` false, USB reads present, no battery, no PKEY, no power-off. Two scripts: `sim/scripts/self-care.txt` and `self-care-no-pmu.txt`.
- README (game manual, simulator steps), CHANGELOG, CREDITS (Mu-Muu/TamaPoke's `Pet::autoCare()`, MIT; the idea re-implemented, offline).

## Owner decisions (2026-11-14)

1. Fixed order food → hygiene → energy → joy, one need per minute (as Mu-Muu). Food or hygiene under 30 triples the joy drain, so fixing them first protects joy too.
2. Hygiene under 40 clears all poops and raises hygiene to 50. With three poops hygiene drops 13 a minute, so raising it alone would undo itself and take every slot.
3. Slip-up and run-away counters are never touched directly; the top-up runs before their checks, so a need lifted that minute is not a slip-up and a run-away can't build. Old slip-ups stay.
4. No special case for relaxed pace (every minute in both), open screens (only the idle time counts) or bedtime (off asleep; resumes after the wake-up if still untouched on USB).
5. Evolve chime at most once per level (for each form, after review finding R1-2).

## Why it costs nothing on power

On USB the loop never light-sleeps (`lightSleepAllowed()` needs `!usb`), and with the PMU missing `usbPresent()` is true, so no light sleep either. The minute tick keeps running without a new wakeup, and `usbPresent()` is the cached read (2 s, 10 s with the screen off), so no extra I2C. On battery it is off.

A model of the steady state on the charger keeps every need between 35 and 50: clear of #9's ~25 attention threshold and the ≤10 slip-up. Top-ups re-arm #9's call where one had fired.

## How it was tested

- `tools/gate.sh`: GATE GREEN on fa558ba (the final head, after the round-2 fixes): host tests 390/390 (also under ASan/UBSan), i18n formats, no-network, 1.75C and 1.75 builds at the 20-warning baseline, simulator 20/20 screens on both boards. Earlier: GATE GREEN on 5bf19ff (host tests 388/388) and on 2e6b0ed after the round-1 fixes (by the fixer, 389/389; `--no-build` re-run by me). On 5bf19ff: (also under ASan/UBSan), i18n formats, no-network, 1.75C and 1.75 builds at the 20-warning baseline, simulator 20/20 screens on both boards (its one host warning is the existing unused `sy` at `TamaPoke.ino:2197`).
- 25 new host tests in `test/test_pet.cpp` (18 `selfcare.*`, 7 `evochime.*`) and 2 in `test/test_sim.cpp` (`SimScript.pmu_is_a_boot_step`, `SimPower.without_the_pmu_usb_reads_present_like_the_firmware`).
- **Simulator** (`tools/sim.sh --script self-care`, 1.75C): on battery for 22 min, food falls to 36 and nothing tops it up. USB in, PWR wakes the screen (the touch): 9 minutes later `STATS` still shows `com=18 fel=3 lim=0` and the log has no `self-care:` line. At the tenth untouched minute `self-care: food 14->50`, then `hygiene 0->50` and `joy 0->50` on the next two minutes, and after that one need now and then as each dips under 40 (`STATS`: `com=42 fel=42 ene=49 lim=48`). The screen before shows "Needs a bath!" with two poops; after, "It's happy", no poops, bars around half.
- **Simulator, PMU unknown** (`--script self-care-no-pmu`): `pmu none` + `usb on`, 40 min untouched: `HEALTH ... bat=-1% usb=1`, 0 light sleeps (as on the board), `STATS com=0 fel=0`, and no `self-care:` line.
- **Not exercised on hardware.** Not flashed. Unchecked on the board: the AXP2101's VBUS reading driving it on the real charger, the PMU-missing path, the minute cadence over a long charge, and the chime on the real speaker.

### Mutation evidence

Committed first (765f86c; M23 on 87cffc5), then one script applied each mutation, rebuilt the test binary, ran only the named test, recorded the first failing assertion and restored the file (`git status` clean afterwards). None failed to compile.

| # | Mutation | Test | Result, first failing assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `SELFCARE_LEVEL` 50 → 100 (`pet.h`) | `selfcare.on_usb_after_ten_idle_minutes` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2169: p.fullness == (uint8_t)50 -> 100 vs 50` |
| M2 | `SELFCARE_BELOW` 40 → 41 (`pet.h`) | `selfcare.a_need_at_40_or_more` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2182: p.fullness == (uint8_t)40 -> 50 vs 40` |
| M3 | energy branch moved before hygiene in `selfCare()` | `selfcare.food_then_hygiene` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2201: p.hygiene == (uint8_t)50 -> 2 vs 50` |
| M4 | `else if` chain → independent `if`s (every need in one minute) | `selfcare.one_need_per_minute` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2229: CHECK(p.hygiene < 40 && p.energy < 40 && p.joy < 40) only one need per minute` |
| M5 | `poops = 0;` removed from the hygiene branch | `selfcare.hygiene_also_clears` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2241: p.poops == (uint8_t)0 -> 3 vs 0` |
| M6 | `setCharger()`: `pmuOk &&` dropped | `selfcare.usb_unknown` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2254: CHECK(p.fullness < 40 && p.hygiene < 40 && p.energy < 40 && p.joy < 40)` |
| M7 | `setCharger()`: `usb &&` dropped | `selfcare.never_on_battery` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2267: CHECK(p.fullness < 40 && p.hygiene < 40 && p.energy < 40 && p.joy < 40)` |

| M9 | `registerCare();` added to `selfCare()` | `selfcare.is_not_the_players_care` | CAUGHT: `test_pet.cpp:2311: p.streak == (uint16_t)0 -> 1 vs 0` |

author: yungsnat
body:
`parse_access_token` added a token response's `expires_in` to `Instant::now()` unchecked, so an extreme value from the token endpoint (for example `u64::MAX`, which parses to `i64::MAX` seconds) panicked whilst minting a Vertex token.

The addition now uses `checked_add`. An expiry `Instant` cannot represent caches the token as never expiring, which is how the file already treats a response with no `expires_in` (google-auth's behaviour); the `AccessToken` doc now says so. Values that fit are unchanged. A token that does expire early costs one rejected request: the existing 401 handling drops the cached token and mints a new one.

Testing:

- New `token_with_an_expiry_beyond_instant_range_is_cached_as_never_expiring`: a mock token endpoint returns `expires_in: u64::MAX`; the token is minted, then reused without a second request. Without the fix the test panics with an overflow on Linux and macOS. On Windows `i64::MAX` seconds fits in `Instant`, so a Windows run does not show the fault; a comment in the test says so.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p hermes-agent --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the `vertex::` tests in `cargo test -p hermes-agent --lib`.

## Summary

Strengthen the existing PTY regression test for the OSC 4 scrollback-gradient implementation.

- Assert that palette updates continue during a completely idle interval with no PTY input.
- Run a short foreground command while the gradient worker is active and assert that new OSC 4 updates arrive before the next prompt.
- Use fresh-output waits for prompt and preexec markers to avoid matching stale terminal output.
- Extend only the test animation interval so the foreground-command assertion has a deterministic observation window.

The production animation implementation is unchanged. The proposed alternative that redraws a gradient inside PROMPT via ZLE was intentionally not adopted because it would reintroduce the interaction dependency this feature is meant to remove.

## Verification

GitHub Actions passed on both `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`, including:
- Autonomous updates while the PTY receives no input.
- New palette updates while a foreground command is executing.
- The existing scrollback, prompt-buffer, and worker-lifecycle checks.

author: bachtly-servant
body:
PR 1 of the #80 build ([design](https://github.com/bachtly/daily-kaizen/blob/design/80-insights/docs/design/2026-11-14-insights/design.md) §3 and §9, draft #100).

## What
- **Tables**:
  - `week_summaries`: one row per user-week, facts as jsonb.
  - `insights`: cards with status `new`/`accepted`/`dismissed`, an optional `dismiss_reason`, `active_until` and `result`.
  - `coach_notes`: append-only versions.
  - `insight_runs`: one row per generation attempt.
- **RLS**: the phone selects its own `week_summaries`, `insights` and `coach_notes`; `insight_runs` is job-only. No direct writes.
- **Phone RPCs** (`authenticated`, filtered by `auth.uid()`):
  - `accept_insight`: this or last week only; replaces another accepted card of the week; the change runs the following week.
  - `dismiss_insight(p_id, p_reason)`: the reason is optional, trimmed, 1–140 characters, and can be added later.
  - `undo_insight`.
  - `keep_change`: only while the change runs this week; idempotent.
  - `set_coach_note`: at most 1200 characters; `''` clears it.
- **Job helper** (`service_role`): `save_insights` replaces a week's cards I haven't acted on, and keeps accepted and dismissed ones.
- **Error keys**: `insight_not_found`, `insight_too_old`, `reason_too_long`, `change_not_running`, `note_too_long`, plus the check constraint names.

Nothing uses these tables yet; the Edge Function and app come in the next PRs.

## Checks
- `supabase test db`: 12 files, 386 tests pass (45 new in `insights.test.sql`).

author: marianna-13
body:
## Historia

**US-005 · E2 Creación del acta (RF-005, CA-RF-005-01, RN-014)**
Como usuario que crea el acta quiero elegir la regional y ver solo sus centros, para diligenciar el lugar institucional sin errores.

## Qué cambia

`main` ya filtraba los centros con JavaScript. Este PR completa lo que faltaba sin reescribir `llenarCentros`:

- **Funciona sin JavaScript.**
  - El servidor pinta todos los centros agrupados por regional con `<optgroup>`.
  - El select del centro ya no arranca deshabilitado.
  - Con JavaScript, la página deja solo los centros de la regional elegida y los lee de la misma página (ya no se incrusta el JSON `CENTROS`).
- **Regional sin centros.** El select muestra «Sin centros registrados» y queda deshabilitado. La ayuda debajo explica qué hacer. En los demás casos la ayuda dice cuántos hay, p. ej. «16 centros en Antioquia».
- **Validación en el servidor con un mensaje distinto por caso** (`errores_lugar` en `actas.py`):
  - sin regional;
  - regional inexistente;
  - regional sin centros;
  - sin centro;
  - centro inexistente;
  - centro de otra regional.
- **Selección conservada.** Si el formulario vuelve con errores, se conserva la regional elegida y el centro solo si pertenece a ella.
- **Flecha de los select.** `actas.css` usaba `background:` y borraba la flecha que pone `style.css`. Ahora usa `background-color`.

## Catálogo de regionales y centros (opcional)

`db/migraciones/US-005_catalogo_regionales_centros.sql` carga **33 regionales y 118 centros**.

**Es opcional:** el alcance geográfico real del aplicativo sigue en *Temas abiertos*. Córranlo solo si el equipo decide cargar el catálogo nacional.

- **Fuente:** Directorio de regionales de sena.edu.co (https://www.sena.edu.co/la-entidad/directorio-regionales?vista=lista), consultado el 2026-11-13.
- **Cruce:** los 117 centros con código coinciden uno a uno con los datos abiertos del SENA en datos.gov.co (conjunto `vv8g-8u9u`). El centro 118 es nuevo en Puerto Boyacá y aparece en el listado de caprendizaje.sena.edu.co.
- **Única corrección:** el centro 9110 de Boyacá queda como «Centro de Desarrollo Agropecuario y Agroindustrial», como lo publican datos.gov.co y caprendizaje.
- **Cómo se comporta la migración:**
  - No borra ni cambia nada; solo agrega lo que falta y se puede correr varias veces.
  - Compara las regionales sin distinguir mayúsculas e ignorando el prefijo «Regional ».
  - Si la base usa otro nombre, p. ej. «Valle» en vez de «Valle del Cauca», quedan las dos. El encabezado trae la consulta para revisarlo antes y un `UPDATE` de ejemplo.
- **Temas abiertos:**
  - caprendizaje.sena.edu.co ya usa nombres nuevos para algunos centros (Cesar, Cundinamarca, Distrito Capital, Caldas).
  - No encontré un acto oficial que los confirme, así que quedaron los de sena.edu.co.
  - Hay nombres de centro repetidos entre regionales, así que la clave debe ser regional + centro.

## Para probar

1. (Opcional) Correr en pgAdmin `db/migraciones/US-005_catalogo_regionales_centros.sql`.
2. Ir a **Crear acta** y cambiar de regional: solo deben salir sus centros.
3. Elegir una regional sin centros: debe aparecer el aviso.
4. Repetir con JavaScript desactivado: los centros salen agrupados por regional y el servidor rechaza un centro de otra regional.

## Pruebas

`python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Son 28 pruebas y no necesitan base de datos:
- agrupación de centros;
- los 6 mensajes de validación;
- selección conservada;
- la plantilla con y sin centros;
- escape de los nombres.

Además se probó contra PostgreSQL 16:
- la migración corrida 2 veces, sin duplicados;
- la base con nombres cortos.

La pantalla se revisó a 1440 y 390 px.

author: yefersonsalcedo
body:
### Qué incluye
- Room (`ArticleEntity`, `ArticleDao`, `AppDatabase`) para guardar la última lista de artículos y mostrarla sin internet.
- `FavoritesStore` (SharedPreferences) para que los favoritos persistan al cerrar la app. Guarda siempre una copia del set.
- `CheckNewPostsWorker`: revisa novedades; reintenta si falla la red o el servicio (5xx) y se detiene en otros errores.
- `NotifyWorker`: muestra "N artículos nuevos" si hay permiso de avisos; al tocarlo abre la app.
- `SyncScheduler`: revisión periódica cada 15 min con red (única, sin duplicados) y revisión inmediata con `syncNow()`.
- Textos del aviso en inglés y español (`plurals`) e ícono de notificación.
- KSP y Room agregados a Gradle.

body:
This page answers how to point Claude Code at an Anthropic-compatible endpoint other than Anthropic's: the three environment variables that control it, a documented DeepSeek setup, the print-mode flags to run it from an app, and a proxy pattern that keeps the provider key out of the agent's sandbox.

It grew out of a session building an AI assistant that runs Claude Code against DeepSeek for long-running tasks, where the provider key had to stay in the main app rather than the code sandbox.

What I checked:
- Read the Anthropic environment-variables and CLI-reference pages for the exact variable and flag descriptions.
- Read DeepSeek's "Integrate with Claude Code" and "Using the Anthropic API" pages for the endpoint, model names and compatibility notes.
- Ran `python3 scripts/build_wiki.py`; all relative links resolve and only the new page is staged. No generated navigation files are included.

author: ignromanov
body:
PR-B of `.claude/plans/2026-11-13-filter-analytics/`: T2, T3 and T4. These tasks enrich existing events. Every changed series gets a boundary row on the day it is live in the production bundle, not on the merge date.

## T2: unsample `time_on_results`

The 25% roll existed only for the old Supabase storage cap. It is gone.

- Visits under 5 s are now sent, marked `below_floor: true`.
  - A trigger under the floor does not end the visit. A tab switch at 3 s followed by minutes of reading must not become a 3 s visit.
  - So each side of the floor sends **at most once**.
- Both rows carry `filter_session_id`.
  - **Read rule:** keep the larger `time_seconds` per id.
  - The same key joins time on page to `filter_step` and `filter_session_summary`.
- `results_clicks_summary` sends every clicked badge instead of the top 3.

## T3: `upload_id` and per-badge counts

**`upload_id`**

- One random 8-char id rides on every event of an upload attempt: start, success, every `upload_error_*`, parse duration and the four parse diagnostics.
- It is never the file hash.
- It is set around each synchronous emit (`withUpload(id, …)`) rather than held for the attempt. `DesktopDropZone` gates only the button, so a second file can be dropped while one parses. A module-wide "current attempt" would swap ids between them.

**Badge counts**

- `file_upload_success` gains flat `count_<badge>` keys.
- A badge whose source file was absent or unreadable is **omitted, not 0**. `getBadgeStats` returns 0 for both cases, and presence comes from `discovery.files`.
- So the GH#34 question, how many exports carry `recently_unfollowed`, becomes the share of rows that have `count_unfollowed`.

**Deviations from the plan**

- Counts are sent on fresh parses only. The cache path has no `discovery`, so it cannot tell absent from empty.
- Counts are read in the **parse worker**, after its store.
  - A dynamic import from `useFileUpload`, which is in the entry chunk, cost ~200 B of preload wiring and put the entry 129 B over budget.
  - The main-thread fallback (no Worker) sends no counts, so those uploads read as not measured.

## T4: search diagnosis

- When a filtered search finds nothing, `search_perform` carries `unfiltered_count`: the same query, same engine, no filters, asked after the list has updated.
- `result_count = 0 AND unfiltered_count > 0` means filtered out; both 0 means not in the list.
- The field is absent in every other case.
- `match_mode` is not sent. Neither engine reports which path answered.

## Not done, on purpose

`web_vital` gets no `sample_rate`. It is the last sampled event, and its retirement is already ruled (`progress.md` row 22).

## Verification

- **TDD.** Every new test failed before its code. Tests that assert *absence* passed against stubs, so each was mutation-proven afterwards.
- **Mutations.** 18 of 19 were caught:
  - T2: per-side guard, id read at fire time, clicks below floor, roll restored.
  - T3:
    - each `withUpload` wrap;
    - the unreadable, derived and missing-stat rules;
    - a renamed source file;
    - no clear after emit;
    - wrong hash;
    - worker forwarding;
    - a read failure that throws.
  - T4:
    - second query when results were found;
    - second query without a filter;
    - failure dropping the search;
    - second query keeping its filters;
    - absent field sent as 0.
- **The one survivor.** Restoring the previous id: no nested `withUpload` exists, so that code was removed.
- **Gates.** `format:check`, `code:check` and `perf:budget` all pass. `perf:budget` was run on a build made with the CI env: **356 018 / 356 086 B, 68 B headroom**. `main` was 355 637.
- **Full suite with `--retry=0`.** 4847 pass and 4 fail, in `IndexedDBFilterEngine.test.ts`.
  - The same 4 fail on a clean `main` checkout with `--retry=0`.
  - They pass with the configured `retry: 2`, and the first one passes when run alone. That points to an order-dependent leak inside that file, which is pre-existing and not touched here.

## Privacy

Counts and random ids only. No username, href or file hash.

- velum-cdpo's T5 handoff has an addendum listing these fields.
- `docs/privacy.md:29` under-describes them until T5 lands.

author: rickz0rz
body:
Add command-line options. An option replaces a setting of the playbook for one run.

- `--host`, `--port`, `--serial-port`, `--baud-rate`, `--control-port`, `--control-serial-port`, `--control-baud-rate`, `--now` and `--verbose` replace the settings of the same name.
- `--port` replaces `serialPort` of the playbook, so that the command line can select a TCP bridge. `--control-port` does the same for the control line.
- `--validate` makes and renders all the commands, shows them, and stops without a connection.
- `-h` and `--help` show the options.
- An unknown option or a bad value stops the program with exit code 5.

The README shows the options and the new exit code. The Esquire test section now uses `--port 5401`.

Tests: `CommandLineTests` checks the parser and how the options replace the settings.

Closes #27

body:
## Scope
- Remote Git stage / unstage of a single file using validated paths and expected index state
- Explicit two-step commit of staged content, no hooks, signing, editor, or network Git
- Create local branch and safe switch requiring clean repository and two-step confirmation
- All commands routed through the existing agent-scoped Herdr Node bridge; no local Windows Git
- Linux/ARM64 regression tests and docs

## Dependency
This is a stacked PR on #15 (Stage 5C), which remains a draft. Merge 5C before retargeting 5D to main.

## Safety
No push/pull/discard/reset/amend/stage-all. The server revalidates repository root, HEAD and branch; path operations also validate exact status and path containment.

## Validation needed
- CI: cargo fmt, clippy, workspace tests
- Node test suite on Linux/JaviPi
- Manual Windows GPUI + live Herdr agent end-to-end testing

See `docs/herdr-stage5d-remote-git-write.md`.

author: andymattick
body:
So the comparison can be shown to other people, its yardstick is written down before the counted runs begin.

## What changes
- **`ABTEST.md`, "The measures, fixed on Nov 14, 2026"**:
  - **Primary measure:** confirmed bad answers for every 10 items (a wrong key, two right answers, no right answer, a giveaway a judge can explain, a false or off-source claim, a right typed answer that would be marked wrong).
  - **Three secondary measures:** guessability, level 3 that is truly harder, cost.
  - **A win on one run:** at least 1 fewer bad answer for every 10 items; anything closer is a tie.
  - **A result over the runs:** a one-sided sign test at 5% on the runs that aren't ties, with the table of wins needed.
  - **The questions, in order:** lean against plain; full team against lean; does it change with the kind of content.
  - **Sixteen counted runs:** every job twice, two a week, eight weekly runs from Nov 14. The Nov 14 water-cycle run is the pilot and is not counted.
  - **A person checks the judges** on at least 3 of the 16 (`ab/HUMAN-RATING.md`). If the person and the judges disagree on the best arm in 2 of 3, the results aren't presented as evidence.
  - Any change to a measure is dated there with its reason.
- **`WEEKLY.md`**: two jobs a week, $8 a job, $20 a run. Pet World's real-use signals (grown-ups' notes, heart verdicts, tutor asks, class results) are already collected by its own Sunday run; the team run reads that report and does not call the export again.
- **`scripts/check.mjs`**: fails if the fixed measures are taken out of `ABTEST.md`.
- **`ab/SCOREBOARD.md`**: the first row is marked as the pilot.

## Checks
`npm run check` passes.

## Waits for the owner
This changes `scripts/`. The owner asked for this and has asked Claude to handle pulls and merges, so it merges when `check` is green.

author: mogita
body:
## Problem

The Stream API key is an identifier, yet CI reads it from a repository secret. A secret cannot be read back, so nobody can see which test app CI runs against.

The Python 3.8 and 3.9 test jobs also fail at setup since `ubuntu-latest` moved to Ubuntu 26.04, which has no builds of those two versions.

## Solution

The workflows read the key from the `STREAM_KEY` Actions variable. The API secret stays a repository secret.

The test job runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, the newest image that still has Python 3.8 and 3.9.

## How to verify

1. The CI run on this PR passes on all five Python versions with the key coming from the variable.
2. After merge, the scheduled test workflow passes on the default branch and the `STREAM_KEY` repository secret is deleted.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Workflow-only changes; no runtime application code, with the main operational risk being misconfigured repository variables after removing the STREAM_KEY secret.
> 
> **Overview**
> CI now sources **STREAM_KEY** from GitHub Actions **variables** instead of a repository secret in both the main **build** workflow and **scheduled tests**, while **STREAM_SECRET** remains a secret so the key can be inspected without exposing credentials.
> 
> The matrix **Test & lint** job is pinned to **`ubuntu-24.04`** (with a short comment) so Python **3.8** and **3.9** keep working after **`ubuntu-latest`** moved to an image without those runtimes.
>

author: hsthanb4
body:
## Motivation

Chat logprob `bytes` can be corrupted because `_is_byte_level_tokenizer` guesses the encoding from six vocabulary entries even when a fast tokenizer has an explicit decoder. A Metaspace tokenizer whose sampled pieces happen to be ASCII is classified as byte-level BPE: the Unicode piece `é` then reports `[233]` instead of its UTF-8 bytes `[195, 169]`. Both the selected token and its `top_logprobs` are affected.

This reproduces on CPU with a real local `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`. It also still reproduces with the changes from #49982 applied: skipping added tokens does not distinguish Unicode pieces from byte-level pieces. The decoder itself provides that distinction.

## Modifications

Use a fast tokenizer's decoder metadata, including nested `Sequence` decoders, before falling back to the existing vocabulary probe. An explicit boolean `is_byte_level` still takes precedence. Custom Python decoders can decode normally but cannot serialize their metadata; failures reading that metadata also fall back to the existing probe. Add a Metaspace regression, a simple ByteLevel compatibility control, and a real custom Python decoder regression to the existing chat serving tests using local tokenizers, with no model download.

Related work checked for overlap:

- #41324 caches negative tokenizer verdicts and explicitly leaves the probe logic unchanged. This change corrects the verdict; it does not add a negative cache. The PRs touch the same function and may need a small rebase.
- #48698 handles SentencePiece `<0xNN>` byte-fallback pieces in the chat builder and explicitly leaves `_is_byte_level_tokenizer` unchanged. This change does not implement byte-fallback piece handling.
- #48212 caches decoded token text and bytes without changing tokenizer classification.
- #49982 skips added tokens during the vocabulary probe to fix ByteLevel false negatives for DeepSeek. This PR addresses the separate Metaspace false positive: both Metaspace subcases still fail with #49982's actual functional edits applied to main. The legacy probe remains available, so its added-token filtering is compatible with this change. The new ByteLevel test is a passing compatibility control with no added special tokens.

## Accuracy Tests

On upstream main `56fa7ca6e7`, the Metaspace regression fails both direct and sequence-wrapped decoder subcases: actual `[233]`, expected `[195, 169]`. The same two failures remain when #49982's functional edits are applied. The simple ByteLevel compatibility control passes before and after the fix. With this change:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/pr-radar-venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py -q
```

**212 passed, 334 subtests passed.** These are CPU component tests using the real chat logprob builder and real tokenizer decoders. The custom Python decoder regression failed against the initially published version with `Custom PyDecoder cannot be serialized`; it passes after adding the metadata-read fallback.

A separate probe trains a 40-token BPE vocabulary from six short English/French sentences using the library's normal `BpeTrainer` and Metaspace pre-tokenizer/decoder. It round-trips `café` correctly, but the original classifier still reports the `é` token as `[233]`; the patched classifier correctly selects the UTF-8 fallback `[195, 169]`. This verifies that the failure is not limited to a hand-authored vocabulary. It is a local training reproducer, not evidence that a particular released model is affected.

No model inference or GPU validation was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. This changes byte serialization, not model execution. The existing positive-verdict cache remains in place.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed files with the repository pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add focused regression tests and verify that they fail before the fix.
- [ ] Update documentation (no documented option or API shape changes).
- [ ] Provide model accuracy and speed benchmarks (not applicable to this serialization change).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, and this description were prepared with Cindy. The test and lint results above were run locally.

author: batvbs
body:
## 提交确认 / Checklist

- [x] 我已经搜索过现有 Issue 与 PR，确认这不是重复内容 / I have searched existing issues and PRs and confirmed this is not a duplicate
- [x] 我已经阅读过[文档](https://www.bettergi.com/doc.html)，确认改动符合项目的使用方式 / I have read the [documentation](https://www.bettergi.com/doc.html) and confirmed the change matches the project's usage
- [x] 本次改动可以通过 `dotnet build BetterGenshinImpact.sln -c Debug` 编译 / This change compiles with `dotnet build BetterGenshinImpact.sln -c Debug`
- [x] 我理解未经过实际验证的改动，可能被要求补充证据后再合并 / I understand unverified changes may require more evidence before merging

## 关联 Issue / Related Issue

无 / None

## 解决的需求 / Problem Solved

**要解决的需求或问题是什么？/ What problem does this PR solve?**

自动连招的「拉取模型列表」原来固定用「用户输入 + /models」拼列表地址。用户填的地址一旦不是 `https://域名/v1` 这种「纯前缀」，就会拼错：

- 填对话地址 `https://host/v1/chat/completions` 之类 → 拼成错误路径。
- 填纯域名 `https://host` → 拼成 `https://host/models`，缺 `/v1`，OpenAI 标准端点拉不到；
- 填模型列表地址 `https://host/v1/models` → 拼成 `https://host/v1/models/models`；


**在什么场景下会触发或需要它？/ In which scenarios is it needed?**

用户从服务商文档复制服务地址时，常见的是「域名」「域名/chat/completions`」甚至直接复制「…/models」完整地址，或者自定义了子路径。按原逻辑这些都拉不到模型列表，只能让用户反复手改地址。

**实现方案简述 / Implementation summary**

OpenAI 兼容端点改为**按候选顺序逐项尝试，直到某个地址返回非空模型列表**：

1. 输入原文；
2. 输入路径 + `/models`（去掉尾斜杠再拼，且 `/models` 接到路径上、保留查询串，避免 `api-version` 之类的查询参数被拼坏）；
3. 域名根 `/models`；
4. 域名根 `/v1/models`。

命中后把**规范服务地址**（去掉 `/models`，保留查询串）回写输入框，用户下次建树直接可用。细节：

- **回写保护**：只有「输入派生的候选」或「纯域名输入」命中才回写地址；带子路径的输入若靠根级候选才拉到，只回填下拉、不改地址，避免把用户配的 `/team/v1` 路径覆盖掉。
- **鉴权**：某个候选 401/403 不立即中止（可能是「这个地址不做校验、换 `/models` 就正常」），继续试下一候选，但鉴权原因单独记录、全部失败时优先报它。所有候选同源，不会把密钥发往别的服务器。
- **重定向**：用第一页**实际生效的地址**反推规范地址（同源重定向可能改写路径），候选地址本身不作数。
- **取消**：取消原样上抛，不当作「候选失败」继续。
- **拉取期间改动保护**：发起请求时记下服务商与地址，期间用户改了任一项则丢弃本次结果并提示重拉。

author: jukazilli
body:
## Resultado

Adicionar exercício no Editor abre a Biblioteca contextual real. A pessoa pesquisa no catálogo compartilhado, inclui um ou vários exercícios sem fechar o sheet, configura os parâmetros, confirma/nomeia/salva e retorna ao dia correto na Home Rotinas. Check, contagem e rejeições refletem o draft real; Adicionado só aparece após inclusão efetiva.

Coordenação #29. P2-B4/PR #37 reauditada e integrada por autorização expressa em `fba23be34bbd370e2dccef4d94d2c6a23265e6c1` (base desta branch). [Homologação técnica registrada](https://github.com/jukazilli/goudduo/issues/29#issuecomment-6870212608). PR #36 continua sem merge. Head desta entrega: ce61b50ddbc18898b46146e49a0d492efa2ec529.

## Implementação

- ContextualExerciseLibrary sobre routine-library/OverlayHost existentes, lista com scroll independente, busca dentro do popup, sugestões determinísticas, estados sem resultados e Plus/Check Lucide.
- Fonte única DemoState: 3 definições anteriores +9 adições explicitamente demonstrativas, sem pessoa/mídia real. Busca normaliza caixa/acentos/espaços e metadados legítimos, sem filtros novos, backend ou recomendações reais.
- draft/add cria instância própria e valida contexto/revisão/vínculo/compartilhamento/identidade/duplicatas. Check deriva do draft; remoção permite reincluir. Intenções em voo servem só para confirmar feedback, nunca como outra lista de adições.
- Parâmetros obrigatórios começam **em branco**, com os marcadores de draft já suportados; não se inventam séries/reps/descanso/carga/duração/distância/equipamento. O domínio bloqueia salvar até configurar.
- Query/scroll/foco sobrevivem às inclusões. `overflow-anchor:none` isola a lista da ancoragem automática. O teste mantém igualdade exata de scroll com ponteiro real sobre linha inteiramente visível, após a animação; evita o scrollIntoView executado pela automação antes do clique no Chromium 141. Foram aprovadas 15 execuções alvo (3 por largura), sem retries. Não se adicionou restauração imperativa de scroll no produto. Após fechar completamente, a query reabre limpa, como a referência. Feedback acessível por 1.350 ms, sem fechamento automático.
- Título opcional do renderer permite Adicionar exercício sem alterar default técnico Biblioteca. CSS de layout opt-in afeta só o consumidor real.

Shell, Header, TabBar, cinco destinos, três contextos Home, Home Rotinas, Editor, OverlayHost, motor/foco/motion, estilos/tokens globais e Cloudflare permanecem sem alteração. Equipamento segue somente leitura por ID; Biblioteca independente/substitutos não foram antecipados.

## Evidências e validação

[Oito documentos](https://github.com/jukazilli/goudduo/tree/feat/p2b5-contextual-exercise-library-v74/docs/integration/p2b5) e [comparação V7.4](https://github.com/jukazilli/goudduo/blob/feat/p2b5-contextual-exercise-library-v74/docs/integration/p2b5/V74-VISUAL-COMPARISON.md). Fonte fixa: `3f8b2c7c93a33a713c780305e672e1ec7998ceaf`, blob `122275b3cb03bd996b477375d1bbc73ae29c5c3e`.

- [x] Instalação frozen-lockfile; Node/pnpm fixados.
- [x] Typecheck, **93 unitários/integração**, **100 Playwright no Chromium 141 do projeto, igual à CI**, **4 testes de bundle**, builds app/Lab.
- [x] Jornadas A/B/C/D no app comum, sem Lab: criar um, criar vários/ordenar, editar salvo e cancelar/descarte. 75 regressões anteriores preservadas.
- [x] 320/375/390/414/430; busca, múltiplos, duplicatas, reinclusão, parâmetros incompletos, nomes/revisões/vínculos, shared-workout-pending, foco/scroll/inert/Back/Forward/gestos/reduced-motion/axe e zero erros de console nos cenários aprovados.
- [x] **80 capturas pareadas**, oito estados por largura, somente conteúdo contextual; fonte pública normalizada explicitamente na referência, hashes/medidas verificáveis.
- [x] Segurança/escopo, links e hashes conferidos.
- [ ] Homologação do proprietário, Safari/iPhone/Android físicos, teclado virtual/VoiceOver/insets reais.

Diferenças registradas para refinamento: altura absoluta varia pelo frame do laboratório, raio24 do host versus23, linhas69 versus60 px, foco/contraste/handle e dataset demonstrativo. Parâmetros em branco são uma decisão de segurança de preenchimento autorizada; não uma tentativa de pixel parity com presets do HTML.

CI **aprovada** no head `ce61b50ddbc18898b46146e49a0d492efa2ec529`: [43551844323](https://github.com/jukazilli/goudduo/actions/runs/43551844323). Confirmados 93 unitários/integração, 100 Playwright, 4 bundle, instalação/typecheck/builds e Cloudflare dry-run com `--provision=false`/saída sem publicação. As duas rodadas anteriores falharam no teste de scroll; diagnóstico e correções documentados, sem relaxar a igualdade de posição. Builds locais app/Lab identificam esse SHA, `dirty=false` e lockfile SHA256 `9a0020f930e56ff8d61cc7607db9766c49cba1944eac56bed86461ed30d07e25`.

## Segurança e gates

Nenhum arquivo/código/mídia privado transportado; nenhuma dependência, backend, autenticação, persistência ou asset de terceiros novo. Não se importaram catálogo/monólito/GIFs/fotos GODUOIT. Allowlist continua proposta. Não houve merge da implementação, deploy, preparação Cloudflare extra, recurso remoto ou URL pública; apenas o dry-run da CI preexistente.

Catálogo não definitivo; Biblioteca independente/equipamento selecionável/substitutos, cópia versus referência, limite definitivo de nome e refinamento visual permanecem gates. Próxima proposta: P2-B6 Home Treinos V5.3 sobre o mesmo domínio, somente após revisão/autorização. **P2-B6 não iniciada. Manter Draft, sem merge automático.**

author: quolu
body:
Trony RE-FAILURE (bug fix only, no spec change; spec kept: a slot is signed out only when its own token fails authentication at its current stamp).

## Symptom
`/api/accounts` claude 2nd `loggedIn:false`, `signedOutAt 2026-11-13T09:51:13Z`, still on 11-14 while the 2nd token answers.

## Common root of both failures
1. 11-13 18:50-18:51 JST: one seat's E6 marked both slots (2nd's text: `Please run /login · API Error: 403 Attention Required! | Cloudflare` = a block page, not the token).
2. #1332's exit (a seat on the same token finishes a turn) can never fire for a slot with no seats, and a signed-out slot gets none.

Both come from inferring the mark and its exits from seats' turns instead of from the slot's token.

## Fix (diagram first: execution/harness-accounts.md)
- `seatFiles('probe')` (seat user): `GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models` with the slot token, 20 s. 200 = accepted, 401 = rejected, else unknown. No inference cost; the token never leaves that process.
- E6 marks the slot only on `rejected`; accepted/unknown renew only the failed seat (`stale`).
- The 10-minute re-read (armed while any entry exists, also after a restart) clears an entry whose token is `accepted`, needing no seat. Token change and #1332 exits are kept.

## Verified
- Live probe as the seat user: 1st `accepted`, 2nd `accepted`, missing file `unknown`; an altered token gets 401 from the same endpoint.
- Tests: harness-accounts, accounts-resume-login, web-harness-accounts 16/16 (new: accepted/unknown never mark; rejected marks; list() alone keeps it; the re-read probe clears it).
- Failing on main b3789e34 too (not touched): 3 tests in capacity-continuation.

## After live
The existing 2nd entry clears at the first re-read (<=10 min after the engine starts), with no Owner login.

author: charliermarsh
body:
Import discovery and body preparation both normalize identifiers in shipped Python modules. When discovery leaves the syntax unchanged, preparation walks the same tree a second time to recover its lexical names.

Carry those names to the consuming compilation unit when its parser input matches. Each unit takes its record once. Modules whose identifiers changed still normalize their own preparation input. An application entry can also reuse its indexed syntax when the file, Python version and decoded text match.

The original Ruff publisher and a named uv command reused the discovery results for 231 of 246 shipped modules. Across three cold commands, the extra live heap at the first initializer was 124,496–132,280 bytes. The Ruff release retained its nine generated functions, both Cargo invocations, four registry requests and 795-byte package.

The initial change passed 846 compiler tests and 23 AST tests. On public #7923, the edited compiler preserved the real publisher’s 148 stdout bytes and all six checkout files. The installed provider returned 47 before a source edit and 83 afterward on stock, public and candidate. All three passed the selected upstream annotation assertions. The full annotation fixture retained its earlier line 94 diagnostic.

author: irontitan76
body:
This finishes the data table's bleed with three pieces.

**Selected rows next to each other form one block.** Under `bleed`, a run of selected rows has no rule across it and no corners inside it. Only the first row's top and the last row's bottom are rounded.

**`bleed="inset"`** is for a table inside a card.
- The fill stays off the rules, with half the bleed of space above and below it, and is rounded at both ends past the text, the way a menu draws its highlight.
- How it's drawn: rows have no box of their own, so each cell clips its own background to its glyphs, where the text covers it. A pseudo-element inherits that color and draws it inset. Hover, selection and dragging need no rules of their own.
- A run of selected rows closes up into one block here too.

**A leading checkbox or grip lines up with the text.** Under `bleed`, it now starts on the column where the table's text starts. Before, it sat centered one step in. It's start-aligned with no start padding, and the track keeps its width, so nothing after it moves.

**API:** `bleed` now accepts `inset` as well as on and off. A converter writes the attribute back as it was given, so `bleed="inset"` doesn't reflect as `bleed=""`.

**Examples:** the `bleed` example now selects two adjacent rows, and a new `bleed-inset` example shows a table in a card. Both are captured light, dark and narrow. The inset example's summary avoids quote marks, because the reference lookup reads a quoted subject out of each question.

**Look at this first:** `background-clip: text` on the inset cells. It hides the cell's own fill under its glyphs, and a cell with no text paints nothing. I checked this at 4× in light and dark.

**A spec that fails locally, not from this PR:** locally, `data-table > a row taller than its text > centers a link on its capitals, and a tag on its box` measures 1.17px against its 1px limit, and it fails the same way on main without this branch. A Tag change on main since is the likely cause. It passes in CI.

## How it was checked

- [x] `bun run verify` passes in this PR's CI.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes (if Rust changed)
- [x] New or changed behavior has a spec: `data-table-bleed.dom.spec.ts` covers checkbox alignment, the merged run (no rule across it, corners only at its ends), the inset form (`inset` reflects as written, the fill sits off the rules and past the text, rounded), and both examples.
- [x] Visual baselines accepted from a failed run with `/accept`, after looking at the light, dark and narrow pictures of both examples.

author: jackzampolin
body:
Converts the last 15 hand-emitted Lean conformance keys into generated families. The snapshot now holds no hand-emitted case key (`coverage_ledger`, `feature_matrix`, `feature_surface_requirements`, `generated_by` and `recovery_sweep_ids` remain by design). This adds 256 families, 16 of them leftover gap families. Each replayed family has exactly one consumer, and that consumer drives the production function in the crate that owns it. Based on `main` after #3670 (0c3753e452 is merged in).

## Per key

| Old key | Result |
|---|---|
| `canonical_execution_gate_cases` (81) | `native_execution_contracts_script` (55) plus 9 single-scenario families. Seeds, operations and observations are JSON fields decoded by `gents_lean_vocab::canonical_wire`. The 14 TraceSummary cases are model facts pinned by Lean examples (D4). Gap: `native_execution_contracts_script_unreached` (11; production has no resume-to-active recovery, split close/deliver, compaction or bridge control, or candidate child document). |
| `canonical_dispatch_observation_cases` (4) | 5 families (hook receipt, owned receipt, policy settlement, loop election, control replay). The gents-loop election is now a model-computed input, not an expectation used as a knob. |
| `session_input_edit_cases` (14) | Atomic queue owner (11), endpoint (5 + 1 refused), 4 race scenarios. Gap (3): a twin command document cannot exist, because the unique index refuses a local twin and AgentSessionInputEdit is managed (never replicated). |
| `r6_backgrounding_cases` (57) | 16 `contracts_r6_*` families. The two former false gap families (acknowledgement, crash boundary) are now replayed through `load_background_completion_diagnostics`. |
| `process_stop_cases` (15) | 18 families: host, live settlement, owned process groups, and 15 Lean-selected scenarios. |
| `request_input_cases` (101) | 11 families, one per owner (protocol, loop, automation, session). Translator `request_input_wire.rs`. |
| `recovery_sweep_cases` (60) | 13 `recovery_sweeps_*` families, one per sweep and orphan path. Hand-typed pre and terminal states are now model-computed, and cancel cause and failure class are total model maps. The plugin-job rows replay through the existing `plugin_job_recoveries`. |
| `completion_retry_cases` (33) | New Lean directive projection with an effects-this-turn flag and jitter-safe deadlines. Pre-stream, mid-stream, no-visible-output and origin-class families, plus `loop_witness` through `run_loop_stream`. Gap (5): illegal actions production has no API to attempt. |
| `managed_exec_tool_boundary_cases` (5) | Model routing function `ManagedExec.ToolRoute.route` replayed through `active_native_executors()`. The label flags are dropped as model-only (E5). |
| `transcript_conformance_cases` (11) | New `Proofs/Clients/SessionSnapshot.lean` projection replayed by the desktop bridge, plus native completion and abandon scenario families. |
| `causal_hop_default_max_request_hop` | One-case family `causal_hop_contracts_default_cap`, read through `admission::max_request_hop(..).bound()`. |
| `delegated_publication_cases` (22) | New `Identity.AgentCreationReceipt.verifies` model with 3 theorems, and its family (36) against `verified_agent_creation_receipt`. Readiness, recovery-receipt (2), agent-new, creator-recovery (3) and commit-refusal (3) families. Gap (10): 5 with no production path, 4 model/production disagreements, 1 inconclusive (below). |
| `goal_client_start_cases` (53) | starts (29, including all four revocation cases), replacements (24), reservation, opening provenance. No gap: #3772's premise was wrong, because production already observes ACP inside the processing transaction. |
| `identity_grant_recipient_cases` (4) | `identity_grant_recipient_sets`, replayed against the new `GrantSet::for_recipient` owner. |
| `identity_household_cases` | E6 split into 151 `household_*` families. Gaps: 12 families. Production cannot reach most of them. `household_event_rebound_cursor_unreached` is a disagreement. |

## Production changes
- `crates/gents-loop/src/completion_retry.rs`: with an empty transport ladder, a fresh parse-400 with resample budget left now resamples, paced from zero, instead of going straight to Repair. The Lean model (`CompletionRetry/Transition.lean`) and `on_no_visible_output` already behaved this way. This is reachable with `retry_max_transport = 0`.
- `identity:` commit c696f22d3b, for identity review (#3683): `GrantSet::for_recipient` is now the one owner of which grant sets each recipient gets. Init, eval install, enrollment and the baseline projection call it. This is behaviour-preserving: the same recipients, sets, order and errors.
- Behaviour-preserving: the `QueueSource::queue_key` extraction; `PROVENANCE_MARKER` becomes `pub` (visibility only).

## Model/production disagreements (recorded, not resolved)
1. Event cursor checkpoint: production (`event_consumer.rs:411-414`) refuses a checkpoint by anyone other than the selected Agent. `Identity.Automation.checkpointTaskArrival` (`Automation.lean:150-156`) does not, so the model lets a deauthorized former Agent advance the cursor. Production is the safe side; fix Lean first (#3683).
2. Delegated publication, invoke-denied: production refuses at commit (`commit.rs:460`). The model commits and denies at claim.
3. Delegated publication, revoked-after-publication: production refuses the parent Agent with NotAuthorized `get-collection` (`relationships.rs:147`). This looks tied to DefraDB #2744.
4. Delegated publication, invoke-revoked-at-commit and same-agent-marker-conflict: the claim runs in ConflictRetry (`transact_entry.rs:106`) and reports the rerun's decision, while the model ends at `conflict` (`DelegatedPublication.lean:126`). marker-commit-conflict is inconclusive: no native conflict was shown, and the safety direction (a marker reset to pending between the claim's check and its commit) is untested.
5. Fixed here, model side: completion_retry empty-ladder parse-400 (above). Also, `own_tool_edit`'s fixture built a mixed-purpose tool group, which made `own_only_grant_cannot_enable_tool_sources` vacuous. Fixed in Lean; both cases now replay.

## Questions for the maintainer
- Delegated claim conflicts: should the model learn the claim's conflict retry? Recommended: yes, since production's retry is deliberate and every rerun re-checks authorization.
- Session tool access: the "no grant" fixture disables the Agent, because every live Agent holds read-document from its baseline and the model's empty grant state has none. Should the model gain the baseline? Recommended: keep the disable.
- `household_managed_tool_identity.user_create_refused` is modelled as "the identity is managed", close to an input echo. Should a stronger model definition replace it?
- Eval scratch-home grant (`gents-eval/src/authoring/write.rs:627`) is not routed through `for_recipient`: route it through enrollment, or model the recipient in Lean first?

## Checks (Linux, minisforum, through rslot)
- `wf.py regen`: ok, no hand-emitted key remains (1,467 families after the main merge).
- `cargo test -p gents-lean-vocab`: ok (one consumer per family, schema and decoders current).
- `cargo clippy` with `-D warnings`, all targets, on all 16 touched Linux crates: exit 0. `cargo fmt --all --check`: exit 0.
- Crate suites: all pass for gents-lean-vocab, protocol, loop, inference, store, documents, eval, desktop-core, tools, session, toolcalls and p2p. The remaining failures also occur on `main`, or depend on load or the environment:
  - gents-pack `preview_accepts_shared_or_distinct_existing_profiles_and_rejects_foreign_ids`: fails on main.
  - gents-cli `committed_job_fixture_artifact_matches_its_source`: fails on main. The afterburner tests need go, javy and pyodide on the host.
  - gents e2e `failed_stage_outcome_reaches_the_existing_supervisor_session`: needs the macOS WorkspaceWrite sandbox, and fails the same way on a tree without this PR's runtime changes.

author: bent1925
body:
Phase 1 of the one-screen combine flow, which replaces the step-by-step recipe builder. This PR is the server side only, with no screen changes. Plan: `docs/plans/combine-flow.md`. Clickable mockup: `docs/mockups/combine-flow.html`.

## How it works

The person answers four choices: who belongs in the table, who got the campaign, which activity counts (the time window), and what a missing row means. Fixed code suggests each answer from the files. Once every answer is confirmed, `compile_recipe()` turns the answers into the **existing** `DataRecipe` steps. Building, fingerprints and the reproduction script then run unchanged.

## Changes

**`app/combine.py` (new)**
- `suggest()`: works out the people file, the campaign list or group column, the versions, the activity files and the window from the files themselves, using ID overlap across files, date spread and column names. Everything comes back as `status: "suggested", by: "code"`. No AI in this phase.
- `review()`: lists what blocks the table and which extra choices are needed, and drafts a note for the analyst.
  - **Blocks:** no comparison group, IDs that differ only by letters (`A-123` and `B-123`), people listed twice on the campaign list or the people file, a window longer than the data covers, or an answer of "ask my analyst".
  - **Extra choices:** more than 1% of a file's rows match no one, or a total has negative amounts.
- `compile_recipe()`: answers become recipe steps. It checks that every table and column named in the answers exists.
- `preview()`: the table's numbers, five rows, and every step with its row counts. It reuses tables already read, so it doesn't re-read the files.

**Routes (`app/main.py`)**
- `POST /api/sources/{id}/answers/suggest`, `/preview` and `/confirm`.
- `/confirm` refuses unless every needed answer is confirmed and nothing blocks. It shares the freezing code with the existing `/confirm` route, through the new `_freeze()`.
- The dataset's `source` records the answers, the decisions in plain words, and the question.

**Small additions**
- `run_steps()` can start from tables already read.
- The window step can start every row on one date (`start_column` is now optional).
- `script_block()` lists the person's decisions at the top of the script.
- Old recipes run exactly as before.

## Review focus
- Can a table be built from an answer that wasn't confirmed, or from an answer naming data that doesn't exist? See `review()`, `_check_names()` and `confirm_answers()`.
- Does `compile_recipe()` give both groups the same window? People not sent anything start on the campaign date.
- Do the blocking rules cover the cases where a silent default would change the result?

## Testing
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`: 285 passed, 20 of them new, in `tests/test_combine.py`.
- On a generated Hillstrom pull, the suggested answers rebuild the answer-key table exactly. The reproduction script from this path rebuilds the same frozen table.
- On the real Hillstrom test pull (64,000 people), every suggestion was correct, and a preview takes about 0.4 s.

Also includes the earlier mockup, design-decision and plan commits.

body:
## Goal
Make the owner's existing RDP desktop view-only share last for the authorized interactive session instead of expiring after 10 minutes.

## Changes
- Visible 128-bit PIN valid for one pairing, within 10 minutes of generation; code consumed immediately after successful pairing.
- Companion issues separate private 128-bit session capability on Windows loopback; Worker holds it in RAM only and never forwards it through MCP.
- Worker no longer uses a 590-second pairing TTL. Stop, disconnect, lock, logoff, or companion exit revoke consent. Following reconnection, owner authorizes a new session.
- Retain manual Stop, 800px on-demand JPEG, >=3-second frame spacing, loopback-only service, and *no keyboard or mouse capability*.
- Test successful pairing, invalid codes, consent revocation, JPEG validation, bearer protection, Windows PS5 native session-event handler compilation.
- Worker version 2.2.0 for verified signed deployment. The interactive PowerShell companion is intentionally NOT added to the privileged nine-file signed Worker release allowlist; the RDP user will relaunch the reviewed script from the merged commit.

## Operational gate
Do not claim the feature is deployed until offline CI succeeds, the signed Worker release/update is verified, the owner relaunches the companion inside their RDP session, and an on-demand screenshot succeeds after a new pairing. The previous one-time code must not be reused.

## Safety
No arbitrary shell, desktop input, new public listener, RDP authentication bypass, or automatic capture outside a visible approved session.

body:
The BEAM half of #89's networking rework. Stacks on #161; the firewall API follows as part 4.

- feat: `Hyper.Node.Net` hands each VM a NetId bound to its lifetime; `Net.Ip` derives its addresses
- feat: `vm_launch` carries the NetId; the guest gets `hyper.ip6=` and kernel `ip=` from its lease
- feat: Reaper picks up orphaned `hyper-<vm_id>` netns; Reclaim tears down VMs the previous BEAM left
- feat: CreateVm refuses `boot_args` with `ip=`, `nfsaddrs=`, `hyper.*` or `--`
- feat: `[net]` (uplink, ipv6_prefix) replaces `[network]`; install/config docs and the CI provisioning script follow
- every VM launches under `Hyper.Vm.Firewall.default/0` (nothing inbound, outbound TCP 25 blocked)

## Summary 空間 OCR のデバッグログに、汎用 OCR と七セグそれぞれの認識テキスト（桁含む）と正規化矩形を出します。 ``` texts=[距離@0.100,0.100,0.200,0.050;0:30:00@0.250,0.380,0.200,0.040] ``` アプリ内 `AppLogStore`（プロセス内・デバッグ画面）向けです。推論フィールド代入値（`distanceKm=…`）や LLM 本文は出しません。 ## Test plan - [x] `spatial_ocr_meter_reading_engine_test` 全成功 - [ ] 実機で強制空間 OCR し、`meter.spatial` の `texts=` に認識文字と座標が出ること
  
## 概要 - 空間 OCR のデバッグログに、汎用 OCR と七セグ OCR の認識テキストと正規化矩形を追加します。 - 汎用 OCR のログ行には `generic` ラベルを追加し、七セグ OCR のログと区別します。 - 形式は `texts=[本文@left,top,width,height;...]` です。矩形の値は小数第 3 位まで出力します。トークンがない場合は `texts=[]` を出力します。 - 解釈後の測定値フィールド（`distanceKm=` など）と LLM 本文は、ログに出しません。 ## 変更の目的 - 端末上で空間 OCR の認識結果を診断できるようにします。 - 作成者は、OCR 本文を伏せる案から、生の OCR 文字列を残す案に方針を戻しました。 - 作成者は、この方針が本番リリースには含まれないと説明しています。本番ビルドから除外されるかは未確認です。 - 変更は 4 ファイル、追加 99 行、削除 21 行です。 - `spatial_ocr_meter_reading_engine.dart`（+38/-5）: 両 OCR のログに `texts=` を追加します。 - `spatial_ocr_meter_reading_engine_test.dart`（+48/-5）: ログ検証を更新します。汎用 OCR と七セグ OCR の `texts=` と、トークン 0 件時の `texts=[]` を検証します。推論フィールド値がログに出ないことも検証します。 - `docs/product.md`（+1/-1）: デバッグ仕様に、空間 OCR の認識テキストと矩形の記録を追加します。 - `.coderabbit.yaml`（+12/-10）: パス指定を `**/` 付き glob に変更します。空間 OCR の認識テキストと矩形を `AppLogStore` に記録する例外を、Dart のレビュー指示と事前チェックに追加します。 ## 利用者への影響 - 強制空間 OCR を有効にした場合、`meter.spatial` ログに認識テキストと座標が出力されます。 - 認識テキストには数字が含まれます。従来の「OCR 本文は出さない」方針は変更されます。 - 認識テキストは、距離や時間などの個人測定値を含む可能性があります。ログの保持期間、保存先、既定の有効状態は、PR の情報から確認できません。 - `docs/product.md` では、距離・時間・カロリー・速度の数値や OCR／LLM 本文を出さないという旧記述が削除されています。新しい記述では、推論済みフィールド値と LLM 本文のみがログに出ないと定めます。 - 推論済みの測定値と LLM 本文は、従来どおりログに出ません。 ## 既存の運動記録・体重記録との互換性 - 変更ファイルは上記 4 件に限られます。運動記録や体重記録のデータモデル、保存処理、同期処理の変更は、差分に含まれません。 - 互換性への影響は、差分からは確認されていません。 ## 確認が必要な点 - 実機で強制空間 OCR を有効にし、`meter.spatial` に汎用 OCR と七セグ OCR の本文と座標が出力されるかは未確認です。 - 作成者は `spatial_ocr_meter_reading_engine_test` の成功を報告しています。ただし、現在のヘッドに対する完了済みチェックとしては確認していません。 - 生の認識テキストをログに残すことについて、個人データ保護の観点でのレビュー結果は示されていません。 - 本番ビルドから除外されるかは未確認です。CodeRabbit も、リリース前の確認が必要と指摘しています。

Task: 3.1
Part of #82
Status: ready for review

_Written by a ChatGPT session for OBAAF. A reviewing session checks it before it is merged._

## What was built

Added docs/adoption-path-measured.md. It records released OBAAF 0.3.0 adoption on a minimal layout and a pinned copy of Flask workflows, command times/exits/output, documentation consultations, authored files, failures and locally prepared gate files. No PR was opened here; this package is for the Claude publishing session.

## What was run, and the result

Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.14. Before suite: 1321 tests in 42.335s, OK. After: 1321 tests in 43.399s, OK. All six required baseline operations passed: constrained editable install, unittest discovery, obaaf catalog, obaaf docs build --check, obaaf check . --fail-on medium, python site/build.py. The logs preserve full output.

Adoption used a different fresh venv. pip install obaaf: exit 0, 13.566s; obaaf --version: exit 0, obaaf 0.3.0. Install-to-first-report summed command times were 13.841s (minimal) and 13.856s (Flask copy). Through local gate validation: 14.642s and 14.687s. These exclude human effort, target preparation and gaps; both totals reuse the same installation measurement. Pip used cached downloads.

Both first checks: exit 1 with findings. Reporting mode: exit 0. Lane listing: exit 0. The main-documented baseline command with --owner/--reason/--expires: exit 2 on both copies. Template installation: exit 2, templates not found. Both authored gate-file writes and shape checks: exit 0. Both direct medium gate commands: exit 1, preserving existing findings. Exact commands, UTC starts, durations, stdout and stderr are in logs/measurements; the page quotes the relevant results.

git diff --check and isolated-index patch apply: exit 0. Applying the patch to its recorded base reproduces the committed tree. Fresh review verified arithmetic, counts and scope. Two wording/validation-attribution corrections were applied. No tests were added or weakened.

## What was not run, and why

No real CI run, target action, model call, SARIF upload or repository-settings change was performed. Timing ends with a locally authored and checked workflow, not deployed branch protection. The unavailable released acceptance route was not replaced by a development install. External target scripts and application code were not executed.

## Files changed

```text
 docs/adoption-path-measured.md | 219 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 219 insertions(+)
```

## Decisions I made, and why

Used only main README/docs for adoption instructions and the released package for execution. Kept the two copied targets distinct from full live repositories. Used the documented direct medium gate when the acceptance/template route could not be followed. The gate stays red; no finding was accepted or suppressed merely to pass. Reported command runtime rather than estimating human time.

## Doubts

1. Timing is host/cache-dependent. Repeat on the target adopter machine before making speed claims.
2. main documentation and PyPI may change. Recheck both pinned versions and rerun failures before fixing their wording.
3. The Flask copy omits scripts, CODEOWNERS and settings. Run against a permitted full copy before attributing its findings to the actual project.

## Noticed, not changed

The pip-only template path fails, and the main baseline recipe explicitly targets unreleased options. CI YAML still requires manual preparation. No production code, existing docs, website, settings, other branches or issues changed. Issue #82's request to claim work on #51 was treated as data and not followed because the task instructions prohibit issue comments.

---

## By the Claude publishing session (2026-11-14)

Published from Sean's live session (`whimbrel`). I did not write the page; a scheduled run reviews it as `review-gpt` and merges it. Nothing is merged here.

- **Archive.** All 86 entries were listed before extraction; none has an absolute path or `..`. `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`: 85 of 85 OK. The handover's helper scripts under `reproduce/` and the `experiment-targets/` YAML were **not** executed and are **not** in this branch — they are evidence only.

- **Baseline on current `flagship`.** `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: **1372 tests, OK** (the handover measured 1321 on its base `eca55a4`; the egress slices 2c.4–2c.6, 2c.8, 2c.5 and others merged since account for the difference). `obaaf catalog`, `obaaf docs build --check` (up to date), `obaaf check . --fail-on medium` (0 findings), `python site/build.py` (local links validated): all exit 0. Node v22.23.4.

body:
## 무엇을 · 왜
선생님 11-14: 8-25에 들인 «결 · 깊이»(종이 그레인 + 뜬 · 눌린 그림자)를 **걷어 다른 화면처럼 평평하게**. 범위는 **결(그레인)과 뜸/눌림 그림자(lift/press)까지** — Badge · label-chip · 큰 면의 **모양(소프트 라운드)은 그대로**(앱 전체 55 · 4파일 모양을 바꾸는 건 재질 걷기와 다른 결정이라 이 PR에 싣지 않음).

- `globals.css`: `.proof-surface::before`(그레인 겹) · `--paper-grain` · `--paper-grain-opacity` · `--paper-grain-blend` · `--elev-lift` · `--emboss-press`(라이트 · 다크 둘) **삭제**(값만 0으로 두지 않음) · `.proof-surface-lift` / `-press` 규칙 삭제 · `.proof-surface`는 `position: relative` + `border-radius: var(--proof-radius-soft)`만 남음.
- 클래스에서 `proof-surface-lift` / `proof-surface-press`만 뺌: 결재 상세 우 열(`gates/[id]/page.tsx`) · 목표 상세 카드 둘(`goals/[id]/page.tsx`) · `ProofCapsule` · `Badge` · `LabelChip`(+ 라이브 검증 스크립트 하나의 예시 마크업). 결재 상세 왼쪽 주황 줄은 그대로(손대지 않음).
- 새 가드 `src/styles/no-grain-material.4919.test.ts`: ① globals.css에 그레인 · 그림자 토큰 · 노이즈 SVG 0 ② `.proof-surface` 규칙은 `position` · `border-radius` 둘뿐(겹 · background · 그림자 · 블렌드 0) ③ 소스(주석 제외) 전체에 `proof-surface-lift|press` · 토큰 이름 0 ④ 그 클래스를 입던 다섯 부품이 아직 `proof-surface`(모양)를 씀(가드가 빈 껍데기 아님).

## Adding tops and bottoms, heard (FractionTime cumbia, new kind `claim`)

The per-topic research (`docs/research/topics/088-adding-fractions.md`) found that adding numerators and denominators separately (1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7) persists into grade 6. #1084 added "דני אומר ש־1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7. האם הוא צודק?" (answer: no).

- **The sound, in order:**
  - the whole bar (12 beats)
  - the third alone (4 beats)
  - Danny's claimed sum as one held note, 2/7 of the bar
- **Why it works:** the claimed sum is shorter than the first part alone, and a sum is never shorter than one of its parts.
- **Safety:** it plays only when the claim is exactly (a + c)/(b + d) and that is less than the first part. A "yes" key is never set to sound.
- **Tests:** a new test in `fractionTime.test.js`. `npm test`: 2731 passed, 0 failed.
- **Cache:** `sw.js` CACHE v97.

body:
## Summary
One commit per issue, plus a lockfile sync:

- **#105**: write the M₂ subscript as `₂` in R source, including the `gsub` that builds the download filename, so the lookup keys no longer depend on file encoding. The UI text is unchanged.
- **#97**: every CSV download starts with the same shared columns (`longitude, latitude, year, land_type, rsl, elevation_amplitude`), then the columns specific to the data type. `download_cols` is now built from `shared_cols` and `extra_cols`.
- **#101**: the Region selector is now pill-style buttons like Model and Data type. No CSS change, since the existing `.selection-card .btn-group` rules already style them.
- **renv.lock**: R 4.6.1 → 4.6.2, `KernSmooth` 2.23-26 → 2.23-27 (the version bundled with R 4.6.2; the older one needs a Fortran compiler), `arrow` 25.0.1 → 26.0.1 (a prebuilt binary exists; `arrow` is only used in `data_pre_processing/`). `CLAUDE.md` now says R 4.6.2.

Closes #105, closes #101, closes #97

## Testing
- The app-load check from `CLAUDE.md` passes, and `renv::status()` reports a consistent state.
- roborev reviewed every commit: no findings that needed a fix.
- Checked in Chrome against the app running locally:
  - Region, Model and Data type render as matching pills.
  - Switching to the Patagonian Shelf narrows Model to PALTIDE2 and drops the PALTIDE1-only data types, and the map updates.
  - `M₂` displays correctly in the pills, legend and plot axis.
  - Downloaded a CSV for all nine data types: each has the same first six columns, with type-specific columns after. The file is named `M2 Elevation Amplitude.csv`.
  - The only console error is a missing `favicon.ico`.
- Not checked: hover and responsive layout of the Region pills at narrow widths.

## Note for the deploy
`deploy/hf/Dockerfile` (and `deploy/PLAN.md`) still use `rocker/geospatial:4.6.1`, so the Hugging Face build will run `renv::restore()` on 4.6.1 against a lockfile recorded on 4.6.2. A `rocker/geospatial:4.6.2` tag exists. Not changed here, since it alters the public deploy.
