author: patrick-erichsen
body:
## What problem this solves

Template Add can create the agent but its tools-disabled opening cannot finish the declared setup or recover a failed opening without repeating creation.

## What changes

After creation, one hidden setup turn uses the new agent’s ordinary tools and retained permissions. It greets in the Template’s voice, creates declared automations paused, reports MCP sign-in needs, and shows exact-package plugin cards without installing or enabling those plugins. Explicit tool denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.

The ordinary session owns the retryable setup continuation. Retry uses the same agent, workspace and conversation without reinstalling dependencies. When its one-shot receipt has already been consumed, Retry returns a truthful partial/unverifiable outcome instead of inventing readiness or creating another agent. Plugin inventory includes canonical package identity so the agent does not infer a plugin ID from its package name.

This layer follows https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198070. Early-opening/dependency concurrency and composer responsiveness remain a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

### Current repair qualification

Head `577e12a6b457945be951b6e97a753b9c2cfebaef`, base `9ed5a58794db142be41f5e142e68a5cd92d72bd0`:

- Promotes the existing stale/concurrent Retry fix into this independently landable layer. Three Gateway regression cases fail before the fix with false complete/ready results. After the fix the complete owning request suite passes **14/14**, exit0 (144.61s wrapper): `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server-methods/templates-add-chat.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The same agent, workspace, edited files and dependency-install counts are preserved. External registry/model I/O is fixed; admission, config, workspace, session, rollback and retained setup ownership remain real. No new test seam or mock was introduced.
- Moves the unchanged setup input contract into a type-only leaf and updates all three consumers. Both runtime and Madge import-cycle guards now report **zero cycles**. The leaf does not prematurely add the responsive follow-up callbacks.
- Adds the incident reference beside the bootstrap exception, without changing model-facing prompt bytes.
- Six-file **type-aware lint**, formatting and diff checks pass. Test-line ratchet is **+281 <=400**, no setup allocation or global-limit changes.
- Seven existing setup commits were restacked onto the creation allocation-only repair. UI source and performance inputs are unchanged from the prior setup qualification below; prior results are reused, not claimed as fresh executions. Exact-head hosted compiler/build/CI and completed re-review remain required.

### Retained prior qualification

Prior setup `e68f2ecdbc3b54fea242e6ca545d1f0830bc0aff` above `b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`:

- Complete strict paired production-UI performance passes, exit0: document **14,019 B <=14,026 B**; chat JS **1,315,006→1,315,005 B**, New Session **818,001→818,000 B**, startup **90,860 B unchanged**. Requests and CSS unchanged. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance-base.mts b7235cc095dff0eebd90cd268b2695ca96f98a08`.
- Owning Gateway14/14 and setup prompt6/6, complete two-shard command exit0 (161.15s). Explicit denies and operator ceilings remain authoritative.
- Deletes the old tools-disabled outcome prompt and uses the existing session continuation owner, not a parallel Template ledger.

The prior hosted native Talk and UI failures were compared with scheduled main run43540514362 and have identical failure signatures; they are not passing CI. New-head checks still need reconciliation. No inherited-failure qualification covers an introduced defect.

## Real product evidence and remaining gap

Earlier integrated Travel Copilot proof, not this exact head: baseline creation opened chat at19.9s, failed on a disabled referenced plugin at35.6s, leaving an empty workspace. Earlier integrated creation/setup opened pending chat in104ms and produced output at52.2s, preserving original CLAW.md and goplaces while leaving Expedia disabled and Travel Themes uninstalled. The later retained responsiveness recording showed the original-chat card without narration and working review navigation without installation; that follow-up is not part of this PR.

These historical screenshots do not prove the current setup head, completed plugin installation, latest-stable upgrade preservation, or final combined-head video. The historical live-card omission is addressed by the current foundation and its three producer-to-renderer paths. Fresh combined-head real Add/install/caption/video proof remains open before final delivery. No production Gateway was changed.

![Before: disabled plugin leaves setup failed and workspace empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7a4341a-0747-4407-9706-752ae0b08659)

![Earlier integrated creation/setup, not current-head proof](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df1f8f27-bb36-4603-8ff7-d63686ddbff7)

author: katagaki
body:
Fixes #74

Links in cells used to be carried through a save as raw XML: they could not be seen, followed, added, edited or removed. Now each cell's link is part of the model. It's drawn as a link, can be followed, and can be added, edited and removed on iOS and Mac.

## What changed

- **Engine:**
  - `CellHyperlink` and `Worksheet.hyperlinks` hold each cell's link: a web address, a `mailto:` or file address, or a place in the workbook such as `'Data Sheet'!B5` or a defined name, plus display text and tooltip.
  - `HyperlinkParts` reads `<hyperlinks>` and resolves each `r:id`, and writes them back with a fresh relationship per outside address. The old raw copy and its relationships are dropped, and hyperlinks are no longer listed as something Tables can't edit.
  - A link set on a range is stored on each of its cells.
  - Links move with their cells when rows or columns are inserted or deleted and when cells are moved.
  - A cell whose formula is a `HYPERLINK` call can be followed to the address it names.
- **Shared editor actions:**
  - Setting a link from what was typed: `example.com` becomes `https://example.com`, `a@b.com` becomes `mailto:`, and `Sheet2!A1` becomes a place in the workbook.
  - A new link takes Excel's blue underlined Hyperlink look. Removing a link also removes that look, including a file's `FF0563C1` colour.
  - Following a link opens an outside address, or selects and scrolls to the place in the workbook.
  - Strings are added in all five languages.
- **Mac:** Insert menu items Link… (⌘K), Open Link and Remove Link, plus matching items in the cell menu. The editor dialog fills in the current link and has a Remove Link button.
- **iOS:** the cell menu gets Open Link, Add/Edit Link… and Remove Link, with an alert for editing the link.

## Testing

- Added `HyperlinkTests` (14 tests). They cover reading every kind of link, the save round trip and its relationships, a new link saved from a new workbook, dropping a link with a dangling `r:id`, row and column edits, moving and copying cells, resolving places and defined names, parsing typed links, `HYPERLINK` formulas, and the add, edit and remove actions.
- Updated two `UnsupportedFeatureTests` cases that assumed links were kept as raw XML.
- `HyperlinkTests`, `UnsupportedFeatureTests`, `WorksheetStructureTests` and `CommentFileTests` pass (51 tests). The full suite shows only the known Shortcuts failure.
- **The iOS app was not checked by hand.** The simulator device agent was unavailable, so iOS is covered by the unit tests and a successful build only.
- **Mac app (VM):** checked with a test file that has a web link, an email link and a link to another sheet. In order: open it, follow the web link (Safari opens example.com), follow the in-workbook link (it jumps to Data Sheet B5), add a link, edit it, remove the email link, then save, quit and reopen. After reopening, the kept links are still links, the removed one is plain text, and the edited link points at `https://www.apple.com`. The saved XML matches.

| Opened: links drawn as links | Following the in-workbook link |
|---|---|
| ![File opens with links](https://github.com/AtelierSuite/Tables/blob/assets/issue-74-screenshots/mac-01-file-opens-with-links.png?raw=true) | ![Jumped to Data Sheet B5](https://github.com/AtelierSuite/Tables/blob/assets/issue-74-screenshots/mac-04-follow-workbook-link-jumps-to-data-sheet-B5.png?raw=true) |
| **Edit Link, filled with the current link** | **After save and reopen: B3's link removed, others kept** |
| ![Edit Link dialog](https://github.com/AtelierSuite/Tables/blob/assets/issue-74-screenshots/mac-07-edit-link-dialog-prefilled.png?raw=true) | ![Links sheet after reopening](https://github.com/AtelierSuite/Tables/blob/assets/issue-74-screenshots/mac-12-after-save-reopen-links-sheet.png?raw=true) |
| **After save and reopen: the added and edited link is kept** | |
| ![Data Sheet after reopening](https://github.com/AtelierSuite/Tables/blob/assets/issue-74-screenshots/mac-13-after-save-reopen-data-sheet-link-kept.png?raw=true) | |

## Left out

- A plain click on a link cell does not follow it: Open Link is in the menus. On Mac it is in the Insert and cell menus, and on iOS in the cell menu.
- Copy and paste does not carry links.
- A link's target text is not rewritten when a sheet is renamed (Excel doesn't do this either).
- A link set on a range of more than 100,000 cells, such as whole columns, is dropped on read.
- The iOS UI was not checked by hand (see above).

author: ventura8
body:
QA round 2 on Windows 11, natively, against v0.1.1 installed with the one-liner.

**Regressions in 0.1.1, fixed here**
- **Every local run failed on Windows again**, and `tutti machines` showed `here` unreachable. The review of #1 changed the Windows line to `f=$(mktemp) && echo … | base64 -d > $f && { bash $f; … }` to keep stdin, but WSL's `bash.exe` received it as `syntax error near unexpected token '&&'`. 4 tests failed natively.
  - I tested three forms on this PC. Only `source <(echo <b64> | base64 -d)` kept stdin, the quotes and the exit code (`read x; echo "got:$x" | cut -d":" -f2; exit 7` with `hello` as input gave `hello`, exit 7). The merged form failed, and `eval "$(…)"` lost the output.
- **Updates kept the broken CRLF scripts.** `install.ps1` updates with `git pull`, which never rewrites files that didn't change, so an install made before `.gitattributes` still had `slot.sh` with 25 CRLF lines. An update now writes the shell scripts out again (that folder is the installer's own clone).

**Not a bug, but worth a line in the changelog:** `tutti usage` still said "3 h before the reset", because a config copied from the old example keeps `lead_hours: 3`. Existing users have to change it to 1 themselves.

**Tests:** 55/55 natively on Windows 11 and 55/55 on Linux (WSL; the new Windows-only test is skipped there). The update step was tried on the real install: 25 CRLF → 0, and `tutti --version` still works.

**Note for the code:** WSL's `bash.exe` also drops arguments after `-c` (round 1), so anything Windows-bound must go inside the line, and the line must avoid quotes, `&&`, `$(` and braces.

author: hoejriis
body:
**Issue #537, stage 1 of 3: the checks a manager-supplied native packet passes before a Repeater queues it.** No operation yet. The operation and the contract text land together in stage 2, since the docs describe only what has shipped.

`src/helpers/iface/PacketTransmit.h`, `checkRawPacket(bytes, n, info, pkt)`:
- **It parses `Packet::writeTo` bytes with every length checked against what was received:** the version (it must be `PAYLOAD_VER_1`, as the receive parser requires), the transport codes when the route has them, `path_len` and its bytes, and a payload of 1 to 184 B.
  - `Packet::readFrom` and `Dispatcher::tryParsePacket` read the transport codes without that check. They parse what the radio heard; this parses what a caller sent.
- **The payload-type allowlist:** REQ, RESPONSE, TXT_MSG, ACK, GRP_TXT, GRP_DATA, ANON_REQ and PATH. ADVERT, TRACE, MULTIPART, CONTROL and RAW_CUSTOM answer `unsupported-type`.
- **It fills a `mesh::Packet` unchanged**, so stage 2 sends exactly what was supplied.

**Tests** (`test/test_packet_transmit`, 5 cases):
- every allowed type on all four route types, built by MeshCore's own `writeTo` and rebuilt byte for byte;
- the 254-byte maximum, and one byte past the payload bound;
- every truncation, with the input placed flush against an unreadable page so a read past it crashes rather than passing unseen;
- the version and path-length checks, an empty payload, the refused types, and 2-byte path hashes.

**Mutants** (`368_packet_transmit.sh`): 4 run, each killed. `raw_path_unchecked` is noted as equivalent: path bytes are read only once every check has passed, and the payload bound catches the wrapped length anyway.

author: marble098
body:
## چه چیزی درست شد

### ۱) باگ «Can't load widget» — ریشه‌یابی کامل
سه علت واقعی پیدا و رفع شد (همه در یک جهت: ویجت با inflater لانچر ساخته می‌شود، نه با inflater برنامه):

| # | علت | جای اثر | رفع |
|---|---|---|---|
| ۱ | `android:fontFamily="@font/vazirmatn_*"` در چیدمان ویجت — اندروید از میانه‌ی ۲۰۲۱ فونت سفارشی را در RemoteViews ممنوع کرده (issuetracker 190444596) | `widget_usage.xml` (۲۰ مورد) و `widget_preview.xml` (۱۶ مورد) | حذف کامل `@font/`؛ استفاده از `android:textStyle` و فونت سیستم |
| ۲ | ویو خام `<View>` (سه مورد) — `android.view.View` برخلاف `FrameLayout`/`ImageView`/`ProgressBar`، `@RemoteView` نیست و `INFLATER_FILTER` آن را رد می‌کند → `InflateException` | نقطه‌های رنگی و فاصله‌گذار وزن‌دار | `ImageView` و `FrameLayout` |
| ۳ | `onUpdate` بدون هیچ رسم فوری، فقط کار async با مهلت ۸ ثانیه؛ اگر مهلت تمام می‌شد یا خواندن آمار خطا می‌داد، `updateAppWidget` هرگز اجرا نمی‌شد | `UsageWidgetProvider` | رسم فوری آخرین داده (یا کارت حداقلی) پیش از کار سنگین + نگه‌داشتن تصویر قبلی در خطا |

همچنین بررسی و تأیید شد که بقیه‌ی مسیرها سالم‌اند: همه‌ی `set*`ها در `@RemotableViewMethod` قرار دارند (`setLayoutDirection`، `setBackgroundResource`، `setBackgroundTintList`، `setColorFilter`، `setProgressTintList`، `setProgressBar`، `setViewPadding`، `setTextViewTextSize`)، PendingIntentها `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` دارند، هیچ `?attr/`/AppCompat/vector-with-attr در چیدمان یا drawableها نیست، و `initialLayout`/`previewLayout`/`resizeMode` درست‌اند.

**لایه‌ی محافظ جدید:** `widget_fallback.xml` + `WidgetRenderer.fallback()` / `renderFallback()`؛ اگر ساخت چیدمان کامل شکست بخورد، یک کارت سالم و قابل‌ضربه (باز کردن برنامه) جایش می‌نشیند، نه پیام قرمز لانچر.

### ۲) لوگوی رایتل قطعاً بریده نبود؟ بود — و درست شد
تصویر قبلی یک **کادر بسته‌ی حلقه‌ی رایتل** بود: پیکسل مات روی y=0 و y=191 و شروع/پایان افقی روی x=6..184، یعنی خودِ فایل از چهار طرف بریده شده بود؛ هیچ تغییر رندری (ContentScale/padding/اندازه‌ی کاشی) درستش نمی‌کرد. لوگوی رسمی از نو گرفته و فقط حلقه‌اش جدا شد، سپس روی بوم شفاف ۱۹۲×۱۹۲ با حاشیه پخش شد:

- ستون/ردیف مات روی لبه‌ها: **۰** در همه‌ی چهار طرف (قبلاً top 26 / bottom 29)
- `alpha bbox = (22, 22, 170, 170)` — کامل، وسط‌چین، با حاشیه‌ی ۲۲ پیکسلی

### ۳) لوگوهای روشن‌تر
لوگوهایی که میانگین روشنایی‌شان بالای ۰٬۷ است و روی کاشی سفید محو می‌شدند، حالا روی کاشی رنگ برند می‌نشینند: سامان‌تل، تله‌کیش، آپتل، مبنا تلکام، مبین‌نت، اسپادم/MTCE (به‌همراه فن‌آوا و لیزر که از قبل بودند).

### ۴) اینترنت ثابت: پوشش کامل‌تر
- **۱۱ ارائه‌دهنده‌ی ثابت تازه:** ایران تلکام، آرین‌نت، آسیانت، آفتاب‌نت، داتیس‌نت، ایران‌سرور، ابرآروان، پارس‌پک، هاست‌ایران، میهن‌وب‌هاست، میزبان‌فا → مجموع `fixed` از ۱۸ به **۲۹**
- **تطبیق نام کامل:** `fromName` حالا نام فارسی و انگلیسی خودِ اپراتورها را هم امتحان می‌کند (نه فقط کلیدواژه) — مثلاً «Iran Telekom» و «شرکت مخابرات ایران» شناسایی می‌شوند
- **ISP ناشناخته دیگر «نامشخص» نیست:** اگر کد کشور `IR` باشد یا نام نشانه‌ی ایرانی داشته باشد، نام واقعی ISP با نشان «ثابت داخلی» ذخیره می‌شود (شناسه‌ی `f:` که بعد از ری‌استارت هم ایرانی می‌ماند)
- **تمیزکاری نام سازمان:** پسوندهای حقوقی (`PJSC/LLC/شرکت/سهامی خاص/Group/Telecommunication…`) و نام‌های بی‌محتوا (`Internet Service Provider`) حذف می‌شوند
- رفع یک تداخل واقعی: `"ارین"` در آرین‌تل باعث می‌شد «آرین نت» به آرین‌تل نسبت داده شود (نرمال‌سازی آ/ا) → کلیدواژه‌ی کوتاه حذف شد

## تست‌ها
- `WidgetRemoteViewsLayoutTest` (تازه): فقط ویوهای مجاز، بدون `@font/` و `?attr/` و `app:`، وجود همه‌ی `@drawable/`ها در چیدمان‌های ویجت
- `FixedIspDetectionTest` (تازه): تشخیص ۱۱ ارائه‌دهنده‌ی تازه با نام فارسی/انگلیسی/دامنه، نام کامل بدون کلیدواژه، عدم تشخیص نام‌های بی‌ربط (`Netcity Broadband`, `Google LLC`, `Comcast`…)، ماندگاری ISP ناشناخته‌ی ایرانی، `cleanIspName`، یکتایی شناسه‌ها و وصل‌بودن همه‌ی لوگوها
- منطق تطبیق با ۵۷ نمونه (شامل کل تست‌های قبلی) جداگانه شبیه‌سازی و تأیید شد

## یادداشت برای بررسی
- فونت داخل ویجت حالا فونت سیستم است (اندروید اجازه‌ی فونت سفارشی در ویجت نمی‌دهد).
- تغییرات چیدمان ویجت را یک‌بار روی گوشی با لانچر خودت ببین؛ اسکرین‌شات در CI قابل تولید نیست.

author: latxh
body:
- **Clicking a cluster** (e.g. "Toronto +5") or **opening a city** now flies in until every city in view that has venue art shows its image stack. The selected city keeps its dot, since its panel is open. The cities of the cluster stay in view. If they can't all fit (on a phone, "Toronto +6" includes Ottawa), it keeps as many as fit around the main city instead of flying to the empty middle.
- **How the zoom is chosen:** `stackZoom` steps the zoom up 15% at a time. Each step gets a quick check, then a replay of d3-zoom's own flight path and easing, because names keep the side they had in earlier frames and a name can block a neighbour's stack. If every stack never shows, it picks the first zoom that shows the most.
- **Names make room:** a name blocking a neighbour's stack now moves to the other side of its dot when it fits there. Stacks show sooner (desktop Toronto: k 13 instead of 20) and don't depend on where names settled earlier.
- **Phones zoom further:** k = 1 fits Canada to the screen's width, so a phone's k covers more ground. The max zoom now scales with width (40 on desktop, about 113 on a 390 px phone).
- **Refactor:** stack layout moved into `layoutMarkers`, shared by the map and the zoom search.

Checked: typecheck, tests and build pass. Playwright on desktop (1440×900) and a phone (390×844): Toronto cluster, Vancouver cluster, Montréal & Laval, and opening Toronto all end with every nearby city showing its stack. The click costs about 50 ms of JS (about 210 ms at 4x CPU throttle); pan and zoom frame cost is unchanged.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> All changes are isolated to frontend map zoom calculations and marker layout logic in `SportsMap.tsx` with no external state or data dependencies.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Optimizes map zoom behavior** when selecting a city or clicking a cluster so the viewport flies in far enough to display venue card stacks for nearby cities while keeping cluster members in view. The new `stackZoom` calculation samples the flight path using `interpolateZoom` to determine the minimum zoom required to resolve venue stacks and keep relevant markers visible.
> 
> **Refactors marker placement** into a shared `layoutMarkers` function that allows label anchors to flip to the opposite side of a marker when doing so frees up space for an adjacent venue stack. Additionally, `maxZoomFor` now scales the maximum zoom limit inversely with viewport width so mobile screens can zoom in further.
>

author: chunw
body:
https://hrigley-style-git-book-deeplink-mobile-2-c4243f-chunws-projects.vercel.app/catalogs/book?section=negotiated
(Preview needs a Vercel Deployment Protection sign-in. The link above is the deep link this PR fixes: it should open the book directly on the Negotiated Intelligence chapter — folio 238 — on desktop and on a phone, with no waiting on the cover.)

## The bug

On a phone (artist's report, 2026-11-13, in-app browser), `https://www.chunwangshop.com/catalogs/book?section=negotiated` loaded the book — toolbar read "285 PP" — but stayed on the front cover and never jumped to the chapter.

## Diagnosed cause (measured, not guessed)

The deep-link jump in `src/pages/CatalogBook.tsx` had exactly one trigger: `document.fonts.ready.then(… two animation frames … scrollIntoView)`, plus a one-shot correction on window `load` that does nothing until a first jump has happened.

- The book's first layout requests 61 font files (Google Fonts + the Zhuque Fangsong subsets from fontsapi.zeoseven.com; 161 subsets exist). `fonts.ready` resolves only when every pending one settles.
- Measured on the current main build (mobile emulation, 390 px, touch, iOS UA; fonts served from local copies of the real CDN files):
  - fonts failing fast → lands in ~1.8 s
  - fonts at local speed → lands at ~4.4 s
  - fonts slowed 400 ms/file → the cover sits for ~26.8 s before the jump
  - one subset stalled (the production-like failure) → **never lands**: 30 s of samples, scrollY = 0 throughout, zero `scrollIntoView` calls, nav label "Front cover" the whole time. That is the reported symptom, reproduced.
- The desktop's familiar 6–11 s pause on the cover is the same gate on a fast network; a phone on a slower or stalled connection stretches it to "never". No timeout and no fallback existed.

## The fix

The effect no longer waits for fonts at all (page geometry is inch-fixed, so a target's offset never depends on them). It jumps promptly, then re-checks every 500 ms: landed = target at the top of the viewport with the scroll position settled (two consecutive settled checks stand the loop down). While off target it jumps again, absorbing late drift (scrollbar appearance, zoom recompute, image decode). The reader stays sovereign: wheel / touch / pointer / key input stops the loop immediately, a scroll position that moves without us after a jump stands the loop down, and the attempt gives up after 60 s regardless. No-param opens, pagination and print paths are untouched.

## Verification (local build of this exact tree, tsc clean)

- Mobile, font files stalled forever (fonts stuck on `loading`, the failing condition): **lands on folio 238 in about 3 s** (previously: never).
- Mobile `?section=road` → folio 48, lands ~4.2 s. Mobile `?page=200` → lands ~3.4 s, jump fired while fonts were still loading.
- Desktop `?section=negotiated` → lands ~1.7 s (previously ~6–11 s).
- Page count unchanged: 287 PP / 289 sheets (current main's count). Designed pairs spot-checked unchanged on the rebased tree: sheets 36/37 (Residuals #1 plate ↔ its exhibition page) and 72/73 (New York ↔ Hawaii) still form their spreads.
- Re-verified after the rebase onto current main (this branch is one commit on top of the PR #286 merge; only the deep-link effect differs from main): with every font file stalled forever, the mobile build (390 px) reaches the target within ~2.5 s and is settled by ~3.9 s; on a normal network it lands on folio 238 the same way.

author: denkoushi
body:
## 概要
CSV ダッシュボードの追記(APPEND)取り込みで溜まり続ける古い生の行を、同期の成功後に小分けで消す(設計 B)。

- 対象: 製番の機種名補足(SeibanMachineNameSupplement)、CustomerSCAW、吊具点検(RiggingSlingsInspection_PowerApps)
- 基準の回 = 「COMPLETED、completedAt あり、rowsAdded > 0」の最新回。その startedAt より前の行を消す。CustomerSCAW は 0 行の回が続くので、0 行の回は基準にしない
- 吊具は backfill で全履歴を作り直せるよう、中身(rowData)ごとに最新の1行を残す
- 1回の DELETE は 1,000 行、1回の後処理で最大 20,000 行。バッチの間に休みを入れる。残りは次の取り込みで続ける
- 同期が失敗したときは消さない。削除が失敗しても取り込みは失敗にしない
- 削除は後処理から裏で動かす(手動アップロードの応答や取り込みのスケジューラを待たせない)。同じダッシュボードでは重ねない
- `CSV_APPEND_RAW_ROW_PRUNE_ENABLED=false` で止められる(既定 true)
- 確認用 CLI `pnpm prune:csv-append-raw-rows:prod`(既定 dry-run、`--execute` で削除)
- KB: `docs/knowledge-base/api.md` の CSV ダッシュボード項目 10)

## 本番で消える行数の見込み(11/14 読み取りで、同じ条件の SQL を数えた)
- 製番の機種名補足: 71,771 行中 68,488 行(基準 11/07 の回の 3,283 行が残る)
- CustomerSCAW: 35,772 行中 35,764 行(基準 7/25 の回の 8 行が残る)
- 吊具点検: 119,108 行中 115,941 行(中身の違う 3,167 行が残る)
- 1回の取り込みで最大 2 万行ずつなので、全部消えるまで数回の取り込みがかかる

## 確認したこと
- 各同期は、その回に作った行だけを createdAt の窓で読み、行数を rowsAdded と照合する。古い回を後から同期し直す経路は無い(Gmail と手動アップロードは毎回新しい回を作る)
- `CsvDashboardRow` を onDelete Cascade で参照する9表(本番の外部キーも同じ9つ)に、3種の行への参照は無い(本番で 0 件)
- 本番で3種を参照する可視化・サイネージは無い
- 次の取り込みの行は基準の startedAt 以降に作られるので、削除の対象にならない
- 前提: 3種の同期は毎回その回の CSV 全体だけを読む(過去の回の行を合わせて使わない)。そのため最新の回より前の行は、どの読み手にも使われない
- 守り: APPEND 以外のダッシュボードは消さない。基準の回の窓の行数が rowsAdded と合わなければ消さない(本番で3種とも一致: 8 / 10 / 3,283)。6時間以内の PROCESSING の回が先に始まっていれば、その startedAt を上限にする。候補の id は1回だけ取る
- 吊具は rowData ごとに最初の1行を残す。backfill は createdAt の古い順に読み、同じ点検日時では先の行を採るので、それと同じ優先にした

<!-- deploy-impact:start -->
| Item | Declaration |
| --- | --- |
| Risk | api-agent-config |
| Target machines | pi5 |
| Changed surfaces | api, docs |
| Required files/artifacts | N/A: API の通常デプロイだけで、追加の成果物は無い |
| Database | no: スキーマ変更なし。取り込みの後処理で古い生の行を消す |
| Secrets/config delivery | no: 既定 true の env を足すだけで、配布する設定は無い |
| Success evidence | 削除サービスと後処理の単体テスト 50 件合格、api の型チェック合格 |
| Rollback/cleanup | 前の版に戻すか CSV_APPEND_RAW_ROW_PRUNE_ENABLED=false で削除が止まる。消した行は戻らないが、どの同期も読まない行 |
| Production verification | デプロイ後の取り込みで append raw row prune completed のログの deletedCount を見て、行数が減ることを確認する |
<!-- deploy-impact:end -->

## Test plan

- Commands and environments: Mac の worktree で `check-summary`(api 型チェック)、`vitest run` で csv-dashboard-append-raw-row-prune.service.test.ts / csv-dashboard-post-ingest.service.test.ts
- Evidence: 型チェック合格、2 ファイル 50 件合格
- Not run / reason: 実 DB の integration テストは CI に任せる。本番の削除は行っていない(件数は読み取りの SQL で数えた)

author: entelecheia
body:
Part of #553 (E5 T3: repository scanner and the review-then-save flow).

## What changed
- **`scan_repository`** (tauri-plugin-maru-diagram, new `src/scan.rs`). It is native only and runs on an awaited `spawn_blocking` worker. Its only filesystem scope is the root `DiagramHost::scan_root(workspace)` resolves. It is a new trait method with a refusing default, so a host without scan support exposes nothing.
  - Read-only: no process, no network, no writes. Every read, listing and folder open is resolved from one handle on the canonical root the host resolved, with `O_NOFOLLOW` per component, and a folder is charged against the entry bound while it is read. The "no-follow leaf handle" wording and the "intermediate-directory swap remains a nit" line below describe earlier heads; see "Anchored reads and bounded listing" for the code as it stands.
  - A picked folder outside the root, a `..` path or a link out of the root is refused with `diagram_scan_outside_workspace` and a next step.
  - Inventory: the git index when one lies inside the workspace root (v2/v3/v4 parser, tracked regular files still on disk). Otherwise a walk that applies nested `.gitignore` files (negation, anchored, directory-only, `**`; DP matcher, no backtracking blowup).
  - Bounds: 5,000 files (max 20,000), 24 levels (max 64), 20 s, 64 MiB read, 1 MiB per parsed file, 400 nodes, 2,000 edges. Any bound stops the scan with code, cause and next step. No partial map is returned.
  - Imports: TS/JS (`import`/`from`/`require`, extension, `index`, `.js` to `.ts`), Rust (`mod`, `use crate::`/`self::`/`super::`) and Python (absolute, relative, `from . import`). Files are aggregated to folder nodes two levels deep with the parent chain kept. Cross-folder imports become `import` edges. External packages go to `packages`.
  - Output: a `floorplan/architecture@1` document. No Floorplan code is used; the format is the only reference.
- **Maru host** (`engine_host.rs`): `scan_root` accepts only a *registered* workspace (new `vault_list::registered_workspace_root`, read access for every registered workspace).
- **Review-then-save UI**: File ribbon > Scan repository (`ScanRepositoryDialog`). It shows counts and inventory. "Open as unsaved document" runs the proposal through the same `parseFloorplanSpec` checks as an import (provenance `generated`, `sourcePath` the scanned folder) and opens it unsaved. Saving is the ordinary Save, so nothing is written before that and nothing outside the chosen save path. A refused proposal is not opened. Strings are in ko and en.
- **Isolation**: the command count goes from 393 to 394. Permission is `maru-diagram:allow-scan-repository` in the main-only `diagram-render` capability and the plugin default set. Evidence was regenerated with the existing tooling: `plugin-command-mock-ipc.json` via `MARU_PLUGIN_COMMAND_EVIDENCE` and `plugin-acl-mock-ipc.json` via `MARU_PLUGIN_ACL_EVIDENCE`. The Sites window and the Sites child webview are denied. The ACL probe uses a missing workspace, and the refusal reaches the main handler. `phase08-current-registrations.json` came from `--refresh-current-manifest` on clean committed source head ec20b7a2 after merging main a5c1e3b7. No hand edits. Expected count 394 is updated in Makefile, README, AGENTS.md and the guard and its tests. AGENTS.md also still said 392; that is fixed.
- `docs/diagram.md` §Floorplan: a new "Repository scan" paragraph. The stale "Scanning a repository belongs to #536" line is removed.

## Acceptance criteria (this task)
- [x] **AC2** (the owner amended maru#553 AC2 on 2026-11-14: synthetic trees with recorded expectations satisfy it; the no-write clause is covered by the T123-R5 fix): a synthetic polyglot tree (TS, Rust, Python, `.gitignore` with negation, ignored `dist/` and `vendor/`) yields the recorded modules `root, analysis, core, core.src, shared, tools, web, web.src`, the edges `tools→analysis` and `web.src→shared`, and the packages per node (`a_synthetic_repository_proposes_the_recorded_modules_and_import_edges`). The scan leaves the tree byte- and mtime-identical (`the_scan_never_writes_into_the_tree`). The proposal passes the shape rules, and `repoScan.test.ts` shows it parses as a floorplan dataset carried verbatim and that a refused proposal is not opened. No public repository content is copied; test data is synthetic only.
- **AC3**: refusal tests cover `..`, `../x`, an absolute outside path, `/`, a link out, a file, a missing path and an empty path. Bound tests cover files, depth, time and limit range. A git index above the workspace is not read. Large files are counted but not parsed.
- **AC5**: the scanner's only scope comes from `DiagramHost::scan_root`. The plugin owns no Maru paths, and the command-isolation guard passes.

## Checks
- Exact-head `make verify` at 242fac31 via `dot remote verify`: PASS (TS 3356 passed; app Rust 2286 passed, 7 ignored; plugin 31 + 1; fmt, clippy, frontend build, budgets; command isolation 394).
- Plugin scanner unit tests: 19 passed.
- Native real-app check (WKWebView, `e2e-native/specs/diagram-scan.spec.ts`): **1 passing**. It covers ribbon → dialog; refusal of an outside folder showing code and next step; a proposal from a fixture-workspace folder with the counts pinned in `the_native_spec_tree_has_its_recorded_counts` (5 folders, 1 import link, 6 files); the scanned tree unchanged; and opening the proposal writes no document.
- UNVERIFIED: the native "Browse…" folder picker (OS dialog; the spec types the path instead), and Save of the opened map in the real app (the ordinary Save path, unchanged here).

Local note: this Mac's WASM link fails with both installed toolchains (rustup 1.98 `rust-lld` lacks `libLLVM.dylib`; Homebrew 1.99 has no wasm std). The native build used `CARGO_TARGET_WASM32_UNKNOWN_UNKNOWN_LINKER=/opt/homebrew/opt/lld@22/bin/wasm-ld` as a local env var only. No repo change.



## Review round 1 (claude, at 242fac31): fixed at fdd83c68
| Finding | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|
| T123-R1 links in index mode | `regular_file_without_links` checks every path component with lstat (no link, folders are folders, leaf is a regular file). It runs in the inventory and again right before each read in `propose`. | `a_tracked_path_under_a_folder_now_linked_out_is_never_read`: a tracked `vendor/x.ts` under a folder now linked out is left out, and its imports and packages never enter the map. |
| T123-R2 v4 expansion | `parse_index(bytes, deadline)` charges each rebuilt path before it is kept: max 4,096 B per path and 64 MiB total. The deadline is checked while parsing. Exceeding a limit refuses with `diagram_scan_index_too_large` and a next step. | `v4_prefix_expansion_is_bounded_before_paths_are_kept`: a 20,000-entry growing v4 index is refused fast, and a small growing index still parses. |
| T123-R3 wide folders | The entry budget (200,000, ignored entries included) and the deadline apply while reading each folder. Ignored entries are dropped as read. The file limit applies before the sort. | `a_very_wide_ignored_folder_stops_at_the_entry_budget` |
| T123-R4 use paths and deadline | `use` paths are cut at 16 segments. The deadline is checked per source file, after the import pass and before returning. | `a_long_rust_use_path_resolves_in_bounded_time`, `a_scan_that_overruns_its_budget_is_refused_not_returned` |
| T123-R5 writes before Save | "Open as unsaved document" goes through `handleOpenProposal`: no `persistLastDocument`, and the snapshot scheduler is held clean until the first explicit Save. Any other document open or new clears the hold. | The native spec now waits past the 2.5 s snapshot debounce and asserts `.maru` (history, workspace state, settings) is unchanged. **Red without the fix** ("Opening the proposal wrote under .maru") and **green with it** (1 passing). |

author: scuttletoby
body:
## Why

This fork is public, Issues are on, and agents read its issues as owner questions. A repository interaction limit (`collaborators_only`) keeps strangers out, but GitHub ends every limit after six months at most. If it lapses quietly, anyone can open issues and comments again. This makes the lapse impossible to miss: a weekly check that goes red and opens one issue, plus a script the owner's machine runs to renew it.

- `.github/scripts/fork-interaction-limit.sh`
  - `check`: reads the limit. Exit 0 when it is the configured one and ends in more than N days (default 30), 1 when it is missing, another limit or ends sooner, 2 when it cannot be read.
  - `renew`: sets the limit for six months, then reads it back and checks it took. With `--if-under N` it only reads while more than N days remain. A monthly timer should use `--if-under 75`.
  - `report`: opens one issue, "Interaction limit needs attention", or comments on the open one. It closes that issue on the next good run. It only ever touches an open issue that GitHub Actions opened, never a stranger's issue with the same title.
- `.github/workflows/fork-interaction-limit.yml`: weekly plus `workflow_dispatch`. No pull request trigger. `permissions: {}` at the top; the job gets `contents: read` and `issues: write`. The token is read only on `main`: a manual run on another branch stops red with a notice.
- `fork-gh-guard.sh`: it used to refuse every run outside Actions or tests. Now `FORK_GH_LOCAL=<script file name>` lets a script run on a person's machine, for the renewal timer, but only a script on the guard's fixed list (today just `fork-interaction-limit.sh`), and only when the running file, symlinks resolved, is that file beside the guard. Every other script still refuses.

**Owner step needed: the check needs a read token.** I tested this with a temporary probe workflow on this branch, since removed. GitHub's workflow token gets **403** on `GET /repos/{repo}/interaction-limits`, and GraphQL `interactionAbility` returns `null`, which looks the same as "no limit". So the read step uses the repository secret `FORK_INTERACTION_LIMIT_TOKEN`: a fine-grained token for this repository with **Administration: read-only** and nothing else. Until that secret is set, every run fails and says so, and the issue says the same.

## General vs project

- **General (in the fork):** the script, the workflow and the tests. The repository comes from `--repo`, or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` inside Actions only. The limit and the margin come from the optional repository variables `FORK_INTERACTION_LIMIT` and `FORK_INTERACTION_LIMIT_DAYS`. Nothing personal.
- **Project or machine (private, not in the fork):** the owner's monthly renewal timer, its list of repositories (a private config file), and the read token secret.

## State question: what happens when this runs again, stops half-way, or meets existing, old or empty state?

- **Runs again:** `check` only reads. `renew` is a PUT that just moves the end date six months on, so a second run is harmless. `report` looks up the open issue by its exact title among the open issues GitHub Actions opened (the issue list, not search, whose index can lag) and comments on it, so it never opens a second one. A failed issue lookup opens nothing and fails the run.
- **Stops half-way:** if the PUT went through but the read back failed, `renew` exits 2 and the next run reads and renews again. If the check step dies without writing its result file, `report` treats that as a failure and opens or updates the issue.
- **Existing or old state:** another limit (even a stricter one) fails `check`, and `renew` sets the configured one. A limit that has already ended, or ends within the margin, fails. A limit set at user level is shown with its origin.
- **Empty state:** no limit (`{}` or an empty answer) fails `check` and says anyone can post. An answer the script does not understand, or an unreadable end date, is an error (2), never a pass.

## Failure table

| Situation | `check` | Workflow | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configured limit, more than 30 days left | 0 | green | closed if one was open |
| Configured limit, 30 days or fewer left, or already ended | 1 | red | opened or commented |
| No limit / another limit | 1 | red | opened or commented |
| Token cannot read (403), secret missing, odd answer | 2 | red | opened or commented |
| Issues disabled | (as above) | red when the check failed | none, and the summary says so |
| Issue list or close fails | (as above) | red | nothing duplicated |
| `renew`: PUT refused / did not take / read back fails | 2, never claims "renewed" | n/a (renew runs locally) | n/a |
| Limit set for the whole user or organization (409 on renew) | 1 when it differs or ends soon | red | says to change it where it was set |
| Stranger opened an issue with the same title | (as above) | (as above) | left alone; the bot opens its own |
| Manual run on a branch other than `main` | not run | red, with a notice | none |
| Script run on a machine without `FORK_GH_LOCAL` naming it | refuses before any gh call | n/a | n/a |

## Tests

`bash .github/scripts/fork-interaction-limit.test.sh`: 76 cases against a fake `gh` set up through `fork-test-gh.sh`. No token, `GH_HOST` is a `.invalid` host, an empty gh config, and the script refuses when the stub is not the gh it would call. Four hand mutants (off-by-one on the margin, skipped read back, issue duplicated, `--if-under` ignored) each turn a case red. Run locally and green: `fork-contracts.test.py`, `fork-follow.test.sh` and `fork-release.test.sh` (guard change), `fork-ci-tests.test.cjs`, `fork-workflow-triggers.test.cjs`, `fork-fleet.test.py`, `fork-release-workflow.test.py`, `fork-tests-drift.test.cjs`, `fork-secret-scan.test.sh`.

## Review fixes

From the security and correctness lenses (commit 766ff086d):

- **Stranger's issue (sec medium, corr low 6):** `report` lists only open issues GitHub Actions opened (`gh issue list --author github-actions[bot]`, the issue list, no search) and also checks the author `app/github-actions` and the exact title in `--jq`. Note: the list API's author filter needs `github-actions[bot]`; `--author app/github-actions` (search syntax) returns nothing there, checked against a public repository. Tests: a stranger's same-titled issue is never commented on or closed, also when the list ignores `--author`.
- **`REPOSITORY` (sec low):** never read. Outside Actions `--repo` is required; in Actions `--repo` or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`. Tests.
- **`FORK_GH_LOCAL` (sec info 3, corr note 8):** fixed allow-list in `fork-gh-guard.sh` (`FORK_GH_LOCAL_SCRIPTS`, today just this script) plus a resolved-path check. Tests: another script naming itself refuses; a symlink with the allowed name refuses; a copy whose guard lives elsewhere refuses; a copy of both files side by side (the owner's pinned copy) runs. `fork-follow.test.sh` and `fork-release.test.sh` green.
- **Dispatch on another branch (sec info 4):** the token and issue steps run only on `refs/heads/main`; elsewhere a first step prints a notice and fails the run.
- **Renewal margin (corr medium):** documented 75 days for a monthly timer (check margin 30 plus a month and some), in the script header and the workflow comment. The script itself has no default margin: `renew` without `--if-under` always renews.
- **Configured limit in the issue (corr low 2):** the workflow passes `--limit` to `report`, and the issue's renew command carries it. Test.
- **Octal (corr low 3):** `--days` and `--if-under` are read as base 10 after the digits check. Tests (`0110`, `08`, `075`).
- **Shifted fields (corr low 4):** jq prints one field per line plus an end marker, read with `mapfile`; a missing or null `origin` stays in place. Tests.
- **User/organization level (corr low 5):** check's message and the 409 from `renew` say to change the limit where it was set; the issue text says so too. Tests.
- **Close-only failure (corr note 7):** the run fails with "Could not close i

Replaces the sidebar search box with a command bar, as planned.

**Desktop**
- `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` or `/` opens it from anywhere (except while typing in a field). The sidebar has a `search ⌘K` row for mouse users. It shows `Ctrl K` on Windows and Linux.
- `↑`/`↓` move, `Enter` opens (`⌘/Ctrl+Enter` or `⌘`-click opens in a new tab), and `Esc` or a click outside closes.

**Mobile**
- A search icon next to the menu button opens the bar as a **full-screen sheet** with a Cancel button. The search box in the menu drawer is gone, so there's one way into search on each layout.
- The input is 16 px, so iPhones don't zoom in. Rows are at least 44 px tall, the keyboard shows a search key, and the sheet resizes to end above the on-screen keyboard.
- The **back gesture closes the sheet** instead of leaving the page.

**What it finds**
- **Posts:** every word must match. Title matches rank above tags, then the description, then the text. Matches are highlighted, and a post that only matches in its text shows a snippet around the match. The last row is "See all results on the posts page →" (`/posts/?q=…`).
- **Pages:** home, posts, series, topics, about, works, projects, uses, services, also matched by keywords from each page's description ("pilot" finds /about).
- **Actions:** switch theme, next accent colour, copy link to this page, RSS feed. Theme and accent keep the bar open so you see the change.
- With nothing typed, it shows the 5 latest posts, the pages and the actions.

**How**
- `src/pages/search.json.ts` builds the post data with the site: 30 KB, 12.6 KB gzipped. It's only downloaded the first time the bar opens, or when the pointer reaches a trigger, so normal page loads don't change. Drafts are left out.
- `src/components/command-bar.astro`: a native `<dialog>` (keeps focus inside, closes on Esc) with combobox/listbox roles, `aria-activedescendant` and a live result count for screen readers. Results are built with DOM methods, never `innerHTML`. Enter is ignored while composing with an input method (e.g. Thai). The open animation is off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
- No new inline scripts, so the CSP hashes are unchanged (still 10). The triggers are links to `/posts/`, so search still works without JavaScript. `/posts/` keeps its own search box.

**Tested locally** with `wrangler dev` (real `_headers`/CSP, no violations), desktop and mobile (375 px), dark and light:
- ⌘K, Ctrl+K and / all open it.
- Arrow keys and Enter work.
- Opening a result replaces the bar's history entry, and Back returns to the previous page with the bar closed.
- Esc, Cancel and Back each close it, and history comes out right even when reopening immediately.
- Theme toggling, ignored composing-Enter, 16 px input and 56 px rows checked on the sheet.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the last red in the B-300 acceptance (runbook §118.5): after #2111 the user's original memory stays valid, but the same subject still ended with near-duplicate user rows. Measured on test (8ef6b0a21): the extra `user_stated` row differed from the original **only by a trailing full stop** (same kind, same agent slot, different `content_hash`, so the DB unique index — case / edge-whitespace only — let it in). It came from a user-side candidate X that the model UPDATE'd onto a similar assistant row while an equivalent user row already existed.

**Deterministic "same content" check before the reconcile model call** (`graph_builder/memory.py`)
- A non-correction candidate whose text equals a valid neighbour's text — same kind, same `agent_name`, neighbour provenance ≥ candidate's (user-side > assistant / unrecorded) — is a NOOP with no model call (`op="noop"`).
- **"Equal" only ignores differences that keep the meaning** (user decision 11-14, after prior-art review: mem0 / Cognee / Dolma hash raw text; Graphiti exact / deer-flow / OpenViking fold only case and whitespace; punctuation-stripping schemes — SQuAD, MLQA, datatrove, WeKnora — collide 69.1/691, 50%/50, -3/3; UAX #15 warns against blind NFKC): NFC, width folding only (`<wide>`/`<narrow>`), casefold, whitespace collapse, and trailing `. ! ; 。` at the very end. Nothing else is removed — not `?` (question ≠ statement), not inner punctuation, signs, `%`, brackets, superscripts, circled digits. Tests pin 21+ "different" pairs (69.1/691, .5 mg/5 mg, Rh-/Rh, 尿蛋白(-)/尿蛋白, HER2-/HER2, 10⁵/105, 3-5/35, 1/2/12, it's/its, emails, questions vs statements, …).
- **Corrections**: always go to the model; the reconcile prompt says an identical existing user-stated / corrected memory makes the candidate a NOOP, except a correction, which DELETEs the memory it contradicts, otherwise NOOP. A correction restating an existing user memory never lands as a new row: the model's decision is rewritten — DELETE of another memory runs (guards apply), UPDATE of a different target runs as DELETE of that target, everything else (ADD / NOOP / touching the identical memory / missing decision / no similar neighbours) is a NOOP. Debug log at the rewrite (no content).
- Known, accepted (design §6.2): casefold merges Cal/cal, Mg/mg, ß/ss; an identical NOOP does not raise the existing row's confidence or refresh its validity.

**Docs** — design §6.2 / §10.2 (decision 9, user 11-14) / §13.3; runbook §118.5 re-check notes.

## Test plan
- [x] Red first on every step (6 / 9 / 14 / 4 failing before the respective fixes); mutations for each guard (normalization steps, digit/inner punctuation, kind/agent scope, correction exemption, rewrite of the model's decision, "?" handling) all turn tests red; restores byte-exact
- [x] orchestrator unit 6724, ruff check / format, CI mypy (1067 files)
- [x] Independent review: 4 rounds (fresh reviewer each time); final round no MEDIUM+, its LOWs fixed (tests that certified a broken rewrite now go red)
- [ ] After 「发测试」: rerun §118.5 on test (budget left from the approved ¥2: ≈ ¥1.67)

author: ph-li
body:
## Summary
Adds optional accounts so presentations sync across devices. The app stays **offline-first**: everything still saves to the browser instantly, and sync runs in the background.

- **Sign-in:** email magic link on a new `#/account` page, so there are no passwords. A status chip on the home page shows Sign in / Syncing / Synced / Offline.
- **Sync engine** (`services/cloudSync.js`):
  - Pulls and merges on sign-in, on coming back online and when the tab regains focus.
  - Uploads changes about 0.8s after they're made, and retries every 30s on failure.
  - When the same presentation was edited in two places, the newest edit wins. Deletes propagate between devices, including deletes made offline.
- **Accounts on one device:**
  - Each user gets their own local cache, so accounts never mix on a shared device.
  - Presentations made while signed out are added to the account on first sign-in.
  - Sign-out first uploads any pending changes (it refuses if it can't, so nothing is lost), then removes that user's cached copy.
- **Config:** `scripts/write-config.js` turns `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` into `public/config.js`.
  - It is now Netlify's build command, and `npm start` runs it too.
  - It fails the build if given a `service_role` or `sb_secret_` key.
  - It also accepts the variable names Netlify's Supabase extension uses.
  - With no env vars, the app runs exactly as before (local-only).
- **Database:** `supabase/migrations/…_create_presentations.sql` creates the `presentations` table with RLS that limits every operation to `auth.uid() = user_id`. It's idempotent, so it's safe if the table was already created by hand. `supabase/config.toml` is included for the Supabase CLI / GitHub integration.
- **supabase-js** is loaded from jsDelivr only when sync is configured, so there are still no npm dependencies.

## Setup needed before merging
1. **Netlify env vars:** set `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (anon / publishable key) under Project configuration → Environment variables.
2. **Supabase Auth → URL Configuration:**
   - Site URL: `https://presentassist.netlify.app`
   - Redirect URLs: `http://localhost:3000/**`, `https://*--presentassist.netlify.app/**`
3. **Table:** confirm the migration was applied. The GitHub integration should do this once it's on `main`; otherwise run it in the SQL Editor.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run check` (25 modules) and `npm test`: 48/48 pass, including:
  - the three-way merge cases
  - the sync engine against an in-memory fake cloud: two devices, offline edits, deletes, signed-out notes added on sign-in, sign-out
  - secret-key rejection in the config script
- [x] Headless Chrome, sync **off**: home, present and account pages work as before ("Sync isn't set up").
- [x] Headless Chrome, sync **on** with a fake project, signed out: supabase-js loads from the CDN, the home chip says "Sign in to sync", and the account page shows the email form. Checked at phone width.
- [ ] On the deploy preview with the real project: sign in by magic link, create and edit, check the row in Supabase, open on a second device, delete, go offline and back online, sign out.

author: penguinztech
body:
## Findings (alpha 2026-11-14, read-only evidence from `dal2alpha`/`waddlebot`)

1. **(a) TRUE - no DEK single-flight.** `CachedDekProvider::get_dek[_version]` (`core/hub_client/src/dek.rs`, old L441-L490) did `cache check -> broker.fetch().await -> store`: every concurrent miss called `KeyService.GetStreamDek`. Callers: svc-process decrypt (`svc_process/src/identity_crypto.rs:257`, ~160 per-app consumers share one provider) and svc-ingest encrypt (`get_dek`).
2. **(b) TRUE for cold-start/refresh/failure, FALSE for steady state.** `MachineJwtClient::get_token` (`core/service_auth/src/lib.rs`, old L790) *does* cache (900 s TTL), but had **no single-flight** and cached **no failures**: all concurrent misses each minted (each one a K8s TokenReview in hub-api), and every failed/timed-out mint (and every retry in `HubClient::call_with_retry`, which re-calls `get_token` per attempt) minted again. Tokens are per-scope (`MintServiceToken(scope)`), so the cache is per-scope. (`identity_crypto.rs:~486` named in the brief is a test helper, not a provider.)
3. **(c) TRUE - breaker.** `CircuitBreaker::record_failure` (`core/hub_client/src/lib.rs`) re-stamped `opened_at` and re-logged on *every* failure past the threshold (stragglers of one burst), and half-open let *all* concurrent callers through (not one probe).
4. **Live evidence:** hub-api 3 min: 44 `service_jwt.issue` (42 svc-process; 35 `key:stream-dek:read`), all within ~5 s (02:15:22-27), ~100 ms apart (serialized TokenReview). svc-process: 125 `dek_unavailable` dead-letters in the same burst - **103/125 are `failed to obtain machine JWT ... Timeout expired`** (the *mint* timed out, not KeyService), 22 `hub-api internal gRPC ... Timeout`; 118 `circuit_opened` (105 in one second, counter reaching 6+ = stragglers). Self-reinforcing loop: mint stampede -> hub-api slow -> mint timeouts not shared -> more mints.

## Fix
- `service_auth::MachineJwtClient`: reuse until 80% of lifetime (or exp-30 s), single-flight refresh, failed refresh shared for a jittered ~500 ms (old still-valid token served meanwhile), per-scope; `waddles_hub_service_jwt_total{result=reuse|refresh|refresh_failed,scope}`.
- `hub_client::dek::CachedDekProvider`: per-`(tenant, version)` single-flight, shared failure + jittered exponential negative cache (250 ms -> 5 s), bounded (4096 keys), invalidate-vs-in-flight generation guard; `waddles_hub_dek_cache_total{result=hit|miss|inflight_wait|negative}`. AEAD/seal semantics untouched; fail-closed unchanged; cache key includes tenant (provider is per service identity).
- `hub_client::CircuitBreaker`: opens once per burst (generation guard ignores in-flight stragglers), exactly one half-open probe, caller-error probe releases the lease; thresholds documented (5 failed attempts; one failed call is <= 3 attempts so a coalesced failure cannot open it).
- Docs: `docs/observability/data-plane-metrics.md`.

## Tests (real path: in-process tonic `KeyService` fake + counting tonic `MintServiceToken` mock)
160 concurrent cold decrypts = 1 broker call + 1 mint; 1000 decrypts over 3 TTL windows = 3 calls + 1 mint; new key version refetches; invalidate-during-fetch not cached; broker failure: 160 waiters from 1 call (3 attempts), 160 more shed with no wire traffic, retry after backoff; mint failure: 1 mint for 160 waiters, 0 broker calls; token reuse/80% refresh once/stale-token on failed refresh/scope-specific; breaker burst/probe/neutral; metrics through the real global meter.

## Results (examined / passed / failed)
| crate | passed | failed | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| hub_client | 110 | 0 | 98 lib (11 new) + 3 + 1 + 7 integration + 1 new `cache_metrics` |
| service_auth | 122 | 0 | 6 new single-flight tests; 4 fail with the gate removed (mutation-checked) |
| connection_resolver / bundle_host_media | 46 / 44 | 0 / 0 | |
| svc_process | 772 | 6 | the 6 = `reputation_pg_e2e` (Postgres container, `backend` error): **fails identically on base `release/v3.0.X`** and does not touch hub_client/service_auth |
| svc_action | 666 | 2 | `get_context_config_kill_switch_both_states` **fails identically on base**; `relay_..._real_valkey` needs `VALKEY_URL` |
| svc_ingest | 1513 | 93 | all 93 are "VALKEY_URL / TEST_DATABASE_URL not set" (real-service tests, no silent skip); not run here, so **not claimed passing** |

`cargo fmt --check` + `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`: hub_client, service_auth, svc_process clean. No dependency changes (no `cargo deny` run needed). One existing test (`a_key_broker_outage_dead_letters_visibly_and_recovers`) asserted "failure not cached"; it now waits out the <=312 ms negative window, which is the intended behavior change.

Not verifiable pre-merge: the live alpha effect (needs the image built + deployed; check `waddles_hub_service_jwt_total{result="refresh"}` ~ flat and hub-api `service_jwt.issue` ~1 per scope per ~12 min).

author: borgesinmas
body:
## Qué cambia y por qué

- **«Cómo se calcula» en los duelos** (amigos, partida rápida, clasificatoria y bot): al terminar cada ronda se puede desplegar el mismo panel del reto diario (cuenta por pasos, razonamiento, supuestos y fuentes). Como el resultado de la ronda solo dura 10 s, al final del duelo hay un **repaso** con cada pregunta, la cifra real, las dos respuestas y su cálculo.
- **Sin preguntas repetidas entre partidas:** antes cada duelo barajaba las ~290 preguntas sin mirar las partidas anteriores, así que en tres duelos seguidos se repetían dos o tres. Ahora, al empezar un duelo, se evitan las preguntas de los últimos 25 duelos de **los dos** jugadores; si no hay bastantes sin ver, salen primero las vistas hace más tiempo.
- El servidor solo manda el cálculo cuando la ronda ha terminado. En Supabase se leen solo los ids (`state->questions`) de `duels`: **sin migración**.

Decisión [[0048](https://github.com/Faraday-gg/Faraday.gg/compare/preprod...feat/docs/decisiones/0048-calculo-y-sin-repetir-en-duelos.md)](docs/decisiones/0048-calculo-y-sin-repetir-en-duelos.md).

## Cómo probarlo

1. `node preview-server.mjs` y abrir la app.
2. Duelo 1 vs 1 → Retar a un amigo → Practicar con el bot. Responder: en el resultado de la ronda aparece «Cómo se calcula · también al final del duelo».
3. Terminar el duelo: bajo el marcador de rondas aparece «Repasa las preguntas»; cada una se despliega con real, tú, rival y el cálculo.
4. Jugar otro duelo: no sale ninguna pregunta del anterior.

## Comprobaciones

- [x] `community`, `editorial`, `vercel`, `publicar`, `generar`, `cofres`, `casi`, `auth`, `ligas`, `medallas`, `rangos`, `apuestas`: OK.
- [ ] `node tests/duelos.test.mjs`: **ya fallaba en `preprod`** en «El bot contesta a veces (8 de 8)» (azar con semilla fija), sin relación con este cambio. Con esa comprobación desactivada en local, el resto pasa, incluidas las nuevas: 3 duelos seguidos → 30 preguntas distintas; con un rival nuevo salen primero las que el otro no ha visto; el cálculo no viaja durante la pregunta y sí en el resultado y en el repaso final; la consulta a Supabase pide solo los ids. Apuntado en `docs/mejoras/`.
- [x] Revisado en el navegador (duelo completo contra el bot, escritorio y 375 px).

## Riesgos y pendientes

- La búsqueda por jugador en `duels` usa contención en `state` sin índice (como ya hacía la reconexión). Si la tabla crece, conviene un índice GIN (en mejoras; necesita migración y confirmación).
- No se evitan las preguntas que el jugador ya vio en el reto diario: el servidor no lo sabe por jugador.

author: aiselfmyselfresearch-max
body:
## 内容

2026-11-10 に発効した `read_log` 層2 の規則について、設計報告（`readings/2027-03-15-how-to-make-layer-two-mandatory-without-manufacturing-records.md`）を全文再読し、発効後114セッション・949ペアをセッション別に測りました。新しい資料・仮説・問いは追加していません。

### 主な結果

- 適格114セッション、949ペア。手書きの読み910、`未読の選択:` 10、未充足29、集計96.9%。
- 未充足29はすべて **`used_as_context` のみ** のペアで、どの行も無いペアは0。
- 29ペアは一セッション `SESSION-20261113-1650a1` に集中（文脈39、手書き10、未充足29）。このセッションは10点を `interpreted`、29点を `used_as_context` で記録していました。素材を無視したのではなく、層2 が数えないラベルで記録しています。
- 最初の10セッションはすべて充足（うち `SESSION-20261110-167875` の3ペアは `未読の選択:`）。ただし最大文脈は26で、30以上の事例は通っていません。
- 文脈30以上は1セッションのみで、そこに29ペアが集中。n=1 のため因果とは言えませんが、集計値96.9%はセッション内の29/39 = 74.4%の未充足を薄めます。

### 設計上の発見

`未読の選択:` は `sessions.notes` に書く設計ですが、`sessions` は追記専用で、行が確定した後は書き換えられません。したがって設計の修復手順は**セッションがまだ書かれていない間だけ**有効です。行が確定した後の未充足は、検査が検出できても直せません。29ペアを遡及して埋めることはせず、`read_log` に読んだ行を足すこともしませんでした。

author: nithishreddy5771
body:
### Problem

Kinesis can return partial PutRecords failures without raising a request exception. The sink currently accepts those responses during flush, allowing a checkpoint to advance despite undelivered records. It also retains submitted buffers and completed futures, so later flushes resend successful records and keep raising for old failed requests.

### Changes

- Remove each buffered batch when it is submitted.
- Drain the checkpoint's request futures and wait for all of them to settle before retrying.
- Reject partial Kinesis responses as well as request exceptions using the existing SinkBackpressureError and retry delay.
- Cover normal/eager batches, failed delivery followed by checkpoint replay, repeated flushes and the 500-record boundary across partitions.

This restores the documented at-least-once behavior. Checkpoint replay remains responsible for retrying the batch, including possible duplicates for records that already succeeded.

Refs #1199

### Validation

These checks were run by an AI assistant on my behalf using a mocked boto3 client and the real executor, without AWS calls:

- Regression on unchanged production source: 11 tests fail, including the expected missing partial-failure rejection and repeated-send assertions.
- Python 3.13: Kinesis, sink-base and file-format tests: 35 passed.
- Python 3.11: Kinesis and sink-base tests: 17 passed.
- pre-commit run --all-files: Ruff, formatting, conda requirements and mypy passed.
- git diff --check passed.

Live AWS, broker-backed checkpoint tests and the full test suite were not run. No changes to the documented delivery contract or public configuration.

author: samargulies
body:
## What and why

`MapJr` passed a new `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` object to its map element in each render. The React that Next.js 14.2 bundles for the app router (`18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218`) sets `innerHTML` again for each new object without comparing the strings, so the first re-render deleted the canvas of the map. The component now keeps one object for its whole life (`useState`), and the HTML of the server render is unchanged.

The test adds that exact React build as two aliased dev dependencies (`react-next14`, `react-dom-next14`). They are used only by `test/react.mjs` and are not in the built files. The new check renders `MapJr` with that React under `StrictMode` (double effects), renders the parent again twice, unmounts the map, and mounts it again. It checks that there is one canvas after the renders, none after the unmount, and one after the remount.

Fixes #188

## How it was checked

- `node test/react.mjs`: without the fix, the new check fails (`{"version":"18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218","first":0,"rendered":0,"removed":0,"remounted":0}`). With the fix, all 9 checks pass, including the server render check.
- `pnpm build && pnpm test`: passes. On the first run one unit test failed on time under load (`tile truncated to 444502 bytes: took 2182 ms`); the second run passed with 66 of 66.
- Size: `dist/react.js` went from 1611 to 1618 bytes gzip (measured with `gzip -9`; `pnpm test:size` has no line for it). The other built files did not change.
- Not checked: a real Next.js app, Safari, a GPU.

**Intent:** a request posted with no title stops repeating its first line as the heading. It gets a short, proper title (e.g. "Profile won't open from comments"), and the description stays as the body.

**How**
- New edge function `feature-request-title`: names untitled requests with the free model tier, cleans the answer, writes it once.
- Migration `20261114030000`: `title_auto` column, insert trigger that calls the function, 15 min catch-up cron, and a write RPC that only replaces the exact old title and does not bump `updated_at` (board order doesn't change).
- Web: board looks again 4s / 12s after posting so the new title shows.

**Constraints**
- Only rows whose title is still a copy of the description are touched; typed titles are never changed; each row is named once.
- Posting never waits on or fails because of the title call.

**Results:** `title.test.ts` passes (untitled detection, bug-report details stripped, answer clean-up). Backfill of the ~91 existing untitled requests runs right after deploy.

body:
## What this fixes (external review of the agent harness, items 3.1 to 3.7)

Each finding was reproduced on current main first; all seven reproduced. Each fix has a regression test that fails before it.

- **3.1 (blocker)**: a lone surrogate escape in a tool input made the request unparseable for the engine, which allowed it unjudged. `cannot_place` now refuses an agent's edit where `acceptance` or `protected-paths` is `on_unjudged: deny` (same rule as `adapter_failure`). SPEC-24 amended. Tests: `a_request_the_engine_cannot_parse_is_refused_where_a_gate_denies_and_allowed_loudly_otherwise`, `a_lone_surrogate_in_a_tool_input_is_refused_by_the_translator_where_a_gate_denies`.
- **3.2**: an MCP object with two different strings under content keys is unplaceable and gets the targeted refusal. Test: `an_mcp_call_with_more_than_one_candidate_content_string_is_unplaceable`.
- **3.3**: an unusable cwd. The engine falls back to `project_dir`, else refuses under deny. The translator uses PROJECT_DIR as the cwd and as the engine's working directory, and the config-text fallback reads both. Tests: `a_cwd_that_cannot_be_entered_is_replaced_by_the_project_directory_or_refused_under_deny`, `the_translator_runs_the_engine_in_the_project_directory_when_the_payload_cwd_is_unusable`.
- **3.4**: `harness status` reports `disableAllHooks` among its problems (status `drift`). Test: `status_reports_the_kill_switch_and_compares_versions_numerically`.
- **3.5**: `is_git_root` is memoised per directory for one request, `targeted_denial` reads the raw config once, and the engine judges at most 512 paths, with the overflow handled like `MCP_MAX_ITEMS` (refused under deny). Tests: `the_engine_judges_a_capped_number_of_paths_and_refuses_the_overflow_under_deny`, unit `a_directory_is_asked_of_git_once_however_many_paths_are_under_it`, `a_request_beyond_the_path_cap_hands_the_rest_back_as_absolute_paths`.
- **3.6**: the timing test is replaced by `two_thousand_files_with_the_protected_one_last_cost_one_gates_request_and_one_for_the_overflow`, which asserts on the request log via `logging_engine`.
- **3.7**: three docs statements corrected (AGENTS.md on `.claude/settings.local.json`; the 512/24 refusal names the tool, not a file; `.urzua/cache` is not ignored for adopters until they add it). Version comparison is now numeric (`version_is_older`, in `status` and `session-start`); unit test `versions_compare_as_numbers_not_as_text`.

SPEC-24 is bumped to 0.33 with revision rows. Patch changeset added. Translator and bundle copy changed together; `harness update` refreshed the lock and hook hashes.

## Engineering choices (internal)
- The cap is 512, matching the translator's `MCP_MAX_ITEMS`; the overflow goes through `adapter_failure`.
- The git-root memory is a thread-local cleared at the start of each request.
- Two different content strings is treated as `partial` (the existing unplaceable path); identical duplicates stay a whole-file write.
- `status` reads only the adapter's settings file for the kill switch, as `session-start` does; `settings.local.json` is documented as not read.
- The commit trailer follows the session's attribution reminder (Sonnet 5.5).

## Re-pins (`fix --rebaseline --apply --by beauwilliams --actor agent`), for the reviewer to check

The pins went stale because this diff changed AGENTS.md, `.claude/settings.json` (only the translator sha256 in the three hook commands), the translator, `run.rs`, `mod.rs` and the hardening test file. Each record's revision row states the actual delta:

- settings.json and translator pins: MILE-178, MILE-191, MILE-202, MILE-204 (translator hash, cwd fallback, decoy content strings).
- run.rs and mod.rs pins: MILE-178, MILE-195, MILE-198, MILE-200.
- SPEC-24: run.rs, mod.rs, translator, harness_hardening_integration.rs.

author: tejhorwdev
body:
That line was the app's own bug, not a fact about your PC.

2.9.21 took the account session asynchronously at launch. The Appearance panel could read the workspace status *before* that finished — so it printed "not signed in" on a machine that was signed in, one tick away from being right. The publisher existed; the panel asked too early and then never asked again.

### 2.9.22

- The workspace session is read **synchronously out of the encrypted account store** on every status read, every publish, every reconcile. Status and publishing can no longer disagree.
- The panel asks the server once whether the row may be written, then re-reads twice before it is allowed to say "not signed in".
- A rotated token is refreshed in one place, so the app cannot sign you out of itself.
- If it still says no, it says which of the two it is: no account signed in at all, or the workspace was unreachable.

### Straight answer on your bigger point

Everything that *can* live on the server already is: accounts, projects, documents, presentations, the workspace row, the video, the portrait. The one thing that must remain on the PC is the offline workspace, which you asked for.

What was failing is narrower and worse: the console was writing to a row as an identity the server would not accept, or not writing at all, and said "saved" either way. That is a bug in the app, not a limit of the design — and 2.9.22 is the version where the panel tells you the truth instead of assuming it.

2.9.22.

author: anatolykoptev
body: ## What `WHISPER_COMMIT` 6e4ab85 (master, 2026-09-28) -> `d1be6fde11ac6e0407606b4e42fe72d34add8037`, the commit `v1.9.5` points at (checked with `git rev-parse v1.9.5^{commit}` on a clone). We pin the latest stable release, not master. For Parakeet the only change in the 142 commits is `60c0be6ac` (`whisper : add check for ttype in whisper and parakeet`, #4091): a malformed model file now fails at load. The rest is ggml syncs. ## Patches: one structural change, please review this part The ggml Metal backend moved a lot (new FWHT, mma/tg mat-vec kernels, a tensor-API flash-attention branch). `patches/ggml` is shared by whisper.cpp's vendored ggml and qwentts.cpp's older ggml, and no single hunk can serve both for the places upstream rewrote. Every patch still applies, but only after this: - **Shared `patches/ggml`** keeps the hunks that apply to both trees in the same function. Four hunks got less context (the lines both trees share): `device.h` mul_mm_tg declaration, `device.m` flash-attention `supports_op`, and two in `0002` (`device.h` props, `device.m` MPS init; whisper's `device_init` has no `supports_gpu_family_apple7` any more). Two hunks of `0001` moved out (below). - **`patches/ggml-qwentts/0001`**: the `use_vec` call site and the `get_tensor` copy-back, verbatim from the old patch. - **`patches/ggml-whisper/0001`**: the same two (the copy-back goes before the new `[buf_dst release]`), the `use_vec` call in the new tensor-API branch (`true`: that branch needs simdgroup matrix support, so behaviour is unchanged), and the `max_tg_mem` argument the new `use_fwht(op, max_tg_mem)` takes in the MPS helpers. - `build.sh`: `ggml_patches [tree]` appends `patches/ggml-` after the shared set; stamps include it. `git apply` tolerates offsets, so a clean apply is not proof of a correct placement: one hunk applied inside `ggml_metal_buffer_clear` and was only caught by the compiler. I audited the placement of every hunk by enclosing function against the old patches. **Oracle for qwentts (no behaviour change there):** on a clone of the pinned ggml (`40e16e4`), shared + `ggml-qwentts` gives a tree that is `diff -r`-identical to the tree the old single `patches/ggml` produced. The qwentts stamp changes, so its tree is rebuilt once. I did not rebuild `tts-server`. ## Regression (old pin vs new, same flags, one run at a time, `pmset -g therm` clean) Models: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 q8_0 and Silero v5.1.2, sha256-verified against `scripts/fetch-models.sh`. Audio: 20 min windows (10:00-30:00) of five public council/board meetings, 16 kHz mono, plus the first 10 min of a Russian recording. `ox-stt -m -f x.wav -o out.json`. | file | words | WER new vs old | old s | new s | |---|---|---|---|---| | Thornton CC (DZmkcF3FNjY) | 3208 | 0.000 % | 7.5 | 7.4 | | Rancho Mirage CC (O4FxJYzvAtk) | 3267 | 0.000 % | 7.5 | 7.2 | | Eugene CC (jjMNg6hdIU4) | 2997 | 0.000 % | 6.8 | 6.8 | | Sacramento BoS (_z2lWu-Rgkc) | 2967 | 0.000 % | 7.4 | 7.4 | | Long Beach BoE (zht4os6M9TQ) | 2727 | 0.000 % | 7.0 | 6.9 | | Russian 10 min | 1351 | 0.000 % | 3.8 | 3.8 | The JSON differs only in `elapsed_s` (text, segments and word timings equal). No slowdown: the new binary is equal or up to 4 % faster (the commit message says "within 3 %"; the Rancho Mirage run is 4 %). Engine checks: the four C++ unit tests from CI (segmenter, edge pad, redecode, wav reader), `scripts/test-engine-checks.sh`, `scripts/test-check-release-tag.sh`: pass. `scripts/test-stt-edges.sh` (model test): 0 failures on old and new. `samples/jfk.wav`: identical text on Metal and with `-ng` at the new pin (this is the README's whisper.cpp claim; the README pin reference is updated). ## Not established - The audio is not the original `~/tmp/ox-say-m1` set: `~/tmp/ox-say-m1` and the model copies in `~/tmp/ox-say-16gb-gate` were gone when this ran (the models there were symlinks into the app's support directory, which I did not read). I re-downloaded the pinned models and five of the same videos with my own windows. The old-vs-new comparison does not depend on the choice. - Apple Silicon only. The patched paths are inert there (AMD discrete, `!has_simdgroup_mm`); the new ggml has new mat-vec/mma and tensor-flash-attention routes whose interplay with `use_tg`/MPS/`use_vec` on an Intel Mac with an AMD GPU is untested. That needs a run on the Intel test Mac before a release that ships this pin to Intel. - `tts-server` was not rebuilt (qwentts tree is byte-identical to before). Tier: gate (engine pin, patch rebase, deploy path). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

author: danielmellen-university
body:
Fixes the clipped 6-var map in short browser windows (around 1024×500 with tab and bookmark bars), the stretched legend, and the nested sidebar scroll.

- Cell size is computed from the map container’s measured width and height with a ResizeObserver, including layer labels, headers, and gaps.
- The map is centered in its pane and stays fully visible. The page itself does not scroll on desktop.
- Legend rows are a fixed 38px. The sidebar is a single scroll for the answer, legend, and extras.
- Group colors are a 32-color max-min OKLab palette. The N groups in a solution get the N most distant colors, assigned with a stable per-term hash and a fresh seed each page load, so the first group is not always the same hue.

Local `node --test` is green (39/39). Overflow, in-viewport cell, and legend-height checks passed at 1024×500, 1024×576, 1280×650, 1366×657, 1536×730, and 1920×960 for 4-, 5-, and 6-var maps, with extras expanded, plus a 32-group 6-var checkerboard.

author: imizik
body:
## What Isaac gets

One dot at the left of the desk's buttons answers "is a quiet desk a quiet market or a dead feed?"

- **All fine:** a small green dot, nothing else (its name and tooltip say "All live").
- **Something behind:** the dot turns amber and names it ("Robinhood down", "2 sources behind").
- **Can't tell:** a grey dot ("Prices unknown", or "Health unknown" if the check itself failed). Unknown is never green.
- **Tap it:** each source with its state and last good time in plain words: Robinhood, Prices, Level 2, Chatter, TradingView, Fill emails, Radar, Copilot budget. Tap a source for one line on what it affects and the fix that already exists (Gmail's **Reconnect Gmail**; the Robinhood sign-in steps). No new fix flows.
- **Market closed / weekend:** prices, Radar and chatter say "closed", not stale. Level 2 says "Off · no Tape session open" (not an error). TradingView with no alert today is "quiet" (none may have fired), never green.
- **Phone:** the dot alone in the header; a tap opens the list.

| All live | Robinhood down | List, Robinhood tapped |
|---|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imizik/TradeJournal/pr-assets/desk-health/desktop-all-live.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imizik/TradeJournal/pr-assets/desk-health/desktop-amber.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imizik/TradeJournal/pr-assets/desk-health/desktop-list-robinhood.png) |

| Phone | Phone list |
|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imizik/TradeJournal/pr-assets/desk-health/phone-amber.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/imizik/TradeJournal/pr-assets/desk-health/phone-list.png) |

Screens are from the UX sandbox with the fixture desk (invented rows; the Gmail banner above is the sandbox's own missing Gmail token).

## How

- `GET /copilot/desk/health` (`backend/app/engine/desk_health.py`) is owner-only (`access_manifest.DOMAIN_ROUTES`), read-only, and **rides the desk's minute request**: it is added to `desk_minute.PATHS` / `deskMinute.BATCHED`. There is no poll of its own. The idle pin in `copilot-desk-load.spec.ts` is unchanged and passes. There is one extra read about 8 s after the desk opens or comes back into view, so a cold start never reads as "behind".
- Each source reads only what it already keeps:
  - **Robinhood:** the feed's cached snapshot and its order-history pass status.
  - **Prices:** the live ticks' last good and failed read (`desk_ticks.health`, memory only; Tradier single-flight and cap untouched).
  - **Chatter:** ApeWisdom's state file.
  - **TradingView:** the newest stored alert on a *followed* ticker (hidden tickers stay silent).
  - **Fill emails:** the existing `gmail_health`.
  - **Radar:** today's passes, store opened read-only.
  - **Copilot budget:** today's spend against `COPILOT_DAILY_BUDGET_USD`.
- **No provider call, no write.** A source that throws becomes "unknown".
- Thresholds live in one table, `STALE_AFTER`, with a comment each.
- **Robinhood boundary:**
  - `desk_health.py` never imports the feed; the desk router (already an allowed reader) hands it facts via `feed.snapshot(kick=False)`, which never starts a read.
  - Two pure accessors were added to `robinhood_book.Feed`: `last_read_at` and `reading`.
  - No change to `robinhood_read.py`, its allowlist or `test_robinhood_read.py`, and no new caller.
- **Level 2** comes from the Tape's own moomoo session in the browser (`reportLevel2` in `DeskTape.tsx`).
- Docs: `docs/copilot-lab.md` § Data health.

## Review

- **General (Opus) review.** Findings fixed:
  - False amber for up to a minute on a cold open or after unlocking the phone. Reads in flight or not yet asked are now "unknown", plus the one settle read.
  - Old green rows stayed visible after a failed check; they are now hidden.
  - Escape also closed the Feed drawer behind the list.
  - `aria-haspopup` was wrong.
  - The docs overstated how the Robinhood feed refreshes.
  - Chatter showed as on in the dot trial, where its reader never runs.
- **Focused Robinhood-boundary (Opus) review:** no change to Robinhood access, no new call or caller, no account data in the payload, nothing reaches the copilot. One docstring nit fixed.
- **Header jump found in testing:** the dot's words changing after load widened the top bar and shifted the chart (it broke `copilot-desk-draw`). The dot now shows words only when something is amber, so it never changes width while fine.

## Tests

- **Backend:** `tests/test_desk_health.py` (20). `test_robinhood_read.py`, `test_desk_minute.py` and `test_docs_links.py` pass unchanged.
- **e2e:**
  - New `copilot-desk-health.spec.ts` (7): all live, amber + fix paths, unknown, failed read, failed-after-good, rides the minute, phone.
  - Level 2 live/off assertions added to `copilot-desk-tape.spec.ts`.
  - Health stub added to the load spec.
  - Health, load, tape, draw, layout and phone specs pass (33).
- **Full copilot/desk e2e run:** 368/371 before the fixes.
  - `copilot-desk-option-standing` "What if…: folded by default…" **also fails on plain main** (its earnings button stays disabled), so it is not from this PR.
  - Its sibling "needs an IV" test failed once and passed on rerun.
- **Browser check:** the dot, list and Robinhood detail in the running sandbox at 1440 px and 390 px.

Not user-gated, in my reading: no Robinhood access change (per the boundary review), and a new owner-only read route with no auth/CI/deploy change.
