Markdown report for PR comments, a small GitHub API client that creates or updates the comment in place, and a composite GitHub Action (`action.yml`) that runs a suite on the PR's base commit and on the PR, compares them, comments, and fails the job on a gate. This repo's own CI now runs it on a tiny deterministic demo suite (FR-C3).

## What & why
- **`markdown` report format** (`agentlens.report.MarkdownRenderer`, `marker_comment`, `DEFAULT_MARKER`): verdict headline (✅/❌ always paired with words), metrics table (baseline, candidate, Δ, Δ%, 95% CI, status), gates table + notes, case regressions/improvements in collapsed `<details>`, footer with experiment names/ids/git shas and the bootstrap method. The first line is a hidden `<!-- agentlens-report -->` marker (configurable key). User text is escaped (tables/HTML can't break); case lists are capped at 50 rows.
- **`agentlens.integrations.github`**: `upsert_pr_comment(body, *, context, marker, client=None)` lists the PR's comments via REST (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/comments`, following `Link` pagination), PATCHes the one with the marker (skips when the body is identical), else POSTs. `GitHubContext.from_env()` reads `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, `GITHUB_API_URL`. The token never appears in errors or `repr`. Errors on 401/403/404 include a hint about `pull-requests: write` and fork tokens.
- **CLI**: `agentlens github comment --file report.md [--marker --pr --repo]`. `run --json PATH|-` writes the experiment report with its gate verdict, so a run without a baseline renders with its gates. `report --format markdown --marker KEY`.
- **`action.yml`** (composite): setup-uv → venv with AgentLens (the action's own source by default, or `agentlens-version` from PyPI) + `install` args → **baseline**: by default the PR base sha is checked out in a temporary `git worktree` and the suite runs there → candidate run → `compare --gates --json` → Markdown (also to the step summary) → PR comment (a warning if it fails, e.g. fork PRs) → exit with the gate code. If the suite doesn't exist at the base commit (new suite), or with `baseline-ref: ""` and no database, only the absolute gates are checked. Outputs: `passed`, `exit-code`, `report-path`, `json-path`, `baseline-experiment`, `candidate-experiment`.
- **Baseline strategy (ADR 0006)**: re-running the base commit in the same job is always comparable and needs no stored state. The cost is running the suite twice. The stored-baseline route (`--set-baseline` on main + `actions/cache`, `baseline-ref: ""`) is supported and documented with its trade-offs.
- **Demo**: `examples/ci_demo` (MockLLM FAQ agent, 12 cases, gates on pass rate, pass-rate delta, case regressions and steps; latency is measured, so it isn't gated) and `.github/workflows/agentlens.yml` (`pull_request`, `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `uses: ./`). On this PR the suite doesn't exist on `main` yet, so expect the no-baseline report (absolute gates only). From the next PR on it compares against the base commit. #30 switches it to the real demo agent.

No new dependencies (`httpx` was already a runtime dependency, `respx` a dev one).

## How to review
1. `src/agentlens/report/markdown.py` and `tests/report/snapshots/comparison.md` (what the comment looks like)
2. `src/agentlens/integrations/github.py` and `tests/integrations/test_github.py`
3. `action.yml`, then `.github/workflows/agentlens.yml` and `examples/ci_demo/`
4. `src/agentlens/cli/github.py` plus the `run --json` / `report --marker` changes in `cli/app.py`
5. `docs/adr/0006-ci-baseline.md`, README "GitHub Action", design §8 notes

## What you can learn here
- **Composite actions**: an `action.yml` with `runs.using: composite` bundles shell steps and other actions. Inputs arrive as `${{ inputs.x }}` and are passed through `env:` instead of being interpolated into scripts (no shell injection). Outputs are mapped from a step's `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- **Updating a bot comment in place**: a hidden HTML comment marker and a list → PATCH/POST upsert keep one comment per PR instead of one per push.
- **`git worktree`** checks out a second commit next to the first, without touching the working copy. That's how the baseline runs in the same job.
- **Snapshot tests for text output** plus respx for HTTP make the integration testable without network.

## Test evidence
- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy src && uv run pytest` → 1665 passed, 2 skipped (live), **100% coverage**
- The action's main script was run locally against throwaway git repos in three modes:
  - baseline at the base commit: a broken FAQ answer gives `exit-code=1`, `passed=false`, and the report shows the case regression;
  - suite missing at the base: absolute gates only, `passed=true`;
  - `baseline-ref: ""`: no db falls back to no baseline, an existing experiment is compared, and an unmarked baseline exits 2.
- `tests/examples/test_ci_demo.py` checks that the demo passes its gates and that the action's inputs, outputs and the workflow are wired consistently.

Closes #27

author: christophesamueldhp
body:
## Summary

On the phone, the mascot acts out what its session does, and can face left and right.

```text
mascotState(session, live, online)            daemon/remote/web/mascot.js
  Mac out of reach, pane gone, silent, stopped  -> asleep   (grey, eyes shut, z's)
  needs                                         -> needs    (waves, "!")
  working
    a tool of the reply in progress runs        -> tool     (turned right, hammers)
    the reply in progress has text              -> writing  (types, reads along)
    else                                        -> thinking (paces left and right)
  done / failed                                 -> done (hops) / failed (droops)
  else                                          -> idle     (blinks, looks left and right)
```

Each state is a class on one SVG; `style.css` moves its parts by whole grid pixels in steps. The turned views are the same parts with the front narrowed and a shaded side, always on four legs; facing right is facing left, mirrored.

```diff
 Chat
   <header>
     back
+    #avatar            mascot in mascotState(...)
-    #title             name
+    #title             name, and the session's state under it
   #log
     #msgs / #live / #pending
-    #working           "✻ Working…", until the reply shows something
+    #working           mascot + "Thinking…" | "Writing…" | "Running bash…" + turn timer, all turn long
   #float               status pill
-    "Working for 3m"   always
+    "Working for 3m"   only when scrolled away from the log's end
-  composer             attach · textarea · send
+  composer             one rounded card around the three
 List
   <header>
+    #avatar            fleetState: asleep off the Mac, waves if any needs, thinks if any works
   rows                 unchanged: agent view's glyphs
 Loader, empty states, pairing: the mascot (looking about / idle / waving)
```

Also, from T3 Code (MIT): a hairline after each ended turn, a glass status pill, buttons that give when pressed, bordered code blocks, a tail corner on the user's bubble.

The working line no longer shows the session's `detail`: until a tool runs it is the previous answer's last line.

`daemon/remote/web/mascot.svg` (the raster copy the pairing screen drew) is removed with its test; `ext/branding/mascot.svg` stays the source, and `GRID` is still tested against it.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `✻ Working…` in the log and `Working for 37s` in the pill at once; a static mascot only on the loader and pairing.
  **After:** a streamed reply in `scripts/remote-web-dev.ts` (`touch <dir>/reply`), header mascot and working line read from the page:

  ```text
  idle     |                | rebuilds 0
  writing  | Writing…       | rebuilds 1
  tool     | Running bash…  | rebuilds 2
  thinking | Thinking…      | rebuilds 3
  idle     |                | rebuilds 4
  ```

  The working line is rebuilt once per change of state, not per streamed chunk, so the mascot keeps moving.
- `test/remote-web-mascot.test.ts` (new, 9 tests): the state mapping, which views each state turns between, four legs in every view, every animation name defined, and no mascot motion outside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` but the loader's.
- With reduced motion emulated, a working Chat runs 0 animations. No horizontal overflow at 320 px. Send and attach are drawn 40 px and tapped as 44.
- `npm run check` passes in the pre-push hook on this commit.
- Checked in Chromium (light and dark) only. **Not checked on iOS Safari**, the real target.

To see it: `node scripts/remote-web-dev.ts`, pair, then `touch <dir>/busy` (Gamma thinks) or `touch <dir>/reply` (Alpha writes, then runs a tool).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Only the phone's web app, its dev script and tests change; no daemon, protocol or stored data. Reverting the commit restores everything, the raster included.

**Blast Radius:** phone

The app's shell version goes to 0.0.59, so phones fetch the new build on their next open. A WebKit-only rendering fault in the SVG animations would show on every screen that has the mascot.

## Summary

RV-05 (Specialized Kernels and Memory Layouts) worked through Gate 4, plus the S1 MTP reference audit it depended on. Gate 4 outcome: **NO-GO** for an optimized-path claim, confirmed by the maintainer. Split-K attention is kept as the default internal improvement.

## Changes

body:
## Summary
While verifying that admin access actually works end-to-end (requested after the last PR), found that it didn't: `PasscodeGate` is a shared component but was hardcoded to the site-wide `PASSCODE`/`isUnlocked`/`setUnlocked` — so the admin gate in the controls panel never checked `ADMIN_PASSCODE` at all.

Concretely, two real symptoms:
- Typing the documented admin code `4242` into the admin gate always failed ("Code incorrect"), since it was compared against `1234`.
- Once the site-wide code is already unlocked (the normal case for anyone using the panel), the admin gate's internal `unlocked` state was *also* already true on mount, so it rendered its `{null}` children immediately — no code prompt ever appeared, and admin mode could never actually be turned on through the UI.

`PasscodeGate` now takes optional `passcode` / `checkUnlocked` / `persistUnlocked` props, defaulting to the previous site-wide behavior. Only the admin gate (`src/ControlsPanel.tsx`) passes the admin-specific overrides (`ADMIN_PASSCODE`, `isAdminUnlocked`, `setAdminUnlocked`); the other three gates (leaderboard, chutes, field-report page) are untouched.

Confirmed the Firestore rules side needs no change — `woundedDeer`/`warnings` delete/update rules are already permissive by design (the "reporter or admin" restriction is UI-only, documented in `firestore.rules`), so once the UI correctly shows the admin controls, the backend already accepts those writes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` succeeds
- [x] Traced the admin-unlock flow end-to-end in code: `ControlsPanel` → `PasscodeGate` (now admin-scoped) → `onAdminUnlock` → `App.tsx`'s `adminUnlocked` state → gates the Supprimer/edit buttons on others' deer/warning reports

author: chrisnourse
body:
## Change

The Thread tool puts a thread on the cylindrical face at a picked point. This fixes a thread that goes on the wrong part. Fixes #16668.

Two components built alike each have a cylinder at the same place in their own coordinates: two studs, or two standard screws of one size. A thread made in the second component was cut into the first component's body, and the second component stayed plain. A cosmetic thread was recorded on the first body in the same way.

The search for the face ran over every body and kept the nearest, and the first of equal candidates won. A Thread feature now prefers a face on a body of its own component when that component has one at the point. With no such face, the search is as before, so a thread on another component's body still works.

Changes a default: no

## Validation

- New test `a_thread_goes_on_a_body_of_its_own_component` in `crates/engine/src/thread_tests.rs`: two components, each with a Ø8 x 20 cylinder at its origin, and a thread made in the second.
  - Modelled M8x1.25: the first body keeps the plain volume π·4²·20 = 1005.3 mm³ within 0.5 mm³, and the second loses more than 20 mm³.
  - Cosmetic: `model.threads` has one thread, on the second component's body.
- The released 0.41.0 fails both: the reproduction scripts in #16668 show the thread on the first body.
- `cargo test --profile ci --lib -p solidcraft-engine -- thread_tests cmd::parts`: 77 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test --profile ci --lib -p solidcraft-doc -- thread`: 23 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --profile ci -p solidcraft-doc -p solidcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask mesh-decisions`: pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` on Windows 11, run on a larger local branch that holds this same change: the format, assets, icons, licences, lists, skills and layers gates pass. The run then stops in the shared-crates gate: the `solidcraft-viewport-gpu` tests end with an access violation on this machine's GPU. This change does not touch that crate or anything it depends on. I ran the later gates one by one, as listed above.

## Screenshots of the behavior (when observable)

`solidcraft-cli snapshot` of the first script in #16668. Stud B is the active component when the thread is made.

![Before: the thread is on Stud A. After: the thread is on Stud B.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChrisNourse/solidcraft/refs/heads/evidence/insert-part-fasteners/thread-wrong-component.png)

## Integration status

Branched from `main` at 22aa00d00 on 2026-11-14. No conflicts. Open PRs #13325, #13359 and #14862 also change `crates/doc/src/eval_thread.rs`; this change is 16 lines in `thread_on` and the one call to it in `eval`.

author: voyager163
body:
Closes #63.

## Problem

For a Go part, `tests.coverage-gate` was compliant whenever `tools/coverage/main.go` existed, even as an empty file. Every other gate was reported as unknown, so an adopted Go project that gated coverage its own way never got a clean assessment.

## What changes

A Go module's coverage now counts as gated when one of these is found:

- **A workflow step runs Liftoff's tool with a threshold:** `go run ./tools/coverage <profile> <percent>` with a percentage above 0. The step must run in the module, either from its own or its job's `working-directory`, or through the tool's path, as in `go run ./backend/tools/coverage …`.
- **A workflow uses the go-test-coverage action** with `threshold-file`, `threshold-package` or `threshold-total` above 0.
- **A `.testcoverage.yml` or `.testcoverage.yaml`** (go-test-coverage's configuration) with a threshold above 0, in the module or at the repository root. Assess now reads these files as declarations (ASSESS-001).

The tool's file name alone no longer counts. A gate kept anywhere else, such as a Makefile, is still reported as unknown, because it can't be read statically. The next action now names the conventions that assess does read.

Liftoff's own Go projects still assess as fully compliant: their CI runs `go run ./tools/coverage cover.out 80` in the backend.

## Requirements and tests

- ASSESS-001 adds `.testcoverage.yml` to the files assess reads. ASSESS-003 says where a Go gate is found.
- Tests cover:
  - a working directory, a path prefix and a different module;
  - a zero threshold;
  - the action with and without a threshold;
  - the config file in the module and at the root, with no threshold, and invalid.

## Checks

`npm run check` passes: 1,450 tests.

author: fagenorn
body:
## Why

Adding an account today takes a terminal: claude-account add creates the account profile and a later launch signs it in. The owner wants to add an account from the console page and never from a terminal. This is step 3 of the resolution of issue 842 (accounts on the page).

## What changes

- The page gets an Add account action. The owner types a name; the page and the console accept only the launcher account-name rule (lowercase letters, digits, dash and underscore, not default) and refuse an existing name as a 409 with the reason shown.
- The console creates the profile through the launcher own add, so there is one implementation: mode 0700, each shared entry linked to its ~/.claude/<entry> path, and a login-less .claude.json copy (ADR-hosts-005).
- The add is a page write through the one guarded write path (console origin plus install token, ADR-console-008) and appends one owner-action row naming the profile.
- After an add the page goes straight into the sign-in for the new profile and shows its sign-in link. A profile whose sign-in was not finished stays, shows as signed out and offers Sign in again.
- The view lists page-added accounts and the host capacity check reads them (the page-add mode of the verify-pending check).
- ADR-console-025 records the add route, and the Hosts glossary entry for Account profile says the console creates profiles through the launcher.

## Acceptance

| id | criterion | kind | shown by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1 | Adding a valid new name creates the profile with every shared entry linked to its ~/.claude/<entry> path, a login-less .claude.json and mode 0700, the same result as the launcher own creation | code | tests/test_console_account_add.py compares the console-created profile with one the launcher add creates, under a temporary home |
| AC2 | An invalid name, default or an existing name is refused as a 409 with the reason and creates nothing | code | tests/test_console_account_service.py |
| AC3 | The add route is refused without the console origin or the install token, and an accepted add appends one owner-action row naming the profile | code | tests/test_console_writes.py write-guard tests |
| AC4 | After an add the page shows the new profile sign-in link from the sign-in action | code | tests/test_console_page.py and the service tests with a fake client |
| AC5 | On anis-desktop, after the owner just switch, a profile added from the page exists with its shared links and, once signed in, has a sign-in state other than unknown | evidence | verify block: home/common/verify-pending/checks/console-capacity-reading with --page-add on host anis-desktop, once the deployed config includes 65a954821e11a1ff72a2f1358223a04bf6e3f5b8, expires 7 days after merge |
| AC6 | On a macOS host Add account works the same | note | held as a criterion on issue 894, since the darwin configurations cannot be evaluated on the Linux host; this issue places no hold for it |

## Evidence

Verification: nix-build, pass. just build completed; new configuration built successfully.
5 tasks reviewed.
Accepted head: 5216b712a23b724587f55f1cccfadf95606dad90

## Merge danger

The change is confined to the console package, its page, its tests, docs and one verify-pending check. It does not touch the launcher, the lifecycle guard or host activation. The darwin configurations are not evaluated here, and AC5 is verified on anis-desktop only after the owner runs just switch.

Refs #1027

author: shuymn
body:
## What

Two changes to `.github/renovate.json`:

- wrangler, miniflare, `@cloudflare/vitest-plugin` and `@cloudflare/workers-types` get their own "cloudflare workers" group, so they no longer ride in "non-major dependencies".
- A Node.js major update (setup-node's `node-version` and `@types/node`, matched by dep name) gets a note in the PR body. It asks for `node` in `mise.toml`, `mise.lock` and the Node.js version named in `packages/kopje/RELEASING.md` to move too.

## Why

- These packages bring in workerd, the runtime the Store's SQL runs on. In #1444, a workerd release whose SQLite refused Kopje's notification statements failed the tests and held back every unrelated patch in the same group.
- Renovate's mise manager is disabled: `mise-update.yml` advances the major ranges. So #1318 (Node 26) changed only the workflows and `@types/node` and left `mise.toml` on 24.

## Verification

- `renovate-config-validator --strict` passes.
- A Codex review checked:
  - The new group comes after both general groups, so it takes precedence for minor, patch and pre-1.0 updates.
  - Majors stay separate (`separateMajorMinor`).

author: archaiosmagister
body:
## Piloto reproducible de verificación lexicográfica individual de Latín II — no publicar todavía

**Resultados reales de GitHub Actions, SHA 195c78455685:**
- 22.049 pares de análisis individualizados a partir de 720 fichas del banco general (Latín II).
- 976.489 filas UniMorph Latin, SHA congelado `050924c9f013e6aba4d7c87be243a1d79b6c5b10`; 0 filas descartadas. Corpus procedente de Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 3.0.
- 12.934 coincidencias de lema y forma (contando análisis distintos de un mismo homógrafo). 4.304 análisis con coincidencias morfológicas parciales; 166 discrepancias de rasgos para comprobar; 7.307 expresiones compuestas pendientes de analizador específico.
- 9.676 análisis de lemas ausentes del corpus y 596 formas no halladas en un lema presente: **la ausencia de UniMorph NO demuestra error del banco**.
- 106 entradas de prioridad P0 (grafías PAU y cuaderno), 1.056 P1 (en uno de ambos), 20.887 P2 (resto).
- **Una sola fuente independiente** hasta integrar y comprobar una exportación real de LEMLAT3/Collatinus; la copia UniMorph de Vocabula no cuenta como fuente adicional.
- **277 pruebas de Node + 107 del núcleo, 0 fallos**; superadas navegación Chromium, PWA sin conexión, enlaces y seguridad AAL2. GitHub Pages **no desplegado** porque no hay merge a main.
- Informes docentes privados: `resumen.json`, `evidencias.ndjson`, `revision-prioritaria.tsv`, artefacto `latin2-verificacion-lexicografica-fase1` de la [ejecución](https://github.com/ArchaiosMagister/ScholaClassica/actions/runs/43590844422), retención 30 días, **fuera de dist y GitHub Pages**.

### Qué hace
- Identidad de `lema + forma + análisis + registro`, comparación conservadora de rasgos morfológicos, generación de evidencias y prioridades de auditoría.
- Corpus completo congelado y recuperado en CI sin modificar los repositorios originales.
- Posibilidad de incorporar una segunda fuente independiente con `source, revision, reference, nativeFeatures, tagset, lemma, form, features`, una vez generado y contrastado su archivo real.
- Nunca modifica ni certifica automáticamente una flexión: las etiquetas de cotejo no equivalen a testimonio textual.
- Comprueba que se usa el corpus completo (>900.000 registros válidos) y que no se generan informes en `public/` ni en `dist/`.

### Próxima fase
Integración efectiva de LEMLAT3/Collatinus con concordancia comprobada de etiquetas y prioridad a los 1.162 análisis procedentes de PAU o cuaderno. Los 166 casos de rasgos discrepantes no se consideran errores académicos hasta su cotejo.

**Estado:** PR en borrador, lista para revisión técnica del piloto. No fusionar ni publicar sin decisión de integrar esta funcionalidad en el flujo principal.
---

## Segunda fase incorporada (14/11/2026): LEMLAT 3.0 REAL

**Actualización posterior al piloto de una sola fuente descrito arriba.** Se ha incorporado la herramienta oficial de LEMLAT3 (`CIRCSE/LEMLAT3`, revisión fija `e8328948fb4b9b73b625aeda3639137c5e49a1ff`, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) y ejecutado el cotejo real como *workflow independiente de auditoría*, sin fusionar ni desplegar ScholaClassica.

- CI de dos fuentes **verde**: https://github.com/ArchaiosMagister/ScholaClassica/actions/runs/43593474252
- En el lote P0/P1: 1.162 análisis (463 grafías simples; 28 análisis compuestos reservados). LEMLAT analiza 461/463 grafías, 693 análisis nativos, 2.097 filas de evidencia; no analiza `duos` ni `segestae`.
- **Solo análisis prioritarios:** 481 acuerdos entre fuentes (sin atribuir atestiguación textual), 589 coincidencias parciales, **4 discrepancias** de rasgos pendientes, 53 lemas sin cobertura, 7 formas no halladas en lema conocido, 28 compuestos.
- 4 discrepancias para cotejo filológico individual: `segestae` nom./voc. pl. del topónimo Segesta; `nonnullae` gen./dat. sg. fem. de nonnullus. **Ninguna se considera automáticamente errata.**
- En 22.049 análisis totales, 481 acuerdos y 153 discrepancias restantes; el segundo corpus solo se consulta para grafías simples de PAU/cuaderno, **no** para las 7.307 expresiones compuestas.
- Pruebas específicas: 9/9; ejecución reproducible y artefactos docentes aislados de Pages; no se modifican respuestas, sorteo, bancos originales o estados individuales de verificación.

Detalles técnicos y reserva docente: [documentación fase 2](docs/VERIFICACION_LEXICOGRAFICA_LATIN2_FASE2.md).

**Estado:** mantener esta PR en borrador. No fusionar ni publicar todavía.
---

## Fase 3 — cierre estructural de 7.307 perífrasis (14/11/2026)

- **Revisión editorial persistente y no destructiva**: las dos lecturas de `nonnullae` (genitivo y dativo singular femenino) son regulares; las dos lecturas plurales de `Segestae` siguen reservadas por falta de evidencia onomástica de uso. El informe conserva la discrepancia documental y añade la conclusión editorial; no cambia el sorteo.
- **Compuestos**: 7.080 análisis verbales personales + 227 infinitivos. 7.249 estructuras compatibles con el paradigma, 54 variantes documentadas `adgressus/aggressus`, 1 `futurum esse` irregular y **3 reservas reales** de la presentación de `utor`: `usurus esse`, `usuri esse`, `usurae esse`. No se han modificado las casillas.
- LEMLAT analiza componentes de los compuestos además de formas prioritarias: **957 consultas, 955 analizadas**, 7.564 filas de evidencia; las dos ausencias siguen siendo `duos` y `segestae`.
- **5.463** compuestos con evidencia de ambos componentes, **1.844** con evidencia parcial y ninguno sin evidencia de componentes; esto NO acredita el uso textual de ninguna expresión completa.
- Auditorías docentes `compuestos-resumen.json`, `compuestos-evidencias.ndjson` y `compuestos-reservas.tsv`, aisladas de `dist/`. **Sin certificaciones individuales ni cambios de banco**.
- [Documentación completa de la fase 3](docs/VERIFICACION_LEXICOGRAFICA_LATIN2_FASE3.md).
- [Última ejecución validada de análisis de compuestos](https://github.com/ArchaiosMagister/ScholaClassica/actions/runs/43595555441).

**Mantener abierta y en borrador; no publicar ni fusionar.**

---

## Fase 4 — cierre de reservas de `utor` y revisión de integración (14/11/2026)

**Resultados sobre el commit `f06e0fbc3f6d`:**
- `usurus esse`, `usuri esse` y `usurae esse` se aceptan como **citas morfológicas de paradigma** (participio futuro en nominativo), NO como ejemplos ya validados de acusativo con infinitivo. Las tres decisiones están persistidas y respaldadas por pruebas; no se ha modificado el banco docente ni la PWA.
- Las **7.307** perífrasis quedan clasificadas: 7.249 compatibles con paradigma, 54 variantes documentadas, 1 excepción `futurum esse` y 3 citas paradigmáticas de `utor`. **0 reservas estructurales abiertas; 0 certificaciones individuales; 0 testimonios textuales atribuidos.**
- El límite de ocho ejemplos por fuente afecta solo a la **presentación**. La clasificación coteja todos los análisis únicos y preserva una muestra relevante para explicar los acuerdos. En el banco completo se obtienen **495 acuerdos**, 4.693 coincidencias parciales y 152 discrepancias técnicas pendientes; entre las 1.162 fichas prioritarias, **487 acuerdos** y cuatro discrepancias documentales con decisión editorial anexa.
- Se comprueba también que un archivo de segunda fuente vacío, mezclado o de revisión inconsistente no pueda contabilizarse falsamente como independiente.
- [Cotejo UniMorph + LEMLAT3](https://github.com/ArchaiosMagister/ScholaClassica/actions/runs/43598815939): verde, 22 pruebas específicas.
- [Validación general](https://github.com/ArchaiosMagister/ScholaClassica/actions/runs/43598815950): verde, **293 pruebas del proyecto y 107 del núcleo**, 0 errores, navegador/PWA/área docente superados.
- GitHub informa que la PR es **mergeable**; continúa en **borrador**, sin integrar ni publicar. **Fusionarla en `main` iniciaría la publicación ordinaria por GitHub Pages**. Requiere decisión expresa de publicación.

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Type | Update | Change | |---|---|---|---| | [hugo](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo) | uses-with | minor | `0.169.0` → `0.170.0` | --- ### Release Notes
gohugoio/hugo (hugo) ### [`v0.170.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/tag/v0.170.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/compare/v0.169.0...v0.170.0) The big change in this release is that **the *extended* edition of Hugo is gone**. LibSass has been deprecated for a long time, and it was the only remaining reason we needed a CGO-enabled extended build. There is now only one Hugo binary, and apart from LibSass it has all the features the extended build had. ##### Notes - Setting `transpiler` to `libsass` in [`css.Sass`](https://gohugo.io/functions/css/sass/) now returns an error. [Dart Sass](https://gohugo.io/functions/css/sass/#dart-sass) is now the default and the only transpiler, so you need to [install it](https://gohugo.io/functions/css/sass/#installation-overview) if you use Sass. - We no longer publish `hugo_extended_*` archives. To avoid breaking existing CI setups, we publish aliases for the most downloaded extended archives (e.g. `hugo_extended__linux-amd64.tar.gz`, `hugo_extended__Linux-64bit.tar.gz`, the `linux-amd64.deb`, `linux-arm64.tar.gz` and `windows-amd64.zip`), but you should update your scripts to use the standard archives. The `extended_withdeploy` builds are also removed. See [Installation](https://gohugo.io/installation/). - [`hugo.IsExtended`](https://gohugo.io/functions/hugo/isextended/) now always returns `false`, and the module config setting `hugoVersion.extended` is deprecated and has no effect. - Command-line flags (e.g. `--buildDrafts`) now override OS [environment variables](https://gohugo.io/configuration/introduction/#environment-variables) (e.g. `HUGO_BUILDDRAFTS`). This also fixes `HUGO_ENVIRONMENT=qa hugo build -e staging` loading the `staging` config but reporting `qa` in `hugo.Environment`. - [`strings.Truncate`](https://gohugo.io/functions/strings/truncate/) has been rewritten on top of a proper HTML scanner. It now handles comments, void elements, quoted attributes with `>` and raw text elements such as `script` correctly, and it's faster and allocates less. On a curious note, the old version was implemented by [Mathias Biilmann](https://redirect.github.com/biilmann), the Netlify CEO. - `time.Time` values now keep their named time zone, and [`eq`](https://gohugo.io/functions/compare/eq/), `ne`, `in` and `uniq` compare `time.Time` values by instant. - [`resources.Match`](https://gohugo.io/functions/resources/match/) and friends now preserve the directory casing in the matched paths, so e.g. `resources.Match "gallery/Travel/Iceland/*"` now works on case-sensitive file systems. - Syncing of static files is much faster for big unchanged files, as we now skip the content check for files with the same size and modification time. - Several fixes and hardening of the WASM based image codecs (AVIF crash at `encoderSpeed` 6 and lower, recovering from broken WASM instances in the server). ##### Security ##### Hugo - [Passthrough](https://gohugo.io/configuration/markup/#passthrough) content is now HTML escaped when no passthrough render hook is set, unless `markup.goldmark.renderer.unsafe` is enabled. Before this, e.g. `\(\)` in a content file emitted raw HTML. - The `wrapperClass` option, settable from the [`highlight`](https://gohugo.io/shortcodes/highlight/) shortcode and [`transform.Highlight`](https://gohugo.io/functions/transform/highlight/), is now escaped. - [Vendored](https://gohugo.io/hugo-modules/use-modules/#vendor) module paths are now restricted to the `_vendor` directory (symlinks pointing outside are rejected). Thanks to [@​R0X4R](https://redirect.github.com/R0X4R) for finding and reporting the last two issues. ##### Go This release is built with Go 1.27.4, which [includes 12 security fixes](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM/m/KsU1KfWgAQAJ). The one most relevant for Hugo is a crash in the `net/http` HTTP/1 server (used by `hugo server`) caused by a race in `MaxBytesReader`. The other 11 are in the `cmd/go` toolchain (cgo flag and linker injection at build time) and mainly matter if you build Hugo from source with untrusted dependencies. ##### Dependencies - `golang.org/x/net` v0.62.0 [fixes two issues in the `html` package](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q4/407): quadratic complexity when coalescing text nodes, and a namespace issue when rendering raw text. Hugo uses this package when collecting HTML elements for `hugo_stats.json` and in the AsciiDoc integration. - `github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4` v4.1.6 (indirect dependency) contains a number of [security fixes](https://redirect.github.com/go-jose/go-jose/releases), among them GHSA-mgcc-cww5-fp2q (RSA modulus size limit when parsing JWKs) and a stack depth limit in the JSON decoder. ##### Changes - Remove libsass and the extended build tag [`c2f9cb8`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/c2f9cb82) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15405](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15405) - _Requested by **Ali** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JwbQWJW6stPfLkPzEYCCbg?thread=cmsg_01JwbQWJW6stPfLkPzEYCCbg94viHEpfRmsnkza7qRdFSM)_

Part of #35 (tracker #22): the Android counterpart of the public mission catalogue (#106). Does not close #35.

## What changes

**Meer missies (new screen, linked from Home)**
- The app goes online only when the student taps **Downloaden**: one plain `GET https://breinhap.com/p/missies.json`, `credentials: "omit"`, only an `Accept` header, 20 s timeout. No account, cookie, device id or answers.
- The answer is kept on the device as text and validated again at every start, so the missions work offline afterwards. A copy that no longer fits is dropped. **Gedownloade missies wissen** removes it.
- A list of the downloaded objects with jaar (defaults to the student's year) and vak filters, then an object page (leerdoel, one Start per mission). Missions play in the existing mission screen: Opwarmen → Leren → Doen → Check, pause/resume, Klopt./Nog niet.
- Calm messages for offline, server unavailable, a download made for a newer app, and a failed save. The copy already on the device is kept when a download fails.

**Home**
- Downloaded missions join the bundled samples in the vak + "Ik heb __ minuten" picker (`pickMission`, unchanged and deterministic).
- The bundled samples still ship in the app and work with no download at all.

**@breinhap/content**
- `parsePublicCatalogue`: validates each object on its own against the current `LearningObject` schema (without `review`), and skips and counts anything that does not fit, such as a newer schema, bad data or a duplicate id. A bad object is never a crash. Authoring fields such as `sources` are stripped. Public objects count as reviewed on their publication day, because the management site publishes only reviewed releases.
- `mergeContent`: a published release of a bundled object replaces it. A downloaded object that reuses another object's mission id is left out, so a paused mission can never resume inside different content.

**Safety of paused progress**
- Checkpoint cleanup and the mission screen wait until the downloaded copy has been read. Otherwise the cleanup that runs at start would wipe paused progress for downloaded missions.

**Privacy text**
- Privacy policy (nl/en) gets a "Meer missies downloaden" section, and the About screen mentions the download. `POLICY_UPDATED` is now 2026-11-14.

**Versions:** mobile 0.1.1 → 0.1.2 (app.json 1.0.0 → 1.0.1), content 0.1.1 → 0.1.2, site 0.1.4 → 0.1.5.

## Depends on
- The JSON endpoint is in #108, which is stacked on #106. Until #106 and #108 are merged and the operator's `breinhap.com/p/*` edge route is on, a download shows "breinhap.com geeft de missies nu niet" and everything else works as before. `EXPO_PUBLIC_CATALOGUE_URL` (https only) can point a build at a test server.

## Not in this PR
- Student sign-in, assigned content and progress sync (ADR 0003, #36).
- Opening M6 practice links in the app. Those runs are recorded server-side for the adult and belong to the web player.
- The Play Console Data safety form likely stays "no data collected" (the request carries no user data), but Ali should confirm it. The matching asafarim-docs note isn't in this repo.

- `packages/content`: 43/43 (new `catalogue.test.ts`: reviewed mapping and stripping, skips, envelope refusals, size cap, merge and replace, mission id clash).
- `apps/mobile`: 36/36 (new `tests/catalogue.test.mjs`: no network until download, plain GET without credentials, offline reuse, failure keeps the old copy, timeout, dropped corrupt or outdated copy, failed save).
- `apps/site`: 11/11. Typecheck ok. `expo export --platform android` bundles.

body:
## What and why

The staging `-mutate` kit run against TrueNAS 25.10.7 (14 Nov) failed `limit-combine`: `home_quota` held nil.

**Root cause (kit).** The kit's account got no home folder. By deduction, no `home_root` is chosen on staging: the create succeeded, and TrueNAS refuses any create that carries a home (see below). With no home there is no user quota to read, so `homeLimits` leaves `home_quota` out of `state`. AUTHORING says that means "not known", never "no limit". The add-on was right. The kit judged it as a FAIL in `limit-combine` and as a PASS in `limit-empty`, on reads that saw no limit. Both checks now skip a limit that `state` leaves out and name it. When no limit was read, the check is a skip (`check.unjudged`).

**Found beside it (add-on, the fake hid it).** With `home_create`, TrueNAS takes `home` as the **parent**. It refuses that path unless it is already a folder, then makes `<home>/<username>` itself. Sources: middlewared `plugins/account.py`, TS-25.04.2 and TS-25.10.7 (`validate_homedir_path`, `setup_homedir`, `do_update`). The add-on sent `<place>/<name>`. So on the real NAS every home it tried to make was refused, and an existing folder would have been nested one level down. `homeFields` now sends the place. The fake (`mutatingRPC.homeFor`, `folders`) now does what TrueNAS does: it refuses a missing parent and joins the username.

## Tests
- `TestTheKitSkipsALimitThisAddOnDoesNotReport`: the staging run reproduced, with no home root chosen. Before the fix it reported exactly staging's FAIL, and `limit-empty` passed.
- `TestTheConformanceKitPassesThisAddOn`: against the faithful fake, the old `homeFields` gets 502 APPLY_FAILED on create.
- `TestARoleMakesAPrivateHomeFolder`: sends the place, and the account reads back at `<place>/charlotte`.
- Mutation checks: each `unjudged` call removed, and `homeFields` reverted. Every one goes red.

author: thoenissen
body:
## Summary

- **RH8301, RH8302, RH8303:** a `///` comment written behind code (`int A; /// <summary>…`) is judged as if it started its own line. RH8303 reports it on its first `///`, and its fix moves the whole comment onto its own line above the declaration, with one empty line in front of it.
- **RH8401, RH8402:** both rules now report in `DocumentationMode.None` exactly as in `Parse`.
- **RH8307:** only top-level elements of a `///` comment are reported (`<summary>`, `<param>`, `<remarks>`, …). Nested elements such as `<para>` or `<b>` and `/** */` comments are no longer reported, and the rule page says so.
- **RH8302:** a blank line directly followed by an active `#region` or `#endregion` is no longer reported, so its fix no longer undoes RH5031's.
- **RH8106, RH8203, RH8305, RH8306:** every element or event of its kind is checked, whatever its position. RH8106 and RH8306 report one diagnostic per reported element; a partial property is still reported once by RH8306.
- **RH8032:** an unnamed extension receiver (`extension(long)`) is no longer reported, which removes a diagnostic without a source location.
- **RH8201, RH8203:** each part of a partial method, property, indexer or event is judged by its own documentation, while whether the member inherits documentation is decided for the member as a whole. As a result:
  - an implementing part counts as implementing the interface member;
  - RH8203 reads only a part's own comments, its later comments and `<include>` content included;
  - RH8201's fix replaces only the reported part's summary.

The change doc `sdd/changes/2026-11/documentation-rules-reported-elements.md` records the maintainer's decisions on RH8307, RH8106/RH8306 and the partial-member judgment.

## Why

Each rule disagreed with a shared requirement or with a decision taken in earlier question rounds:
- comments behind code (SHARED-DOC-004);
- the documentation-mode gate (SHARED-DOC-008);
- shapes the formatter keeps (SHARED-DIAG-010);
- fixes that undo each other (SHARED-FIX-004);
- position-independent verdicts (SHARED-DIAG-006);
- locations (SHARED-DIAG-007);
- partial members (SHARED-DIAG-004).

## Linked issues

Closes #1345
Closes #1346
Closes #1347
Closes #1348
Closes #1270
Refs #1092
Closes #1153
Closes #1617

## Review notes

- **#1092 is not implemented.** Taking a partial type's group from all its parts alone would only move the report on the issue's own input from RH8002 to RH8001. That contradicts the #1037 Q3a decision tracked in #1091. A characterization test pins today's behavior, and #1091 and #1092 now cross-reference each other.
- **#1347 departs from the issue's text.** The issue argued that inline elements are left alone by the formatter. The formatter does rewrite them; by the maintainer's decision RH8307 instead reports only top-level elements. Checking nested elements is #1712.
- **#1617's own example reproduces nothing,** because it carries no documentation comments. The defect appears once documentation is added. The example stays as a characterization test.
- **RH8401/RH8402 in `DocumentationMode.None`** parse the file a second time in `Parse` mode. That is one extra parse per file, and only in projects that use mode `None`.
- **RH8203 on a partial part whose own comment holds `<include>`** expands it through a small separate compilation, so the compiler's own include resolution applies. Without `<include>`, the part's comments are read from syntax.
- **Two changes required by unchanged requirements:**
  - RH8303 no longer reports the continuation line of a documentation comment written behind code in front of `}`.
  - RH8301–RH8303 also judge behind-code `///` comments in method bodies, parameter and argument lists, enum members and behind attribute lists, matching how the same comments are judged on their own lines.
- **FMT-BLANK-010** now states the existing output, one blank line between a documentation comment and an active region directive. No formatter output changes.
- The self-hosting scans ran only in CI.

## Follow-up work

- #1708 — RH4105 reports an unnamed extension receiver without a location
- #1709 — RH8107 and RH8202 mark only the first of several elements
- #1710 — RH8306 on both summaries of a partial property
- #1711 — other documentation rules on partial members (unconfirmed)
- #1712 — checking nested elements of documentation comments
- #1713 — one owner for the blank line above a region directive in the formatter
- Comments added to #1091, #1092 and #1449

author: dofam1nch1k
body:
`with_config_and_hard_settings()` restores the in-memory config and hard settings, but tests inside it call `Config::set()` and write the normal user's `RustDesk.toml`. A successful test can therefore leave its synthetic ID and default fields in the user's real config after the test process exits.

Use the existing `ConfigFileRestoreGuard` for the main file, while holding the existing test mutex. Its lifetime encloses the state guard, so the original file contents are restored after the in-memory state is restored, including during unwinding. This follows the restoration mechanism already used by the Config2 tests; production code is unchanged.

Actual Windows x86_64 verification: I launched the compiled test process for `config::tests::test_store_keeps_existing_enc_id_when_id_is_unchanged` and compared the real user config bytes before and after it exited. An outer backup/restore wrapper protected the user's data and observed the file before doing its own restoration.

- Before: test exit code 0, but `RustDesk.toml` changed to the test's config.
- After: test exit code 0, and the original `RustDesk.toml` bytes are unchanged.

The complete `cargo +1.75 test --locked -p hbb_common --lib` run also passed all 105 tests with normal parallel execution. The external observer reported no changed user config files after that run.

The source change is one line in the test helper, using an existing guard rather than adding test infrastructure. It restores contents after these tests; it does not redesign global test isolation or promise file-timestamp preservation.

author: dezoxy
body:
## Summary

Ideas round, step 15. Before replacing working stubs, the check read only one file of the new release. A pack whose other episodes didn't read could therefore pass.

- **What's checked:** a **sample of up to 3 files** (`replacementSampleSize`), deterministic. It's the file being replaced, plus the first and last episode of the sorted episode list, deduplicated. Samples and extras are never chosen, because the list holds only files that name an episode, and a sample clip loses to the larger file for the same episode.
- **How:** each sampled file gets `min(64 KiB, length)` read. The reads run **concurrently, under one shared `replacementReadTimeout`**, so a dead pack costs one wait, not three. The first failure cancels the rest.
- **On failure:** the same log line and the same 422 as before, "replacement release delivered no data …; existing files kept". The old stubs, registry rows and torrents stay.
- **Single-file release:** one read, as before.
- **Private torrents:** the same `ReadFileHead` as before, so only their existing peer sources (hard rule 3).
- **Docs:** a new README section, "Replacing a release". It states the trade-off: a dead file outside the sample can still pass.

## Tests

- New tests:
  - a pack whose sampled other episode doesn't read keeps the stubs;
  - a pack whose sampled files all read replaces, with a dead file outside the sample passing as documented;
  - the sample is the first and last episode, never a sample clip or extra;
  - a single file reads once;
  - the sample never exceeds the constant.
- The existing pack test now expects 2 reads.
- **Native runs:** `go test -race -count=3 ./internal/library` passes, as do gofmt, vet (also for linux) and `make docs`.
- CI runs the full race run, errcheck and tidy for the engine module. Docker was unavailable.

author: motercode
body:
## Cambios

**Apilado sobre #43** (agrupación): hasta que se haga merge de #43, este PR muestra también sus commits. Hay que hacer merge de #43 primero.

Los datos de las fotos salen de la página a ficheros estáticos generados en el build (opción decidida en el issue).

- **`/datos/base.json`:** posición, autor y viaje de cada foto, en arrays compactos. **`/datos/detalles/<n>`:** la URL de Maps y la miniatura, en 43 bloques de 500 fotos. Se generan con route handlers estáticos (`force-static`, y `generateStaticParams` para los bloques); cualquier otro número da 404.
- **Bloques por cercanía:** las fotos se ordenan con una curva de Morton (`spatialOrder`), así que las de una zona caen en pocos bloques. El navegador solo pide los bloques de las fotos sueltas visibles (`useDetails`). Si se pulsa una foto antes de que llegue su bloque, la pestaña se abre en el momento del clic, para que no la bloquee el navegador, y se lleva a la foto cuando llega.
- **Página:** solo lleva los viajes. Las fotos las pide al cargar y, mientras tanto, muestra un indicador; si fallan, lo dice.

**Medido** (versión de producción, 21 393 fotos):

| | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| HTML de la página | 11,5 MB (+ 11 MB de RSC) | 28 KB (5 KB comprimida) |
| Datos al entrar | todo (~3 MB comprimidos, dos veces) | base, 120 KB comprimida, + 1 bloque de 60 KB |
| Bloques pedidos tras acercarse por varias zonas | — | 14 de 43 |

- **Tests:** unitarios de `map-data.ts` (orden estable y por cercanía, compactar y recuperar, bloques). E2E nuevo: con un viaje pequeño, pasar el ratón por una foto suelta carga su miniatura y el clic va a Google (la petición se corta para no salir a internet). Los E2E anteriores pasan sin cambios.

Step 4 of the plan `cyberspace-mode`, the folder tower (`docs/cyberspace-mode-spec.md`, *Scene 1*, *Tower world*, *Camera and input* scene change 1). One pull request: `index.html` gains 956 lines.

## What it does

- `#|~space` opens the folder as a tower of glass floors, one per `.dev` file: drawn, then written, then knowledge, with labels, group brackets, the folder card and the pulled-out floor's card. The first drawn view is slid out, with its city standing small on it.
- Clicking another drawn floor slides it out as the one out slides back (450 ms, at once with reduced motion), a new history entry `#<folder>|view:<file>|~space`.
- **Enter the city**, a double-click on the drawer, or Enter flies down into the city (600 ms). The city then takes the small one's place in one frame, fitted as step 2 fits it, while the tower fades out behind it (200 ms). Esc in the city with nothing selected flies back up. Back and Forward retrace those moves.
- Written and knowledge floors open the inspector, with **Read it in Flat**. So do `view:<file>|~space` and `entity:<file>#<id>|~space`.
- Esc slides the drawer back.
- **Enter its folder** and the inspector's links open towers; a link to a part opens its city.
- A folder with no drawn views has no drawer and says so.
- Flat is unchanged: the diff touches only the Cyberspace CSS and the Cyberspace section of the script.

## Departures from the spec (changed in the spec in this commit)

- **The tower's camera is framed in the whole window**, as artboard 1 is, with the canvas as the part under the bar. The view offset is fixed as asked: three.js moves the window right by the offset. Framed in the canvas alone, the stack stood 28 px lower and 6% smaller than `strata.webp`. Framed in the window, the labels land within 2 px of it.
- **Both floors slide in the same 450 ms**, rather than the old one first.
- **Sliding back replaces the entry with `#<folder>|~space`.** That address also means "first drawn view out", so the floors stay in only until the reader moves on, and a reload pulls the first one out again.
- **The glow's falloff is a rounded square**, so it keeps the floor's corners.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 35 pass, 7 of them new: `towerWorldFrom` on the frozen 239ab8e fixture (7 / 3 / 14, `component` at the bottom, top at 26.95, climb 0 and 1.05), no drawer without drawn views, k ≈ 0.23, floor plans, and the round-trips of the slide, enter and up addresses.

- Browser (Chrome for Testing, headless on the M1 Pro's GPU, 1440 × 900):

  - Worker: **Enter its folder** opens `#worker|~space`. Written and knowledge inspectors work, and so does `.github`'s no-drawn-views card.
  - Reduced motion: the slide and both flights are instant.
- retro-games: the tallest tower, `games/lodestar`, has 16 floors, so nothing there climbs. `games/lodestar/src/hosting/godot` has no drawn views.
- `perf/400-parts`, the one-floor tower with a 352-tower city on its drawer:

  - 0.4 ms GPU frame time while orbiting, with rAF gaps of 16.7 ms (median and p95).

author: hvasconcelos
body:
## What
Implements [KNSH-023](specs/00-stories/KNSH-023-cli-knsh-history-and-knsh-events.md): `knsh history` and `knsh events`, in text and `--json` form, on `user.sock`.

- **`knsh history`**: filters `--session`, `--since`/`--until` (a UTC date or an engine timestamp), `--text` and `--limit` (default 100, maximum 100,000). Records print newest first. `--json` prints each API record object unchanged, one per line.
- **`knsh events`**: `--session` and `--since <seq>` (which needs `--session`). It follows events until interrupted. `--json` prints one notification `params` object per line and flushes after each. `events.lost` is reported in the stream; a gap is reported on stderr.
- **Daemon not reachable**: both commands only connect to the socket and never start `knshd` themselves. They exit 1 with a clear message.
- **Terminal safety** (`cli::terminal`): C0, DEL, C1 and bidirectional controls become visible escapes in text output and `\uXXXX` in `--json`. One record or event is always one line.

## Key decisions
- `records.query` pages oldest first and has no reverse order. The CLI reads every matching page (1000 records per call) and keeps only the newest N in a ring buffer. A cursor that does not advance is a protocol error, so the read cannot loop forever.
- The read timeout is lifted right after `hello`, before subscribing. A quiet engine may send nothing for hours. macOS also refuses `setsockopt` once the peer has closed, which a stand-in daemon test exposed when the timeout was lifted after subscribing.
- `events.lost` in `--json` gets an `"event":"events.lost"` member, so every line can be told apart by the same field.
- Spec updated: `specs/06-api/cli.md` gains the sections History, Events, Reading commands and the daemon, and Terminal safety. `knsh-proto` gains `ToJson for RecordsQueryParams`. `forget` now shares `parse_instant`, `user_socket()` and `usage()`.

## Testing
- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `build --locked` and `doc -D warnings` are all clean. Workspace tests: **552 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored**.
- Unit tests: `history_json_uses_api_field_names`, `history_escapes_control_characters`, `events_json_one_event_per_line`, plus tests for paging, cursor safety, validation, the human formats, lost events and gaps.
- End-to-end tests (`crates/knsh/tests/history_events_integration.rs`) run the real `knsh` binary against a stand-in `knshd` on `user.sock`: history paging and escaping, events streaming, no daemon (exit 1) and usage errors (exit 2).
- An independent review agent found no crucial issues.

## Follow-ups / known limitations
- **Pending:** a manual run against a real launchd-started `knshd`. It only serves launchd sockets, so tests cannot start it in an isolated home.
- `knsh history` scans all matching pages. A descending or "last N" option on `records.query` would make it cheaper.
- `knsh events` has no deadline on `events.subscribe`, so a hung `knshd` blocks until Ctrl-C. The alternative is to lift the timeout after subscribing and treat `EINVAL` as the connection having closed.
- Memory: up to 100,000 records are held in memory. Consider a lower `MAX_LIMIT`, or storing only the printed fields.
- An endless run of empty pages whose cursor keeps advancing is bounded only by the size of the ID space. Consider a cap.
- U+2028/U+2029 and zero-width characters are passed through. Terminals do not act on them; consider escaping them anyway.

author: madevmuc
body:
Work package 2 of V1.0 ([ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-v1-scope-and-work-packages.md)): data model, sign-in and the REST API. The setup wizard now saves for real.

## What's in it

- **Store:** SQLite (pure Go, `modernc.org/sqlite`) with embedded, numbered migrations. WAL, foreign keys and FTS5 are verified by tests (FTS5 is needed for search in package 3).
- **Data model:** households, people and `household_members` with the role on the membership, so a child can later belong to two households ([ADR 0010](docs/adr/0010-households-memberships-and-credentials.md)). Accounts, sessions, API tokens and the display PIN.
- **Credentials:** Argon2id for passwords and PIN; TOTP per RFC 6238 (tested against the RFC vectors, ±30 s drift); 256-bit tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes.
- **Setup wizard:** town plus state/canton (all 51 DACH regions), first parent with password, PIN. Then a TOTP step with the key and an `otpauth://` link; setup counts as complete only after the first code is confirmed. A half-finished setup can start over.
- **Sign-in:** username + password + one-time code, 30-day session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax), sign-out. 5 failed attempts per username within 15 min → 429. Unknown usernames take the same time as known ones.
- **CSRF:** form posts and cookie-authenticated API writes need a same-origin `Origin`/`Referer`; bearer-token calls are exempt.
- **REST API** `/api/v1`: `GET /me`, `GET/POST /people`, `GET /people/{id}`, `POST /tokens`, `DELETE /tokens/{id}`, plus `openapi.yaml`. Permission = role × token scopes (`read`, `write`, `<resource>`, `<resource>:<action>`); unknown scopes are rejected.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| Box without configuration → setup wizard (home location, first parent account, parent PIN) | ✅ now including saving: `TestSetupSavesAndConfirmsTOTP` |
| Read-only token → create → 403 | ✅ `TestReadOnlyTokenCannotWrite` (people and tokens); the event variant follows with events in package 3 |
| Child profile cannot delete an event | ✅ in the permission model (`TestRolePermissions`); the end-to-end test follows with events in package 3 |
| Box CI, `docker compose up` < 60 s | ✅ unchanged; locally healthy after 5 s |

**Contract tests:** every API call in the tests is validated against `openapi.yaml`, both request and response. A further test makes sure every served route is documented and every documented route is served. I checked that a deliberate break in the spec makes the tests fail.

## Decisions (documented per the decision framework)

- **Passkeys are not included** (V1.x, need HTTPS — [ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-authentication.md)).
- **TOTP enrolment shows key + link, no QR code yet.** A QR library comes with display pairing in package 5 and will be reused here.
- **No TOTP replay protection yet:** a code stays valid within its ±30 s window. It is acceptable on the LAN; I'll add it when remote access (V2) arrives.
- **The display PIN is stored and validated;** it is used once displays exist (package 5).
- **Migration `0001` was still unreleased** and got the `totp_confirmed_at` column directly. From the first 0.x release on, migrations are append-only.

## New dependencies

| Module | License | Why | In binary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `modernc.org/sqlite` (+ `modernc.org/libc`, `mathutil`, `memory`; `google/uuid`, `dustin/go-humanize`, `mattn/go-isatty`, `ncruces/go-strftime`, `remyoudompheng/bigfft`) | BSD-3 / MIT | SQLite without a C compiler, so ARM64/x86 builds stay a single static binary | yes |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` | BSD-3 | Argon2id | yes |
| `github.com/getkin/kin-openapi` | MIT | OpenAPI contract tests | **no, tests only** |

## Measured locally

Image 25 MB · RAM after setup 48 MB (budget 150 MB; Argon2id uses 19 MiB per hash) · 21 server tests, all packages green with `-race`.

body:
## Problem
`information-discovery` (shipped in #247) runs in NEW mode with `agent: librarian` as its executor. `SkillRuntime.invoke` refuses an executor that isn't granted the skill:

> The selected executor is not granted that skill. Nothing ran.

`librarian.md` listed no `skills`, and `LibrarianDefinitionTest` asserted that it had none. So the skill could never run for any caller (`interlocutor`, `farnsworth`, `aristoxenus`, or an Application agent such as Network Privacy Watch's assistant). Unit tests mock the executor, so nothing caught it.

## Fix
- `librarian.md` now has `skills: [information-discovery]`. This follows `diagnose-conversation`, where the executor (`conversation_diagnostician`) lists the skill it runs.
- The grant also exposes `skill_run`, so the prompt now says never to call it. When the skill is running, Librarian is already its worker.
- New test `every_shipped_skill_executor_is_granted_its_skill`: for every shipped skill with an `agent`, that agent is granted the skill and is delegable.
- `surface/librarian.txt` is regenerated with `-Dplowshare.surface.write=true`. The diff is the three new prompt lines; the tool schemas are unchanged.

## Not changed
`SkillRuntime`'s executor check stays as it is. It is the executor's opt-in, so the fix is the grant, not weaker enforcement.

## Tests
- `:plowshare-server:test --tests 'io.aeyer.plowshare.server.agents.*'` passes. That includes `LibrarianDefinitionTest`, `SkillsTest`, `SkillRuntimeTest` and `ModelSurfaceTest`.
- The new tests failed before the change ("librarian is not granted information-discovery").
- Run with `-x :plowshare-console:pnpmBuild`, because the console's node modules aren't installed in the local worktree.

Related: myrddian/plowshare#254 grants this skill to Network Privacy Watch's assistant, analyst and coordinator. Those grants only work once this lands.

body:
**Stacked on [#19](https://github.com/mikkvillem/bike-registry-next/pull/19)** — it needs the translations that PR recovers. GitHub will retarget this to `main` once #19 merges. Merge #19 first.

## Why

`/b/[id]` is where a QR scan lands: someone standing next to a bike, outdoors, on a phone, who wants one fact. The old page opened with the bike *type* as its heading, put the status in a small bordered box below it, and never showed make or model at all.

## What changed

- **Status band** across the top, above the fold and readable at arm's length — a red panel when stolen, the design system's inverted neutral panel when not. The status word says the same thing the colour does, so it doesn't depend on colour alone.
- **Make and model** as the heading, type as the eyebrow.
- **One large cover photo** to match against the bike in front of you, the rest as thumbnails, instead of a uniform grid of squares.
- **Theft report** as its own labelled section. The "Seen this bike?" box shows the contact when the owner opted in (decision 0002) and the police pointer when not — Q3's default, unchanged.
- **Specs** now include make and model, and rows stack on a narrow phone.
- Framed design system throughout (`CornerMarks`, `HorizontalDivider`), as on the landing page. The old `red-50`/`green-50` boxes had no dark variants; the new panels are dark-mode safe.

## How it was checked

The layout moved to `src/app/b/[id]/bike-status.tsx`, which takes its data as props — the route now only fetches. That let me render it against fixtures (registered, stolen with a public contact, and stolen with no contact and no photos) at 375px, in both locales and both colour schemes. The live database is empty, so this was the only way to actually look at it.

It caught a real bug: Estonian **"REGISTREERITUD" overflowed the status band** at 375px, on the one page that exists to be read on a phone. The band is now sized to fit.

The preview scaffold was deleted before committing. A permanent render test would need `@testing-library/react` — a new dependency, so I logged it in `docs/status.md` rather than adding it.

## Two things for you

- The **serial number is still absent** here, pending Q2. While checking, I found `/search` already prints the **full** serial on every public result — so Q2's answer has to cover both pages, or they'll disagree. Noted in `docs/questions.md`.
- The **header nav wraps to two lines per item** in Estonian at 375px, eating the top of every page. Pre-existing, out of scope here, logged under "Design to hone".

`npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (28 passing) and `npm run build` all pass.

author: bjbraams
body:
This PR adds the roadmap `MathematicalStatisticsAsymptotic`, on first-order asymptotic statistics and robustness. It is the first of the follow-up roadmaps announced in [MathematicalStatisticsFoundations](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/2111), covering the asymptotic and robust part of that plan. The scope is the standard graduate content of van der Vaart (1998) and van der Vaart–Wellner (2023), with the robust theory of Jurečková–Sen, Lehmann (1999) and Huber–Ronchetti (2009). Headlines that restate a source result cite theorem, definition, section or equation locators with printed pages; corollaries and adaptations are derived in the proof routes.

There are nine layers:
1. Euclidean limit theorems that Mathlib lacks: multivariate Lindeberg–Feller and i.i.d. central limit theorems, Gaussian quadratic forms (including the singular case) and the second-order delta method.
2. Weak convergence of maps that need not be measurable, in the sense of Hoffmann-Jørgensen, and the space `ℓ^∞(T)`.
3. Empirical processes: maximal inequalities, Glivenko–Cantelli and Donsker theorems under bracketing and uniform entropy, VC classes, and the classical Donsker theorem with the Brownian bridge limit.
4. Hadamard differentiability, the functional delta method and the argmax theorem.
5. M- and Z-estimators, maximum likelihood, rates of convergence, misspecification and sample quantiles.
6. Hájek projections, U-statistics (including the degenerate case) and L-statistics.
7. Contiguity, local asymptotic normality, and the representation, convolution and local asymptotic minimax theorems.
8. Likelihood-ratio, Wald and score tests, power envelopes, Pitman efficiency, Pearson's tests and GMM.
9. Robust statistics: influence functions, Hampel's and Huber's optimality, breakdown points and regression M-estimators.

**This roadmap is a supplier.** Four later roadmaps on the material of the same plan (semiparametric, higher-order and resampling, nonparametric, high-dimensional) are drafted but not yet submitted, and will consume its empirical-process toolkit and its limits of experiments. The headlines they use are listed under *Supplied to later roadmaps*, and the README treats their names and statements as part of this roadmap's contract.

**Dependencies.**
- [MathematicalStatisticsFoundations](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/2111), which is open: the finite-sample vocabulary, the information matrix, stochastic order symbols, Slutsky and contiguity definitions (its 2.4, 4.2, 4.3 and Layers 8–9). `Suggested.lean` carries local copies of the few Foundations definitions it needs, each with a docstring naming the owner.
- [StochasticCalculus](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/tree/main/TauCetiRoadmap/StochasticCalculus) §1.2 and §1.4: Wiener measure and the Brownian bridge on `[0, 1]`.
- From Mathlib: convergence in law and in measure, the central limit theorem, Cramér–Wold, Gaussian measures, tightness, sub-Gaussian variables, covering numbers and VC dimension, `klDiv` and kernels.
- From Tau Ceti: covariance matrices and their pseudo-inverses, the central and noncentral chi-squared laws, multinomial moments and quantiles.

**Prior formalization.** Most targets are formalized in `CKSD/Asymptotics/` of our project [lean-CKSD](https://github.com/bjbraams/lean-CKSD) (Core Knowledge of Statistics and Data Science), many of them proved. The README lists the differences: varying observation spaces, local asymptotic normality at each fixed `h`, and a developed empirical-process library, which lean-CKSD does not have as such. The QMD definition follows the shape of `Statlib/Inference/QMD.lean` in [Statlib](https://github.com/stat-lib/statlib) (Apache 2.0) at commit `af349698`; no Statlib code is copied.

**Review and AI assistance.** :robot: I chose the scope and its division from the other follow-up roadmaps, and I reviewed the roadmap. Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code) did the following:
- surveyed Mathlib, Tau Ceti and lean-CKSD;
- drafted the README and `Suggested.lean`, which compiles against the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti and states the headlines of Layers 1–9 that have Lean names, each with all the conclusions the README attaches to it; its 87 targets are admitted;
- located the source theorems in local copies of the cited texts.

The draft was refined after a review by GPT (Codex).

The lean-CKSD project was developed with extensive help from Claude and from GPT (various models).

author: s0up4200
body:
## Description

This continues the work in #4078. The recorder now stores a large Transfer history write in parts of at most 2,000 torrents, each in its own transaction, so that on SQLite the other writes of qui run between two parts. Before, the first write of an instance held the single SQLite writer for 18.3 s at 300,000 torrents (the median in Performance), and a save in the web UI waited for it.

```text
write(instance)
  if a part with an unknown outcome can be stored again
    read the stored write count
  for each part (2,000 torrents, sorted by hash)
    one transaction, one write number:
      records, counters, torrent days, tracker and category totals of these torrents
      first part only: Recording gaps, library day, instance hour, hash changes
      instance row: last reading time; complete_reading_at only in the last part
    on failure: keep the parts that are not stored in memory, stop
```

- Migration 121 adds `complete_reading_at` to `transfer_history_instances`: the reading time of the last write that stored all its parts. It is NULL while the first write lacks parts. After a load, the first reading uses it, so a stop between two parts keeps the Baseline of each torrent that qBittorrent had at the first recording, and the transfer of each torrent that the user added later.
- A part with no rows that add up (the normal first write) keeps its changes in memory after an unknown commit outcome. qui does not load the stored history again for it.
- The code calls a piece a "part", because `GLOSSARY.md` uses "Piece" for a BitTorrent piece.

The Brief amendment on #4081 lists each place where the code departs from the ticket.

Closes #4081

**Merge danger:** two-way door, because an older qui ignores the column of migration 121. After a downgrade, an instance that the older qui adds has no `complete_reading_at`. After the upgrade, qui treats that instance as a first write that lacks parts until its next write. Blast radius: recording.

## Breaking change

No breaking change.

## Behaviour change

No behaviour change. The Statistics page shows the same totals. During the first write of a large instance, other saves no longer wait.

## How has this been tested?

A live run on SQLite with a stub qBittorrent of 50,000 torrents and headless Playwright saved "Keep daily detail for" in Settings > Statistics during the first write of the instance. On develop, the save took 1,282 ms and 1,897 ms, because it waited until the write committed. On this branch, the write had 25 parts and took 1.1 s and 1.4 s, and the save during it answered in 34 ms and 25 ms.

## Performance

The first write no longer holds the SQLite writer longer than about 0.1 s. A full write also takes less time, because each transaction is smaller.

| Path | Longest transaction | All transactions | Full write | Worst other write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First write, 50,000 torrents | 1,740 → 63 ms (−96%) | 1,740 → 870 ms (−50%) | 3,277 → 2,442 ms (−25%) | 1,693 → 44 ms (−97%) |
| First write, 300,000 torrents | 18,298 → 81 ms (−99.6%) | 18,298 → 5,047 ms (−72%) | 28,239 → 14,470 ms (−49%) | 18,275 → 50 ms (−99.7%) |
| Later write, 3,000 of 50,000 changed | 42 → 26 ms (−39%) | 42 → 35 ms (−17%) | 71 → 67 ms ~ | not measured |
| Later write, all 50,000 changed | 924 → 38 ms (−96%) | 924 → 270 ms (−71%) | 985 → 388 ms (−61%) | not measured |

The table gives the median of 5 runs of each side, alternated. A Go test harness that is not committed times each write transaction from `BeginTx` to `Commit` and the module from `Record` until it settles. A second goroutine runs a small write every 50 ms during the first write. The torrents are synthetic, on 20 trackers, and the SQLite file is on disk. Base d8955ab4, head d2e58bae. Go 1.27.4 on a 6-CPU Xeon E5-1650 v3 VM with a virtual disk on btrfs (not an NVMe SSD), with other work on the host.

The size of a part comes from a measurement at 300,000 torrents. Parts of 2,000 torrents held the writer for 68 to 183 ms in four runs. Parts of 5,000 reached 301 ms, and parts of 10,000 reached 494 ms. The target is less than 250 ms.

Two costs remain, and neither shows in the numbers above. Each part writes its own tracker and category totals, so a write of 25 parts upserts the same total rows up to 25 times. In memory, qui now keeps the transfer of each torrent for each hour until a write stores it. While writes keep failing, this uses about 140 MB a day at 50,000 active torrents, against about 6 MB before.

- [x] If this changes the database schema, I have added migrations for both SQLite and PostgreSQL

author: darti
body:
## What

- **CPU clock**: `CPU_CLOCK = CpuClock::_240MHz` in `src/device/mod.rs`, passed to `esp_hal::Config::with_cpu_clock`. esp-hal 1.2.2 defaults the ESP32-S3 to `CpuClock::_80MHz` (`soc/esp32s3/clocks.rs`), so the firmware was running at a third of the chip's speed.
- **Release profile**: `opt-level = 3` instead of `"s"`. The release-only `esp-radio` override is now redundant and removed; dev builds stay at `"s"` (with `esp-radio` at 3).
- **Docs**: new ADR-0025 (decision + board measurements), ADR-0004 amended with the underrun result at 240 MHz, AGENTS.md lists the CPU clock among the board settings in `src/device/mod.rs`. The `IDLE_SPIN_LIMIT` comment (`esp_qspi.rs`) now says it is a poll count, not a duration.

## Why

Everything CPU-bound (Slint software renderer, software rotation, TLS GHASH, storage CRCs) ran at 80 MHz by default, not by choice. The image used ~2.3 MB of a 16 MB app partition, so optimising for size bought nothing.

No peripheral timing moves with the CPU clock: SPI and the TIMG timers (watchdogs, Embassy time driver) run from the fixed 80 MHz APB, I2C and SYSTIMER from the 40 MHz crystal. No cycle-counted delays exist in the firmware.

## Measurements (on the board)

Temporary build (not in this PR) redrawing and resending the whole 368×448 frame every 16 ms while a task copied PSRAM (the t-27 conditions of ADR-0004), both at `opt-level = 3`:

| CPU | Frames | Failed flushes | Render avg / max | Flush avg / max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 80 MHz | 1,200 | 0 | 25.8 / 27.4 ms | 31.8 / 44.3 ms |
| 240 MHz | 1,800 | 0 | 15.7 / 16.7 ms | 29.8 / 40.1 ms |

- Render 1.64× faster; flush is bus-bound and barely moves.
- No DMA underrun at 240 MHz under PSRAM load: the ADR-0004 margin holds.
- Normal image: boots without panic or watchdog reset, no bands on the panel, IMU rotation works.

`.text`: 2,306,741 → 2,975,953 bytes (+29%), well within the partition.

## For reviewers

- Not measured: `opt-level = 3` vs `"s"` on its own, power draw (higher active current on a battery device), and 160 MHz.
- Rebased on main (t-160..t-163, t-133): the ADR became 0025 (main has its own 0019). The underrun measurement predates ADR-0022 registering PSRAM ahead of the internal heap; not re-checked under that layout. `.text` on the rebased base is 4,258,481 bytes at opt-level 3.
- The microSD LittleFS mount failure seen on this board is identical at 80 MHz, so unrelated.
- The 12-reviewer `/review` ran on the 240 MHz + Slint-only `opt-level = 3` diff; its major findings are fixed here. The switch to `opt-level = 3` for the whole release profile was not re-reviewed.
- Checks: `just fmt`, `just check`, `just lint`, `just test` pass.
