author: kantorcodes
body:
## What was wrong On Cursor, three everyday commit spellings asked for approval even though a plain `git commit -m 'msg'` in the same repository goes through quietly: 1. `git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`, the multi-line message form agents write most often. 2. `git commit -m 'subject body'`, a multi-line message typed straight into the quotes. 3. `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=... commit ...`, including `git -C -c user.name=... -c user.email=... commit ...`. Cursor has no workspace sandbox, so a local Git write there is only quiet when Guard's local Git write proof accepts it. None of these three ever reached that proof: 1. The heredoc projection only accepted the bare `cat` the substitution runs when the sandbox would contain it. Without a sandbox, `cat` gets the ordinary "no rule proves this" review, so the projection gave up and the whole command was reviewed. 2. The write proof refused any line break in the command text, including one inside quotes. 3. The write proof required the subcommand to be the first word, so any `-c` pair in front of it closed the proof. ## What changed - The `cat` in a `$(cat <<'EOF' ...)` substitution now also counts as unrefused when it gets that plain review with nothing matched: no extension observation, no permission observation, no evaluation error, no uncertainty. A control that actually refuses `cat`, such as lockdown or a disabled extension, still matches or blocks, and the projection still stops. The projected command, with the message as a literal, is then judged exactly as before. - The write proof no longer refuses a line break inside quotes. An unquoted line break still ends the command, and the existing shell-control scan still refuses it. - Leading `-c user.name=` and `-c user.email=` pairs are dropped before the write proof runs. These two settings only label the commit and cannot start a program. Any other `-c` setting keeps the review, for example `core.hooksPath`, `commit.gpgsign`, `user.signingkey`, `gpg.program` or `core.fsmonitor`, even when it sits beside an identity pair. A leading `-C ` stays where it is, so the existing worktree route proof still decides where the commit runs. ## Regression coverage - Rust: `tests/pretool_git_heredoc_message.rs` adds `cursor_settles_a_heredoc_message_and_a_named_author`, which runs on the stamped Cursor path and expects `native_exact_safe_git_local_write` for all three spellings, the `git add -A &&` chain, `git merge origin/main -m "$(cat ...)"` and the `-C ` forms. `cursor_keeps_reviewing_settings_that_change_what_a_commit_runs` keeps every other `-c` setting, expanding heredocs, heredocs piped to a shell and unquoted line breaks under review. Both fail on the parent commit. - Benign gate: five Cursor allow rows (substituted heredoc message, `git add -A &&` with one, a quoted multi-line message, an identity-pair commit, and an identity-pair commit behind `git -C` into a sibling worktree), plus two not_allow rows across every harness (a heredoc piped to `sh`, and an unquoted line break followed by `rm`). The settings that stay reviewed beside an identity pair are covered by the Rust test, since the gate fixture already settles a commit with an absent hooks directory or the default signing program through other proofs.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; no new blocking issue was found.

Summary

The PR lets Cursor quietly allow Git commits with quoted heredoc messages, quoted multiline messages, and author identity settings. Other Git settings still require review. - Quoted multi-line commit messages can pass the local Git write proof. - Git commits with a named author can pass the local-write proof. Reviews (2) · Last reviewed commit: ["test(guard): drop two gate rows the repl..."](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/commit/115348dcc60b1ea7bae891e59ac593112995111e) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=hashgraph-online/hol-guard) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Quoted, multiline Git commit messages and author name or email overrides are now handled as local Git writes, including messages built with quoted heredocs and commits in sibling checkouts. * Quoted line breaks in Git write commands no longer trigger review by themselves. Git settings that affect hooks, signing, or execution, executable heredocs, extra commands, and unquoted shell controls continue to require review. * A bare `cat` command can proceed when its verdict does not refuse it.

Closes #159.

## Why

The download page (#155, #156) offers a macOS download and no workflow builds one. A notarised build needs a paid Apple Developer ID, so the choice was an unsigned build now rather than no macOS download.

## What changed

- **`build-macos` in `release.yml` and `snapshot.yml`**, on `macos-latest`: `wails build -platform darwin/universal`, the same version stamp and `-version` assertion the other jobs make, then `codesign --force --deep --sign -` over the finished bundle and `hdiutil` into `kommands-darwin-universal.dmg`. `publish` waits for it, and its `kommands-*` asset glob picks the DMG up.
- **Ad-hoc signing is required, not cosmetic.** Apple silicon refuses an arm64 binary with no signature at all and calls the download damaged. Ad-hoc signed, Gatekeeper refuses only the first launch, and the user allows it under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway (since Sequoia, Control-click no longer bypasses it).
- **Release and snapshot notes** say which file is which and give that macOS step beside the existing SmartScreen one.
- **`docs/distribution.md`**: four artefacts instead of three, why the build is unsigned, and that on macOS a `kommands://` URL arrives through `options.Mac.OnUrlOpen`, which #43 will need beside `onSecondInstanceLaunch`.

## Changelog

- feature: Offer a macOS build with each release and snapshot

## How it was verified

- Both workflow files parse, and `publish` lists `build-macos` in its `needs`. `.claude/suite-check.py`: all 21 checks pass.
- **Not run:** neither workflow runs on a pull request, so the macOS job has not executed yet. The first proof is a Snapshot run after merge (Actions > Snapshot > Run workflow), which republishes the public `snapshot` release. That run is what to watch: if `wails build -platform darwin/universal` or `codesign --verify --strict` fails, the publish job does not run and the existing snapshot stays up.
- The Gatekeeper and ad-hoc signing behaviour comes from Apple's [Mac User Guide](https://support.apple.com/en-lb/guide/mac-help/mchleab3a043/15.0/mac/15.5), the [Wails macOS packaging guide](https://v3.wails.io/guides/build/macos) and [Michael Tsai on Sequoia's Gatekeeper change](https://mjtsai.com/blog/2024/07/05/sequoia-removes-gatekeeper-contextual-menu-override), not from a run on a Mac.

author: keegan-fit8531
body:
## Money put aside (a car fund: WOF, tyres, a service)

A cost can be ticked **Put aside, don't pay out**. Each payday sends its share (a monthly amount as-is, a yearly one spread over the year), and the money stays in the account until it's needed, so the balance builds up.

Before, Motor maintenance and WOF were monthly payments. Balancing moved the account to Exact, and Exact counted the money already saved towards the next "bills", so payday sent **$0** while the app projected the fund draining away. With Motor maintenance $130 and WOF $70 a month, payday now sends **$200 every pay**, however much has built up.

- What's built up is never counted as free to pay bills, and never as spare when a pay is short.
- An account with money put aside is never a fixed amount: payday follows what's put aside.
- A short pay can pause what's put aside for that pay only (never the bills); the next pay is the usual amount.
- Shown as "put aside" on Deposits, the Planner and Accounts; left off the payments list and the weeks calendar.
- Costs already named as set-asides are marked as put aside once.

## One-off costs and an account history

- **One-off cost** on each account card (e.g. a tyre puncture): it comes off the balance and is kept in the account's history. Before saving, it shows what's left and whether next payday sends more to make up for it.
- **History** in the card's details: one-off costs and every balance entered, latest first. A one-off cost can be removed, putting its money back or leaving the balance as it is.
- **Update balance** is now an edit icon beside the One-off cost button.
- **Details**, and every other section that opens, grows open and fades in (no movement with reduced motion turned on).

## Checks

- `npm test`: 40 passed (new tests cover set-asides, balancing and one-off costs; one older test was rebuilt because it relied on name matching).
- `npm run lint`: no errors (only warnings that were already there). `npm run build` passes.
- Clicked through Deposits, Planner and Accounts in a browser, on a computer and a phone, with no console errors.

## Summary

S16 ranked nonresidential space fifth among its follow-ups. In this PR I count the storefront, office and medical-suite candidates among L1's rows, read a weighted sample of them with Sonnet readers, screen them against L1's held-out predictions, and score the predictions I committed before the reads. Nothing is fit, nothing goes to Modal, and I make no OxyLabs request and fetch no photo or floor plan.

- `docs/notes/nonresidential-2026-11-14.md`: the earlier work, the candidates, the predictions (first commit, before the draw), the reads, precision, the screen and the scored predictions.
- `docs/notes/nonresidential-2026-11-14/`: scripts `n1_prior.py` to `n5_screen.py` and the reader prompt. Outputs go to `/data1/apartments/tmp/nonresidential-2026-11-14/`.
- `docs/research-record.md` and `docs/TODO.md`: a row and the follow-up.

## Results

- 26,123 candidate rows, 2,611 held out outside S16's draw. 129 rows carry a commercial unit label.
- Weighted precision from 60 reads: the labels 0.88 (0.53 to 0.98), medical and professional offices 0.67, the draft rule 0.47 (0.26 to 0.69), live/work, ground retail and the broad words 0 in 22 reads, the whole pool 0.013.
- Screen: all held-out candidates miss L1's median by -0.0047 ± 0.0021, the same as all held-out ads, with a spread of 1.15 and in80 of 0.749. The draft rule's 30 held-out ads come to +0.004 ± 0.030 with a spread of 1.74.
- Predictions: 3 hit, 4 missed, 2 in part (the stratum precisions, 4 of 6, and the own-signal screen), 1 not scorable. The rule's bar of 0.85 was missed, so I write no rule.

## Recommendation

No rule and no fit. Nonresidential stays last among S16's follow-ups. If anyone wants the commercial rows out, the cheapest path is a reading pass over the 129 label rows into the ledger, with the label as a second kind of evidence, or a fresh pre-registered read of the label rows before any rule on labels.

## Test plan

- [x] `ops/fmt` and `ops/lint --changed` pass.
- [x] The predictions commit precedes the reads commit.
- [ ] Reviewer checks the precision weighting, the clustered standard errors and the scoring of each prediction against what the first commit wrote.

body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
> 审查修复批次的第 6 个 PR（共 8 个，线性栈，base 是 #95 的分支）。**合并方式请选 Create a merge commit**，不要 squash 或 rebase，否则后面的 PR 会和已合入的内容冲突。先合 #95，再合这个。计划见 `docs/exec-plans/active/20261110-codebase-review-fixes.md`。

## 变更摘要

一个审查条目（M10），11 个提交，196 个文件，+3,628 / −769。绝大部分是把旧写法换成新写法；不是照原样替换的地方都列在「行为变化」里。

**要解决的问题**

三处是同一类问题：名字是字符串，类型由用的地方自己断言。名字写错、字段写错、提供方改了签名，编译器都不报，要到运行时才出错。

| 组 | 改之前 | 改之后 |
|---|---|---|
| 事件（`a95c4f01`） | 往会话日志里写 `@actspace/core` 名下的事件，靠各包自己的 `core(type: string, data)`：7 份拷贝，6 份返回 `as never`；另有 9 处直接写对象。合计 13 个文件 16 处 | 42 种事件的 `data` 记在 `@actspace/shared` 的 `CoreEventDataMap` 一张表里，只从 `coreEvent(type, data)` 写。63 个调用点，13 个文件，9 个包 |
| 服务（`291342c6`） | `ctx.get?.("llm.service") as LlmServiceContract \| undefined`：52 个文件 132 处；直接调 `.getService()` 7 处；按字符串 id 注册 38 处 | id 和类型绑在一个定义上，57 个 id 共 77 个定义。`getService`、`requireService`、`provideService`、`getLeasedService` 四个函数按定义取用和注册，167 处。剩 9 个文件 11 处记在检查的清单里，每条带原因 |
| 干预点（`e330de17`） | 八个干预点（7 个 waterfall、1 个 serial）声明成同一个宽松的形状，payload 是 `Record<string, unknown>`。Loop 为了凑类型写了 5 处 `as unknown as` | payload 和结果按名字定类型，契约由分发它的包声明（`agent-loop`、`tool-runtime` 各一个 `hooks.ts`）；监听器用 `onHook(ctx, 名字, 监听器)` 注册 |

**三个检查**

旧写法仍然能编译，没有检查就拦不住下一处。三个都随 `pnpm test:scripts` 在 CI 里跑。

| 检查 | 提交 | 拦什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:core-events` | `1509bb8c` | 绕过 `coreEvent` 手写带 core 来源的事件。清单里 3 处：`coreEvent` 的实现自己、规模测试生成合成会话的辅助函数、浏览器 mock |
| `pnpm check:service-access` | 随第 2 组，用例在 `8622ae7c` 补齐 | 按 id 取出后断言类型；直接调 `.getService()`；有定义的 id 按字符串注册；视图没有对照行 |
| `pnpm check:harness-events` 新增一条 | 随第 3 组，`e863e728` 补查 `.tsx` | 干预点的监听器直接用 `ctx.on()` 注册 |

**给接口写类型时发现的两个原有问题**

`main` 上同样存在，不在审查的 24 项里。

- **「编辑提问再发送」在真实运行环境里总是失败**（`d3716f26`）。注册在 `session.storage` 下的不是存储本身，是一个手写转发的包装类，存储后来加的 `refresh`、`rewritePrefix`、`retireInto` 没有同步过去。这三个方法在接口里是可选的，消费方按「有没有这个方法」判断后端支不支持，所以不报错：编辑之前的提问再发送，每次都提示「这条提问不能再编辑。」，走到这一步之前这个会话正在运行的子智能体和后台任务已经被停掉；查看已经释放的空闲会话，每次都把整份记录重读一遍。相关测试都自己新建存储或用内存存储，没有一条经过包装类。补了转发，包装类加 `implements` 约束，另加一条按真实方式启动的用例。
- **`llm/stream` 的监听器不调 `next()`、直接给出流时，路由不归还**（`5cb8589f`）。准备好的那次调用占着路由的 lease，派发了才会归还；监听器不派发就没有人归还，这条路由之后注销会等到超时。现在读完流之后归还。目前没有生产插件注册这个干预点。

**规范按代码改的两处（要不要补能力需要你来定）**

`agent/pre-step`、`agent/turn-stopping` 两个干预点，规范写的能力代码里没有实现：

- `agent/pre-step`：规范写「接受、改写或跳过候选 step」。Loop 只把返回值写进 `step/start` 的 `metadata`，跳不过也改不了这一步。
- `agent/turn-stopping`：规范写「返回第一个继续 / 停止决策」。Loop 不读返回值，这一轮照常结束。

补能力是新功能，要先定「跳过一步之后这一轮怎么继续」「监听器要求继续时循环怎么走」，不在类型安全这一条的范围里；类型契约照着没实现的能力写，会让插件作者以为返回值有用。所以规范、契约、契约矩阵都按代码现在的行为写，两条用例把它固定下来，要不要补记在 `docs/exec-plans/tech-debt-tracker.md`。

**几个设计决定**

- **事件表放在 `shared`，不放在 `session-journal`。** 写这些事件的 13 个文件分在 9 个包里，`shared` 在最底层，谁都能引。`session-journal` 的 codec 仍然负责运行时校验，并加了一行编译期检查：表里有、codec 没登记的事件名编译不过。
- **`session.append` 的参数类型不收紧。** context、task、todo 这些插件写自己名下的事件也走它，收紧到 core 的表会把它们挡在外面。代价是手拼一个带 core 来源的对象仍然能编译，所以加 `pnpm check:core-events`。
- **定义由类型所属的包声明。** `cordis-adapter` 在依赖的最底层，引用不到各个包的类型，写不出一张带类型的总表。总表里已有的条目用 `bindServiceType<T>` 补上类型（15 个），不在总表里的用 `serviceKey<T>(id)`（42 个）。
- **下层包取上层包注册的服务用视图。** 为了拿类型去反向依赖，会被依赖环检查拒绝。`serviceView<T>(id)`（20 个）只写取用方用到的成员，不能拿来注册。视图和真实服务对不对得上，由同时依赖两边的 `@actspace/runtime` 在 `startup/service-views.ts` 里逐行核对：服务改了签名而视图没跟上，对应那一行编译不过。
- **会被工具插件引用的定义放在只引类型的模块里。** Default Harness 把每个工具插件单独打包，定义和服务的实现类写在同一个模块时，实现类会被打进每个工具插件的产物。定义放在各包的 `service-keys.ts`，`agent`、`tool-runtime`、`llm-service` 三个包标 `"sideEffects": false`。在第 2 组那次提交上量：内核 339,617 → 343,721 字节（多 4,104），14 个工具插件合计 283,199 → 272,234 字节（少 10,965）。
- **两个 app 各留一处断言。** CLI 和桌面端主进程只能动态加载 Runtime，拿不到定义这个值。Runtime 导出类型 `ProfileServices`（7 个 id 对应的类型），两个 app 各有一个 `profileService(profile, id)`，app 里的断言只剩这一处。
- **干预点的契约由分发方声明，分发结果是 `unknown`。** 监听器来自单独构建的插件，编译期的类型约束不到运行时拿到的值，分发方本来就逐个字段检查，结果类型写成 `unknown` 让这些检查省不掉。
- **lease 在读完流之后归还，不在钩子返回之后。** 监听器可以等流被读取时才调用 `next()`；钩子一返回就归还，这种写法会收到 `Prepared LLM call has been released`。

**行为变化（合并前请留意）**

- **编辑之前的提问再发送可以用了**；查看已经释放的空闲会话不再每次重读整份记录。用户可感知，发布记录加了两行。**没有在真实的桌面窗口里点过**，见下面「没有做的验证」。
- `llm/stream` 的监听器不派发时路由不再被占住。已派发的调用仍由流结束时归还，没有变化。
- **CLI 的 Agent Host**：Profile 里没有 `agent.runtime` 时，启动就报 `Agent runtime unavailable`；原来要等到第一次用它时才抛 TypeError。正常安装里走不到。
- **五个插件多了 12 处「服务不在就报错」的判断**：`english-learning`（1 处）、`desktop-app` 的会话标题（2 处）、`subagent-claude-code`、`subagent-codex`、`tool-subagent`（各 3 处）。原来把取出来的服务断言成「一定在」，不判断；现在服务不在时在取用的地方报 `<取用方> requires <id>.`，原来是之后第一次用到时抛 TypeError。这五个插件的 `inject` 都列了这些服务，正常挂载时走不到。
- **`plugin-manager`**：Host 端口整个不在时报 `Harness evolution is unavailable on this Host`，原来是抛 TypeError；同样只有绕过 `inject` 才会走到。第 2 组一度把它读 Host 端口的时机从每次执行工具改成了挂载时读一次，对照改动前后时发现，已经改回去并加了用例（`5881f29c`）。
- **压缩插件不再自己拆 `llm.service` 的包装**，直接用注册的包装服务。压缩只用到 `routes.list()` 和 `prepareAsync`：包装服务的 `routes` 和里面那个是同一个对象，`prepareAsync` 原样转发。结果相同。
- **给插件作者的写法变了**：干预点的监听器用 `onHook` 注册，并要先引入声明契约的包（只用类型时 `import type {} from "@actspace/agent-loop"`），否则名字编译不过。八个干预点的分发时机、内置行为、对监听器返回值的处理都和原来相同。
- **类型和依赖上的变化**：`desktop-app` 不再依赖 `@actspace/session-journal`；`background-tasks`、`session-storage` 新增对 `cordis-adapter` 的依赖；`inspectCapability` 的第一个参数从字符串 id 改成定义；`ToolJournalPort.recordPermission` 改成按事件名取 `data` 类型的泛型方法；`AgentEventDispatcher.serial` / `waterfall` 的 `next` 从可省略改成必填；原来 8 条宽松的干预点声明和 `AgentWaterfallEventHandler` 删掉。

**没有动的**

- 别的插件（context、task、todo 等）写自己名下的事件，`data` 的类型仍然靠断言，由各自的 codec 在运行时校验。
- 两个干预点没有实现的能力（见上）。
- `tsconfig.base.json` 的 `"baseUrl": "."`。它让声明文件里出现以仓库根目录为起点的路径（`import("packages/…")`），两个 app 解析不到时那个类型会悄悄变成 `any`，类型检查不报错。强制重建后 634 个声明文件里有 4 处，都是原有的。这个 PR 只绕开了自己碰到的那一处（`ProfileServices` 逐行写明类型），两个 app 各加一行编译期检查守着；根因影响全部包的构建配置，计划放在栈顶单独一个可以不合的 PR。
- 三个检查都只按文本匹配，各自认不出的写法写在脚本开头。例如把取出来的服务先存进变量、隔一行再断言类型，把 core 的名字先存进别的常量再用，干预点的名字不是字面量，都认不出来，还要靠评审。

**对提交说明的更正**

仓库约定不改写已有提交，更正写在 history 里：

- `291342c6`（第 2 组）的「行为变化」只列了 CLI 的 Agent Host 一处，后面写「其余不变」。实际还有三处没有列：上面的五个插件 12 处判断、`plugin-manager` 的读取时机（已改回）、压缩插件不再拆包装。这三处是提交之后逐个文件对照改动前后才看出来的。
- 同一个提交把定义的个数写成「共 78 个」「`bindServiceType`：16 个」，实际是 77 个、15 个：当时按文本数，把一行注释里的示例也数了进去。
- `118f580a`（文档）写 `packages/` 下六份 README「各自写明对应的检查命令」。写了命令的是五份；`packages/composition/README.md` 没有写，它指向 `cordis-adapter` 的 README。

## 验证情况

- [x] `npm run ci`（`./scripts/ci.sh` 通过）
- [x] 已完成相关测试或手工验证：
  - 三组的提交说明都写了「运行时行为不变」，这句话是这样核对的：
    - 事件：用 TypeScript 的语法树找出改动前后构造 core 事件的地方，改之前 71 处，改之后 69 处；67 处的文件、事件名、`data` 表达式、`surface`、`provenance` 逐字相同，其余在两个文件里，逐处看过，写出去的字段相同。
    - 服务：把改动前后每个文件里「取用或注册哪个 id」找出来比较，前后都是 255 处、69 个文件，逐个文件一致。改之前的 132 处断言里有 16 处断言成「一定在」，逐处对过现在服务不在时的表现；非测试代码的改动（122 个文件，+895 / −461）整份读过。上面「对提交说明的更正」里那三处就是这一步找出来的。
    - 干预点：产品代码里分发干预点的 9 处（Loop 6 处、Tool Runtime 3 处），逐处对过改动前后传的 payload、内置行为和对返回值的处理。
  - 类型拦不拦得住：每一组都有「必须编译不过」的反例。事件 6 个，写在桌面端 renderer 的类型测试里，由类型检查守着（把其中一个改对，`tsc` 报 TS2578）。服务 8 个、干预点 14 个，写在夹具文件里，由用例调 TypeScript 把夹具编译两遍：原样必须没有报错，去掉 `@ts-expect-error` 后每个反例必须报出指定的错误码。
  - 三个检查：`check:core-events`、`check:service-access` 在改之前的代码上跑，报出的就是这次改掉的那些（15 个文件 18 处；清单留空时 139 处）。`check:harness-events` 新增的那条在改之前的代码上报 0 处（产品代码里本来没有插件注册监听器），另由一条用例往仓库的真实源码里放一处来确认会报。把三个脚本逐处改错再跑用例：55 种、144 种、78 种改法，除了 `check:service-access` 有 1 种改了结果一样之外，每一种都有用例失败。改错的验证在仓库外的副本上做。
  - 两处修复和一处恢复，新增的用例都回到改之前的代码上确认过失败：`session.storage` 的两个新测试文件在旧包装类上失败；lease 的两条用例，去掉修复报 `did not drain`，把归还挪到钩子返回之后报 `Prepared LLM call has been released`；`plugin-manager` 的用例在第 2 组的版本和第 2 组之前的版本上各失败在不同的一步。
  - `pnpm check:hot-path-reads`、`pnpm check:scale-tests` 通过，基线和登记没有变化。
  - 全量验证跑了两遍，最后一遍在 `5881f29c` 上带着文档跑：桌面端构建图检查、依赖构建、契约矩阵检查、全部包和桌面端的测试、`pnpm test:scripts`、`scripts/ci.sh`、`pnpm lint`、`pnpm typecheck`、`markdownlint-cli2@0.24.0`、`pnpm check:docs`、`pnpm check:packages`、官网的检查与构建、`pnpm build`，13 步全部通过。73 个包和应用的测试都通过，其中用 vitest 的 70 个合计 5,407 个用例通过、28 个跳过。之后只有文档里的几句话有改动，又跑了 `scripts/ci.sh`、markdownlint、`pnpm check:docs` 和官网的检查与构建，通过。
  - 没有做的验证：
    - **没有在真实的桌面窗口里点过「编辑提问再发送」。** 新增的用例按真实方式启动 Runtime，建会话、写三条消息、回退到第二条，确认记录只剩前面的部分；界面到 Runtime 之间的那一段云端验证不了。步骤和预期结果列在 `docs/exec-runs/20261110-codebase-review-fixes/execution-summary.md`（必须验证第 6 条）。
    - 没有在真实的桌面窗口和真实的 Provider 连接上把日常用法走一遍。这个 PR 改了 122 个非测试文件里取用和注册服务的写法，建议合并前照执行摘要的建议验证第 9 条走一遍。
    - 没有生产插件注册干预点，`

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>go-fleettools/landingkit (github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit)</summary>

### [`v0.32.0`](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/releases/tag/v0.32.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/compare/v0.31.0...v0.32.0)

#### What's Changed

- check: a repeat is a strip fact standing alone, not a phrase inside a sentence by [@​tannevaled](https://redirect.github.com/tannevaled) in [#​48](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/pull/48)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/compare/v0.31.0...v0.32.0>

### [`v0.31.0`](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/releases/tag/v0.31.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/compare/v0.30.0...v0.31.0)

**wasmcache hardening** ([#​47](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/issues/47), closes [#​45](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/issues/45)).

- **The recovery page reloads at most once.** The "Updating…" page that replaces a playground page failing its hash check now reloads a single time, marked with `?wasmcache-reset=1`. If the page still fails, it shows a static "clear this site's data" message instead of reloading, even when removing the service worker keeps failing. Before, that case reloaded without end. The marker is removed from the address bar once the page is healthy.
- **Cache names are restricted (breaking).** `-name` now accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`, and anything else is refused at generation time. Before, only `|` was refused, and a name containing `</script>` could break out of the generated recovery script. `<` is also escaped as `<` where the name is embedded, as defense in depth.
- **Tests.** The test kit makes removing the service worker always fail, and asserts exactly one reload followed by the message. It also checks that the restored page matches its manifest hash. Each check was proven by mutation: removing the bound gave 240 page requests against an expected 2.

Upgrade: if your `-name` uses characters outside the allowed set, rename it. go-slides uses `go-slides-playground`, which is unaffected.

### [`v0.30.0`](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/releases/tag/v0.30.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/compare/v0.29.0...v0.30.0)

**New: `wasmcache`, a local cache for playground wasm with update detection** ([#​41](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/issues/41)).

A playground no longer downloads its wasm on every visit. A service worker keeps the files listed in a build manifest, checked against their sha256, and reloads when a newer build is deployed. This release shares the cache code across playgrounds; it does not share one cache between them.

- **Hash-checked everywhere.** A cached or network copy whose bytes do not match the manifest is never stored or run. If the playground page itself fails the check after a deploy, a fixed recovery page built by the worker removes the worker, deletes only this playground's caches, and reloads.
- **No version skew.** Worker and loader URLs carry the build's `?v=`, and a worker from another build never answers them.
- **Lazy files.** `-lazy <path>` keeps a file out of the precache. It is fetched on first use and then cached under the same hash check.
- **Test kit.** `wasmcache/testkit` runs a browser end to end. It covers first load, a cached reload, update detection, a tampered network copy, the recovery page, and lazy files: none requested from server start until `use`, cached after.

Hardening follow-ups from the review are filed as [#​45](https://redirect.github.com/go-fleettools/landingkit/issues/45): a one-shot bound on the recovery page's reload, and a restricted character set for cache names.

</details>

body:
## Description

Applied lab implementing **lifecycle request cleanup and regression testing** for Day 13 (Controlled vs Uncontrolled Input). It handles asynchronous delayed requests and prevents race conditions when query parameters change rapidly or when the component unmounts mid-request. Includes a regression mutant check proving that omitting the decisive cleanup guard triggers a race-condition failure.

## Related Issue

Fixes: #15

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] UI/UX Improvement
- [ ] Performance Improvement
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring / Maintenance
- [ ] CI/CD

## Changes Made

- `13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/applied-labs/r19-t010/example.jsx` — UserProfileFetcher component with cancellation and mutant testing modes
- `13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/applied-labs/r19-t010/check.mjs` — Playwright test covering race protection, unmount safety, and mutant validation
- `13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/applied-labs/r19-t010/README.md` — Invariants, contract, and regression mutant details
- `13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/applied-labs/r19-t010/package.json` — Pinned dependencies
- `13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/13_uncontrolled_input.md` — Added Activity section under # Exercises
- `work/R19-T010/evidence.txt` — Tool versions and full test run transcript
- `work/R19-T010/screenshot.png` — UI verification snapshot

## Screenshots / Recordings

UI verification snapshot is recorded at work/R19-T010/screenshot.png.

## Testing

Tested locally with Playwright test runner: `node 13_Day_Controlled_Versus_Uncontrolled_Input/applied-labs/r19-t010/check.mjs`

All assertions passed with status code 0.

Zero console errors and zero unhandled page exceptions detected.

Key verification points:
- Slow request A does not overwrite fast request B (race condition prevented).
- Unmounting component with an in-flight request results in 0 console errors and 0 unhandled exceptions.
- Focused mutant test confirms that removing the decisive cleanup guard produces a test failure.

## Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally.
- [x] I have added or updated tests, if needed.
- [x] I have updated documentation, if needed.
- [x] I have followed the project's coding guidelines.
- [x] I have run the relevant tests and checks.
- [ ] I have addressed previous review feedback, if applicable.

## Additional Notes

Evidence stored in work/R19-T010/evidence.txt.

Coursework PR submitted against S-AI-Projects/30-Days-Of-React base repository as required by submission guidelines.

body:
Terminal music player for YouTube Music with Vim keybinds, written in Rust.
Homepage: https://github.com/socatlolmeow/drift

`mpv` and `yt-dlp` are runtime dependencies, so the binary is wrapped to have
both on `PATH`.

The package is named `driftmusic` because `drift` is already taken by an
unrelated screensaver. The installed binary is still `drift`, so the two
packages conflict if installed together. Happy to rename the binary if
reviewers prefer.

I am the upstream author.

## Things done

- [x] Fits [CONTRIBUTING.md], [pkgs/README.md], [maintainers/README.md] and other READMEs.
- [x] Follows the [automation/AI policy].
- Built on platform:
  - [x] x86_64-linux
  - [ ] aarch64-linux

author: lujack88
body:
## Why

After every Tern restart or plugin reload the board sat on "Connecting…" until the workspace was added again. The key was in the keychain the whole time.

The window half handed the key over once: `start()` → `inject()` on `window_start` and on the 300 ms load timer. At that moment the board's block is missing or still starting (its host VM restarts on a reload too), so the event was dropped. Nothing retried and the board never asked. Adding a workspace only helped because `activate()` calls `inject()` again.

Reproduced on `main` before the change: a board block opened without **Linear: open board** was still on "Connecting…" 15 s later.

## What changed

- `host.luau` / `model.luau`: a board that has a workspace but no key sets its title to `Linear · connecting…` (`Model.KEY_TITLE`), the same title channel it already uses to ask the window half for a key prompt or a chat.
- `window.luau`: the existing 1 s tick hands the keys to any board showing that title. It waits while a keychain read is in flight, and stops asking for a workspace the keychain has no key for until that workspace is added or switched to, so the "Missing Linear API key" toast shows once.
- `window.luau`: `send` no longer lets one board that takes no event stop the others from getting it. This was the "no program runs in that pane" warning in `tern.log`.
- `openBoard` drops its 1 s and 3 s re-injects; the new board asks instead.
- `host.luau`: cards and rows no longer set the issue URL as their tooltip (asked for separately; **Open in Linear** and **Copy link** stay in the ⋮ menu).
- 0.9.2, changelog entry, `docs/sync-model.md`.

## Verified on Tern 0.9.18

- `tern plugin reload linear-todo`: two open boards both synced with no manual step.
- A board block opened directly (`cx:new_block`): left "Connecting…" in about 1 s.
- `tern restart` (window and session daemon both restarted): the board lists the FIX issues and synced again 63 s after the daemon came up.
- Self-test: 45 passed.

Not run: the path where the keychain has no key (the toast showing once).

## Merge order

Branched from `main`, as asked, so it overlaps #8 (0.9.1) in `CHANGELOG.md`, `plugin.toml` and the missing-key lines of `inject`. Whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

author: lgtm-ai-bot[bot]
body:
## What changed

- `backend/pyproject.toml`: `anthropic>=0.40` → `anthropic>=2.6.0,<3`, with a comment naming the supported line and the test that verifies it.
- `backend/uv.lock`: relocked; only the recorded specifier changed (see below).
- `backend/tests/test_anthropic_transport_contract.py` (new): contract tests that run both services through a real `anthropic.Anthropic` client whose `httpx2.Client` uses an `httpx2.MockTransport`. The SDK builds the request, adds headers, applies its retry policy, maps error statuses to its own exception classes and decodes the body itself. Only the socket layer is replaced.
- `backend/src/podex/services/llm_response.py`: `first_response_text` now raises `MalformedResponseError` when a success body has no content list, or when a text block has no text. `MALFORMED_RESPONSE_ERRORS` groups that error with the SDK's `APIResponseValidationError` and the `json.JSONDecodeError` that `messages.create` raises for an invalid JSON body.
- `llm_extraction.py` / `llm_transcript_cleanup.py`: both services now report those cases as a `Malformed API response: …` result error, alongside the existing API and network error handling. The cleaner's provider call moved into a private `_request_text` method so `cleanup_transcript` stays within the existing return and local-variable limits. Model identifiers and request parameters are unchanged.

## Why

The declared range allowed any release from 0.40 on, across two major lines, while the lock held 2.6.0 (httpx2-based). Existing tests only used fake clients, so a new SDK major could change construction, transport, request serialization or error classes without any test noticing.

The new transport-level tests found a defect. When the provider returned a 200 whose body was not a Messages API response, both services crashed instead of returning their error result. The bodies tested were an HTML page, truncated JSON, a message without `content`, `content` that is not a list, and a text block without `text`. On the unchanged code all 10 cases (5 bodies × 2 services) fail with `AttributeError`, `TypeError` or `JSONDecodeError`. The SDK does not validate success bodies by default, so the services must.

### Range choice

- Floor `2.6.0`: the locked release, verified by these tests. Older 2.x releases were not tested, so they are not claimed.
- Cap `<3`: a new major needs review and a run of this contract suite before the cap is raised.
- No extras are needed. `anthropic` 2.x depends on `httpx2<3,>=2.0.0`, which the project already declares (`httpx2>=2.14`).

## What the contract tests cover

- **Request**: `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, JSON content type, `anthropic-version` present, the dummy credential in `authorization`, and the complete body for each service. The expected values are written in the test, not imported from the code under test:
  - Default models are literals (`claude-opus-4-8` for both services), so changing a default requires a matching test change.
  - `max_tokens` is 4000 for extraction and 8000 for cleanup. The extraction user turn is the delimited transcript. The cleanup user turn is compared in full for a fixed input (podcast, host, guest, terminology, transcript and the closing instruction).
  - Each system prompt is checked by the SHA-256 of its exact text plus a few anchoring phrases. A digest is used instead of a copy because prompt text may live only in `prompts_default.py` (see `.semgrep/prompt-boundary.yaml`). After a deliberate prompt change, recompute the digest with `hashlib.sha256(prompt.encode()).hexdigest()`.
- **Responses**: success bodies decoded into extracted items and cleanup corrections; a response with only non-text blocks yields an empty result with no error.
- **SDK error classes**: 400/401/429/500/529 map to `BadRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`, `RateLimitError`, `InternalServerError` and `OverloadedError`, all `APIStatusError` subclasses. A read timeout maps to `APITimeoutError`, an `APIConnectionError` subclass.
- **Service behaviour through the SDK**:
  - 429 is retried twice and honors `retry-after`; the `x-stainless-retry-count` values are 0, 1, 2.
  - 500 and 529 use SDK back-off.
  - 400 is not retried.
  - Timeouts and connection failures become `Network error: …`.
  - The five malformed 200 bodies become `Malformed API response: …`.
  - Every failure is reported once, and the cleaner keeps the original text.
- **Default construction**: without an injected client, both services build `anthropic.Anthropic` with the default base URL and retry count. The test supplies a dummy key from the environment.
- **Isolation**:
  - An autouse fixture blocks outbound network use through the `socket` module: connection setup (`connect`, `connect_ex`, `create_connection`), name resolution (`getaddrinfo`) and datagram sends (`sendto`, `sendmsg`). It records any attempt and fails the test on teardown if one occurred. Code that bypasses the `socket` module (for example direct `_socket` use) is outside this guarantee. A separate test shows the guard stops a default SDK client and loopback UDP sends.
  - All `ANTHROPIC_*` variables are removed for each test.
  - Retry delays are recorded through a `time.sleep` replacement, so nothing waits.
- The existing fake-client parsing tests in `test_llm_extraction.py` are unchanged and still pass.

## Lockfile comparison against `main`

I parsed both lockfiles and compared them package by package:

- Packages: 98 on `main`, 98 on this branch. None added, none removed.
- Version changes: none. `anthropic` stays at 2.6.0 and `httpx2` at 2.16.0.
- The only entry that differs is the `podex` package's own `[package.metadata] requires-dist` line for `anthropic`: `>=0.40` → `>=2.6.0,<3`. This is the intended constraint change.
- No top-level lock keys changed. `uv lock --check` passes.

## How it was tested

- Test-first: the new file was run on the unchanged services. 22 passed and the 10 malformed-response cases failed with the crashes listed above. All pass after the fix.
- Mutation checks. Each change was temporary, run against the contract file, then restored; each one fails a test:
  - Extraction default model changed to another identifier: 2 tests fail (extraction request, default construction).
  - Cleanup default model changed: 2 tests fail (cleanup request, default construction).
  - One instruction line in the cleanup system prompt reworded: the cleanup request test fails on the SHA-256 assertion.
  - The cleanup user-message instruction replaced with different text: the cleanup request test fails.
  - One sentence in the extraction system prompt reworded: the extraction request test fails.
- `uv run pytest --cov` (backend): 807 passed, 4 skipped (opt-in PostgreSQL and R2 smoke tests). Total coverage 88.71% (floor 85%). `llm_response.py` coverage is 100%.
- `uv run lintro chk` (backend): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 info.
- `uv run lintro chk --tools osv_scanner`: pass, 0 issues.
- `uv lock --check`: pass.
- `uv sync --locked --python 3.11` and `--python 3.15`, each in a temporary environment: resolved to Python 3.11.15 and 3.15.2, both with anthropic 2.6.0 and httpx2 2.16.0. The LLM test files (47 tests) pass in each.
- Newest in-range SDK, run as an ad-hoc overlay that does not touch the lock: the same 47 tests pass against anthropic 2.8.0.
- No test reaches the network or needs an API key.

## Rollout

None. This is a code-only change, with no migrations, backfills or settings changes, and the locked SDK version is unchanged. To roll back, revert the PR. The supported range is recorded next to the constraint in `backend/pyproject.toml`, and the release changelog picks it up from this commit.

Closes #487

author: jonperron
body:
## What

Enforces ElementDefinition `fixed[x]` / `pattern[x]` (PLAN 11.6.2-D4) and `type.profile` (D2) in the validator. Both have been loaded since #82.

- `PROFILE_004` (error): an occurrence is not exactly the profile's `fixed[x]`. The check uses deep equality, and numbers compare by decimal value, so `3 == 3.0 == 3.00`.
- `PROFILE_005` (error): an occurrence does not follow `pattern[x]` as a recursive subset. Each pattern array item must match some instance item.
- `PROFILE_006` (error): R5 `vitalsigns` keeps its fixed category coding inside the `VSCat` slice, so slices whose discriminators are all `value`/`pattern` are now counted against their min/max. Other slicings stay unevaluated, as a documented shortcut.
- Type profiles: `Claim.item.quantity` (SimpleQuantity) now gets `sqty-1` and `comparator` max 0 (`CARDINALITY_002`). Profile invariants already on the type are not run twice, findings already made are not repeated, and conforming to any one profile is enough.
- `meta.profile` rules now apply at every depth, not only to the root's children. Slice children no longer count as children of the sliced element. A single XML `<profile>` was silently ignored before and is now applied.
- Refactor: `resolve.rs` and `cardinality.rs` are moved out of `nested.rs` unchanged, so `profile.rs` can use them without a module cycle.

## Why

`elementdefinition.html`: fixed "SHALL be exactly the value", pattern "each occurrence ... SHALL follow". A resource claiming `vitalsigns` passed with any category, and a SimpleQuantity accepted `"comparator": "<"`.

## How it was tested

- `crates/fhir-validator/tests/fixed_pattern_tests.rs` has 12 tests against the real Registry. Each one failed on the code before its fix. They cover vitalsigns wrong/right/duplicate category, document-bundle fixed code (JSON and XML), history-bundle pattern code, the logiclibrary pattern CodeableConcept subset, the ldlcholesterol fixed Quantity at depth (decimal equality), the Claim comparator, bp slice isolation, and a lone XML coding.
- Behaviour diff on all fixtures (origin/main vs head): 88 lines added, 0 removed, and every one was checked against R5. 75 are `PROFILE_001` warnings for IG profiles that are not loaded, on XML files whose single `<profile>` was never read before. The rest are `CARDINALITY_001` (shareablevalueset/codesystem, cholesterol), `PROFILE_004/005` on the cholesterol/triglyceride bad cases, and `PROFILE_006` on obs-quantity.json (bp slices missing).
- Manifest pass rates: JSON 78/111 (70.3%) before and after. XML went from 77/108 (71.3%) to 81/108 (75.0%). Four bad cases are now caught: cholesterol-bad-wrongcode, triglyceride-bad-wrongcode, cholesterol-bad-referencerangemissing and cholesterol-bad-referencerangehighfixedquantitywrong. None regressed.
- `null_placeholder_profile_version_tests` asserted that no `PROFILE_*` code appeared on a vitalsigns Observation that has no category. It now gets a correct `PROFILE_006`, so the assertion is narrowed to `PROFILE_001`/`PROFILE_003`.

## Behaviour changes users will see

New `PROFILE_004/005/006` errors on resources that claim R5 profiles. New `CARDINALITY_002`/`INVARIANT_sqty-1` on SimpleQuantity elements. Profile checks now run on XML resources with one `<profile>`.

Known limits (code comments): decimals are compared as f64, because the parser has already parsed them that way. Closed or ordered slicing, reslices and non-discriminator slice content are not evaluated.

## What remains

- Answer the Sourcery review and watch CI on the head (`626366b`). Neither was finished when this was written.
- The behaviour diff ran on `88bde0f`. Two small changes came after it and the diff has not been re-run: lone integer/decimal XML values against a one-item fixed array, and a test cleanup.
- Coverage gaps the test agent found, none of them blocking: the `discriminator_value` bail-outs and `$this`, `matches` on bool/integer/arrays, and `check_type_profiles` with an unknown or multiple profiles.

Enforce fixed, pattern, slice, and type-profile constraints across FHIR resource validation.

New Features:
- Enforce profile fixed values, pattern values, and supported value-discriminated slice cardinalities throughout nested resources.
- Apply type.profile constraints, including invariants and cardinality restrictions, with support for multiple alternative profiles.
- Validate singleton XML meta.profile values and apply profile checks at every resource depth.

Bug Fixes:

- Prevent profile rules from leaking across slice boundaries and avoid duplicate diagnostics from base validation.

Enhancements:

Build:

Documentation:

Tests:

Spec: .kiro/specs/integrations/ (task 5)

Stacked on #47; merge after it.

Adds the pure `PlayTracker` and its event types to `nemo-core/src/hooks.rs` (ADR 0004 Decision 4 row 30). It turns player events and position samples into the events Last.fm, Discord, media controls and listening stats need, with the real heard time and the shared `PlayRule` decision. Nothing runs it yet; the `nemo-app` hub comes later.

## Changes
- `crates/nemo-core/src/hooks.rs`: `FinishedPlay`, `PlayHookEvent` (`TrackStarted`, `StateChanged`, `PositionJumped`, `DurationKnown`, `TrackEnded`), the `PlayObserver` trait and `PlayTracker` with the design's `new`, `on_player_event`, `tick` and `flush`.
  - Heard time grows only while `Playing`, by `min(position advance, wall time spent playing since the last sample)`. Paused, buffering and stopped time is not counted.
  - A forward jump beyond that time plus 1 s, or a backward jump of more than 1 s, emits `PositionJumped` and adds nothing (a backward jump resyncs).
  - `TrackChanged` (also for the same track on repeat one) closes the old play and opens a new one from the snapshot's track; on close, playing time since the last sample counts up to the track's end, so a gapless handover credits the last fraction of a second and never more than the rest of the track.
  - `flush` closes the last play. `DurationKnown` updates the length the rule uses.
  - Arithmetic saturates; no panics.
- New `crates/nemo-core/src/hooks/tracker_tests.rs` (kept apart so `hooks.rs` stays under 500 lines): table tests for pause, seek forward and back, repeat one, gapless handover, skip and `DurationKnown`; `proptest` that the summed and per-play heard time never exceeds wall time.
- `crates/nemo-core/Cargo.toml`: `proptest` as a dev-dependency (the workspace pin 1.12.0 already in `tech.md`; `Cargo.lock` gains only that edge).

author: ar4mirez
body:
## Intent

Ship slice S2 of spinel issue #39 (https://github.com/ar4mirez/spinel/issues/39), `require`, `load`, `$LOAD_PATH`, `autoload`. The plan (owner decisions D1-D6 taken as recommended) splits #39 into S0-S4; S0 and S1 (CRuby's feature lookup) have merged, and this is S2, provided features and the native-extension slot:

- At boot, `$LOADED_FEATURES` holds CRuby 4.0's eight provided features: `enumerator.so thread.rb fiber.so rational.so complex.so pathname.so ruby2_keywords.rb set.rb`.
- `BUILTIN_FEATURES` and its special case go away. `rbconfig` and `io/wait` move into the table under the names CRuby records.
- The search gains the native-extension step per D2(a): extensions are `.rb` → `.spinel` → `.so`. A `.so` found on the path raises `LoadError` with `path == nil` and a message saying it is a CRuby C extension. An explicit `foo.so` in a require name also finds `foo.spinel`. The real file name is recorded, and `.so`/`.spinel` match each other when checking whether a feature is loaded. `DLEXT` stays `"so"`.
- Expected delta: `require_spec.rb` 78 → 80 of 80, so `spec/tags/core/kernel/require_tags.txt` is gone and `core/kernel/require_spec.rb` newly passes, ticking #39 DoD box 1. `require "pathname"` must still load stdlib `pathname.rb`.

## What Changed

- `$LOADED_FEATURES` now starts with the eight features CRuby 4.0 provides at boot (`enumerator.so thread.rb fiber.so rational.so complex.so pathname.so ruby2_keywords.rb set.rb`), so `require` of any of them returns false. `require "pathname"` still loads the stdlib `pathname.rb`. The old `__builtin_features__` list and its special case are gone. `rbconfig` and `io/wait` are now looked up in a small table and recorded under `RbConfig::CONFIG["rubyarchdir"]` (as `rbconfig.rb` and `io/wait.so`) the first time they are required. A recorded feature path that doesn't start with `/` is no longer resolved against the working directory.
- `core/load.rb` gains the native-extension step. A name without an extension is searched as `.rb`, then `.spinel`, then `.so` (`DLEXT` is unchanged). A `.so` found raises a `LoadError` with `path == nil`, and its message says it is a CRuby C extension. A `.spinel` found raises a `LoadError` saying Spinel extensions can't be loaded yet, until the loader in #104 lands. An explicit `foo.so` also finds `foo.spinel`, and `.so` and `.spinel` count as each other when checking whether a feature is already loaded.
- `spec/tags/core/kernel/require_tags.txt` is deleted (`core/kernel/require_spec.rb` goes from 78 to 80 of 80, as the roadmap records). A new integration test in `crates/spinel-cli/tests/require.rs` covers this, using a `provided.rb` fixture and a stub `native/cext.so`. `docs/engine.md` and `docs/roadmap.md` describe the new search order and this slice.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is confined to `core/load.rb`'s require lookup. I traced the eight provided features (thread → :r; fiber, enumerator and pathname.so → :s, then a Ruby-only search, so `require "pathname"` still loads stdlib pathname.rb), the `.rb` → `.spinel` → `.so` search order, `foo.so` also finding `foo.spinel`, the `LoadError` with a nil `path`, and rbconfig/io-wait recorded under rubyarchdir, and each matches the stated intent and CRuby's load.c with no wrong result found.

## Testing

I built spinel and ran a scenario script with throwaway load-path fixtures, comparing its output with CRuby 4.0.9's on the same script. The script covered boot features, provided features answering false, rbconfig and io/wait, pathname, refusal of a C extension, an explicit .so finding a .spinel, .rb being preferred over .so, and a missing feature. I also probed how a loaded .so or .spinel answers a later require, and ran the require.rs integration test and core/kernel/require_spec.rb (80/80). Everything matches the intent. The one difference I found, an explicit x.so not being satisfied by a loaded x.spinel, matches CRuby's own behaviour for x.so against a loaded x.o.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 10 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| At boot, $LOADED_FEATURES starts with CRuby 4.0's eight provided features, in CRuby's order | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, boot features section |
| require of each provided feature (and its .so/.rb form) returns false | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, provided-features section |
| rbconfig and io/wait are recorded under the architecture directory; require io/wait returns true then false; DLEXT is "so" | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, rbconfig/io-wait section (rbconfig answers false because RubyGems loads it at boot, as CRuby with gems also does) |
| require "pathname" still loads stdlib pathname.rb and Pathname#find exists | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, pathname section |
| A CRuby .so on the load path (bare name or explicit .so) raises LoadError with path nil and the C extension message | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, cext section |
| An explicit foo.so finds foo.spinel first, even when no foo.so exists | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt, both.so and onlyspin.so lines |
| A .rb file is preferred over a .so of the same name, and a missing feature still raises cannot load such file | ✅ pass | live | spinel-scenarios.txt |
| A loaded x.spinel or x.so makes a later require of the bare name answer false | ✅ pass | live | spinel-so-spinel-match.txt |
| The require.rs integration test passes against the built binary | ✅ pass | live | `cargo test --release -p spinel-cli --test require`: 2 passed |
| core/kernel/require_spec.rb passes 80 of 80 with no tags file | ✅ pass | live | require_spec.txt |

author: gamehunterkaan
body:
The required Security policy check now reports four advisories against the locked `soupsieve` 2.9. They appeared after `main`'s last security run (2026-10-30), so the next run on `main` and every pull request fail:

| Advisory | Severity | First fixed | That release needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GHSA-4j63-6c4x-wfg4 | medium | 2.10.0 | Python 3.10+ |
| GHSA-6655-6qjp-jx7x | high | 3.0.2 | Python 3.11.5+ |
| GHSA-7g44-g9rc-x53w | medium | 3.0.2 | Python 3.11.5+ |
| GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f | high | 4.0.0 | Python 3.11.5+ |

Three of the four have no fix that supports Python 3.10, which reached upstream end of life in October 2026. Rather than waive them with VEX statements, this drops Python 3.10 and moves `soupsieve` to 4.1.

**Breaking change:** AutoPWN Suite needs Python 3.11.5 or newer. On Python 3.10, pip and pipx keep resolving 2.9.0, and `install.sh` refuses before it touches an existing installation. The Docker image and the standalone binaries bundle Python 3.13 and are unaffected.

**What changes**
- `pyproject.toml`: `python = "^3.11.5"`, the 3.10 classifier removed, ruff `target-version = "py311"`.
- `poetry.lock` (Poetry 2.5.1): `soupsieve` 2.9 -> 4.1. The dev-only `tomli` and `exceptiongroup` backports, which only 3.10 needed, leave the lock. `requirements-locked.txt` is re-exported. The packaging and bandit requirements pin neither, so they are unchanged.
- `scripts/export_locked_requirements.py` imports `tomllib` directly. Ruff now sorts `tomllib` with the standard library in `scripts/security_policy.py`.
- CI: `tests.yml` and `install-smoke.yml` use Python 3.11 instead of 3.10. The required check names are unchanged. The install smoke checks, which are not required, are now named `Wheel on <os> / Python 3.11`.
- `install.sh` refuses interpreters older than 3.11.5, and `tests/unit/test_install_scripts.py` expects the new message.
- Docs: README, `docs/BUILDING.md`, `docs/CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/SECURITY_TESTING.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, the `docs/ROADMAP.md` decision on Python 3.10, `AGENTS.md`, and a CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry with the CVE IDs from the GitHub advisory records.

**Impact of the advisories:** all four are in compiling or matching CSS selectors. AutoPWN Suite parses target HTML with Beautiful Soup but finds elements by tag name and never compiles a selector, so there is no known impact on scans. beautifulsoup4 4.13.4 works with soupsieve 4.1.

**Checks:** the lockfile check, ruff, the locked-requirements export check and the full pytest run with coverage pass locally. The Security policy check was not run locally because `osv-scanner` is not installed; this PR's run is the first. No new lint exceptions and no skipped tests.

This also unblocks GamehunterKaan/AutoPWN-Suite#100: with Python 3.11.5 as the minimum, it can take `dnspython` 2.9.2 instead of a VEX statement.

author: dash0-dev[bot]
body:
## Summary
`auth.user_id` was only on the root request span (`lorekit.mcp`, `lorekit.memories`), while the facts a per-user view needs are written on the child operation span: `lorekit.write.inserted` on `lorekit.memory.write`, `lorekit.memory.count` on `lorekit.memories.get/quota` / `lorekit.memory.quota`. Span metrics group one span's attributes at a time and cannot join a child to its parent, so "memories held per user" and "new memories per user" could only be answered with a trace-level join. This stamps the same id on the operation span too.

## Changes
- `mcp/mcp-handler.ts`: set `auth.user_id` on every `lorekit.<tool>` span (covers `memory.write` and `memory.quota`), using the `analyticsUserId` the dispatcher already resolves for the usage event.
- `_shared/api/router.ts`: set `auth.user_id` on the REST handler span `hs` (covers `lorekit.memories.get/quota` and the write route), using the `usageUserId` already stamped on the root span.
- Both follow the existing rule: absent, never empty, for service-role callers.

author: septimionicolas
body:
## Qué pasó

El 14-11-2026 a las 08:03 se perdió el aviso «Listo para retirar» en Salón. El log de Railway mostró `polling_failed` y después `telegram_edit_failed` y `telegram_send_failed role: salon` con «fetch failed». El evento `kitchen_ready` quedó registrado; se perdió solo el mensaje, porque cada llamada a Telegram se hacía una sola vez.

## Qué cambia

- `server/telegram.js`: cada llamada se reintenta hasta 3 veces (a 1, 2 y 4 s) si fetch falla o Telegram contesta 5xx. Un 4xx no se reintenta nunca, por ejemplo «message is not modified». Un 429 tampoco: queda afuera.
- Freno: si se agotan los reintentos, por 30 s las llamadas hacen un solo intento. El freno se levanta apenas Telegram vuelve a contestar.
- `getUpdates` no reintenta adentro, porque el polling ya tiene su espera.
- Apagar el servidor corta la espera, y el log guarda el error del corte.
- Log nuevo: `telegram_retry { method, attempt, waitMs }`.
- `docs/decisiones.md` (D11 y valores de fábrica) y `docs/CONTRATO-API.md`.

## Cómo se probó

Primero se escribió el test que reproduce el corte, en `tests/flow.test.js`: «si la red se corta un momento, el «Listo» llega igual al salón y una sola vez». Antes del arreglo fallaba así:

```
test at tests/flow.test.js:125:1
✖ si la red se corta un momento, el «Listo» llega igual al salón y una sola vez (0.86775ms)
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
  
  0 !== 1
  
      at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///Users/pablocolombresgarmendia/verdel/tests/flow.test.js:135:10)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
      at async Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1409:7)
      at async Test.processPendingSubtests (node:internal/test_runner/test:974:7) {
    generatedMessage: true,
    code: 'ERR_ASSERTION',
    actual: 0,
    expected: 1,
    operator: 'strictEqual',
    diff: 'simple'
```

`tests/telegram.test.js` prueba la regla de reintento. `npm run verificar` da 28 de 28 en verde.

## A decidir en la revisión

Un aviso puede llegar repetido si el corte ocurrió después de que Telegram lo recibió. Se prefirió eso a perderlo (D11).

## Queda afuera

- Timeout propio por intento.
- Bandeja de avisos pendientes para cortes de más de 7 s.

author: matteooxx
body:
A fresh install could not know the OS, the shell, which models the account
has, whether Codex is connected, or how deep each phase should think. It
guessed all of them, and the guesses produced advice that failed. This adds a
first-run interview that asks, and fixes seven defects found by running things
rather than reading them.

## New: `/council-setup` and `scripts/council-detect.sh`

The interview asks in this order, and asks what to build **last**:

1. **OS and shell, before any command is suggested.** The scripts are POSIX
   `sh` and run on Linux, macOS and Windows, but what the user types differs,
   and the shell the assistant runs tools in is not necessarily theirs.
2. **"I don't know, check for me."** `council-detect.sh` answers by running:
   the per-shell invocation for the detected OS, the required tools, both
   planner CLIs and Codex's login state, which models actually answer, the
   agent roster, and a canary that proves the blindness rule is honoured on
   this machine. `--no-model-check` skips every live call and then says so —
   unknown is not the same as fine.
3. **Models**, offering only what answered, with prices stated.
4. **Effort per phase** (`low`…`max`), with a table of what each phase is
   worth paying for, and the note that Codex takes no effort flag.
5. **A spending cap** (`--max-budget-usd`), with the cap's own cost: a run
   that reaches it stops instead of finishing.
6. **The config**, written as a small delta that sources the plugin's own
   rather than copying it — copying is how a plain assignment spreads.

Models and effort are now settings (`COUNCIL_MODEL_*`,
`COUNCIL_{PLANNER,ATTACK,ARBITER,ASSIGN}_EFFORT`, `COUNCIL_BUDGET_USD`), so
the interview can choose them without editing a function. `planner_fable`
ships ready.

## Fixed

| Defect | Now |
|---|---|
| The setting announcement reported an intention, not an outcome: a config with a plain assignment made a run say the environment had won while the config had overridden it | The run refuses to start, naming both values and the line to write |
| The arbiter could read `council.txt` and learn which planner wrote which plan | Every child is denied the run directory; the review phases deny every earlier run too, because an arbiter refused the current one then read an older run's mapping, which carries over when the planner order is stable |
| A deny rule written as an MSYS path matched nothing and blocked nothing, in silence | Rules are built with `cygpath -m`; the doctor checks `cygpath` is present |
| Plan-phase logs carried the planner's name, and Codex's log holds its whole plan verbatim | Job labels are letters, so no log attributes a plan to a model |
| `council-doctor.md`'s YAML frontmatter did not parse, so every field was silently dropped at runtime | All `argument-hint` values are quoted |
| CRLF line endings killed the scripts under `dash` (`set: Illegal option -`) while still running under Git Bash's `sh` | `.gitattributes` pins `*.sh` and `*.conf` to LF |
| The deny-rule check itself inspected function bodies with `type`, which dash does not expand, so it raised a false FAIL on a correct config | It reads the function out of the config files with `awk` |

## Corrected as false

The context root is **not** a boundary. A read-only child agent reads an
absolute path outside it with no refusal at all. `lib.sh`, `SKILL.md`,
`council-plan.md` and the README all said such a read was silently refused.

## Verified

`claude plugin validate` passes; `claude plugin test` 7/7; the full fake chain
(plan, review, assign) with three planners under `sh`, under `dash`, and from
PowerShell; `/plan-council:council-setup` is discoverable once loaded; the
blindness fix proved against an arbiter actively asked to break it, which
tried Read, Grep, Glob, `find` and PowerShell and was refused on all of them;
`gitleaks` clean on history and working tree.

Still not covered: the deny rule is a Claude Code permission rule and does not
reach Codex, so with Codex as a planner the attack phase's blindness rests on
the prompt — `/council-doctor` names every function it cannot cover. Native
Linux, macOS and WSL remain untested.

body:
## Why

Diagrams could not be shared. They had no people list: only the creator and the admin could manage a diagram, and anyone else saw it only through a doc that embeds it.

## What changes

- **Migration 0021 `diagram_members`**: same shape and roles as `doc_members`. Every existing diagram's creator becomes its owner, so nobody loses access.
- **Roles on a diagram**: owner (share, move, delete), editor (edit in Draw.io, rename, theme, get XML), commenter (comment), viewer (see). The admin still owns every diagram.
- **Diagram page**: Share button using the doc share panel (no Export segment), Delete only for owners, commenting for commenters and up.
- **Library**: diagrams shared with you appear under Diagrams with your role.
- **Invites**: email with the diagram's title and link; a diagram-only invitee can sign in and claims the invite.
- **MCP**: `share_doc`, `list_members` and `unshare_doc` accept `diagramId` instead of `docId`. `list_drawio` returns your role. Guide and error wording updated.
- **Seeing via a doc still works**: a doc that links a diagram shows it to its readers when any owner or editor of the diagram can edit that doc (before: only the creator). Those readers do not see the people list.

Doc sharing goes through the same code, now generic over doc or diagram, with no change in behaviour.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun run test` 1320 passed (9 new: each role, invite email, sign-in by invite, leaving, last owner, link-only viewers, MCP sharing), `bun run build` ok.
- Local `bun run dev` with migrations applied: the owner shared a diagram as Commenter from the panel. The invitee signed in, found it in their library, and saw Review and Share but no Edit, Rename or Delete.

author: chrishotza
body:
## Bug
Inside `BlocRelocV2.refine`, `accepted += 1` occurred for *every* improving destination block evaluated, before the algorithm committed exactly one destination to the partition. The acceptance trace could therefore count one vertex multiple times in the same iteration even though only one move took place.

## Fix
- Increment the accepted counter once only when the chosen block is actually committed.
- Preserve candidate comparison, best-cut selection, partition constraints, random seed, and existing two-swap counting.
- Add a synthetic six-node graph where one vertex has two improving destinations but only one move is committed. Verify committed count, cut and final partition. Add a zero-move regression and explain trace semantics.

## Scientific boundary
No archived experiments, benchmark values, figures, graph generators or stored results changed. Fresh acceptance telemetry is now counted correctly; past traces remain historical evidence and should not be silently reinterpreted.

CI runs the existing offline NetworkX unittest suite.

body:
## Cause

Après un rechargement de `/saisie` avec une séance en cours, la suite d'un exercice à zone de routine devient « Prochaine séance : 80 kg × 8 » au lieu de « La prochaine fois : une rep de plus, 90 kg × 6 ». Course sans re-rendu, quatre causes :

1. le premier rendu part avant l'arrivée des routines (`zonesDeRoutine = {}`) ;
2. les re-rendus de `chargerSiBesoin` / `afficherSaisie` ne jouent que si `vues.saisie` est visible, alors que la vue visible est la séance ;
3. `planActuel()` mémoïse le plan sur 23 clés dont aucune ne porte `generationRoutines` ;
4. `consigneDe` FIGE la consigne et l'écrit sur le disque avec `routines = []` quand aucun brouillon `consignes` n'existe (B1 du contradicteur).

Hors ligne les routines ne se chargent jamais.

## Correctifs (3 commits de code)

- **Le coach se tait sur ce que les routines décident, tant qu'elles ne sont pas prêtes** : `routinesPretes()` (état `ok` OU routines gardées en mémoire ; absent du plan = prêt). Clé du mémo = `generationRoutines` + état « prêtes ». `consigneDe` ne fige ni n'écrit une consigne à zone de plan sans routines ; `suiteDe` se tait ; l'exercice fini dont la suite se tait ne montre ni constat ni l'en-tête d'avant (`x.suiteMuette`) ; la carte « Au max » ne se propose pas. **I168** le vérifie.
- **Un seul point de re-rendu** : le succès de `chargerRoutines` (tout chargeur), seulement si les routines n'étaient pas prêtes. Jamais sous la frappe (remis au `focusout`), ni sous une feuille, ni pendant « Il t'en restait combien ? » ; n'écrit rien. Retentative au `online` et à l'ouverture de la séance (20 s).
- **Jamais « La routine change » sans qu'elle change** : routine illisible, le choix « Changer la zone de cette routine » est grisé avec sa raison ; `poserZoneDePlanDe` et « Oui, dans ma routine » refusent sans écrire ; le remplacement au plafond lit d'abord les routines.

Spec : MOTEUR §9.49 ; CLAUDE.md §4 ter (I168).

## Avant → après (banc `f2`, 16 contrôles : rouge avant, vert après)

| Scénario | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Live (contrôle négatif) | 90 kg × 6 | 90 kg × 6 |
| Rechargé en ligne | « Prochaine séance : 80 kg × 8 » | « La prochaine fois : une rep de plus, 90 kg × 6 » sans geste |
| Retour par l'onglet Saisie | idem après rechargement | 90 kg × 6 |
| Rechargé hors ligne | « Prochaine séance : 80 kg × 8 » | silence sur la suite et le verdict, en-tête d'avant absent ; 90 kg × 6 au retour du réseau |
| Zone de routine changée en avion | « Nouvelle zone : Mix » (80 kg), routine inchangée, promesse dite | choix grisé + raison, rien posé |
| Brouillon `consignes` effacé, hors ligne | consigne figée 77,5 kg × 8 « Nouvelle zone » | coach muet, rien sur disque ; consigne juste au retour |

## Décision à connaître

Le verdict du jour naît de la même consigne suivante que la suite (`constatEnDeux`) : il ne peut pas rester seul. Hors ligne, un exercice à zone de plan fini ne dit donc ni verdict ni suite jusqu'au retour des routines (avant : un verdict, parfois faux, et une suite fausse).

## Vérifs

- `node -c`, `npx jest tests/unit` : 407 suites, 11 236 tests verts.
- Banc réduit : `f2`, `ondulation`, `5a-bis`, `au-max-pr3`, `plafond-salle`, `1` : 57 contrôles, 0 échec.
- Mutations (`tests/banc/mutations-f2.json`) : 9 tuées + 1 témoin survivant.
- Garde de vitesse `tests/banc/vitesse.js` : démarrer 29,5 × (plafond 100), valider 15,6 × (27), suivant 10,7 × (90), fiche 22,0 × (85).
- Service worker non touché.

## Risques

- La garde de développement (I168) ne tourne qu'en `localhost`, `*.pages.dev` ou `?garde=1` : en production la tenue repose sur le code.
- Silence à la reprise hors ligne (voir ci-dessus).
- Justifié sans changement : la question de fin de séance « mettre à jour ta routine ? » se tait sans rien dire de faux hors ligne ; `unExerciceALElastique` lit aussi la séance et le catalogue.

## À vérifier sur appareil (prévisualisation)

1. **En ligne, rechargement** : finir un exercice d'une routine à zone, recharger la page : la suite dit « La prochaine fois : … » (jamais « Prochaine séance : 80 kg × 8 »), sans toucher à rien ; changer d'onglet et revenir.
2. **Avion + onglet tué** : mode avion, tuer l'app, la rouvrir sur la séance : pas de suite ni de verdict faux sur l'exercice fini, pas d'en-tête de consigne devant une série déjà faite.
3. **Changement de zone en avion** : toucher la puce de zone : « Changer la zone de cette routine » est grisé avec sa raison, « Juste pour aujourd'hui » marche.
4. **Retour du réseau** : réseau rétabli, la suite revient d'elle-même ; si un champ de saisie a le focus, le redessin attend qu'on le quitte.

body: ## Summary Two AsyncAPI bugs: the generated output didn't match the spec. **1. AsyncAPI 2.x messages with a `name` but no `messageId`.** `@asyncapi/parser` returns `undefined` from `message.id()` for these. The result: - `events()` crashed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; - native targets named the model `UndefinedMessage`. The new helper `messageId(message)` in `ir/asyncapi.ts` returns `message.id() ?? message.name()`. It replaces every `message.id()` call, in `asyncapiSchemas`, `events`, `event-map` and `inferEventType`. **2. AMQP bindings were parsed, then dropped.** `Events` entries now also carry whichever of these the spec sets: ```ts userCreated: { type, routingKey, exchange, exchangeType, contentType, // unchanged exchangeOptions: { durable: true, autoDelete: false }, // channel exchange binding queue: { name: 'user-created', exclusive: false }, // channel queue binding publishOptions: { deliveryMode: 2, priority: 5, expiration: 60000, cc: ['audit'] }, // binding of an operation that sends this message } ``` `amqp.gen.ts` applies them, and options passed by the caller still win: - `assertExchanges` sets `durable` and `autoDelete` from `exchangeOptions`. - `bindAndConsume` accepts either a queue name or `Events.x.queue`, which brings the queue's `durable`, `exclusive` and `autoDelete`. - `publish` maps: - `deliveryMode` to `persistent`; - `priority`, `expiration` and `mandatory` directly; - `cc` and `bcc` to amqplib's `CC` and `BCC`; - `userId` directly; - `timestamp: true` to the current Unix time in seconds, which is what AMQP expects. What this PR still doesn't do: - `vhost` is not applied, since it's set per connection. - Channels with only a queue binding (`is: queue`, no exchange) are still skipped by `events()`, as before. **Tests:** - New `tests/sdk/asyncapi/asyncapi-2.test.ts`. It covers 2.x naming, each kind of binding, and a channel where two operations send different messages. - The RabbitMQ testcontainers end-to-end test passes locally. - The asyncapi golden snapshots each gain the new `QueueDescriptor` line. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/77c7dff1552c4d1fb65c2037a2f5cc04 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/77c7dff1552c4d1fb65c2037a2f5cc04?variant=devin Requested by: @ahmedrowaihi --- 🟢 Devin Review found nothing to fix · [View findings](https://app.devin.ai/review/ahmedrowaihi/ir-kit/pull/159) · [Follow Devin's work](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/77c7dff1552c4d1fb65c2037a2f5cc04)

author: shiv3
body:
Part of the `integ/sim` stack (#928 → #929 → #930). Sub-PR 3 of 3; builds on #942 and #943.

## What

**1. Persistent cellular availability gate** (core, both modes). For a station whose selected path is `cellular`, the link is available only with a modem, a card, an `active` subscription and no `blocked` policy; independent reasons `modem_absent`, `sim_missing`, `subscription_suspended`, `sim_network_blocked` (`resolveCellularLink`, pure).
- Going down closes the socket with the `simulated` cause (not an error / fault); power and transactions stay; queued messages are salvaged like any lost link.
- While down **no path opens a socket**: operator `connect`, `reset`, the reconnect timer and daemon restart (the gate is evaluated when the CP is built, before it connects) all end without a connection. A `connect` is remembered; an operator `disconnect` forgets it.
- The outage consumes **none of the #609 attempt budget**; on restore the station dials with a fresh budget via the normal `connect()` — no reboot, and no fabricated BootNotification: 2.x resumes without one while boot data is unchanged (#702); a Reset issued during the outage still sends its own boot; 1.6 boots on every connect as always.
- Ethernet/Wi-Fi stations are untouched by their unused SIM; no implicit failover.

**2. SIM-scoped policies** (daemon): `network_sim.cellular.get|save|status`, persisted in `kv` (`networkSim:cellular`), pushed to every CP and to CPs created later; selection by `simId`, `iccid` or `operator`, re-evaluated on every SIM insert/replace. Per-direction byte caps. Existing `network_sim.global/cp` layers and golden behaviour are unchanged (they cannot reactivate a blocked SIM).

**3. Byte-aware throttling** in the existing `NetworkSimController`/pipeline: a frame occupies the link for `bytes / cap`, one at a time per direction, FIFO, deterministic (no RNG), additive to latency rules and active even when they are disabled. Queue bound = the existing pipeline budget; overflow and cancellation (`socket_closed` on link loss) are explicit.

**4. Observability**: `link` (available, reasons, effective caps, matching policies, `enforced`) in `modem.get` / the status wire; `network_sim.cellular.status` gives affected-CP counts and each governed CP's link; MCP `cellular_policy_get` / `cellular_policy_set`; timeline `cellular_link_lost`, `cellular_link_restored`, `cellular_throughput_changed` (timeline format 1.7); log lines.

Tests: resolver matrix + policy validation, bandwidth controller (size-proportional, order, direction, latency additive, overflow, cancellation), real-socket station + fake CSMS for 1.6 and 2.0.1 (suspend → stays down against connect / reconnect budget / reset, restore, start-up suspended, operator disconnect, Ethernet unaffected, policy by ICCID/operator, SIM replacement moves the station, missing SIM, timing of capped frames on the wire), daemon RPC (save/get/status/validation, later-created CP, persistence + restored CP governed), MCP parity.

## Decisions (nobody was available to ask)

| Open point | Decision | Rejected alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Toxiproxy (maintainer comment) | Keep the in-process engine as the backend: it works in the browser and the daemon with no extra infrastructure. The policy resolution is independent of how caps are enforced (`setBandwidthLimits` seam), so a proxy backend can be added later. A POC needs Docker, which this environment does not have | Building a Toxiproxy adapter / POC first |
| Policy precedence | Policies only restrict: `blocked` beats `online`, lowest cap wins, result independent of order and selector; one selector per policy | Specificity ordering with overrides (an `online` rule could reactivate a suspended/blocked SIM) |
| `no_coverage` | Reserved in docs, not simulated | A fake coverage toggle |
| Policy scope | Daemon-only store; browser Local mode honours the SIM state (gate) but has no policy store | Porting policies to the web store atoms |
| SOAP | Not gated/throttled (not a socket); link reported with `enforced: false` | Faking an outage for SOAP |
| Bandwidth accounting | UTF-8 bytes of the OCPP-J frame; no WS/TLS/TCP overhead; queue = existing 512 frames / 2 MiB budget | A new bytes-per-direction budget |
| Reset while down | `reset()` always arms its boot; sent when service returns | Dropping the reset's boot (2.x would resume silently) |
| Link-change events | One per availability or cap change, not per reason change | An event per reason change |
| Timeline | New kinds, format `1.6` → `1.7` (additive); no incident opened | Reusing `network_fault_injected` (it is a rule firing, not an outage) |
| Console | No policy editor in this PR | A UI |

## Docs (wiki)

`network-simulation.md` (new "SIM-scoped service and throttling" section, RPC table, limitations: SOAP, TCP/TLS/radio not simulated, Toxiproxy decision), `cellular-modem.md` (link state), `operational-timeline.md` (3 kinds, 1.7), `control-plane.md`, `mcp-endpoint.md`, `state-persistence.md`, `index.md`.

Closes #930

author: bikiran
body:
This makes a fortnightly clean or a monthly pool service a real repeating job, so the industry guides no longer need the repeat-bookings workaround.

## What it does
- **Repeat this job.** It's on the job page's new **Repeats** panel and works on any job with a date.
  - How often: *Every week / 2 weeks / 4 weeks / month / 3 months*, or *Custom* (every N weeks or months).
  - Ends: *Never*, *After N visits* or *On a date*.
  - A live preview shows the next dates.
- **Each visit is its own job.** Colvy makes visits about 5 weeks ahead, and always at least the next one.
  - Each visit has its own J- number and status Scheduled.
  - It copies the customer, address, team, checklist (unticked) and price.
  - It's at the same local time, including across daylight saving.
  - It's on the board, the Calendar and the team's phones like any other job.
- **The panel shows:**
  - the rule and end, and "this is visit N";
  - the visits coming up, as links;
  - what comes after.
- **Change.** The change applies from this visit on. Later visits nobody has started are called off and replaced, a visit already in progress is kept, and new visits copy this job as it is now.
- **Stop.** No more visits are made. You can also call off the upcoming visits nobody has started, which takes them off the Calendar too.
- **Daily cron.** `/api/cron/repeat-jobs` (guarded by `CRON_SECRET`, added to `vercel.json` and the platform-admin jobs list) keeps every series topped up and finishes series that reach their end.
- **Board and calendar** mark repeating visits with ↻. The board list still loads before V435 is run.
- **Permissions.** Field staff limited to their own jobs can't set or stop repeats.

## Database: `migrations/COLVY_V435_REPEATING_JOBS.sql` (after V427/V428)
- `job_repeats` holds the series: rule, start day and time, duration, what each visit copies, `last_seq`, and active/ended.
- `jobs.repeat_id` and `jobs.repeat_seq`, with a unique index on `(repeat_id, repeat_seq)`.
- Each visit is claimed by compare-and-set on `last_seq` before it's made, so two runs never make the same visit twice.
- Server-only, like V427: RLS on, no anon/authenticated grants.

## Tested
- **V428 + V435 on a real Postgres 16.** The migration runs clean and re-runs safely. A duplicate `(series, visit)` is refused and `every_n = 0` is refused. Deleting a series keeps its visits (`repeat_id` is set to null). anon has no access, and RLS is on.
- **Date maths: 13 checks.**
  - fortnight steps, including across the new year;
  - months keep the day or clamp (31 Jan → 28 Feb → 31 Mar), quarterly across years, leap years;
  - bad rules refused;
  - "after N" and "until a date" (inclusive) ends;
  - labels.
  - Plus a daylight-saving check: 7:00am stays 7:00am local across April.
- **End to end** against the mock DB with a production build: 34/34 checks pass.
  - Refusals: no date, nonsense rule, end date before the first visit, restricted staff.
  - Set up from the dialog: series fields, visits 2 and 3 made (visit 4 not yet), the right dates and local time; customer, address, team, price, checklist, Calendar entry and own job numbers all copied.
  - Panel contents.
  - The cron: no-op when nothing is needed, refills a missing visit exactly once, finishes a "2 visits" series, needs the secret.
  - Board marks.
  - Change to weekly: the in-progress visit is kept, the untouched one is called off, new weekly visits made.
  - Stop with call-off: visits cancelled and their Calendar entries cancelled; a stopped series makes nothing.
  - No page errors, and the net trap saw no outside requests.
- `tsc` clean, marketing route test passes, `next build` passes.

**Gate at 85e3c80d4906a756f48681431479bba3fae129ec (this thread's cloud container, full clone).** typecheck exit 0 (12 GB heap); eslint exit 0 on the 3 code files; prettier exit 0 on all 6 changed files; zero-dice exit 0 (nothing new); tests exit 0, 124 of 124: src/director/bribe-wanted-named.test.ts (new; Yigo, Guam, pinned draw `bribe-wanted:0`), bribe-offer-scene, bribe-pressed-scene, bribe-offer-player-seat, src/core2/pending-bribe-not-reported, src/bench/printed-bribe-offer and tests/english-parts-banks; `npx vitest run --dir . tests/guards --maxWorkers=2` 151 of 152, the one red is current-pointers (red on the train and main, none in this PR's files); `npm run guards` exit 0, all 20; `release:check --mode pr` exit 0, OK at 85e3c80; `npm run pool -- --check` lists one old item not in this PR (standin-story-read-talk-moves-views).

Nothing you can see yet. This is the read the lines need. Today a person offering you money says only "this" or "the contract", and your refusal answers a favor nobody named, on 159 bribe paths (the Words lead's scene-path gaps). After this, the offer, the refusal and the pressing records carry what the money is for, and the scene can say it: "the highways contract" for an award, or the bill for a vote.
