author: surrealroad
body:
Closes #812. Two behaviours most animated data visuals need, built as shared helpers instead of per-family code. This is part of the data-visuals phase of Pixerate/surreal-ui#47, and it follows the page kit (#868), which now carries them too.

### Draw-on in pieces (`@pixerate/editor/animation`, `animation/draw.ts`)
- `drawPieces(pieces, { total, at, span, ease })`: each piece is `{ from, to }` along a shared line length. Without `total`, the length is the furthest `to`.
  - `drawAt(p)` gives each piece `{ visible, length, fraction, dasharray, shown }`, so the pieces draw on as one continuous stroke. Pieces may overlap or leave gaps.
  - It is frame-pure, and `p = 1` is exactly the line at rest.
  - `shown` is false while nothing of a piece is drawn, because round caps draw a dot for a zero-length dash (see GOTCHAS).
- `ease` is any animation easing (names, cubic-bezier, spring, elastic) or a function. The head is clamped, so a spring's overshoot can't run past the line.
- `windows` gives each piece's start and end in the overall progress, found by bisection.
- `drawPiecesToFlair(plan, pieces, durationMs)` exports Flair draw-ons (`{ id, delay, ms, draw: true, ease: 'linear' }`). It is exact for a linear line. For an eased line, each piece matches the curve only at its ends.

### Linked focus (`@pixerate/editor/tools`, `interaction/linkFocus.ts`)
- **The model:** `createLinkFocus({ marks, links, order, labels, dim })` is headless. Each mark has keys: `[item]`, `[tag]`, or `[item, tag]` for a link. Focusing a key puts that key and every key linked to it, either way, in focus. A mark is lit when all of its keys are in focus, so a link lights only when both its ends do. This covers one-to-many and many-to-many.
- **Keyboard:** the arrows walk `order`, wrapping, by default every key that has a mark of its own. Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape clears. This is the same idea as the chart's keyboard walk.
- **Screen readers:** `describe()` gives a sentence such as "Data, 7 of 9: linked to 3 others, Beacon, Cinder, Ember."
- **Pure version:** `linkFocusLit(marks, links, key)`.
- **Errors:** unknown keys throw, and the message names the keys that exist.
- **React:** `useLinkFocus` returns `markProps(key)` (pointerenter and focus) and `rootProps` (keydown, pointerleave, and blur that clears only when focus leaves the picture). It also gives `opacity(i)` and `description`.
- **Svelte:** `linkFocusOf` does the same with runes: `mark(key)`, `root`, `opacity`, `description`.
- **Dimming:** `dim` sets how far marks out of focus fade. Hosts pass their theme's value; the default is 0.25.

### Also
- **Page kit 1.1.0:** `drawPieces`, `linkFocus` and `linkFocusLit` are in `window.pixerateKit`, with rows in the guide. The kit is now 49.7 kB of its 60 kB budget.
- **Swift:** `DrawPieces`, `drawPiecesToFlair`, `LinkFocusModel` and `linkFocusLit` are in PixerateCore. `DrawLinkFocusTests` checks them against `Fixtures/draw-link-vectors.json`, recorded from the TS by `swift-draw-link-vectors.test.ts`. SwiftUI bindings are marked Planned (#533) in the parity row.
- **Demo:** a **Linked focus** view on the Page kit tab shows five projects and four skills, many-to-many. It responds to hover and arrow keys, Escape clears, a live region gives the description, and a draw-on replay uses `drawPieces` per link.
- **Docs:** a parity row, and a mention in the pixerate-chart skill's sandboxed-pages note.

### Tests
- **Core:** pieces draw as one continuous stroke at 201 sampled values of p, with no gaps or overlaps (the visible lengths add up to the head's position, and only one piece is partly drawn). `p = 1` is at rest, frames depend on p alone, `at`/`span` and windows are covered, and a spring stays inside the line. Bad pieces are refused, and the Flair export is checked.
- **linkFocus:** truth tables for one-to-many and many-to-many, state and subscriptions, opacities, the keyboard walk, descriptions, and the `order` checks.
- **React** (jsdom: hover via pointerover and pointerout, keys, focus and blur) and **Svelte** binding tests.
- **Page kit:** a smoke test of the new exports. The guide-versus-exports check still passes.
- **Run locally:**
  - `pnpm build` and `pnpm test`: 727 files, 10,090 tests, all pass;
  - the contracts, conformance and page-kit checks are up to date;
  - `swift build --build-tests`, and `swift test --filter DrawLinkFocusTests` passes.
- **Demo, checked in the browser:** hover and the arrow keys light the right marks, with the description in the live region. The draw-on ends with every link whole. I couldn't watch it mid-animation because the preview pane was hidden and the browser throttles animation frames; the unit tests cover the in-between frames.

This PR is AI-drafted and needs human review before merging.

author: miguelperezcolom
body:
Fixes the GA round-2 security blockers **J1, J2, J3** and the should-fixes **J4, J5** (`design/ga-review-2/1-security.md`).

## J1 (blocker, Java + .NET + Python): YAML route `access:` only held for the exact spelling in `routes.yaml`
**Root cause.** The access check matched the route as the caller sent it. A route that no authored entry answers was served by convention from `specs/ui/<route>.yaml`. So the layout file's own path (`/pages/user` for `backoffice/users/:id`), a dot segment (`/hello/../admin`, `/./admin`, `%2e%2e`), a backslash, or a case variant (`/Admin` on a case-insensitive file system) served a restricted definition-only page and proxied its server-held calls (`${secret.X}`). The ports could also read a `.yaml` outside the specs directory.
**Fix (identical in the three backends).**
- A route with a `.`/`..` segment (also percent-encoded) or a backslash is refused with 403 before any lookup, and the spec loaders never read one (`hasUnsafeSegments` / `HasUnsafeSegments` / `has_unsafe_segments`).
- When a path is served by convention, the `access:` of every authored entry whose definition is that file applies, along with the entry's ancestors. The file is either the entry's `layout:` or the convention file of its route, and the match ignores case (`refusingByDefinition` / `RefusingByDefinition` / `refusing_by_definition`).
- .NET and Python: a convention path must resolve under the specs directory.

**Tests.** The review's table is run as a load and as a `__restfetch__` of the page's proxied action: `YamlRouteSpellingAccessSyncTest`, `RouteSpellingAccessTests`, `test_route_spelling_access.py`. All failed before the fix. Existing type-binding tests that sent a dot-segment route now expect the refusal.

## J2 (blocker, Java): dotted state keys wrote past field access rules
**Root cause.** The reflective writer followed `pay.salary` through the parent's getter and checked only the leaf. On a CRUD save the map is built as the server, so not even the leaf was checked.
**Fix.** The client never sends dotted keys: nested forms travel as maps or as flattened `a-b` keys. They are now dropped by the `Hydrater`, by `FieldAccess.writable` and by `ClientWritableFields.restrict`.
**Tests.** `DottedAndHeldStateSyncTest` (view action and AutoCrud save). It failed before the fix.

## J3 (blocker, Java): client state was written into beans a view holds
**Root cause.** For a `final` or `@Inject` field, `ActualValueExtractor` poured the client's map into the held object. It set every editable field and nulled the missing ones, so a shared store or service changed for every later request.
**Fix.**
- A final or injected field is never written from client state.
- The one exception is a declared sub-form: a final `@Inline` field of an application type. It is updated in place with the keys that were sent, under the same field rules.
- Held dependencies (injected fields, and final fields typed by an interface or abstract class) are left out of the state sent to the browser.

**Tests.**
- `DottedAndHeldStateSyncTest`: a shared bean in a `final` field, a getter-exposed bean, an `@Inject` field, and the read side. It failed before the fix.
- `FinalNestedAndWideNumbersHydrationTest` now marks its in-place sub-form `@Inline`, and pins that a final field that is not declared a sub-form is never written.

## J4 (should-fix, Java + Python Y3a): the union of locks depended on the wire `serverSideType`
**Root cause.** `foreignBindingsOf` keyed on the wire name. At the `@UI` route of a class that `routes.yaml` also binds, a request naming no type (in Python, also a garbage type) skipped the locks of the class's YAML routes.
**Fix.** The decision now uses the type that runs: the named type, otherwise the class the route resolves to. Java checks this only when authored routes bind some view model.
**Tests.** `YamlRouteTypeBindingSyncTest`, `test_route_type_binding.py`. Both failed before the fix.

## J5 (should-fix, Java): the read filter followed declared types only
**Fix.** `FieldAccess` now also walks `Map<String,X>` values, `X[]` and `Optional<X>`. The state read walk (`ComponentState`, `StateMapper`) follows the runtime class of each nested value, so a `Derived` held in a `Base` field or list is filtered by `Derived`'s own rules.
**Test.** `ReadFilterShapesSyncTest`. It failed before the fix.

## Verified
- `mvn install -pl shared/core`: 3046 tests pass and the coverage gate is met.
- Adapter tests (`mvn verify` on MVC, WebFlux, Micronaut, Quarkus and Helidon MP core): all pass.
- .NET `dotnet test`: 2261 pass.
- Python `pytest`: 2495 pass.

## Not covered here
- **J3 read side:** a `final` field of a concrete class with a getter is still serialised to the browser. It can no longer be written from client state. Removing it from the state would break immutable entities, whose constructor reads it from the CRUD-save baseline.
- **Java J1 rows:** the dot-segment and case rows did not reproduce through the test's `URLClassLoader` overlay before the fix. The layout-path row did, and all rows are guarded now.
- **Untouched:** .NET D2–D9, Python Y2/Y4–Y6, and the client findings C1–C4.

author: bunsdev
body:
## Context

- Summary: The daemon answers a request as soon as it has read the request line, the headers and the declared body, then closes the connection without waiting for the client's half-close. When that close lands first, macOS fails `shutdown(Write)` with `ENOTCONN` (os error 57), although the whole response is still queued for reading; Linux reports success. `daemon::tests::unix_serve_loop_isolates_per_connection_errors` failed this way under load, and three production Unix clients return the same error even though the daemon answered.
- Refs #1641.

## Reproduction (macOS 27.2.1 arm64, 18 CPUs)

- Standalone programs with explicit ordering and no timing (`repro.rs`, `pair.rs` in the evidence folder): when the peer has written its response and closed before the half-close, `shutdown(Write)` returns `NotConnected` (os error 57) and the full response is still read afterwards; when the peer closed without answering, the read returns 0 bytes.
- Which call fails: a temporary build that labelled each half-close in the test failed 32 of 54,000 runs, **27 at the malformed request's `bad.shutdown` and 5 at the health probe's `good.shutdown`**. Fixing only the malformed-request side would have left about one failure in six.

| Test binary | Load | Runs | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfixed (`2ea2d6ab`) | 72 concurrent loops × 750, the #1641 test | 54,000 | 35, all os error 57 |
| unfixed | 24 loops × 25 × the four daemon socket tests | 2,400 | 1, os error 57 |
| fixed | 72 loops × 750, the #1641 test | 54,000 | 0 |
| fixed | 24 loops × 25 × the four daemon socket tests | 2,400 | 0 |

## Implementation

- One helper per crate half-closes the request after its last byte and treats `NotConnected` as "the daemon already finished", leaving the outcome to the response read. A daemon that closed without answering still fails there (empty or incomplete response). Every other `shutdown` error is still returned. No timeout, retry or deadline is involved.
- `coven-cli`: `daemon::finish_daemon_request`, used by `post_daemon_request` (`main.rs`), `post_mobile_control_inner` (`mobile_memory/mod.rs`) and the five daemon socket tests, including both half-closes in `unix_serve_loop_isolates_per_connection_errors`.
- `coven-client`: private `transport::unix::finish_request` (the crate is published, so no new public API).
- `tests/smoke.rs`: a local copy for its two raw Unix clients.
- The test still proves that a malformed request does not end the serve loop, that the health probe then gets a real `200 OK`, and that the socket file survives; none of its assertions changed.

## Tests that fail before the fix

Four new deterministic socket-pair tests order the daemon's close before the half-close explicitly:

- `daemon::tests::finishing_a_request_after_the_daemon_answered_and_closed_keeps_the_response`
- `daemon::tests::finishing_a_request_after_the_daemon_closed_unanswered_yields_no_response` (also checks that `parse_http_status` refuses the empty response)
- `transport::unix::tests::finishing_after_the_daemon_answered_and_closed_still_reads_the_response`
- `transport::unix::tests::finishing_after_the_daemon_closed_unanswered_still_fails_the_request`

Mutation: with both helpers changed to propagate `NotConnected`, all four fail with os error 57 on macOS; restored, all four pass (`mutate.py`, `mutation.log`). Limit: on Linux they pass with or without the fix, because Linux never reports the error.

## Verification

Local gates on head `78d85323d2c908aae9c68df91ae1bd1f61e14dcb` (tree `7a79a464de747c387d4918b6960558a93c585a7c`, base `0b355398`), macOS arm64:

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`: 0
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: 0
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --locked`: 0 on the rerun, 5,806 passed, 0 failed, 28 ignored (`coven` unit binary 4,984 passed). The first run, made while a Linux VM load test shared the machine (unit binary 1,450 s instead of about 520 s), had one failure in a file this change does not touch: `api::tests::post_familiar_edits_serializes_commit_through_audit_persistence`, "timed out after 10s waiting for first direct apply to reach the pre-audit pause". The same binary then passed that test 20 of 20 times in isolation, and the full rerun passed. The first log is retained.
- [x] `python3 scripts/check-secrets.py`: 0
- [x] `check-docs-ownership.py --range` and `check-coven-privacy.py --range` against the base: 0
- [x] Full Policy guard from AGENTS.md: `Policy guard (local): 0`
- [x] New tests pass and the mutation check fails them, as described above.

## Expected textual conflicts

Small hunks in files other open work also edits: `daemon.rs` (#1731, #1674, and uncommitted work for #1736), `main.rs` (#1742, #1731, #1703, #1700) and `mobile_memory/mod.rs` (#1731, #1675). The `daemon.rs` change outside the tests is a new function after `daemon_socket_path`; the call-site edits replace one statement each.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk: low. The only behaviour change is that a client no longer fails when the daemon has already answered and closed; failures without a response are unchanged.
- Rollback: revert this commit.

Evidence (repro sources, load harness and summaries, the labelled diagnostic patch, mutation script and log, gate logs) is retained outside the repository in `coven-1641-evidence/` with `SHA256SUMS`.

author: himehiro98
body:
## 何を
運用を楽にするための設定ファイルを追加します（アプリの動作は変わりません）。

- `.github/dependabot.yml` : npm と GitHub Actions の依存更新を毎週チェック。同時に開く PR は最大 3 件、minor/patch はまとめて 1 本の PR にします
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` : PR を出すたびに `npm ci` → 型チェック（`npx tsc --noEmit`）→ `npm run build` を自動実行（Node 22、権限は `contents: read` のみ、シークレット不要）
- `CLAUDE.md` : Claude Code 向けのプロジェクトメモ（構成・起動方法・デプロイ・注意点）
- `.github/workflows/update-live-data.yml` : `actions/checkout@v4` をコミット SHA（v4.4.0 相当）に固定。このリポジトリは public のため、タグが書き換えられても影響を受けないようにする対策です

## なぜ
- 依存の更新漏れを PR で気付けるようにするため
- 壊れた変更がマージされる前に CI で気付けるようにするため
- SHA 固定は、public リポジトリでのサプライチェーン攻撃対策として一般的な方法です（Dependabot が SHA の更新も提案します）

## 確認したこと
- 追加した YAML が文法的に正しいこと
- CI と同じコマンド（`npm ci` / `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npm run build`）がローカルで成功すること（環境変数なしでビルド可能）
- SHA は `gh api repos/actions/checkout/git/ref/tags/v4` で実物を確認（`11d5960a...` = v4.4.0）

## 補足
この PR の CI 自体は、マージ後（または PR 上で初回実行）に GitHub 上で動きます。

author: richerwang228
body:
## 這次合併了甚麼

這個 PR 把三部分一起合進 `main`：

1. **`feat/deepseek-live` 的後端**（含已合併的 PR #3：PDF 提取、SQLite、會話、DeepSeek 調查工具）。之前 `main` 只有靜態前端原型。
2. **Policy Lens v3 前端**（新目錄 `v3/`），用 `npm run start:v3` 啟動，打開 http://localhost:4185 。
3. **v3 後端**（`server/v3.ts`）及對 `app.ts`、`store.ts`、`ingest/documents.ts` 的修改。

## v3 功能

- 上傳真實保單 PDF（最多 120 頁），快速預檢後出 2–3 道情境題。
- 解讀：Agent 先查條款，再流式寫出六格結論、最容易看錯的數字和邊界場景；第一張卡約 7–9 秒出現，全部約 17–21 秒；可隨時停止。
- 補充材料：附表、批單、宣傳單 PDF，或貼上顧問回覆。
- 補件與續查：列出還缺的材料；加入附表或批單後可續查，只有新材料原文作證的格子標為「已更新」。
- 自定義情景：輸入自己的情況，生成一張場景卡。
- 核對承諾：把顧問回覆和宣傳單裏的每句承諾逐條對照合同原文。
- 提問：勾選的場景和承諾寫成發給顧問的消息。

詳細說明見 `v3/README.md`。

## 修過的問題

- 解讀一直轉圈：SSE 改用 `res` 的 `close`。`req` 的 `close` 在 Node 16+ 讀完請求內容就觸發，會立即中止 Agent，並令連接一直不關閉。任務最長 150 秒。
- `No object generated`：DeepSeek 的 JSON 模式在大 schema 上常回傳空白；改為強制函數調用交結果，失敗只重試寫結論一步。
- 引文找不到原文時會標出，不再拿別的句子頂替。
- 中文輸出用繁體書面語。

## 合併 main 時的衝突

`experience.html`、`refine.css` 封面文案衝突：採用 `main` 精簡後的文案，封面不再連到舊的調查工作台（`materials.html` 仍保留）。

## 驗證

- `npm run check`、`npm run check:api`、`npm run build` 通過。
- `npm run test:api`：41/41（新增 `server/tests/v3.test.ts`）。
- 用真實 DeepSeek 和匯豐《意外萬全保》、保誠《旅遊樂》、中銀《周全家居綜合險》實測；核對承諾和續查使用模擬的顧問回覆和批單。

`.env`、資料庫和上傳文件沒有提交。

author: teddyalbina
body:
Add a Windows HIP dense Llama backend with DirectStorage/D3D12 imported weight buffers, packed Q4_0/Q8_0 GGUF computation, F16 activations and independently paged F16/Q8 KV. HF F16 loading is included; application routing and additional HF GPU formats follow separately.

Q8 KV requires exactly `DOTLLM_HIP_ALLOW_Q8_KV=1` from this first backend exposure. Actual 1K–8K qualification previously failed the original Q8 logit-error gates at every window; the flag acknowledges that loss. F16 remains the default. This PR carries the measurements and limitations with the feature.

Depends on #1807 (and #1805). This draft targets `dev`, so its GitHub diff includes unmerged prerequisites. Review the [focused prerequisite-to-head comparison](https://github.com/BlueCurveCorp/dotLLM/compare/issue/1800-packed-cpu...issue/1801-windows-hip). Extracted from `9e85fd2`, with backend gate/tests and precision documentation from `26fc9c4`/`317c5b8`.

Fresh Windows RX 6900 XT validation:
- 95 HIP/backend/file-range tests passed, no skips, with the native source rebuilt using HIP SDK 6.4 and VS2022 C++ tools.
- The same 95 passed again using the exact committed code objects.
- Nine CPU-only Q8 opt-in tests passed. OR-to-AND mutation failed five cases; removing the constructor gate failed three. Restored tests passed.
- Tests cover native numerical oracles, direct byte loading, lifetime/errors, prefill/decode/rollback and packed KV. Historical 8K results are documented; the long-context run was not repeated for extraction.

Windows only at this slice. Other GPU architectures and physical Linux GPU/storage are not qualified. This is an initial correctness path, with sequential prefill, not a throughput claim. DirectStorage has internal staging; the application provides no host-copy fallback.

Closes #1801. Related to #976, whose broader backend-parity scope remains open. Context: kkokosa/dotLLM#125.

author: regibyte
body:
Replaces #572, which conflicted with step 6 (quota and drafts) on main. Same change, rebased.

## What

Review threads have been the bundled `reviews` extension since 1.93. The core still kept an old copy of them so 1.x renderers and scripts kept working. This removes that copy. The extension stays and is now the only home of review threads.

About 1,000 lines leave `src/`: four whole files (`src/shared/reviews.ts`, `reviews-legacy.ts`, `reviews-panel.ts`, `anchors-legacy.ts`), the mod's `tower:review` alias skill, and the old fields, verbs and helpers listed below.

## What breaks, for whom

Every entry is in `docs/migrating-to-2.md`, each with what to use instead.

**Renderer and script authors** reading the board's old names:
- `card.reviews`, `card.threadState`, `card.unseen`, `card.checkoutState.filed`, the card's `note` and `review` verbs, `floor.threads`, `floor.tidy.threads`. Use the extension's parts: `card.x.reviews.*`, `floor.x.reviews.threads`, and the reviews entries in `board.adds`.
- The tidy plan's and reply's `threads`, and the discard reply's `thread`. Use `plan.x.reviews`, the reply's `x.reviews` and `done.reviews`.
- The verb `review/append`, the read `GET /reviews/<project>` and the module `/reviews.js`. Use `reviews/append`, `GET /reviews/history/<project>` and `/x/reviews/reviews.js`.
- `reviewerOf`, `threadCheckoutOf`, `pairLine` and `whereLine` of `/cards.js`, and the reviews panel and anchors of `/panels.js`. Use the extension's client and views (`reviews/thread`, `reviews/checkout-thread`, `reviews/composer`).
- The reviews extension's own deprecated `REVIEW_SKILL`, `reviewPrompt` and `reviewedIn`. This is a change to the extension's contract.

**Everyone with a config**:
- A config holding `keys.pane-reviews` is now refused. `tower config check` names the line to write instead: `"reviews/thread": <value>`. If `reviews/thread` is set too, it says to remove `pane-reviews`.

**Scripts reading the CLI**:
- `tower agents` and `tower agent` no longer print "reviews X". A reviewer's line reads "in X's crew, by reviews". RegiByte picked this in wave C §4.1, option A.

**Old reviewers and old links**:
- A worker spawned before 1.95 on the prompt `/tower:review <CALLSIGN>` logged no reviewer facts. It no longer reads as a reviewer: no crew edge by reviews, no exemption from the hiring limits, and its thread is its own checkout's. Reviewers are known only by the facts `reviews/hire` logs at spawn.
- The page's `#<id>/reviews` short link opens the worker's card without the thread tab, since `pane-reviews` held that name. The grammar form `#v/tower/card/card%3A<id>;reviews/thread` opens it.

## How

- The board, dispatch, http routes, `LEGACY` and `bridge/legacy.ts` lose every reviews row, and `LEGACY` loses its now-empty `action` kind.
- With reviews' rows gone, the moved-route helpers that served them (the dispatch's `legacy`, the http `legacyRead`, the flows' `moved`) have no users and go. The `LEGACY` applier tables are now empty.
- The keymap loses `pane-reviews` and the deprecated-command machinery that only it used. A small retired-id table turns the old key into a refusal.
- The extension now defines its own `reviews/append` input and reply types. It used to borrow them from the core's `review/append`.
- `test/served-exports.json`, `board.schema.json` and the Tower 3D fixtures were regenerated.

## Tests

Tests were removed or rewritten to the extension's names:
- `test/reviewers.test.ts` and the legacy cases in `legacy.test.ts`, `keymap.test.ts` and `server.test.ts`.
- The desk fixture's reviewer now logs its facts the way `reviews/hire` does, so those server tests still exercise a reviewer's thread.
- One keymap case now checks the `pane-reviews` refusal. It replaces the three cases that checked the alias.

No new test files were added.

## Checked

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (833 pass after the rebase), `npm run tower3d`, `test:tower3d-boot`, `test:page-boot`.
- `kb verify` and `verify --since origin/main`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `tool:frames` recorded before (on main) and after, on every fixture board: identical. No visual change, so no screenshots.
- Not yet run: the hand check with real Claude workers ("get yourself reviewed", "review X"). It is set up on a sandbox for the maintainer. The extension's server tests cover appending, reading, resolving, hiring and Tidy through the extension.

author: futin
body:
`/kaizen skill <name> [N]` reviews the last N (default 50) finished sessions that ran one skill and turns them into ranked, evidenced improvements to that skill, plus one lesson in the log. Until now this was a throwaway script written per review; the counting half is now `kaizen.mjs --skill`, the judgement half a SKILL.md mode.

Subsystem doc: `docs/subsystems/analytics.md` (new `--skill` bullet)

## What's new

- Kaizen can now review the recent runs of a single skill: how each run ended, what every run pays before its first turn, which errors keep coming back and what fed the context, then suggests ranked fixes to the skill.

## Why this shape

A mode, not a new skill: kaizen already parses transcripts and owns the lesson log, and a mode adds a few words to one `description` where a new skill would add a whole listing entry to every session's preload (skill listings were ~7.5k of the ~55k first-turn context in the backlog-tick review below).

Deterministic vs judgement split: finding the runs, token splits, preload sizing, error grouping and sinks are code (tested, repeatable); deciding what an outcome *means* stays with the model, because every skill's contract differs. The bridge is `--outcome <regex>`: the model reads the skill's contract (a verdict JSON line, a PR URL) and hands the analyzer one capture group, so the tally and per-outcome medians come out deterministic too.

Lessons log under `[skill:<name>]` with cohort **medians**, not sums: a sum in a project's series would read as one enormous session and trip `--trend` drift; the tag gives the skill its own series instead. Rejected: tagging with the newest run's project.

## What changed

**Plugin (kaizen)**
- `kaizen.mjs --skill <name> [N] [--outcome <regex>]` / exported `reviewSkill()`: newest N transcripts by mtime whose first *typed* prompt invokes the skill (`<command-name>/x</command-name>` or plain `/x`; `plugin:name` also matches bare `/name`), transcripts written in the last 5 min skipped as possibly live. Per session: project, start, duration, args, typed-prompt count (`humanContinued`), models, turns, tokens main vs subagents by kind (reusing `analyzeSession` and `readSubagentUsage`, so message.id dedup is the existing one), first-turn context, preload by record kind (hooks keyed by hook name), tool-call counts, error count, top sinks, outcome. Summary: counts, date range, projects, models, token sums, medians, preload medians, error groups (digits/hex → N, with example ids), sinks (`Read` by basename, `Skill` by skill), outcome tally and `byOutcome` medians.
- `SKILL.md`: a fourth mode, *Skill mode*, plus the trigger in `description`.
- Tests: `test/skill-review.test.mjs` (12 cases, fixture transcripts), one more `skill.test.mjs` case pinning the mode's table row, call, lesson shape and trigger.

**Docs**
- `docs/subsystems/analytics.md`: `--skill` bullet next to `--trend` / `--compare`. `docs/overview.md`: kaizen's one-liner.

## Verification

`node --test plugin/skills/kaizen/test/*.test.mjs` → `# pass 49`, `# fail 0` (13 new). `tsx test/run-some.ts` over kaizen-trend, analyze, plugin-manifest, ci-scope, sync-plugin, outbound → `ALL PASS`. Full `pnpm test` / typecheck / build left to CI (no TS touched).

New coverage:
- Mutation-checked: dropping the live-session window, the bare-name match, the before-first-turn preload cutoff, the digit fold, the typed-prompt count or the `isMeta` exclusion each fails a test.

Verified by hand — real run, `--skill backlog-manager:backlog-tick 100 --outcome '"verdict":\s*"(\w+)"'` over 2,219 transcripts in 6.9 s (2026-11-14):
- outcomes idle 43 · execute 30 · groom 16 · busy 10 · recover 1 — matches the hand review from the backlog-manager session.
- median first-turn context 55.6k (preload attributable ≈ 33k: system prompt 12.2k, skill listing 7.5k, instructions 5.6k, agent listing 2.2k, skill body 2.1k); idle runs median 20k billable / 14 s, execute 223k / 11.6 min.
- top error group: the same Bash failure in 14 runs.

**Not verified, and it needs a human:**
- The SKILL.md mode end to end — a fresh session following *Skill mode* literally (classification, ranking, lesson append). Only the analyzer half was run.
- The Analytics tab showing a `[skill:<name>]` lesson: the parser accepts the tag by its regex, but no such line has been rendered.
- Reaching sessions needs `pnpm plugin:sync` after merge (the installed plugin is a snapshot).

## Known limits

- `--compare` cannot judge a `[skill:…]` lesson (no project dir); review mode gives it the recurrence check only, and a later `/kaizen skill` run shows whether figures moved.
- Preload sizes are chars ÷ 4 over the text-bearing fields of each record; the gap to the measured first-turn context is mostly tool schemas, which the transcript does not record.

## After merge

- `pnpm plugin:sync` once on `main`.

author: xeiculy
body:
## 背景

保存のボタンは「保存する」の1つだけで、押すとその場に留まる。一覧へ戻る道は画面の上のリンクだけなので、問題を書き終えたあとに上まで戻る手間があった。保存の流れには `useBlocker` との順序の落とし穴があるので、画面の外の hook に出し、画面なしで確かめられるようにする。成功は toast（#287）、失敗は帯の `ActionError`（#288）で知らせる（#283 の方針）。

## 変更内容

- `useQuestionSetSave({ setId, draft })` を足した。mutation・最後に保存できた下書き（`savedDraft`）・`dirty`・`useBlocker` を持ち、`save(input, intent)` を返す。#290 で POST/PUT の分かれ道を `mutationFn` に足す
- 保存できたら `flushSync(() => setSavedDraft(sent))` → `notify` → `'list'` なら `/admin` へ、の順にした。`useBlocker` は `disabled` を effect で読むので、ただの set のあとすぐ移ると止められて確かめが出る。`flushSync` を外すと hook のテストが落ちることを確かめた
- `ignoreBlocker` は使わない。送ったときの下書きを `sent` に取るので、保存のあいだに打った分は `dirty` のまま残り、「保存して一覧へ」でも確かめが出る
- 保存の帯のボタンを「保存する」（outline）と「保存して一覧へ」（主）にした。誤りがあれば、どちらでも送らず移らない
- 成功は「「名前」を保存しました」の toast だけにし、帯の「保存しました」（`role="status"`）を消した（2回読まれるため）
- e2e と撮影スクリプトを「保存して一覧へ」に変え、`host-edit-set`・`host-create-room` を撮り直した。ほかの画像は部屋 ID や回答時間で変わるだけなので入れていない。使い方の文と alt、frontend.md を直した

## テスト方法

1. `make check` と `make e2e` が通ることを確かめる
2. `pnpm --filter @zubatto-quiz/web run e2e:serve` で開き、ホストとしてログインする（2026-11-14 に Playwright MCP で確かめた）
3. 問題セットを作り、名前を変えて「保存する」を押す。その場に留まり、右下に toast が出る
4. もう一度名前を変えて「保存して一覧へ」を押す。確かめなしで一覧へ移り、新しい名前と toast が見える
5. 名前を空にして「保存して一覧へ」を押す。誤りが出て、移らない
6. 390×844 で、帯のボタンが折り返して横にはみ出さない

body:
In the *Installation* tab, the detail panel of a PV array or system gets *Belongs to* (and *Battery belongs to* for a system with a battery) plus *Save assignment*. A part moves to another system, or a system under another parent or on its own, without opening its form.

- `systems.owners` / `systems.moved` (core): where a part can go, with the same rules as the forms. `part_owners` and `parent_owners` are now shared with `config_flow.py`.
- New admin websocket command `noxcast/move_part`: it updates the subentry (the entry reloads through its update listener) and answers with this entry's installation. `noxcast/installation` gains `entry_id` and `moves` (additive, so the schema version stays).
- A system moved to the top level drops `phase`, as its form does.

Tier: Interface

author: catborise
body:
Two commits.

**refactor(vrtManager): a new VM's copy of a template is made by clone_volume**
`clone_from_template` wrote its own copy XML next to `wvmStorage.clone_volume`, which the volume and VM clones use. `clone_volume` now takes the volume to copy (of its pool or another), so the template copy goes through it as well; `clone_from_template` is three lines. User-visible: a qcow2 template's copy in a file pool is named `<vm>.qcow2`, like a new empty disk, not `<vm>.img` (create recovery already knows all four names).

**fix(vrtManager): a copy into an LVM or RBD pool is raw and allocated whole**
Found while checking the refactor live: a new VM from a qcow2 template into an LVM pool failed on master too.
1. The copy asked for qcow2 with qcow2's options: libvirt refuses that there ("compatibility option only available with qcow2").
2. Made raw, it still failed: with no allocation libvirt makes a sparse LVM volume, a snapshot that the copy filled; the kernel invalidated it ("Invalidating snapshot: Unable to allocate exception", I/O error at byte 0).

A copy into a pool of no files is now raw, as big as its source and allocated whole, as `create_volume` already makes a new empty volume there.

Not changed: a `disk` (partition) pool. Codex pointed out that libvirt refuses format `raw` there; checked live, but the panel cannot create a volume or a copy in such a pool at all, before and after this change: libvirt wants the next partition's name (`vdb1`), not the name the panel gives.

Checked:
- live on a Vagrant compute (TCP): a qcow2 template copied by `clone_from_template` into its own dir pool (`.qcow2`, lazy_refcounts) and into an LVM pool on `/dev/vdb` (raw LV of the source size; failed before the fix); host inventory unchanged
- live tests with LVM and NFS: `test_live_jobs` (volume clone, VM clone, create from template), `test_live_lvm`, `test_live_clone`, `test_live_create`, `test_live_views`, `test_live_pools`: 98 OK, 4 skipped
- full suite: 2365 tests, only the 13 local environment checks in `webvirtcloud.tests` fail (master too); `ruff check .` clean
- Codex review: the `disk` pool finding above; clean after that

body:
## What changed

In standard Russian the preposition is "во" only in the fixed phrase "во имя" ("во имя моё"). With a possessive before "имя" it is "в": "в моё имя". 23 Russian renderings had "во {{deity_pronoun:моё|Моё}} имя" or "во … твоё … имя". This PR changes only that preposition and leaves the setting spans and all other wording as they were.

- Deuteronomy 18:19, 18:20 (Literal, Balanced)

- Matthew 7:22 (Readable), 18:20 (Literal, Balanced)
- John 14:13, 14:14, 14:26, 15:16, 16:23, 16:24, 16:26 (Balanced, Readable)

Applies the Signal design language to **admin** and **backoffice** with the SmartCoder palette. Lime stops being the base colour and becomes the accent only.

This is a re-skin through tokens and shared components. Routes, data, permissions and contracts do not change.

## Palette roles

| Role | Light | Dark (OKLCH-derived) | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Structure | ink `#111114`, charcoal `#101114` | foreground `#f2f4f7` on charcoal `#101114` | text, frame, neutrals |
| Primary action | forest `#356b26`, white text | `#7fbe6f`, ink text | filled primary buttons, checked controls |

author: boeboe
body:
A patch release on v0.7.0. No exported identifier is added, removed or changed.

What changes:
- scanner: a Forward_Open reply whose O->T connection ID is 0 is refused with `ErrProtocol` and closed at the target, as for the actual packet intervals v0.7.0 checks. `OnState` may call `IO.Close` and `Scanner.Close`, with Reconnect too; its goroutine and re-entry contract is documented. Reopen delays have equal jitter. A `Close` while `Open` waits for its reply leaves nothing running; of concurrent `IO.Close` calls, one closes.
- client: `Conn.Close` fails the request in flight with `ErrClosed` at once; a request whose write fails returns within its context; requests in flight during `Client.Close` fail with `ErrClosed`, as documented; a dialer that returns no connection and no error fails with `ErrConnectFailed`.
- server: an inactivity timeout set to 0 at run time clears the sessions' read deadline. The lifetime of the data passed to `ServeCIP`, `Attribute.Set`, `ServiceFunc` and `SymbolHandler` is documented.
- eds: `Parse` bounds sections (16384) and fields in the file (1048576).

Tests: the L1–L16 lifecycle matrix in TESTING.md with tests for concurrent Close, Close during a read or a write, callbacks that call methods and Close, and Open racing Close; goroutine leak checks in client, server, implicit and scanner; allocation-budget tests for the cip, encap and implicit decoders, eds.Parse and the server's handling of replies beyond their budget. These measure per call over many calls, the way `testing.AllocsPerRun` counts, with no other goroutine of the module running, against budgets derived from what the code must hold; this makes `TestCPFAllocationBudget`, which failed on ubuntu-24.04 in #29 with one measured call, deterministic. Fuzz targets for the Forward_Open and Forward_Close replies and connection failures; `make fuzz` discovers its targets; a nightly GOARCH=386 job; `BenchmarkConsume` measures delivery to the callback, with a new figure in TESTING.md.

Documents: RELEASE.md (v0.7.1), TESTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/LIMITATIONS.md, docs/IMPLICIT.md, docs/EDS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/FEATURE-STATUS.md, docs/api.

Not in this change: recovering handler failures at the library boundary (a behaviour change, for a minor release).

This pull request was first opened for a v0.6.1; v0.7.0 (#28) was released in the meantime, so it is now merged onto v0.7.0, keeps v0.7.0's implementation wherever both fixed the same thing, and targets v0.7.1.

Checked independently: `make check`, otfabric-policy compliant, gorelease (v0.7.1 valid against v0.7.0), the regression tests fail on the v0.7.0 code, linux/386 test run.

author: akojif
body:
Closes #126 (tagging), Stage 3, slice 4. Your real run with Haiku 5.5 is in, and the cost estimate is calibrated on it (below). Tuning the instructions comes later, on the dev split, once the labels are in (#129), as decided.

## What changed and why

- **The send button works:**
  - It needs a key (or an Ollama model), and, if names weren't checked, the confirmation. When something is missing, it says what.
  - It sends exactly the consent step's payload: batches of 25 texts, 2 requests at a time, all through `sendAiRequest`, so every request is logged with its bytes.
  - **Anthropic:** the instructions as the system prompt, the batch's ids and texts as JSON, and structured output held to `ANSWER_SCHEMA` at low effort.
  - **Ollama:** the same schema as its `format`.
- **Every answer is checked** (`core/ai/tagging.ts`) before anything is kept:
  - **Shape:** an answer that isn't the agreed shape gets one retry, then its texts count as "not analysed".
  - **Texts left out** of an answer get one more try, alone.
  - **Cut off** (`max_tokens`): the batch is split in two and both halves are sent.
  - **Quotes:** a quote has to appear word for word in its text, ignoring only spaces and line breaks. **When it doesn't, the tag is kept and the quote dropped,** as decided; dropped quotes are counted and shown.
  - **Labels** holding a placeholder such as `[NAME_1]` are dropped and counted.
- **The run** (`core/ai/run.ts`, plain code):
  - When the provider is busy, it waits as asked (`retry-after`, when the browser can read it) or backs off (2, 4, 8, 16 s), then pauses.
  - A key or access problem pauses it at once, with the reason.
  - **Cancel** starts no new batch and lets the requests already in flight finish, keeping their answers. So **Resume never sends a text twice**, and nothing already paid for is lost. (The first version threw such answers away; the resume unit test caught it.)
- **On screen:** a progress bar with "150 of 200" and Cancel. Then "Analysed 200 cleaned texts with Claude Haiku 5.5", with the dropped quotes and texts not analysed, or the reason it paused and Resume. Results stay in memory, keyed by item, for merging (slice 5). A new review or Start over clears them.
- **`npm run try:tagging`:** the real analysis on the sample file, from Node, with the same code.
  - With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: about three US cents with Haiku 5.5.
  - With `-- --provider ollama`: no cost.
  - It prints the tokens reported against the estimate, plus dropped quotes and texts not analysed.
- **Strings:** run strings in `analyze.json`, both languages. The consent step's placeholder line "Sending comes with the next part" is gone.
- **Plain `fetch`:** the Anthropic API reference prefers its SDK, but that would be a new dependency, which is your call. Say if you want it.

## A real run, with Ollama

I ran the sample through the real pipeline against llama3.2:3b on this Mac. 200 texts took 6 minutes. Results:
- 131 analysed and **69 not analysed** (left out of answers even after the retry);
- 392 jobs, pains and gains;
- **227 quotes dropped,** because the small model paraphrases.

This shows the checks keep invented quotes out of reports. It also shows a 3B model is fine for testing the setup but too weak for analysis; that's noted in the docs. The token comparison isn't meaningful with Llama's tokenizer, so the estimate check used your Anthropic run.

## A real run, with Anthropic (yours, 2026-11-14)

Claude Haiku 5.5 on the sample: **200 of 200 analysed, no quote dropped,** 386 jobs, pains and gains, in 98 s. Anthropic reported 21,652 tokens in and 53,580 out, **$0.0290**.

**The estimate was about three times too low** ($0.006 to $0.012), which failed the ±30% criterion. Two costs weren't counted:
- **Input:** each request carries the answer schema, which Anthropic adds to the prompt for structured output: about 1,700 tokens per batch on top of the instructions.
- **Output:** about 270 tokens per text, not 80. Most of it is the model's thinking (adaptive, on by default even at low effort).

**Fixed in 3eafd81:** for Anthropic, `core/ai/cost.ts` now adds both. On the sample it estimates 21,696 in and 54,000 out, **$0.020 to $0.038**, which holds the real $0.029. A unit test pins the measured run inside the range. Ollama keeps the plain estimate; it's free, and its tokens weren't measured with a comparable tokenizer.

Limits, also in the code and docs:
- Calibrated on **one run with Haiku 5.5**. Sonnet 5.5 isn't measured and may think more per text.
- Switching thinking off would cut the output cost by most of it, but might lower quality. That decision waits for the dev baseline (#129).

## How it was tested

- **`tests/unit/tagging.test.ts`** (14 tests):
  - request shapes for both providers, and the schema forbidding extra fields;
  - reading answers (cut off, refused, broken) and usage;
  - quote checks;
  - keeping a tag while dropping a bad quote;
  - placeholder labels, unknown and repeated ids, texts left out, and wrong shapes;
  - 2 at a time and token totals;
  - the retry, then "not analysed";
  - splitting a cut-off batch;
  - `retry-after` and backoff, then pausing;
  - pausing on an invalid key;
  - **cancel and resume without sending a text twice**.
- **`tests/e2e/tagging.spec.ts`** (4 tests; Playwright stands in for Anthropic):
  - **the requests together hold exactly the downloaded payload** (same model, the instructions as system, every text once, in order), nothing is sent before the click, and the summary counts the dropped quote;
  - the button waits for the key and the names confirmation;
  - an invalid key pauses with the reason, and Resume sends only what's left, never a text twice;
  - Cancel lets the requests in flight finish and sends nothing new, and Resume completes without duplicates.
- `npm run verify`: all 7 steps pass (776 unit tests, 234 end-to-end tests with 1 skipped, name accuracy check).

## Screenshots

To attach: the finished run.

author: jared-woodruff
body:
## What this changes

Players reported that in the original Total Annihilation, reclaiming pays the full metal value only at the end. In TA Reborn the metal came a little at a time as the work went, which made reclaiming better than TA's: its income was felt at once.

- **Features:** a wreck, rock or tree now gives all of its metal and energy when it is reclaimed whole. The work done stays on the feature if it is left unfinished, as before.
- **Own units:** one of our own units taken apart pays its metal when it is gone.
  - The refund for each step is kept on the unit as `Unit::reclaim_owed` until then. It carries across stops and restarts, and is lost with the unit if it is destroyed first.
  - The amount, and how long reclaiming takes, are unchanged.
- **Determinism:** `reclaim_owed` is part of the simulation checksum.
- **Docs:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` states the rule, and the changelog has an entry.

## How it was checked

- **A new test**, `reclaiming_pays_when_it_is_done_not_as_the_work_goes`:
  - a 60-metal rock pays nothing while it is reclaimed, and 60 when it is gone;
  - a 100-metal building taken apart in two goes, with a stop between, pays nothing until it is gone, then 100.
- The existing reclaim tests pass. They check how long reclaiming takes and its totals.
- `cargo test --release -p ta_sim -p ta_net -p ta_config`: 655 passed.
- `cargo test --release -p ta_ai --test snapshot --test skirmish`: the copied game plays on exactly as the game, and the computer players play their game.

## Compatibility

`SIMULATION_VERSION` is 96 and `ta_net::PROTOCOL` is 100, both unreleased. Saved games and replays from earlier builds play differently, and multiplayer needs every player on the same build.

author: friedrith
body:
## Summary

Makes `features-cli` installable with `brew install interaction-dynamics/tap/features`, using a shared org tap repo (`interaction-dynamics/homebrew-tap`, the same style as `hashicorp/tap` and `goreleaser/tap`).

- **Fix: GitHub releases have never had binaries attached.** The `github-release` job never downloaded the build artifacts, so `files: dist/features-*` matched nothing. Every release from v0.9.x to v0.14.0 has 0 assets, even though the release notes say "download the binary from the attachments below". The job now downloads the `cli-*` artifacts, fails if any are missing (`fail_on_unmatched_files: true`), and attaches them.
- **Checksums:** every release now gets a `checksums.txt` plus a `features-*.sha256` per asset (the `dist/features-*` glob picks both up). The release notes explain how to verify them.
- **Formula template:** `packaging/homebrew/features.rb.tmpl`
  - macOS: `features-darwin-arm64` / `features-darwin-x64`
  - Linux: the static musl builds `features-linux-{arm64,x64}-musl`, so it doesn't depend on the host glibc (see the GLIBC entry in the FAQ)
  - installs the binary as `features`; `test do` checks `features --version`
- **`packaging/homebrew/render.sh <version> <checksums.txt> [output]`** fills in the version and SHA256s. It works the same in CI and locally, validates the version, accepts text- and binary-mode `sha256sum` lines, and aborts before writing anything if an asset's checksum is missing.
- **New `homebrew-tap` job** (after `github-release`, `contents: read`):
  - downloads the published `checksums.txt` with `gh release download`
  - renders the formula
  - commits `Formula/features.rb` to `interaction-dynamics/homebrew-tap` using `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`, and does nothing if the formula is unchanged
  - if the secret is missing, every step is skipped with a `::notice::` and the release still succeeds
- Actions in the changed jobs are pinned to full commit SHAs, looked up with `gh api`:
  - `actions/checkout` v5.1.0
  - `actions/download-artifact` v7.0.0
  - `softprops/action-gh-release` v3.0.4
  
  These match the pins on the security branch.
- **Docs:** Homebrew is added to the README quick start, the website's CLI page (`projects/website/src/pages/cli.astro`), the release notes and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which gets a new "Homebrew tap" section with the release step, the required secret and how to render the formula by hand.

## Steps for a maintainer

Steps 1–3 are already done: `interaction-dynamics/homebrew-tap` exists and `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` is set.

1. ~~**Create the tap repo:**~~ `interaction-dynamics/homebrew-tap`, public, with an initial commit (e.g. a README), e.g.
   `gh repo create interaction-dynamics/homebrew-tap --public --add-readme --description "Homebrew formulae for Interaction Dynamics tools"`
   The name must start with `homebrew-` for `brew install interaction-dynamics/tap/features` to work.
2. ~~**Create a fine-grained PAT:**~~ resource owner `interaction-dynamics`, repository access *only* `homebrew-tap`, repository permission **Contents: Read and write**, nothing else. If org policy requires it, an org admin must approve the token.
3. ~~**Add the secret to this repo:**~~ `gh secret set HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN --repo interaction-dynamics/features`
4. **Seed the formula.** Wait for the next release (the first one with assets), or re-run the release workflow (`workflow_dispatch`) after merging. v0.14.0 can't be used as-is because its GitHub release has no assets. To backfill it, upload the binaries to the v0.14.0 release first, then run `render.sh` by hand and push the formula.

- ✅ **Rendered against real v0.14.0 binaries.** The GitHub release has none, so I took the 4 binaries from the published npm platform packages (`@features-cli/feature-cli-*@0.14.0`), which are built by the same workflow.

- ✅ `render.sh` edge cases: missing asset (exit 65, no output file), no args (usage, exit 64), `v`-prefixed version, binary-mode checksum lines.
- ✅ The workflow parses as YAML, and no workflow has duplicate keys (checked after the rebase).

author: haacked
body:
sbd accepted a `pr-merged` request that marks every follow-up waiting on that PR as ready. Only one integration test sent it. sb, the app, and the MCP tool server never send it. sbd accepted it without a test-clock check, so any local client on the user's socket could fire merge-triggered follow-ups by hand.

This removes the request. The poller still fires those follow-ups through `pullRequestMerged` when it sees the merge. The merge-trigger test in PollerWaitTests now checks what the old test checked. A follow-up on another PR stays put, a trigger written as a URL in different case fires once, and a later poll doesn't fire it again. FakeGitHub now matches owner and name without case, as GitHub does, so the URL in different case finds the PR. FollowupTests checks that sbd refuses `pr-merged` as an unknown request.

## Test plan

- [x] `bin/test` passes
- [x] `PollerWaitTests.aMergeTriggerFiresWhenThePollSeesThePRMerge` tests the poller path
- [x] `FollowupTests.refusesPrMergedAsAnUnknownRequest` tests the refusal

author: aryavkarthik
body:
## What this adds

You can now **buy and sell during the live session**, filling at the delayed prices shown (the owner's decision: "as if live"). This completes the `v0.1` milestone.

**Trading domain (`asxsim.trading`, pure Python, Decimal money):**
- Orders (market and limit), fills, per-order brokerage (flat, percentage or percentage with a minimum; default $10 flat), and an account ledger (cash, average cost, realised/unrealised P&L, fees).
- **ExecutionEngine** (details in ADR 0008):
  - a one-tick spread around the last trade, or the feed's bid/ask,
  - a 25% volume participation cap with partial fills,
  - ASX market-to-limit remainders and limit queue estimates,
  - opening and closing auctions, and day-order expiry,
  - rules: price steps, the $500 first parcel, no shorting, and buying power including brokerage.

**Live hub (`asxsim.live.hub`):**
- **One** price feed shared by every tab and the engine. It also keeps streaming any stock you hold or have an open order in.
- **Stale snapshot prices never fill orders.**
- The live account is saved atomically to `~/.asxsim/live_account.json`, outside the repo. A demo gets its own throwaway account.
- The WebSocket accepts `watch` / `order` / `cancel` / `reset_account` commands with replies.

**Frontend:**
- **Order ticket** with a live cost estimate and instant rule checks.
- **Account panel:** equity, cash, buying power, P&L, fees, reset.
- **Positions / Orders / Fills** tabs, with Sell all and Cancel.

## Testing

- 192 backend tests pass:
  - every fill rule on a scripted trading day (spread, partial fills, queue, trade-through, auctions, expiry, next-day orders),
  - rule rejections, persistence round-trip and corrupt-file recovery,
  - stale-snapshot safety, and the WebSocket order flow end to end.
- The frontend type-checks and builds.
- Clicked through in Chrome on the demo:
  - bought 100 BHP at the $59.22 ask (cash $44,068, net −$11 = $10 fee + 1c spread),
  - placed a $59.45 limit sell (Working, shares reserved) and cancelled it,
  - sold all at $59.30: realised +$8, fees $20, net −$12.

## Bugs caught while building

- **Liquidity estimate:** it only looked at the previous minute, so a market order after a quiet minute couldn't fill even when the current minute was busy. It now uses the busier of the two.
- **Display:** average prices showed as `59.2700`. A separate `to_view()` formats prices for display, while saved state keeps full precision.

## Not yet

Stop, stop-limit and trailing-stop orders, GTC, T+2 settlement, halts and short selling (week 2). Spread calibration against real data will follow Monday's live verification.

author: c1b3r-p3d1a
body:
### What

The byte/word placement of the "SDWA f32 rounding and frexp destinations" ops was checked by `agc_driver_sdwa_destination_f32_*` only for finite normal inputs. I measured `v_fract_f32`, `v_trunc_f32`, `v_ceil_f32`, `v_rndne_f32`, `v_floor_f32`, `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` and `v_frexp_mant_f32` on gfx1035 (Radeon 680M) with the hardware oracle. The inputs were 32 special values: signed zeros, denormals, the smallest normal, infinities, quiet and signaling NaNs with payloads, FLT_MAX and values around rounding boundaries. Every op ran in all 18 SDWA destination forms, in three float modes. Evidence: https://gist.github.com/c1b3r-p3d1a/eaeda8986a60aed75a76df22183d2d5a.

- All 12,096 SDWA results equal the test's `InsertResult` placement of the op's plain VOP1 result. So the test pins the plain results, 32 per op and mode, and checks every form through the existing placement model.
- Only the low 8 or 16 result bits reach a byte or word destination, so `IEEE_MODE`, which only sets the quiet bit of a signaling NaN result, can't be observed. The test pins the f32-denormals-kept (`FLOAT_MODE` 0xf0) and flushed (0x00) modes.
- The recompiler already matches in both modes at wave32 and wave64. No code changes.

`agc_driver_sdwa_destination_f32_wave32/64` now also run these 32 inputs through all seven ops in both modes. The kept mode needs `shaderDenormPreserveFloat32`; on a device without it (the RTX 3070 run below) it is skipped with a message, the way `F32FractFloorDenormalModes` skips its modes, and the flushed mode still runs.

No debt change: #19661 (merged) already rewrote the entry with these special-input measurements, so this PR only pins them in the test.

### Tested
<!-- OS, title or homebrew, what was checked. "Not tested" is a valid answer. A performance change: the summary lines of main and of this PR from the same machine and scene, with the traces attached, captured as the Performance report issue form describes. -->
Windows 11, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 (x86_64-ucrt-posix-seh r7), Release, AMD Radeon 680M (gfx1035), driver 32.0.21030.12001.
- Rebased on `main` `63509803a9`. All four `agc_driver_sdwa_destination*` tests pass (staged `.prx` refreshed). With the DenormPreserve 32 check forced off, the kept mode is skipped with its message and the other 14 runs still pass.
- All four `agc_driver_sdwa_destination*` tests pass. The new rows fail with each of these mutations, none of which the existing rows catch: `flushF32Denormal` never flushing (`lane 2` of `v_fract_f32`); `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` off by one on denormals; `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` returning 1 for infinities and NaNs.
- With `ANYPS5_REQUIRE_VULKAN=1 ANYPS5_NO_SHADER_CACHE=1 VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation` (SDK 1.4.363.1), `ctest -V`: pass on `main` and on this branch, 0 `VUID-` lines on both.
- `python tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes. No other open PR touches `SdwaDestination.cpp`.

body:
Version 2.0.0 of the Checkly Terraform provider no longer has nested blocks: nested settings are attributes written with `=`, and repeated blocks became list attributes with plural names. It also deprecates `checkly_check` in favor of `checkly_api_check`, `checkly_browser_check` and `checkly_multistep_check`, and `checkly_check_group` in favor of `checkly_check_group_v2`. The check and group examples only worked with version 1.x.

This PR updates `checks-groups.mdx`, `parameterized-resources.mdx` and `testing-scripts-locally.mdx` under `integrations/iac/terraform/`:

- every check example uses its per-type resource, so it validates without a deprecation warning, and the registry links point at those resources' pages
- every example uses the version 2 syntax (`retry_strategy = { ... }`, `request = { ... }`, `assertions = [ ... ]`, `alert_settings = { ... }`)
- `should_fail` is removed from the Browser and Multistep check examples, because version 2 accepts it only on API checks and monitors
- three sentences say "attribute" instead of "block"

New content for review:

- **Migrating from `checkly_check`**, a new section: change the resource type and add a `moved` block, so the check isn't recreated. It names what the provider's upgrade guide says to do before moving: `should_fail` on Browser and Multistep checks, `double_check`, and the different `checkly_api_check` defaults.
- **Migrating to `checkly_check_group_v2`** uses a `moved` block instead of `terraform state rm` and `import`. Step 1 says which `enforce_*` attributes keep the old group's behaviour, following the upgrade guide's translation table.

The version constraint changes on the overview page in #837; the Terraform PRs #837, #838, #839 and #841 belong together.

author: therealkiranda
body:
Adds renewals so subscriptions can bill beyond their first period.

- `POST /tenant/subscriptions/:subscriptionId/renew` (OWNER/ADMIN/BILLING): advances an active subscription to its next period and issues that period invoice
- Allowed only within 14 days of period end (or after), and only when the current period invoice is `PAID`
- New `Subscription.billedPeriods` counter (migration backfills 1 for started subscriptions); each period end is measured from the original start date, so a 31 January start renews to 31 March, not 28 March
- Period change and invoice are one transaction; a `billedPeriods` match guard stops two simultaneous renewals both advancing
- Body accepts only `dueInDays`; no dates or amounts from the request
- Invoice building moved to a shared `invoice-issuing.ts` used by invoice generation and renewal (no behaviour change for invoices)
- Tests and `docs/renewals.md`; existing docs cross-referenced and a stale line about `PAID` fixed

Not verified locally: Prisma engines cannot be downloaded in my sandbox, so schema validation, client generation, typecheck and tests rely on CI.

author: mzabielski
body:
Fixes #449

## What changed

### 1. Optimistic concurrency for a Project's configuration (additive)

Two new tokens. Both are optional on the request, and **neither is the Project `version`** that moves, closes, reopens and edits name:

| Writes | Token in the body | Where it is read | Moved by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PATCH …/stages/:stageId`, `PUT …/stages/:stageId/tasks` | `version` | `ProjectStage.version` (new column `project_stages.version`) | each of those writes |
| `POST …/stages`, `PUT …/stages/order`, `PUT …/moves`, `PUT …/organizations`, `PUT …/members` | `configurationVersion` | `ProjectDetail.configurationVersion` (new column `projects.configuration_version`) | each of those, and `DELETE …/stages/:stageId` |

If the body sends a token and it is stale, the write answers `409 PROJECT_CHANGED` and writes nothing; the admin then re-reads the Project, as the stage bar already does for moves. A body without a token is served as before. `SetProjectMovesResult` gains `configurationVersion`, the value after the write. Migration `20261114T153132_projects_configuration_versions` adds both columns with `default 1`. Following the platform's version-check pattern, the token is an optional precondition (`version: …optional()` — "when sent and stale → 409", as in `catalog.ts`'s product update and the CMS/blog bodies), and it is checked under the Project row lock inside the Command.

**Decision: why not the Project `version`.** I implemented that first, as the issue suggests: every configuration write took and moved `projects.version`. The backend suite showed it is a **breaking behaviour change**. `stage-tasks.test.ts` and `completion-gate.test.ts` edit a Stage and then `POST /move` with the version they read before, and they started getting `409`, as any external client written that way would. The issue also allows "a per-Stage version", and the additive split above needs no `breaking change` label. A side benefit is fewer false conflicts: editing one Stage does not refuse an edit of another Stage or a title edit. The trade-off is that a move from a read older than a workflow change is **not** refused by the version. It does not need to be: as the issue says, a move re-checks the workflow under the row lock.

### 2. `PUT /organizations` is atomic

The whole set now runs as one Command, `projects.project.organizations_set`. It locks the Project, holds and moves `configurationVersion`, re-checks links under the lock, and runs one **child Command** (`ctx.run`, spec 170 R-22) per Organization: `organization_add` / `organization_remove`. The parent records no entry of its own (`skipAudit`). The trail therefore keeps naming each Organization, exactly as `data-model.md` §2.4 lists, and a failure part-way rolls the whole set back. Because nothing new reaches the audit log, the action-name ruling the issue mentions is not needed. The audit payload keys (`organizationId`) are unchanged, so the history redaction for out-of-reach Organizations still applies.

### Admin

`StageEditor` sends the Stage's `version` on a Stage or Stage Task edit, and `configurationVersion` on adding and reordering Stages and on the workflow; it keeps the value `PUT /moves` answers. It re-reads the Project on any `409`.

Docs EN + PL (`projects.md` API section, with a *Concurrency* paragraph), `contracts/admin-api.md`, `data-model.md`, changeset (`@endora-commerce/contracts` and `@endora-commerce/mod-projects` minor, additive).

**Merge note.** This PR and #1229 (#462) each add a projects migration to `packages/modules/projects/src/migrations/index.ts` and `backend/src/db/migrations-registry.generated.ts`. Whichever merges second needs `origin/master` merged in, then `pnpm --filter backend run composer:generate`. `git merge-tree` is clean against #1216 (#454), #1227 (#452) and the #455/#457/#461 branches.

## Tests (TDD)

- `packages/contracts/src/projects.test.ts`: the optional tokens on all seven bodies, the version-only `PATCH` refused, and the new view and result fields. **Red first** against the `origin/master` schemas: `Tests 7 failed | 44 passed (51)`.
- `admin/test/modules/projects/ProjectDetail.tasks-tab.test.tsx`: a Stage edit sends the Stage version and a 409 re-reads; a reorder sends `configurationVersion`; Stage Task save sends the Stage version. **Red first** against the `origin/master` `StageEditor`/`api.ts`: `2 failed`. The two `ProjectDetail.stage-bar` deadline cases that assert the exact `PATCH` body were updated for the new field.
- `backend/test/integration/projects/configuration-versions.test.ts` (new, 15 cases): two admins on one Stage; Stage versions are per Stage; each Stage write and each set write with a stale token gives 409 and no audit row, and with the current token moves only its own token; without tokens every write works, none moves the Project `version`, and a move with the old version still succeeds; the `PUT /moves` answer; `PUT /organizations` rolls back when a part-way insert fails (FK on a stubbed "ghost" Organization) and still writes one entry per Organization. Not run red against `origin/master`: the fields do not exist there. The rejected first design did go red in `stage-tasks`/`completion-gate`, as described above.
- `backend/test/contract/projects/projects.contract.test.ts`: the `PUT /moves` answer now includes `configurationVersion`. `migration.test.ts`: the new columns are in the column lists.

## Local verification (D-198: the backend suite does not run on this PR)

```

  test/integration/projects/ test/contract/projects/ test/unit/db/migrations-registry.test.ts

## Follow-up commits

- The Polish page's pin (`docs/translation-cache/pl/…projects.md.json`) was re-pinned with `docs:translations:pin` after the English page changed; `check:docs-translations` had reddened `quality`.

author: joshhearne
body:
## Problem

Changing a field's type, option list or MAC format only rewrote the field definition. Documents kept their values in the old shape:

- a VLAN field changed from Text still held the string `"10"`
- a dropdown moved to another option list pointed at options that list doesn't have
- search text still described the old type

## Fix

`updateTemplateField` and `promoteField` (the "Add to template" form can change the type too) now convert every stored value in the same transaction.

**`src/server/fields/convert.ts`** (`convertFieldValue`, pure and unit-tested) converts in three steps:
1. Read the stored value as plain text. A dropdown option becomes its label, a list becomes its items, rich text becomes its text.
2. Shape that text for the new type.
3. Run it through the same validator a save uses.

So `"10"` → `10` under VLAN, `"192.168.1.77/24"` → `192.168.1.0/24` under Network, `"comcast business"` → the Comcast Business option.

Values that don't fit are **kept exactly as they were**, never dropped. Some conversions are never attempted:
- document links and secrets, which only mean something to the field that wrote them
- boolean → text, which would write one locale's "Yes"/"No" into the data

**`src/server/services/field-conversion.ts`** (`convertStoredValues`) finds documents holding the field, archived ones included, and writes the converted values. It also rebuilds `search_text` from each document's full field list.

**What admins see:**
- The doc type page shows how many values converted and how many need fixing by hand, in amber when some were kept.
- The field edit page explains what a type change does.
- The `field.updated` / `field.promoted` audit entry records the previous type and the counts.

No revisions are written for converted values. This is a reshaping of the same data, not an edit, and a doc type with many documents would otherwise get a revision on each one.

Change file: `changes/field-type-conversion.md` (fix, admins).

## Not in this PR

The startup seed still only adds missing fields by label and never changes an existing field's type, so installs from before the network field types keep Text fields for Static IPs, Hostname and VLAN. Upgrading those automatically would override any type an admin chose on purpose. With this PR, an admin can switch those fields themselves and their values come along.

## Tested

- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint .`, `vitest run`: clean, 722 tests including the new `convert.test.ts`.
- Ran the real services against a throwaway Postgres 16 with all migrations applied (scratch test, not committed):
  - Text → VLAN converted `"10"` and `" 30 "`, and kept `"ten"`.
  - Text → Dropdown (Internet Providers) matched `"comcast business"` and kept two values that aren't on the list. The search text showed the option label.
  - Promoting a local Text field as Number converted `"3"` → `3`.
  - A save with no type change converted nothing and left no conversion data in the audit entry.

author: charliermarsh
body:
Clearing a traceback frame can release objects, so the runtime collects again at the next statement. In CPython’s deeply nested JSON encoder test, 10,000 frames clear while an enclosing call still owns the same large object graph. The collector repeatedly traced the enclosing scopes from scratch.

Let the existing collector cache cover the caller scopes that remain live after a frame clears. The next mark reads the active frames and revalidates those scopes. Mutated edges, roots and pending finalizers keep their existing collection paths.

Both production runs passed the unchanged CPython test. Elapsed time on the original Linux pair fell from 1,837.5 to 619.9 seconds. Both attempted 10,002 frame clears, rejected the two active frames and reclaimed the same 35,007 slots. On the joined public parent, all 16 ordinary FILE controls passed, including reentrant cleanup while matching a class, a changed caller edge, a reused object slot and a weak reference.

author: ljguardiola
body:
## Issue

Closes #2137

## How

The return screen is rebuilt on the v27 frame and can start from a sale already known, so the cashier returns a sale from Historial without scanning its ticket and refunds one amount per payment method.

- **Domain (`returns`).** A third ticket source, `HISTORY`, beside `QR` and `TYPED`. `ticketVerificationRequired(source)` decides whether "Ticket verificado" is required: yes for a scanned or typed ticket, no for a sale chosen in Historial. `completeReturn` takes `ticketVerified` and refuses `ticket_not_verified` before it uses any port. Each refundable payment carries the state its refund is planned in (`plannedRefundState`: cash in the act, other methods pending), which the refund table shows as "En el acto" or "Reembolso pendiente". `complete-return` and `preview-return` now use the sales concept's `saleMayBeReturned` instead of their own state check.
- **Domain (`sales`).** The Historial detail answers `returnable`: the sale may be returned (`saleMayBeReturned`) and the register has an open cash session, read through a narrow `RegisterCashSession` port whose adapter lives in the register's core folder. `Supr` shows Anular when the sale can be voided, otherwise Devolver when it is returnable, otherwise neither.
- **Contracts and core.** `find-sale-for-return` reads `{ kind: "sale", sale_id }` as the `HISTORY` source; its `found` outcome carries `ticket_source` and `ticket_verification_required`. `complete-return` carries `ticket_verified`, and each payment carries `refund_state`.
- **Storage, sync and report.** Register migration `0103_returns_started_from_history` and cloud migration `0189_returns_started_from_history` accept `HISTORY`, keeping every existing row and its dependents. The synced return event carries the new source within its current `schema_version`; the cloud keeps accepting `QR` and `TYPED` events from registers in the field. The returns report shows returns started from Historial as their own group, "Iniciadas desde el historial", in the backoffice.
- **Register screen.** D1/D2/D2b/D3/D5/D5b/D6 and M8–M12 are composed from `packages/ui`, with forms on `useRequestForm` and reads on `useCoreQuery`. The `/return` route accepts `saleId` from Historial, and the chosen sale's lookup shows loading and a retryable failure.
- **`packages/ui`.** New `CheckboxKeyCard` and `MethodRefundTable` (with an invalid amount state); `SegmentedControl` gains the `field` variant and an option `status` ("Vencido"); `SummaryRow` gains an opt-in `amount` that keeps an amount on one line beside a long label. Each new state has its story and approved screenshot.

## Technical decisions

- **Authorization is asked when the sale is looked up, not on completing.** D4 draws the authorization modal over D2 on completing. The register already asks for it when the sale is looked up (typed, scanned or chosen in Historial) and does not ask again on completing, so the modal shows over the search step. Moving it to completing would change who may see a sale; the coordinator kept the existing behaviour, and the issue body records it.
- **Historial's `returnable` includes an open cash session.** It is decided from the same facts the operation applies: without an open session `/return` redirects away and completing refuses `no_open_session`, so `Supr` does not offer Devolver then.
- **A cashier's own reading replaces the chosen sale's lookup.** Once the cashier scans or types a reading (valid or refused), the Historial sale's loading or failure no longer holds the table, so D6 and M10–M12 show their empty table and banner.
- **The search is disabled while a return is being completed**, as `Esc` already is, so typing cannot leave a completion in flight and lose its outcome.
- **`SummaryRow.amount` is opt-in.** Making every value no-wrap would break the existing promise that long textual values wrap flush right; a non-breaking space in `formatCents` would change every formatted amount, including what the cloud prints. The return screen's payment rows set it.
- **Visible differences from the v27 boards:**
  - The ticket number shows a five-digit point of sale (`00003-00001198`), as Historial and every other register screen do; the boards draw four.
  - D3 offers only "Reintegro" with "Arrepentimiento": the offered resolutions come from the domain (`offeredResolutions`), which offers "Cambio" only for "Defecto".
  - D5's second method in the captures is Transferencia, since Point débito needs the card terminal integration; the rows and the panel read the same for any method.
  - D5's amount inputs show a `$` prefix, as `MethodRefundTable`'s money input does.
  - D5b's red banner sits below the table card, where the frame places failure notices.
  - The checkbox column header "Marcar" is visible.
  - M8/M9's footer legend follows the issue's text, not the images.
  - The rail has no "Ajustes" item; that belongs to the shell, outside this issue.
- **Texts not written in the issue:**
  - "Marcá Ticket verificado para completar la devolución." for `ticket_not_verified`;
  - "Tipeá el número impreso del ticket, como 00003-00001192." for a typed text that is not a ticket number;
  - the lookup's `lookup_failed` and `unavailable` answers read as one sentence ending "Probá de nuevo."

## How it was tested

- Test-first throughout: each behaviour's failing test was committed before its code. Where a test came with or after its code, it was proved to fail without that code (the Historial `Supr` Devolver tests, the contract and core tests of the ticket source and verification).
- Use-case tests against in-memory fakes for `HISTORY`, `ticketVerificationRequired`, `ticket_not_verified`, `refundState` and Historial's `returnable`; `pnpm mutation --mutate` on every touched domain and contracts file: 100%, no survivors.
- Migration tests for register `0103` and cloud `0189` on databases holding data in the previous schema; sync tests for the `HISTORY` event in the cloud and the upcaster.
- Screen tests for every board's texts, keys and states, tests beside each new part, and browser component tests, stories and approved screenshots for the new `packages/ui` states.
- `REVIEW-GATE: CLEAN — 6 rounds, 16 fixed, 0 refuted, 0 filed as new issues (TARGET 9783420f9)`
- `pnpm verify:static`: exit 0 at 9783420f9 (2760 passed, 0 failed); re-run at a875e2b4e, after the last merge of `main`: exit 0 (2760 passed, 0 failed).
- `pnpm test:changed apps/backoffice/*.test.ts apps/cloud/*.test.ts apps/pos/*.test.ts apps/pos/src/build-output.test.ts packages/ui/.storybook/main.test.ts packages/ui/src/catalog-screenshots.visual.tsx` at a875e2b4e: exit 0, 4377 tests in 82 files passed.
- `main` was merged last at 90ac6cb5c without conflicts; it brought only register text changes of #2271.
- The real register was run against the stand-in cloud and captured at 1366×768 on every board: D1, D2, D2b, D3, D4, D5, D5b, D6, M8–M12, and Historial's C4 with `Supr` Devolver and with `Supr` Anular.
- CI `verify`: pending.

## Delivery impact

- [x] Postgres migration
- [x] SQLite migration
- [ ] New event `schema_version`
- [ ] Hardware adapter change
- [ ] None

author: jjongs2
body:
Closes #331

## Summary

The progress comment's `Duration` column is now written the way GitHub Actions writes durations on a pull request's checks.

```diff
 | Stage | Outcome | Turns | Duration |
 |---|---|---|---|
-| implement | ✅ committed | 46 | 21m |
-| checks | ✅ passed | – | 2m |
-| ci | ✅ passed | – | 0m |
+| implement | ✅ committed | 46 | 21m 14s |
+| checks | ✅ passed | – | 1m 52s |
+| ci | ✅ passed | – | 25s |
 | merge | ✅ #31 | – | – |
```

```text
duration(ms)
  undefined          → "–"
  s = max(0, round(ms / 1000))
  under a minute     → "<s>s"
  under an hour      → "<m>m <s>s"
  from an hour       → "<h>h <m>m <s>s"
```

- The rules: round to the nearest second, start at the largest non-zero unit, keep every unit below it even at zero, and zero-pad nothing.
- A negative duration, which only a clock stepped back can produce, reads `0s`.
- The Run summary keeps the Run's length in whole minutes.
- Sections earlier Runs wrote are carried forward byte for byte, so one comment can read `2m` in an older section and `1m 5s` in a newer one.
- `docs/templates/progress-comment.md` and the progress comment example in the English and Korean Ticket-to-merge guides show the new format.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `progressComment` rendered `0m` for anything under 30 s, and `1m` or `2m` for most Checks and CI rows.
- **After:** `src/progress.test.ts` pins these values:

  | Input | Reads |
  |---|---|
  | -65,000 ms, 0 ms, 400 ms | `0s` |
  | 500 ms | `1s` |
  | 40 s | `40s` |
  | 59.4 s | `59s` |
  | 59.6 s | `1m 0s` |
  | 65 s | `1m 5s` |
  | 3,599.6 s | `1h 0m 0s` |
  | 3,605 s | `1h 0m 5s` |
  | 11,735 s | `3h 15m 35s` |

- A new test carries an earlier Run's section, written in whole minutes, forward unchanged and appends a `1m 5s` row below it.
- In the orchestrator tests, agent rows read the fake Stage's `1s` and wall-clock rows read `0s`.
- `npm test` (2004 tests) and `npm run typecheck` pass locally.
- Unverified: how GitHub renders the new cells on a real Ticket.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Only the text of new rows changes. Comments already on Tickets are left as they were, so a revert only changes how later rows read.

**Blast Radius:** cosmetic

Nothing parses the `Duration` cell back. A human reading one comment may see minutes in older sections and seconds in newer ones.

body:
## Problem

Installed app never locked: LASTINPUTINFO is per-session, so the session-0 service saw idle as huge and TimerManager froze the usage clock forever.

## Fix

Detect services.exe parent (wmi.dll GetProcessInfo); start timers with excludeIdleTime=false in service mode. Dev-run keeps idle accounting.

author: ms2sato
body:
## 何を

- `docs/github-source.md` (新規): GitHub を arata の収集元にするための**検討中の設計メモ**です。ADR は起こしていません (まだ何も決めていないため)
  - 事実 (出典の URL つき): プランごとの監査ログ (画面・書き出し・API)、監査ログの代わりに読める API と、その権限・保持・レート制限、認証の比較 (同じ org の中だから使える融通は文書に無い)、GitHub App の作り方の制約 (private の App のインストール先、API と Terraform では作れない、manifest で半自動にできる)
  - 案: org ごとに private な App を作る (Actions: read と Metadata: read だけ、全リポジトリ)。収集は AWS と GitHub で分け、ストアは共通。CloudTrail の `run_id` (ADR 0055) で突き合わせる。最初のチェックの候補 (消えた実行、承認していないワークフロー、実行の番号の欠け)。痕跡の一覧は期限と出典を必須にした設定にする。PR 番号の欠けは作らない (理由も書いた)
  - 決めていない点と決める順番 (守りの棚卸しを先にする)、価値の見積もり
- `docs/ai/threats/ghostaction-2026-10.md`・`wfx-loot-2026-11.md`: 公開の分析が書く「GitHub に残る形」(ファイル名・コミットメッセージ・枝・後始末) を概要に足しました。「見えないもの」と「予定している改善」も、GitHub を読む案が検討中であることに合わせました
- `docs/roadmap.md`: 残項目に 1 行足し、メモへリンクしました

## なぜ

GhostAction や wfx-loot のように、乗っ取った GitHub のアカウントで CI の秘密を持ち出す攻撃は、GitHub の中の段階が arata には見えません。
どの情報を・どの権限で読めるかを、決める前に事実として残しておくためのメモです。

## threats の対応の直し方

- 事例の帰属は、元から正しいことを確かめました。Aikido の記事は wfx-loot の出典で、GhostAction の出典は GitGuardian と StepSecurity です。ghostaction の本文には、Aikido の記事が別の作戦を扱うことを明記しました
- ghostaction の出典に 2025 年の波 (GitGuardian 2025-09-05) を足しました。同じファイル名とコミットメッセージの出どころです
- 表の「GitHub での準備」の行を、出典の記述 (既定の枝へ PR を通さずに push する) に合わせました。「出典の書き方」は観測のまま、チェックは「—」のままです
- 見えるチェック・重大度・どの段階が見えるかの対応は、変えていません (今の arata は GitHub を読まないので、足した痕跡はどれも「見えない」側です)
- 送り先の IP とドメインは書き写さず、出典に任せました (`docs/ai/threats_test.go` の規則のとおり)

## どう確かめたか

- GitHub の公式文書の本文と、公開の分析 (GitGuardian・StepSecurity・Aikido) を読み、引いた記述を照合しました。読めなかったことは「未確認」「文書に記述なし」と書きました
- 実際の GitHub には GET だけを送り、API の応答の形 (監査ログの 404、Issue を消したときの 410、実行の履歴・activity の項目) を確かめました。特定の org の実測値は書いていません
- `go test ./...` は通りました (threats の見出し・出典・行数・IP の検査を含みます)。`make scan-sensitive` は一致なしです
