author: zerwiz
body:
# Plan 293 parts 5, 6 and 8 — the brief looks before it types, and the finder reads the work

Three doors the hall paid for on 2026-11-14, each now asked to hold its own rule instead of leaving it in a runbook paragraph. Every one carries its own test, its fix note, and its row in the proof list CI runs.

## Part 5 — `bin/agents/eindri-send.sh` judges before it speaks

The door existed as four lines: stamp the text, send it, print `sent`. Everything that made a brief safe was prose, and the prose was written after three faults landed in one day.

**It reads the input box first, and refuses.** `herdr agent prompt` *appends* to whatever stands in the box, and no herdr verb clears it. A new reader, `bin/seat/herdr-editor.py`, answers one question — what is in that box — for the two shapes the hall's harnesses actually draw:

| Shape | How the box is drawn |
|---|---|
| one family | bounded by two full-width rules, opened by its own prompt marker |
| the other | the region between the live status separator and the rule beneath it |

It answers `empty`, `text` (with the draft it read) or `unknown`, and `unknown` is said out loud rather than guessed. A box holding text stops the send with exit 3 and a message that says plainly that nothing was sent and **nothing was cleared** — those words may be the Allfather's.

**It waits, then asks three witnesses.** After the send it waits (default 20 s) and asks, in order: `herdr agent get`; the screen (a spinner, `Working`, `queued` or `esc to interrupt` counts as landed); and the box itself.

| What the third look finds | What the door does | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| the words stand in the box | presses Enter — never retypes a second copy | `enter` |
| the box is empty | sends the line once more | `copy` |
| the box cannot be read | neither, because a duplicate costs more than a retry | `none` |

The screen check exists because three workers read `idle` while their screens showed work, and the resend that followed gave each of them two briefs. The Enter check exists because a prompt delivered while a harness is still starting sits typed and unsent, with no spinner and an `idle` status.

**The far side is probed, never assumed.** A far machine is reached over the home's fleet registry, through a login shell (measured: a non-interactive one cannot see that machine's `herdr` at all), and asked what verbs it has: `agent prompt` where it exists, `agent send` followed by `pane send-keys … Enter` where it does not. A machine the registry does not name is refused by name, and nothing is dialled.

Targets stay unambiguous: a pane id carries one colon, a road two or more, so `<machine>:<pane>` splits cleanly and `--machine` says it explicitly.

## Part 6 — `bin/seat/seat-find.sh` finds the agent by its work

The fault: a brief went to the wrong worker because its tab title looked right, and the Allfather had to stop it. A tab title is what someone typed when the pane was opened; the screen is what the agent knows.

The door reads the recent screen of every pane that carries an agent, matches the query **literally** (case-blind; every word by default, `--any` for one) and prints pane, agent, status, matched words, the last matching line and the title. It skips the caller's own pane — the words being searched for are usually in its own scrollback — and says which pane it skipped. A pane it could not read is named and counted, so "no match" is never the same answer as "could not look".

## Part 8 — a variable is the design, a resolved path is the leak

`bin/gates/guards/private-guard.py` read every `$YMIR_HOME/…` mention in a public document as a *private hoard path*. That is Rule 07's own shape, and 277 tracked files carry it, because it is how every page in this repository says where a thing lives.

Three narrower rules replaced it, and none of them loosens what "leak" means:

- the variable left the pattern list;
- the **resolved home** walked in — computed once through the resolver the guard already called, refused wherever it appears, and never written in the file;
- the bare `svartalfaheim/` alternative left the pattern list (the repository ships that shelf), and in its place the realms that exist in the home are listed at run time — a path naming a **real** one is refused.

An absolute path, a tilde path, a bare hoard shelf, a vault filename, a secret shape and any name declared in the home are refused exactly as before.

## Proof

```text
$ bash bin/agents/tests/test_eindri_send.sh
eindri-send: 28 ok, 0 failed

$ bash bin/seat/tests/test_herdr_editor.sh
herdr-editor: 8 ok, 0 failed

$ bash bin/seat/tests/test_seat_find.sh
seat-find: 13 ok, 0 failed

$ bash .agents/tests/private-guard-variable.test.sh
private-guard-variable: 9 ok, 0 failed

$ bash bin/gates/guards.sh
guards: 16 changed path(s) judged; 3 finding(s) INHERITED (they name files this push did not touch)
```

The sender's test drives a stubbed `herdr` and a stubbed `ssh` under a throwaway home, so both roads are exercised as the hall runs them: the refusal in both box shapes with nothing recorded as sent, the origin stamp, one send when the box is empty, a resend when the line was lost, **no** resend when the screen shows work while the status says idle, **Enter instead of a second copy** when the brief stands typed, a refusal when no agent stands in the pane, the old and new far-side roads, an unknown machine refused with nothing dialled, and a one-colon pane id that never rides ssh.

Live, the same day: a send was refused because the box held the Allfather's own half-written sentence (exit 3, the words quoted back, nothing sent, nothing cleared), and a pane on another machine was refused after its own `herdr` was probed — which proves the ssh road, the login shell and the verb probe in one call.

The private ward's test plants an invented home with its own marker and its own realm, and proves **both directions**: the variable form passes, while the resolved home, a tilde path, a home-declared name, a secret shape, and a real realm on the private shelf are all refused — and a resolved path sitting beside a variable still refuses, so the variable never shields a leak.

## Files

- `bin/agents/eindri-send.sh` — the three witnesses, the roads, the probe.
- `bin/seat/herdr-editor.py` — the input-box reader, one answer for two shapes.
- `bin/seat/seat-find.sh` — find by work, not by label.
- `bin/gates/guards/private-guard.py` — a variable is the design.
- `bin/agents/tests/test_eindri_send.sh`, `bin/seat/tests/test_herdr_editor.sh`, `bin/seat/tests/test_seat_find.sh`, `.agents/tests/private-guard-variable.test.sh`
- `bin/gates/ci-verify.sh` — four gates so none of those proofs is a test nobody runs.
- `docs/features/hand-a-brief-to-a-worker.md`, `docs/features/find-the-agent-by-its-work.md` and their two catalogue rows.
- Three fix notes under `docs/fixes/agents/`, `docs/fixes/seat/` and `docs/fixes/gate/`.

## Owed, and named rather than hidden

`.agents/tests/private-guard-identity.test.sh` is stale and already red at this branch's base: it asserts identity rules that live in `bin/gates/guards/public-guard.py` now, and no gate calls it. It needs an owner — re-pointed at the public guard, or retired by a move (Rule 11). It was not touched here, because rewriting another ward's test is not this errand.

## What this pull request does not touch

Branch protection, the collaborator list, the merge door, the plan ledger, or any ward's strictness. No assertion was loosened to get a green, and no feature was removed.

house: the Allfather's hall
fleet: the ymir fleet
agent: safe-send (role: ship, errand: safe-send)
authority: plan 293 parts 5, 6 and 8, at the Allfather's word — one pull request from a branch off the default branch, the heart merges
proves: the four proofs above, all green; `bin/gates/guards.sh` green on every changed path

author: dr5hn
body:
Part of the #1643 top-23 country close-out, gate W (own Wikidata item). Part 1 of 8.

## What changes

1,851 US rows that had no `wikiDataId` now carry their own item: Indiana 994, Illinois 857. They are township 1,851 rows added from Census county subdivisions in #2200–#2216 and the earlier township passes. Only `wikiDataId` changes, from empty to the item. No existing item is replaced.

## How each item is proved

Each row's ledger (`us_townships_*.jsonl`) records the township's own Census GEOID and GNIS code. An item is admitted only when all of these hold:

1. its own non-deprecated GNIS id (P590) equals the row's GNIS code, or its FIPS 55-3 code (P774) equals the row's state and county-subdivision code
2. exactly one item matches that code anywhere in Wikidata
3. it is a township or civil town by its own class (P31 and its parent classes), not a city, village, CDP or county
4. its P131 chain reaches the same state
5. its coordinates lie inside the row's own Census polygon
6. no other row in any table already uses it

Candidates were found with a few bulk queries on QLever's Wikidata index (University of Freiburg), because the public query service rate-limited the first run. Every admitted item was then checked live against Wikidata itself (`wbgetentities`), so a snapshot alone never admits an item. This follows the method of #2239 and `us_items_v5x`.

## Coverage

After all 8 parts, US rows with their own item: 17,560 / 31,538 (55.7%) → 30,874 / 31,538 (97.9%).

## Source

Wikidata (CC0), so no attribution block. Census Gazetteer/TIGER (public domain) for the polygon check. Query text, response hashes and the live check receipts are recorded in the sidecar and kept with the build's evidence.

## Files

- `contributions/cities/US.json`
- `.github/fixes-docs/ledgers/us_items3_v6x_part1.jsonl` and `.sources.json`: each row's code, item, class path, state chain and polygon check

## Checks

- Diff checked against master: 1,851 rows, only `wikiDataId`, none previously set. No item is used twice across the 8 parts or by any existing row.
- A random sample was re-checked live: each item's GNIS id equals the township's Census code.
- Build checks passed for this part: the PR validators, validator and release unit tests, the migration walk from v4.0, and a MySQL import.

## What changes
- The coding-taste skill is this project's own text and only taste: no sentence of the bundled original survives, every specific the old rules named is still named, and the lone-agent workflow (orchestrate, review until LGTM, PR checks, "do not commit") is in the role files that own it.

## Look here
- `factory/skills/coding-taste/SKILL.md:41-53`: cutting is its own step after building, with all seven targets; proof names the four kinds of check and what finished means; "The reader bills you a dollar a word."
- `factory/skills/coding-taste/SKILL.md:32-39`: the eight learned lines; "invariant over cases" (line 39) has the thinnest evidence.
- `factory/roles/lead.md:23` and `:32`, `CLAUDE.md:18`: the homes of the old orchestration rules (work beside a running subagent, settle every result) and of "main simplification".

## Verified
`make test` passes (653 + 252 Python tests, Go vet and tests); fresh reviewers compared old and new on three questions (specific missing, sentence copied, rule shifted) and the last one approved.

## Not verified / risks
Agents load the installed plugin's copy: the new text takes effect when the plugin is updated. No coder or reviewer has yet worked a real task under the new text.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

Spec: `~/.claude/factory/specs/ccmon/taste-rewrite.md` (not published). Not the short path.

**Words (`wc -w`), before → after** (the brief's same-length limit was withdrawn by the human: the dollar-a-word rule governs what an agent writes, not the skill's length)

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `factory/skills/coding-taste/SKILL.md` (and its `.claude/skills` copy, kept identical) | 468 | 726 |
| `factory/agents/coder.md` | 519 | 487 |
| `factory/agents/reviewer.md` | 576 | 575 |
| `CLAUDE.md` | 380 | 424 |

`factory/roles/lead.md` grows by about 70 words from this task's edits (its total also moved with the merged base). The `.claude/agents` twins got the same edits as their `factory/agents` originals. The `.claude/skills` copy stays because those twins read it by path in sessions outside the plugin.

**Where each old rule lives now**

| Old rule | Home |
|---|---|
| Smallest complete design, never fewer features; the ladder; one path, one owner, one source; the refused list (all 12) | skill, "The smallest complete design" |
| Define done; scope fixed | skill line 15; `lead.md` step 1; `coder.md` "exactly the change you are given" |
| Inspect first (owner, runtime path, helpers, conventions, narrowest test, unrelated changes, environment) | skill, "Building", first line |
| Implement end to end; only required code, errors, security, tests, config, docs | skill, "Building" |
| Simplify: duplication, nesting, indirection, flags, wrappers, files, comments | skill, "Then cut" |
| Validate: focused, integration, end-to-end, repository checks; fix and rerun; finished only when | skill, "Proof" |
| Communicate | skill, "Words" |
| Orchestrate, delegate, one writer per path, read-only reviewers | `lead.md` "Who does what", step 2; `reviewer.md`; `CLAUDE.md` |
| Do the next non-conflicting task, never poll; mark every result accepted, deferred or rejected | `lead.md:23`; `CLAUDE.md:18` |
| PR validation (SHA, CI, mergeability, comments) | `lander.md`, `lead.md` step 5, the dispatch skill |
| Review until LGTM; final report | `lead.md` steps 3-5; the agents' report formats; "main simplification" in `lead.md:32` |
| Do not commit or push without authorization | removed, it contradicted `coder.md` (commits its round, never pushes) and the lander (pushes) |

**Role-file sentences**: the pointers at removed skill sections (Standard, Execute, Communicate) are replaced in `coder.md`, `reviewer.md`, `lead.md:5` and `CLAUDE.md:9`; the only names used now are "Words" and "Refused", which exist. Trims made in earlier rounds to pay for the skill's length were put back: the coder's "including the commands you ran and their results", the reviewer's "the change must be the smallest complete design" with the named refused items, the lead's literal-example clause, `CLAUDE.md`'s line on who plans by the skill.

**Evidence for the added lines**: check, do not assume (#51, #34, two retro entries on counts from memory); deleting names its condition (#45, #11, #22); unknown is not zero (#16, #53); timeouts (#53, #17); invariant over cases (#48 and one recorded decision); script over model (#42, #14); tests (#54, #59); literal contract with types (#47, two retro entries).

**Quality assessment**
- State of the art: a skill preloaded through `skills:` frontmatter, role-neutral, with procedure left to role files; the description says what it is instead of "optional". Checked against the agent files and the plugin layout in this repository, not against outside documentation.
- Blind spots: prose is not executable; nothing measures whether coders follow the new lines. The first tasks after the plugin update are the test.
- Regressions: every pointer at a skill section was found by a full grep for `coding-taste` (six files) and repointed. Each old rule was compared with the new text on three questions (specific missing, sentence copied, direction or condition changed) by fresh reviewers.
- Undocumented behavior: none added; no flag, default or command changes.
- Simplicity: what the design left out is the workflow half of the old skill, which the role files already carried; what could still go is the reviewer's parenthesis of refused items, which repeats the skill.
- Operability: takes effect on plugin update; undo is a revert of this pull request.

**Review history**: eight reviews, a fresh reviewer each time. Rounds 1-3 (under the withdrawn word limit): sentences still following the old skeleton; approved. Round 4, after the human found the dollar-a-word line reversed: an inversion-only pass, no other inversion, four shifts corrected. Rounds 5-8, after the word limit was withdrawn: specifics restored (the seven cutting targets, security in the end-to-end rule, the four kinds of check, what finished means, short concrete statements), then the restored sentences reworded where they followed the old ones, the look-to-steer allowance kept, and `CLAUDE.md:18` given the old examples. Round 8: APPROVE, no issues. That last review covered the two lines of the final commit; the rest of the text was approved in rounds 5-7 line by line, not in one final full pass.

body:
## Why
The tart-runner-fleet is enabling its own Actions artifact store (vitalyiegorov/tart-runner-fleet#509, ADR 0097). After that, `upload-artifact` and `download-artifact` on fleet Linux runners (`trf-linux-*`, `linux-portable-*`) talk to a local gate, while `macos-maestro` runners and GitHub-hosted runners keep using GitHub's artifact storage. A download on one side can't see an upload on the other.

Two handoffs in this repo can cross that line:

| Workflow | Producer | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| `ios-maestro.yml` `e2e` downloading `ios-e2e-app*` | `build` (macOS, native targets) **or** the `expo-base-plan` repack upload (Linux) | `e2e` on Linux |
| `store-screenshots.yml` `capture-ios-e2e` downloading `store-screenshots-app-*` | `build-ios` (macOS) **or** the plan repack (Linux) | Linux |

Which producer runs is decided per target, so a fixed `github-token` would break the repack path.

## Change
Each of those downloads now runs in two steps:
1. Download from the runner's own store, with `continue-on-error`.
2. If step 1 failed, download from GitHub with `github-token`.

In download-artifact v7.0.0 (37930b1c, `src/download-artifact.ts:53`), REST is used only when `inputs.token` is truthy. `run-id` defaults to `${{ github.run_id }}`. On runners that already use GitHub's storage, step 1 succeeds as before.

This PR also releases **v4.13.1**: self-references and documented pins are bumped per RELEASE.md, and there's a README entry.

## Not changed
- **`native-publish.yml` markers:** both producers there are non-fleet in current callers, so the callers will set `control-runner-labels` to `ubuntu-latest`, which is this workflow's default. Changing the reusable workflow would have added an `actions: read` requirement for every caller.
- **`store-screenshots.yml` `upload` job:** it downloads `raw-screenshots-*` made by fleet capture jobs. A token can't fix that direction, so it is tracked separately.

## Validation
- `tests/run-tests.sh` passes.
- `actionlint` passes on the changed workflows and on `docs/examples`.
- `zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml .github/workflows actions` reports no findings.

author: mattias
body:
## What happened

A YouTube video fetched with the YouTube downloader showed up in the library as a title named **"Processed"** (item `Processed/ユートのチャンネル - 誰から何も言われずに1人で英語学習継続できるようになる方法 [pitFobM6z80].txt`, record `show.title: ユートのチャンネル`).

## Why

The downloader writes a single video's transcript directly into `data/<lang>/Processed` (a playlist's videos go in a folder below it). `register` titles a new item by its record's show only when the file is a loose drop (`folder_key_of(rel) is None`). `_below_tier` treats only a tier folder, `Library` and hato's drop folder as no folder, so `Processed` was taken for a show's folder. `_settle_works` then made a new title by that folder: "Processed".

## Fix

`PROCESSED_FOLDER = "Processed"`: a file **directly** in it is a loose drop (`_below_tier` → `""`), as in hato's folder. Registered, it is titled by its record's show, and two channels' videos become two titles. Without a record it is titled by its name (`_stranded_work`). A playlist's folder below `Processed` is unchanged. Existing titles are never regrouped or renamed, so a title already called "Processed" keeps its name until the user renames it.

Not changed: a playlist's title still reads as `Processed/<playlist>` (its folder below the tier, as before). Changing that would move existing playlists' folder keys.

## Tests

- New: `test_a_video_dropped_straight_into_processed_is_titled_by_its_show_never_processed` (ja + zh).
- `test_library_store_works.py`, `test_library_store_register.py`, `test_services_moves.py`: 620 passed.
- Every test file mentioning `Processed`, `_below_tier`, `folder_key_of` or `HATO_FOLDER` (55 files): 3202 passed. One failure, `test_library_store_switch::test_the_updater_waits_for_a_running_helper_then_holds_every_lock`, also fails on 3.0-dev on this machine. The teardown errors pass when their files run alone (407 passed).

author: allianaab2m
body:
Implements: proposals/semaphore-queue.md

Closes #583

`Std.Semaphore` と `Std.Queue` を足し，Scope に `semaphore` と `queue` の操作を足す．JS，C（native），WASM の 3 ターゲットで同じ結果になる．

## 実装の要点

- `with_permits(s, n, f)` は Core IR で with に下ろす．init が `fiber#acquire`（許可を待って取る）で，release が `fiber#release`（許可を返す）．f がどう終わっても返す処理は既存の with の release に任せる．f の中の with の release が先に走る（`crates/emela-core/src/lower/fiber.rs` の `PermitsCall`）．束縛は `()` なので retire しない．JS もこれに合わせ，`()` の束縛は retire しない（LIR は元から operand がない）．
- `offer` と `take` は，ランタイム側では「閉じていたら False / None」を返す操作にした．`QueueClosed` の失敗は lowering で組み立てる（`QueueCall`）．ランタイムはエラー値を作らない．
- 待つ fiber は FIFO の列に並ぶ．許可や値を受け取った fiber は列から外れ，`served` として再開する．その後に来た割り込みは次の suspension point で効く．許可や値が失われることはない．
- 待っている間に割り込まれた fiber は，wait が drop された時点で列から抜ける．Semaphore はそこで列を配り直す．
- scope は自分の Semaphore と Queue を覚えておく．scope が終わった時点で別の scope の fiber がまだ待っていれば，`... was used after its scope ended` の defect で起こす．
- scope が終わった後の release（別の scope の fiber が許可を持ったまま scope が終わった場合）は何もしない．仕様は「使う側の操作」を defect にしているだけなので，この扱いはコメントに書いた．

## ルールと対応するテスト

`[fiber.semaphore]`
- `Fiber.semaphore(permits)`，`permits < 1` は defect → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（Defects）
- `with_permits` は n 個の許可を待って取り，f を走らせ，値・エラー・defect・割り込みのどれで終わっても返す → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（The permits come back however f ends），`lower.rs` `semaphore_and_queue`
- f の中の with の release が先に走る → lowering で with を入れ子にする（`lower__semaphore_and_queue.snap`）
- `try_with_permits` は待たずに取れて，かつ待っている fiber がいなければ `Some`．それ以外は f を走らせず `None`．suspension point ではない → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（First in, first out，try_with_permit while full）
- `n < 1`，`n` が作ったときの許可数より多いと defect（`with_permits` / `try_with_permits` の名前つき） → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（Defects）
- 厳密な FIFO．先頭が待つ間は，少ない許可で足りる後続も待つ → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（a / b / c）
- 待っている間に割り込まれた fiber は列から抜け，許可を取らない → `fiber_semaphore.emel`（big）
- 許可は呼び出しごとに数える（再入しない） → `t.with_permit(|| t.with_permit(|| t.available()))` が 0
- `available` → 上記の各所
- `with_permits` の E と R は f の E と R に Async を足したもの．`try_with_permits` は f の E と R のまま → `emela-types/tests/fiber.rs` `semaphore_and_queue`

`[fiber.queue]`
- `Fiber.queue(capacity)`，`capacity < 1` は defect → `fiber_queue.emel`（Defects）
- `offer` は満杯の間待ち，`take` は空の間待つ．どちらも待った順に配る．値は offer が始まった順に出る → `fiber_queue.emel`（容量 1 に 3 つの producer で `[1, 2, 3, 10, 100, 20]`，Consumers waiting）
- 割り込まれた offer は何も足さない．割り込まれた taker は列から抜ける → `fiber_queue.emel`（An interrupted offer）
- `try_offer`，`poll`，`size` → `fiber_queue.emel`
- `close`：残った値は取り出せる．空になったら `take` は `QueueClosed`．待っていた taker と offerer も `QueueClosed`．`offer` は `QueueClosed`，`try_offer` は False．2 回目の close は何もしない → `fiber_queue.emel`（Close with values left，Close with waiting fibers）

`[fiber.escape]`
- scope の値の型に `Semaphore` や `Queue` が含まれていたら E0425 → `emela-types/tests/fiber.rs` `handles_cannot_leave_the_scope`，`emela-driver/tests/diagnostics.rs` `semaphore_and_queue_cannot_leave_the_scope`
- scope が終わった後の使用は defect → `fiber_semaphore.emel` / `fiber_queue.emel`（later）
- scope が終わった時点で待っていた別の scope の fiber も同じ defect で止まる → 両プログラムの最後の節

仕様の例（11.9，11.10）と proposal の例は `emela-types/tests/fiber.rs` `semaphore_and_queue` で型検査している．

両プログラムは `parity.rs`（JS と C）と `wasm_parity.rs`（JS と WASM）で 3 ターゲットとも走る．WASM のリーク検査として `memory.rs` `semaphores_and_queues_free_their_values_and_lines` を足した（値を溜め込む版は同じ上限で止まることを確かめた）．

## 診断

新しいコードはない．E0425 が `Semaphore` と `Queue` も扱う．新しい defect のメッセージは proposal のとおり．

## 実行したチェック

- `cargo fmt --all --check`，`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --locked`：dbg の変更後に全 1462 件が通った．それ以前の実行では 3 件が落ちていた：
  - `snapshots__suspending_functions_and_fibers`（C）と `bytes_stable`（WASM）は意図した変更で，更新した
  - `emela-driver::c suspend_externals_complete_later` は，C のコンパイルを含む全体が 30 秒未満であることを確かめるテスト．全体実行の負荷で 31.1 秒になって落ちた．単独と，テストバイナリ全体の 3 回の再実行では通った．Semaphore と Queue は使っていない
- `cargo build --bin emela --locked`，`scripts/spec.py check`
- `examples/*`：`emela check`，`emela test`，`emela fmt --check`
- `tests/laws`：`fmt --check`，`test --target js / native / wasm`
- node，C コンパイラ，wasmtime がそろった環境で回した．スキップしたパリティテストはない

## dbg の表示

- 仕様が食い違っていた：`[fiber.semaphore]` と `[fiber.queue]` は `<semaphore>` / `<queue>`，`[trait.builtin]` は「`@external type` は `<external Name>`」と書いていた
- 作者の判断で `<semaphore>` / `<queue>` に決めた．`[trait.builtin]` に例外として書き足した（581ec887，意味を変えない修正なので `spec/history.md` には書いていない）
- 実装は `EnumDef::runtime_display` を JS の show と LIR の show（C と WASM）が使う．両プログラムで `dbg(s)`，`dbg(Some(s))`，`dbg(q)`，`dbg([q])` を 3 ターゲットで確かめた
- Deferred や Fiber など，ほかの `@external type` の `<external Name>` はまだ実装されていない（JS で `undefined`，C と WASM で defect）．この PR の範囲外として残した

La issue pide que la skill quede como motor sin contenido y que el pack oficial sea la fuente por defecto. ### 💡 ¿Cuál fue la solución? - **Fuente `golfo`.** `sources.golfo.{source, ref, updates}` reemplaza a `sources.golfoKit`. Por defecto apunta a `git+https://github.com/guidomodarelli/golfo-agent-profiles` siguiendo `main`. - El lock nombra la fuente `golfo` y registra `kind`, `revision`, `origin` y `requestedRef`. - `agent-ready update golfo [--to ]` la adopta. - Un pack de `sources.packs` no puede llamarse `golfo` ni publicar la base. - **Motor sin contenido.** Se borran del plugin `assets/profiles.json`, `assets/stacks/`, `assets/profiles/`, y en `assets/common/` las rules, las skills, los bloques y el template. `scripts/agent_ready_golfo_kit.py` pasa a ser `scripts/agent_ready_content.py`. - El contenido siempre se compone con el motor instalado en la caché del usuario. - Los comandos que leen contenido lo componen solos cuando reciben el dir del motor: `resolve`, `detect`, `plan`, `finalize`, `pack-scripts` y `status`. - También lo componen `managed-block.sh` y `instruction-normalization.sh`, a través de `resolve_content_skill_directory`. - `load_profile_catalog` pierde el código que descartaba los profiles de CI del contenido, porque la composición ya los rechaza. Queda solo el choque de nombres con los profiles de CI del motor. - **Override de desarrollo.** `AGENT_READY_SETUP_CONTENT_DIR` toma un checkout local del pack tal como está, identificado por su digest. Lo usan los tests y quien prueba un cambio del pack antes de publicarlo. - **Tests.** - Las 18 suites proyectan el pack oficial en el tag fijo de `tests/content-pack.ref` (`v1.0.0`). `tests/prepare-content-pack.sh` lo clona una vez en `node_modules/.cache/`. - La CI lo clona en un paso propio antes de bats, y `test:agent-ready` y `test:bootstrap` lo preparan antes de correr. - `agent-ready-golfo-kit.bats` pasa a ser `agent-ready-content.bats`. En modo Git, usa el pack publicado en la URL real a través de `url.insteadOf`. - **Docs.** - `references/profiles-and-lockfile.md` tiene la sección «El contenido», que reemplaza a «golfo-kit como fuente» y a «Contenido de otro repositorio». - `configuration-keys.md` está regenerado. - Se actualizaron `SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md` de la skill, el README, `stable-delivery.md`, `ai-reviews.md`, `managed-agents-block.md`, `nested-instructions.md` y `ci-check.md`. - La skill `error-observability-diagnostics` ahora referencia las rules del pack oficial. - **Evals.** Hay un caso nuevo, `content-comes-from-the-official-pack`. Los casos de la fuente fijada y del pack de contenido pasan a `sources.golfo`. - golfo-kit 0.90.0, `agent-ready-setup` 1.58.0. ## 🚀 Tipo de Cambio - [ ] 🐛 **Bug Fix** — corrige comportamiento defectuoso - [ ] ✨ **New Feature** — agrega funcionalidad nueva - [x] 💥 **Breaking Change** — modifica un contrato o comportamiento incompatible - [ ] ⚡ **Performance** — mejora tiempos, uso de recursos o escalabilidad - [ ] 🧹 **Refactor** — reestructura código sin cambiar comportamiento - [ ] 🧪 **Tests** — agrega o mejora cobertura sin cambiar producción - [ ] 📄 **Documentation** — actualiza documentación sin cambiar código funcional - [ ] 🏗️ **Build** — modifica compilación, empaquetado o herramientas de build - [ ] 👷 **CI/CD** — modifica pipelines, checks o automatización de entrega - [ ] ⬆️ **Dependencies** — actualiza, agrega o elimina dependencias - [ ] ⚙️ **Chore** — mantenimiento sin impacto funcional directo - [ ] ↩️ **Revert** — revierte un cambio anterior ## 🖐️ Pruebas Manuales **🌐 Entorno:** un repo Git vacío con `package.json`, y `claude` y `codex` falsos en el `PATH`. 1. Correr `python3 plugins/golfo-kit/skills/agent-ready-setup/scripts/agent-ready apply --stack node` sin declarar `sources` → proyecta `.agents/rules/node-security.md`, y el lock registra `source.name: "golfo"`, `kind: "git"`, `origin: "https://github.com/guidomodarelli/golfo-agent-profiles"` y `requestedRef: "main"`. 2. Correr `agent-ready status` → muestra `Locked source: golfo 1.0.0 (git, revision …, from https://github.com/guidomodarelli/golfo-agent-profiles; …)`. 3. Correr `agent-ready update golfo --dry-run` → muestra el salto de versión del contenido sin escribir en el repo. 4. Con `AGENT_READY_SETUP_CONTENT_DIR=`, editar una rule del checkout y correr `agent-ready apply` → el cambio aparece en `.agents/rules/`, y el lock registra `kind: "local"` sin `revision`. 5. Declarar un pack en `sources.packs` con `name: "golfo"` y correr `agent-ready apply` → falla antes de escribir con «reserved for the content (sources.golfo)». ## 👀 Notas para el Revisor *(si aplica)* - **Sin compatibilidad hacia atrás (#60).** Un manifest con `sources.golfoKit` o un lock con `source.kind: "marketplace-snapshot"` no se migran. El próximo `apply` adopta el contenido del pack oficial. - **Ref de los tests.** Los tests no siguen `main` del pack: usan el tag de `tests/content-pack.ref`, así un release del pack no cambia lo que ve la CI. Para subir la ref, primero hay que publicar el tag en el pack. - **Tamaño del diff.** El grueso del diff son borrados de contenido que ya vive en el pack. - **Dónde enfocar la revisión.** `scripts/agent_ready_content.py`, `source_identity` y `enforce_sync_policy` en `scripts/agent-ready-state.py`, y `resolve_content_skill_directory` en `scripts/stack-directory.sh`. - Cierra #62. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01KerzSMSJGJtWYt1NkBFG9e

body:
Part of #312; does not close it.

Brings the `Select`, `Radio`, `Lists` and `Name` fieldtypes under `app/Fieldtypes` to full line coverage. Each had code no test reached: the `full_choices` render data on `Select` and `Radio`, the validation rules `Lists` derives, and the `Name` icon.

## Approach

- New [`tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ChoiceFieldtypeRenderDataTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/uams-statamic/blob/312-fieldtypes-choice/tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ChoiceFieldtypeRenderDataTest.php): for both `select` and `radio`, the handle resolves to the application class with Statamic's icon. `extraRenderableFieldData()` keeps Statamic's option map and adds the option values that have reached their per-choice limit, which is empty while every limit has room.
- New [`tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ListsFieldtypeTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/uams-statamic/blob/312-fieldtypes-choice/tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ListsFieldtypeTest.php): `rules()` always starts with `array`, then adds `between`, `min` or `max` for whichever of `min_items` and `max_items` is a positive integer. Numeric strings are cast; zero, negative, non-numeric and null bounds are dropped. The class is registered under `list`, keeping Statamic's icon.
- New [`tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/NameFieldtypeTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/uams-statamic/blob/312-fieldtypes-choice/tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/NameFieldtypeTest.php): the `name` component, the `fieldtype-users` icon, selectable in forms, and registered under `name`.
- New [`tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/SelectFieldtypeConfigTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/uams-statamic/blob/312-fieldtypes-choice/tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/SelectFieldtypeConfigTest.php): pins the `Selection & Options` field order (the preset fields before `options`, `randomize_order` and the per-choice limit fields after it) and the `if: multiple equals true` condition on `max_items`.
- New [`tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/RadioFieldtypeConfigTest.php`](https://github.com/UAMS-Web/uams-statamic/blob/312-fieldtypes-choice/tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/RadioFieldtypeConfigTest.php): pins the `Selection & Options` field order on `Radio`, with the preset and other-option fields before `options` and `randomize_order` and the per-choice limit fields after it.
- `NameFieldtypeTest.php` also pins all five subfield definitions exactly: prefix, first, middle, last and suffix, with only the first and last names included and required by default.
- `ListsFieldtypeTest.php` also pins the exact Constraints section, `selectableInForms()`, and the truncation of decimal and trailing-text bounds.
- Application code: `Lists::icon()` and `Select::icon()` narrow Statamic's untyped `parent::icon()` with a `@var string` instead of a defensive branch no input reaches. The Constraints section in `Lists` loses an `instructions` key that `createSection()` never read.

## How the gap was measured

Line coverage under PCOV, at `efeba3f96`, taking the union of three runs: `tests/Feature/Fieldtypes`, `tests/Unit/Fieldtypes`, and the tests that build these fieldtypes elsewhere (`tests/Feature/Views/FormsFieldsChoiceDynamicDefaultTest.php`, the choice-limit Forms and Listeners tests, `AllFieldsTagTest`, `ContainsAnyConditionOverlapTest`, `FormsFieldsVisibilityHiddenTest`). The statements no run reached were:

| File | Statements | Unreached before |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Lists.php` | 49 | 18 (all of `rules()`) |
| `Select.php` | 39 | 4 (`extraRenderableFieldData()`) |
| `Radio.php` | 29 | 4 (`extraRenderableFieldData()`) |
| `Name.php` | 68 | 1 (`icon()`) |

The new tests reach each of those statements. They also reach the `icon()` overrides on `Select`, `Radio` and `Lists`, which before were covered only by tests elsewhere.

## Verification

Measured under Git Bash on Windows 11 with PCOV.

- Pint `--test`, a Rector dry run, PHPStan and cspell on the three new files: clean. `scripts/check-parallel-safe-tests.php`: OK.
- Mutation, `App\Fieldtypes\Lists`: 49 mutants, 48 killed. The one left, the `selectableInForms` property default on line 48, gets no coverage from PCOV. Applied by hand: the identical copy exits 0; the mutant fails `Failed asserting that false is true`.
- Mutation, `Select`: 14 mutants, 14 killed. The first run left 8 `RemoveArrayItem` survivors in `configFieldItems()`; `SelectFieldtypeConfigTest.php` kills them.
- Mutation, `Radio`: 12 mutants, 12 killed.
- Mutation, `Name`: 87 mutants. 60 killed, and 26 timed out, all bunched at the start of the run. Hand-applied samples of those (lines 59, 60 and 66) each fail `Failed asserting that two arrays are identical`, with the identical copy exiting 0. The one left, the `selectableInForms` property default on line 28, gets no coverage from PCOV; applied by hand, it fails `Failed asserting that false is true`.
- Each run printed a base-phase `Duration:` well below its mutation phase (Select 23s against 275s, Radio 68s against 298s, Name 12s against 1,427s), so the child processes ran.

## Test plan

- [x] `php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ChoiceFieldtypeRenderDataTest.php tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/ListsFieldtypeTest.php tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/NameFieldtypeTest.php tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/SelectFieldtypeConfigTest.php tests/Feature/Fieldtypes/RadioFieldtypeConfigTest.php`: 31 passed (39 assertions)
- [x] Mutation run on `App\Fieldtypes\Select`, `Radio`, `Lists` and `Name`: no unexplained survivors
- [x] Remote CI green: 69 passed, 13 skipped, none failed, on `a0f4ae8d1`

body:
## Fix for repeated manual More Overlays installation during QA

**What happened:** More Overlays Updated was already an approved, indexed, client-only mod in the 140-mod manifest, but its `mods/more-overlays-updated.pw.toml` used CurseForge `mode = "metadata:curseforge"`. That distribution path can require manual downloads; the user kept having to add the mod after importing Prism test builds.

### Verified, narrowly scoped correction
- Re-pinned **the exact same byte-identical JAR**, not a new mod or upgraded version: `moreoverlays-1.24.2-mc1.21.1-neoforge.jar`.
- Original CurseForge project 391382 / file 6981252 SHA1: `21e8bd61c5e146a9574266015d3f64621c2d9e18`.
- Official Modrinth project `Thy5Pqut` / exact version `Kq8xaqKi` returned **the same SHA1**. Now points directly to its official CDN URL, with SHA512 `6e590a05107b2c49579fa619de93029b3c858079c4baedd52ebbe0f8b18edf82c70c2ea841040610178b764848690e8806d11a532bfa12c28d9a9452b8254cea`. Side remains **client**.
- Packwiz `index.toml` and `pack.toml` hashes refreshed. **No new mod, recipe, mod version, loader, client-side JAR checked into GitHub or shop changes**.
- Prism packaging now invokes `packwiz-installer-bootstrap.jar -s client <exact pinned pack.toml>`, explicitly installing client and both-side mods.
- New deterministic fail-closed `scripts/resolve_more_overlays.py` and `scripts/validate_client_overlays.py` ensure future packaging can't silently omit this mod or substitute different bytes.

### Automated tests and NEW Prism download
- **[Successful resolver and client-import packaging run #43623507516](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/actions/runs/43623507516)**: exact SHA1 match confirmed against Modrinth API, packwiz metadata and SHA chain PASS (**140 mods, 251 files**), all **179 quest objects** static tests PASS, client-side installer mode check PASS, artifact upload PASS.
- **[Download the fixed More Overlays automatic-install Prism candidate](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/actions/runs/43623507516/artifacts/14124687895)**. Extract outer GitHub ZIP; Prism **Add Instance → Import** the enclosed `Too-Much-Magic-More-Overlays-Auto-Prism.zip`. The source snapshot inside is immutable commit `d7e078830e166344ee67f6e16ca7bd4fb3e24a9f`.
- [Client handoff and troubleshooting](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/blob/fix/more-overlays-auto-client-install/docs/MORE-OVERLAYS-AUTO-CLIENT.md): after launch, inspect **Prism → Edit Instance → Mods** or `minecraft/mods/moreoverlays-1.24.2-mc1.21.1-neoforge.jar`; F7 light overlay, F9 chunk overlay, resolve key conflicts if necessary.

### Remaining acceptance gate
- GitHub Actions verifies only the **remote official hash and packwiz/Prism package creation**, not the user's actual Minecraft client download or rendered overlay. Keep draft until a fresh Prism client confirms the file appears and mod works. Other CurseForge-only manual-download prompts may still occur and are separate.

author: declercklouis
body:
The remaining P2 items of #35 that are about what an import writes. Stacked on #42. Three commits, one per theme.

### Port scans (P2-2)
In round 2, "Visitors → Lab devices (unidentified)" carried 58 ports. They came from nmap scans of the top 1000 ports by five visitors' hosts. Unanswered attempts were already skipped. The rest were SYN-scan hits on open ports, plus nmap's version probes, which do send data.
- A TCP connection that was answered but carried no data either way (Zeek history without D/d, else zero bytes) is a probe, not traffic. The port still counts as open on the host.
- A source that tried ≥100 TCP ports, with data on ≤20% of them, is a scanner:
  - the import prints it (`Port scan: 192.168.2.88 (Visitors) tried 1015 TCP ports on 17 host(s) in Lab devices`);
  - the summary has a `scans` field, documented in import-format.md;
  - the flows between the two zones name it in their evidence.
- What a scanner reached with only conn.log to show for it becomes one *port scan* request per destination, without ports. Its protocol-log requests (an S7 or Modbus read) stay, because they did reach the controller.
- 4SICS day 2: the visitors' network went from 8 flows (one with 55 ports) to 3: an unidentified flow with one port (a real telnet session), Modbus TCP and S7comm.
- Lists and the access map show at most six ports per flow plus the total ("TCP/80, ... (58 ports)"). The flow page shows all of them.

### Prefixes and zone types (P2-3, round-2 zone-map type)
- A prefix that already sits in a zone of another site is no longer linked. The import says so and suggests scoping the prefix to its site or using a VRF per plant. In round 2 the global 10.10.10.0/24 and 192.168.x prefixes ended up in zones of three sites.
- When the zone map gives an existing zone a different type, the import keeps NetBox's type and prints the difference. Before, the difference was ignored without a word.

### Re-imports and splits (P2-8, round-2 split)
- When the input puts a device or VM in another zone, the import lists the zones it is still in. The new `--move` drops the old membership. A parent or sub-zone doesn't count as "another zone".
- A split now reports:
  - the hosts of each part that are not devices in NetBox yet (their levels live only in this input, so the next import needs the same zone map until `--unknown-import` has created them);
  - the original zone when it is left without members, with the prefix it still holds.
- I did not turn split parts into sub-zones or move the prefix automatically. That changes data a person may have set up, so reporting it seemed the safer default. Tell me if you want it automatic.

Docs: zeek.md, importer.md, import-format.md; CHANGELOG. Tests: new tests for scans/probes, the port cap, cross-site prefixes, zone type, `--move` and the split reports. Full suite 845 OK on NetBox 4.7.4, ruff clean.

body:
Part of #662, #60 and roadmap #48. #60 remains open.

## Summary

This adds the canonical `.productionAccessAudit` trait to six shared root suites: the peer pairing initiator, peer
trust pairing, peer transport negotiation, the neutral diagnostic snapshot, project package I/O and the production
access receipt sink.

The classification scout marked these roots RISK for clock, actor or temporary-directory use, not for audited
reach. Under the #662 coordinator decisions recorded on #662, a `ContinuousClock` read, a `#filePath`
source scan, an in-memory actor fake and temporary-directory I/O are not among the 14 audited operations (decisions
2, 3 and 5). The coordinator confirmed on #662 that `ProductionAccessReceiptSinkTests` belongs in this slice, and is
not deferred, provided it never records into `ProductionAccessAudit.shared`. That is shown in section d below.
Following decision 1 for Track B, the trait is added on both macOS and iOS without a platform guard.

Line numbers below are labelled **base** (`d0061794`) or **candidate** (this branch). In the three named-root files
the two are identical. In the three bare-root files, candidate = base + 1 for every line at or after the insertion.

The edits take two shapes:

- **Three roots** had a single unconditional `@Suite("<name>")` directly above the `struct`. That line becomes
  `@Suite("<name>", .productionAccessAudit)`, and the display name stays byte-identical:
  - `PeerPairingInitiatorTests`: `PeerPairingInitiatorTests.swift` base/candidate line 10,
    `"PeerPairingInitiatorTests"`
  - `PeerTrustPairingTests`: `PeerTrustTests+Pairing.swift` base/candidate line 10, `"PeerTrustTests+Pairing"`. The
    file name differs from the root name. The separate root `PeerTrustTests` (`PeerTrustTests.swift`, base line 101)
    already carries its own `#if os(macOS)`-guarded attribute (base lines 96–100) and is untouched.
  - `PeerTransportNegotiationTests`: `PeerTransportTests+Negotiation.swift` base/candidate line 124,
    `"PeerTransportTests+Negotiation"`. The file-scope helpers above it (base lines 8–122) are untouched.
- **Three roots** had no attribute. Each gains the single line `@Suite(.productionAccessAudit)` directly above the
  `struct`, after a blank line (no doc comment). The inserted line is at the `struct`'s base line, and the `struct`
  moves down one line:
  - `NeutralSnapshotTests`: `NeutralSnapshotTests.swift` base 9 → `struct` at candidate 10
  - `ProjectPackageIOTests`: `ProjectPackageIOTests.swift` base 97 → candidate 98. `enum PackageIOTestSupport`
    (base lines 10–95) is a helper, not a test root, and is untouched.
  - `ProductionAccessReceiptSinkTests`: `ProductionAccessReceiptSinkTests.swift` base 95 → candidate 96. The
    file-scope declarations above it are untouched (section d).

In total: 6 files, 6 insertions and 3 deletions, one attribute per root.

A scripted scan (local review scripts, not committed) counted **17 distinct files** that declare or extend the six roots, with no file
shared between roots:

| Root | Files |
|---|---|
| `PeerPairingInitiatorTests` | base, `+Handshake`, `+Payload`, `+Status`, `+Timeout` |
| `PeerTrustPairingTests` | `PeerTrustTests+Pairing.swift` |
| `PeerTransportNegotiationTests` | `PeerTransportTests+Negotiation.swift` |
| `NeutralSnapshotTests` | base, `+Fixtures`, `+Grounding`, `+Hardening`, `+Limits`, `+Matching`, `+UnicodeHardening` |
| `ProjectPackageIOTests` | base, `+Hardening` |
| `ProductionAccessReceiptSinkTests` | base |

All 17 files are listed in the `FluxKlangMacTests` sources in `project.yml`. They are also in the iOS
`FluxKlangTests` target, which compiles the whole directory. The helper files `PeerTrustTests.swift`
(`PeerTrustTestSupport`) and `PeerTransportTests.swift` (`PeerWireTestSupport`), and the trait's own file
`ProductionAccessScope.swift`, are in both targets too.

All test bodies, helpers, extension files, imports, doc comments, project membership, manifests and checker policy
remain unchanged. The nonrecursive suite trait is unchanged. This does not establish per-case accounting or qualify
hosted execution.

As with every audited root, the trait records a suite-level issue unless `FLUXKLANG_AUDIT_RUN_ID` is a UUID. This is
by design. `scripts/test-audit-run` sets that variable, so these suites must run through that wrapper to pass. Running
them through plain `xcodebuild test` or Xcode now reports a suite-level issue. Test IDs include source lines, so in
the three bare-root files, tests below each inserted line get new IDs.

`scripts/test-audit-coverage/README.md` (base lines 1519–1524) records an earlier slice's decision not to adopt
`PeerTrustPairingTests`, `PeerTransportNegotiationTests` and `PeerPairingInitiatorTests`, because of the clock, the
actor and the file scan. The #662 coordinator defaults now cover those three reasons. This slice does not edit the
README, so that historical note is left for the coordinator.

## Safety review

The review was read-only and ran before editing, for both macOS and iOS. A scripted scan listed the declaring and
extending files and checked their `FluxKlangMacTests` membership. It also listed conditional compilation, file/scan
lines and audit-neutral lines (clock, `Date`, `UUID`, actor, `await`, `Task`, sleep, defaults) in the 17 root files
and the three helper files. It then grepped those files, plus 82 production sources, for audited-reach tokens,
`.shared`, and process-environment reads or writes. The production sources were all of `Shared/Peer`,
`Shared/Diagnostics/Snapshot`, `Shared/Persistence/Projects/ProjectPackage*.swift` and
`Shared/Store/ProductionAccessAudit.swift`.

### a. No audited reach

- **Forbidden tokens.** The grep covered `AppModel`, `WingController`, `WingTransport`, `WingDiscovery`,
  `CoreMIDIInput`, `MIDIClient`/`MIDIPort`, `NWConnection`/`NWListener`/`NWBrowser`/`NWPathMonitor`, `NetService`,
  `Bonjour`, `socket(`/`connect(`/`bind(`, `URLSession`, `HardwareServiceFactories`, `JSONFileStore`,
  `UbiquitousCloudStore`, `CloudKeyValueStore`, `CloudChangeObserver`, `PermissionProbe`, `LocalNetworkProbe`,
  `Assistant`, `FoundationModel`, `LanguageModel`, `Keychain`, `SecItem`, `AVAudio*`/`AVCapture`/`AVAsset`,
  `CKContainer`, `NSUbiquitous`, `ubiquity`, `SFSpeech` and `import` of CoreMIDI, Network, AVFoundation, CloudKit,
  Speech, Security or FoundationModels. Every hit was a peer-trust method named `bind(`, not a socket call: base
  `PeerTrustTests.swift:106,132`, `PeerSessionAuthorization.swift:52,89` and the `.bind` route command case in
  `PeerControlMessage+Command.swift:110,147`.
- **Production imports.** The production closure imports only `Foundation` (41 files), `CryptoKit` (2) and
  `Synchronization` (1, `ProductionAccessAudit.swift`). Its only conditional is `#if DEBUG` around the test-only
  `PeerPairingInitiator.init(testingLastIssuedAttempt:)` (`PeerPairingInitiator.swift:120–126`). Apart from
  `ProductionAccessAudit.swift`, which defines the type, nothing in it references `ProductionAccessAudit` or calls
  `.record(`.

### b. Clock, actor and source scan (decisions 2, 3 and 5)

- **`PeerPairingInitiatorTests`.** It reads the clock once (`let start = ContinuousClock.now`, base/candidate line
  12). Durations are added to that value, and nothing sleeps. `+Status.swift` (base lines 22–34) resolves
  `Shared/Peer/Pairing` (or the mirror's `Sources/FluxKlang/Shared/Peer/Pairing`) from `#filePath`, checks that it

body:
## What and why (V5 paper dashboard audit, 14 Nov)

Bots page:
- **Fewer reads.** Bots reads only the newest terminal-history page. The full history walk was 8 pages and about 1.1 MB per refresh; Bots needed about 1.9 MB per refresh in total. The caption says "showing the newest N of M published terminal rows". The read keeps its `next_cursor`, so it is never presented as complete.
- **Last complete equity.** When the owner withholds equity on a current wallet (e.g. a missing mark), Bots shows the last complete equity and cash with their time and the owner's reason. Conditions:
  - only for a validated, current (≤ 30 s, not future) wallet read that the owner marked degraded;
  - never for a stale read or a client validation failure;
  - the remembered wallet is never a future value and is shown only when it is older than the degraded read;
  - per bot.
- **Exits in the engine's own words** (Falco's decision). Per pair, the card shows what the owner published, with the owner's own bag state beside it (e.g. "Recovery sell live"):
  - "N positions without a fixed-target exit order";
  - other explicit-false rows as "unprotected", with their reason;
  - unknown flags as "protection not published".

  Nothing infers what the bag policy will do.
- **Settings/Readiness.** "Incomplete" names each partial section and the owner's reason.
- **Removed:** an earlier 120 s "hold the last snapshot" change. It broke the reviewed rule that a snapshot older than 30 s is never shown as current. A separate approved PR will do dimmed stale values.

## Review ladder (read-only, no children)

| Round | Seat | Result | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 2 shoulds | 05fc8775 |
| R1 | Sonnet 5.5 | 1 should | 195600e9 |
| R2 | GPT-6.1 Sol | 3 shoulds | card to Falco → option A, the engine's own words: 18c150a7 + a73ed96d |
| Fresh R2 | GPT-6.1 Sol | CLEAN on 18c150a7 | — |

body:
Third security and documentation audit (main 85691b1): nothing critical or high was found. This PR closes every finding.

**Security**
- **MEDIUM:** `install.sh --harden-vault` now writes its `/etc/fstab` lines with `nofail` and an escaped path (`\040` for a space). Before this, a moved, renamed or deleted checkout stopped the next boot in emergency mode. An existing line without `nofail` is now reported.
- **LOW:** every `_search` from the Security Onion and Elastic connectors carries a limit the cluster enforces (`SO_SEARCH_TIMEOUT` / `ES_SEARCH_TIMEOUT`, default 60s). A body passed through from an agent cannot raise it, and a timed-out search is an error, not partial counts.
- **LOW:** `stop` only passes `run/firewall.json` to sudo when the file is ours, not writable by others, and holds a valid port (1024–65535), a known firewall and plain zone names.

**Docs:** `harness.yaml` explains that a connector sees only its `env:` block; README known limits (one dashboard account by design, live-verified back-test/coverage, SO detection management needs Pro); SETUP troubleshooting row, tool counts and the manual fstab example; the SO connector's settings list.

Tests: 266 passed, 16 skipped (new: forged firewall state refused without sudo; search limit always set and enforced). bandit: no new findings. Verified live (read-only) against Security Onion with the limit in place.

author: obvious-autobuild[bot]
body:
## Why

The repo's seven agent contracts live only in `.obvious/skills/*/SKILL.md` + `obvious.md` (PR #17). Claude Code doesn't read those natively — it auto-loads `CLAUDE.md` and reads `.claude/agents/*.md`. This PR adds the Claude Code layer so Claude Code and Obvious share the same agent contracts on the repo.

## What changed

- **`CLAUDE.md`** (repo root, auto-loaded by Claude Code):
  - One-line project intro (AlphaStock / Grid Alpha, bilingual signal platform, Python pipelines + Next.js Explorer + Supabase).
  - The four non-negotiable rules, **word-identical** to `obvious.md` (fixture-mode default, no auto-send, Tiingo ~50 req/hr pacing with backoff, append-only SHA-256 attestation) — verified programmatically to be byte-identical sections.
  - Universe invariants (Two-Universe Methodology v3.0: two disjoint 100-stock universes, quarterly rebalance, monthly review, PSTG excluded) — copied verbatim from `obvious.md`.
  - The **A7 gate**: QA & Attestation is a human approval role (Richard Lu); Claude Code must never bypass, simulate, or self-approve it — client-facing publication only after A7 approval on the staged artifact.
  - Contract parity rule: change an agent contract → update **both** twins (`.obvious/skills/<agent>/SKILL.md` and `.claude/agents/<agent>.md`) in the same PR.
  - Dev commands copied verbatim from `obvious.md`.
- **`.claude/agents/`** — six subagent files (Claude Code frontmatter format: `name`, `description`, `tools`), one per automated role: `intake-supervisor`, `index-market-data`, `verification-gate`, `daily-alpha-editor`, `weekly-scan`, `weekly-alerts`. Each body carries the same Mission/Workflow/Gates/Verification contract as its `.obvious/skills/` twin (copied from it), names the twin path, and references its workflow files (`daily-alpha.yml`, `index-daily.yml`, `weekly-scan.yml`, `weekly-alerts.yml`) and pipelines under `pipelines/`.
- **No `qa-attestation` subagent** — A7 is the human role, by design.

## Tradeoffs

- Subagent bodies are **verbatim copies** of their `.obvious/skills/` twins (generated from them), not paraphrases — drift is possible if someone edits one twin only, so `CLAUDE.md` states the contract-parity rule: both twins change in the same PR. `.obvious/skills/` remains the source of truth.
- Docs-only change: nothing under `pipelines/`, `web/`, or `db/` is touched, so no runtime behavior changes.

## Verification

- [x] Six `.claude/agents/*.md` files + `CLAUDE.md`; **no** `qa-attestation.md` (checked programmatically).
- [x] CLAUDE.md four rules / universe invariants / dev commands byte-identical to `obvious.md` sections (string-compared in a script).
- [x] Every agent MD frontmatter valid: `name` matches its skill directory name; `description` states when to use it.
- [x] Every agent file contains Mission / Workflow / Gates / Verification + a twin-path line.
- [x] Docs-only diff: `git status` shows only `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/agents/` — nothing under `pipelines/`, `web/`, `db/`.
- [ ] CI green on the pushed head.

body:
## What this asks

# 2026-11-14, raised by first-adopter's upstream flush, from its queue entry of 2026-11-09.
# first-adopter starts its version from a scratch branch named after the branch; how the
# workflow learns the branch is left to the design.
- id: one-end-to-end-spec-runs-on-a-deployed-environment
  title: One end-to-end spec runs against a pull request's environment without a pipeline run
  status: idea
  value: Someone chasing one failing end-to-end spec checks a fix in minutes against the
    environment the pull request already has, with nothing deployed and no other stage
    run. Today the only way to run that stage on the host is a whole pipeline run.
  acceptanceCriteria:
    - A workflow a person starts runs the end-to-end stage for one named spec against the
      environment of a named branch's pull request. It deploys nothing and runs no other
      stage.
    - It names the environment as the pipeline does and joins that environment's
      concurrency group, so it never runs beside the pipeline's own end-to-end job.
    - The project's end-to-end stage is told which spec was chosen, and a stage that
      ignores it runs its whole suite.
    - It leaves nothing behind on the host, whether the spec passes or fails.
    - Asked for a branch with no environment, it stops and says so.
  type: feature
  layer: product
  modules: []
  refs: []

## The problem

a browser spec that fails on the host can only be run again by a whole pipeline run, deploy included.

## Why it is portable

any project that fills the branch slot and the end-to-end stage has the same loop.

## What first-adopter already does

it runs such a workflow of its own.

## Summary

Records what was measured and changed on `hycluster-worker-0` (the hypervisor) on 2026-11-14.

**`docs/phase0-current-cluster.md`**
- **Corrections #10:** the August capture called the module and sysctl persistence missing because it looked for `k8s.conf` file names. Both had existed since 2026-02-04:
  - `modules-load.d/k8s.conf` holds `br_netfilter`;
  - `sysctl.d/99-kubernetes*.conf` holds bridge-nf-call and `ip_forward`.

  `SystemdCgroup = true` matches kubelet's systemd cgroup driver, the packages are held at 1.35.3, and swap is off. All of it survived the 2026-11-05 boot. The only real gap was `overlay` missing from `k8s.conf`, which is now added.
- **Corrections #11 and §Network configuration:** the netplan conflict was real. `netplan get` merged to `enp142s0: dhcp4: true`, and the generated port file had `DHCP=ipv4` with `Bridge=br0`. The fix:
  - `50-cloud-init.yaml` is renamed out of netplan's view;
  - cloud-init's network management is disabled;
  - `01-bridge.yaml` is 0600;
  - applied with `networkctl reload` and `networkctl reconfigure enp142s0`, because `netplan try` refuses bridges with custom parameters.

  A 1 s monitor of the host, both VIPs and a hydra-wl0 control-plane node lost **0** packets, and all 8 VMs and both clusters were unchanged.
- **Open items:** the netplan item is ticked, and the host-prep item is annotated with the correction.

**`docs/host-libvirt-prep.md`:** the "do PET-34 first" caution now says the gaps are resolved. A reboot of this host now stops every Hydra VM, so it needs a window.

author: yoecode
body:
Closes #56

## Resumen
Un intento de checkout ya NUNCA puede crear dos ventas, pase lo que pase después del registro:

1. **Venta idempotente**: el id de la venta se genera UNA vez por intento de pago (al montar el paso de pago) y viaja como PK. Un reintento con el mismo id choca contra la clave primaria (23505) y el servicio devuelve la venta YA registrada en vez de insertar otra. El invariante vive en la BD, no solo en la UI: hasta un doble click en el mismo tick es un no-op.
2. **Guarda de estado post-registro**: al registrar la venta, el botón de pagar se retira y aparece "La venta ya está registrada" con dos acciones: **Finalizar** (flujo de ticket normal) y **Reintentar descuento de stock** (re-ejecuta SOLO el paso que falló). Los fallos ANTES de registrar conservan el reintento actual.
3. **Los errores dejan de tragarse**: un fallo de insert que NO sea duplicado (23505) ahora propaga su código real en vez de un mensaje genérico.

## Cambios
| Archivo | Cambio |
|---------|--------|
| `src/features/sales/salesService.ts` | Insert con id explícito; 23505 devuelve la venta existente; demás errores propagan |
| `src/features/pos/checkout/PaymentStep.tsx` | Id de intento estable + guarda de estado post-registro |
| `src/features/pos/checkout/RecordedSaleNotice.tsx` (nuevo) | UI del estado "venta registrada" (Finalizar / Reintentar stock) |
| `src/i18n/translations/en.ts`, `es.ts` | 4 claves nuevas |
| `salesService.test.ts`, `PaymentStep.test.tsx` | 6 tests de regresión |

## Evidencia
- Observado en vivo en staging: 4 ventas duplicadas (ORD-1044..1047, 499.00) de UN solo intento al fallar el descuento de stock (el crash de #58, ya mergeado)
- El seam elegido (montar el paso de pago) sobrevive a todos los reintentos del intento; un checkout reabierto remonta y genera id nuevo, así que una venta legítima del mismo carrito sigue siendo posible

## Plan de pruebas
- [x] `npm run test:run` — **130/130** (124 + 6 nuevos; spot-check del orquestador)
- [x] `npm run build` — OK
- [x] `npm run lint` — exit 0 (warning preexistente conocido)

## Notas
- 558 líneas: tests + comportamiento + el componente de aviso son la unidad (el guard partido en dos dejaría estados intermedios con el agujero abierto)
- `PaymentStep.tsx` quedó en 463 líneas (ya iba en 410 vs la convención de 300) — refactor de división queda como follow-up

author: livxue
body:
## Summary

A streamed answer repaints on every animation frame, and `md()` renders the whole reply each time. A fenced code block that was still growing reached the Shiki highlighter with new source on every frame, so the highlighter's cache never answered and the whole block was re-tokenised per frame, at about 0.3 ms per TypeScript line. On a long answer the page fell to a few frames per second while it streamed.

Two commits:

- `md()` colours a fence only once its closing marker has arrived. Until then the block renders as escaped plain text inside the same card, with the same header and copy button. It is coloured once, when the closer lands, and served from the cache on every repaint after that.
- `warm()` builds the highlighter and reads each grammar once, in background tasks after boot: `scheduler.postTask` at background priority where the platform has it, `requestIdleCallback` where it has only that, and a 250 ms timer otherwise. A polyfill would be a second script, which this page does not load. `main.tsx` calls it last. This takes the highlighter build and each grammar's first-read regex compilation out of the frame in which the first block closes.

Measured in headless Chromium on the stub page, streaming a 28 KB answer that holds a 300-line TypeScript block and an 80-line Python block, 60 s per run:

```
                          before    closed fence    + warm-up
p95 frame                 250 ms    33 ms           33 ms
frames over 50 ms         588       32-40           35-39
long tasks (count)        709       32-36           35
long tasks (total)        86 s      2.5-2.8 s       2.5 s
longest task              232 ms    684-740 ms      572-582 ms
```

Before, the longest task was short but repeated every frame; after, it is the one frame in which the 300-line block closes and is coloured. Of the roughly 580 ms that remain there, most is now the transcript replacing the whole answer's HTML, thousands of highlight spans included, and re-measuring its height on each frame. That is a separate change and is not attempted here.

The warm-up's own cost, in the 8 s after load: three background tasks over 50 ms (219 ms in total, the longest 85 ms), all finished about 1 s after navigation. The boot task itself is unchanged (323 ms against 331 ms).

## Type

- [ ] Fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] CI / tooling
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Other

Performance (`perf`).

## Verification

<!-- List the exact commands you ran and the result. -->

- `npx vitest run src/lib/highlight.test.ts` in `ui-web`: the new test failed before the `prose.ts` change (the unclosed block came back coloured) and passes after it.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/highlight.warm.test.ts`: all seven tests failed before `warm()` existed (`mod.warm is not a function`) and pass after it. Seven mutants of `warm()` each turn at least one test red: building synchronously, dropping the alias dedupe, reading every grammar in one task, the wrong `postTask` priority, no once-guard, building its own highlighter, and running the timer fallback at once.
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=4` in `ui-web`: 304 files, 5327 tests passed, no unhandled errors.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` over the changed files: clean.
- `npm run build && python3 build.py && node scripts/check-page.mjs && node scripts/check-css.mjs && node scripts/check-class-namespace.mjs`: both boot snapshots match their goldens and every check passes.
- `commitlint --from origin/main --to HEAD`, `scripts/check_commit_messages.py origin/main..HEAD`, `scripts/check_large_files.py origin/main...HEAD`, `scripts/check_source_language.py origin/main...HEAD`: all exit 0. The commitlint, commit-message and source-language runs were each shown to fail on a planted violation first.
- The browser numbers above come from scratch Playwright scripts that are not part of this change. Five interleaved runs per build on a quiet machine agreed to within the ranges shown. Two earlier warm-up runs, taken while the shared machine was under heavy load, were much worse (longest task 1.4 s and 4.9 s), and the profile of the worse one was dominated by the per-frame HTML replacement rather than by highlighting. The closed-fence-only build stayed within its range in the same window, so this is disclosed rather than explained.

- [x] Relevant tests pass locally
- [x] Relevant lint / type checks pass locally
- [ ] User-facing docs or screenshots are updated when needed

No user-facing document describes when a code block is coloured, so none changes.

## Risk

- [x] Security impact considered
- [x] Backward compatibility considered
- [x] Rollback path is clear for risky changes

- Visible change: a code block streams uncoloured and takes its colours when it completes.
- A message that ends inside an unclosed fence, from a model that never closes it or a reply that was cut off, now keeps that block uncoloured, live and when restored. The same holds for a markdown file preview whose last fence is unclosed. The text and the copy button are unchanged.
- Every page load spends roughly 0.7 s of background CPU building the highlighter and reading its 20 grammars, in about 21 tasks after boot.
- No new input reaches the highlighter: it reads the same model-written text as before, only later.
- Rollback: revert the squash commit. No data, config or protocol is involved.

## Related Issues

N/A

author: suprio-dev
body:
## Description

The original HTML document had an incorrect structure where the main transaction container was placed outside the `<html>` and `<body>` elements. Additionally, the `script.js` file was loaded before the transaction container was defined in the DOM.

This could lead to invalid HTML structure and JavaScript initialization issues, as the script might attempt to access DOM elements before they are available.

## Changes Made

- Moved the entire transaction container inside the `<body>` element.
- Relocated the `<script src="script.js">` tag to just before the closing `</body>` tag.
- Ensured the `</body>` and `</html>` closing tags are correctly positioned at the end of the document.

## Why This Change?

These changes ensure a valid and properly structured HTML document. Loading the JavaScript after the main content ensures that the required DOM elements are available when the script executes, preventing potential null reference errors during initialization.

## Impact

- Improves HTML document validity and maintainability.
- Ensures reliable JavaScript initialization.
- Preserves the existing transaction UI and functionality.

**Scope:** HTML structure correction only. No changes were made to the existing transaction logic or styling.

author: alharethh
body:
Part of 0.7.0. Most people don't know Settings is on the bar's right-click menu. Starting a running app again is the usual instinct, and until now it did nothing: the duplicate launch was refused silently.

**What changes**
- A refused duplicate signals `Local\Umbra.OpenSettings` and exits. The running bar then opens its settings window, or brings it forward if it's already open.
- Only the process holding the single-instance lock listens, the same pattern as `DevControl`.
- The duplicate still never builds a `ShellHost`, so it never touches Explorer.
- A restart (`--wait-for`) doesn't signal.
- The duplicate passes on its right to set the foreground before signalling, so the window opens in front.
- `App.OpenSettings` now owns the single settings window. The bar's menu goes through it too, so two settings windows can no longer save over each other.

**Checked**
- 187 + 669 tests pass. New tests: a signal reaches the listener on repeat, `Signal` never creates the event, a disposed listener hears nothing, and a restart doesn't signal.
- Live on the laptop:
  - With the dev bar running, launching `Umbra.exe` again logged "asked it to open its settings". The window opened in front of the Claude app.
  - A third launch with the window open left exactly one settings window.

This builds on master, so it shows the old settings window. Merged with #48, it shows the new one; the two PRs don't touch the same lines.


**Also fixes a bug in every release since the settings window existed**
- The app kept only the settings it loaded at launch, while the window edits a copy. So: change the edge, close the window, open it again, and it showed the old edge. The next change of anything then saved the old edge back and moved the bar.
- The window's saves now go through `SettingsWindow.Remembering`, which hands the app a copy of each save.
- The restart note compares against what the bar was launched with (a new `running` argument), so it still says a restart is needed after you reopen the window.
- Tests: a save is remembered as an independent copy, a reopened window shows the saved edge, and the restart note survives reopening. All three fail with the fix undone.
- Not checked live: changing a setting, closing and reopening needs clicks in the window. That's in the owner's test steps.

body:
Reverses #986.

From October 2026 Minior's IVs, CP and level were rolled again for each player who caught it, so a scanner reported it without stats and an IV, CP or level filter never matched. #986 added a note saying so. The game has gone back to one set of stats per spawn, and Golbat reports them again as of UnownHash/Golbat#438 (merged 2026-11-14), so the note now tells people something false: their IV filters on Minior do match.

body:
## O que muda

A versão 4.1 cuida da experiência de uso, principalmente no celular. O motor de cálculo, os modelos e os resultados são os mesmos da 4.0.

### Simulador (`simulador.html`)
- Versão para celular reescrita num bloco só de CSS: alvos de toque de 44 px, campos com fonte de 16 px, áreas seguras do aparelho, abas de baixo com ícones em SVG, menu agrupado com o nome do projeto e janelas em tela cheia.
- Tela inicial no celular começa pelas três ações; tutoriais em trilho deslizante e lista de exemplos recolhida.
- Busca de equipamentos na paleta e busca nos exemplos (ignoram acento e maiúsculas).
- Gráficos no toque: o arrasto do dedo rola a tela e a barra de ferramentas não cobre mais o título.
- Com o teclado aberto as abas de baixo somem; no celular o Enter quebra a linha no campo do agente.
- Arrastar a folha para baixo fecha o menu e a paleta.
- Acessibilidade: abas com `aria-selected`, foco preso na janela aberta e devolvido a quem abriu, botões de ícone com nome, avisos em `aria-live`.
- Tema escuro: cores fixas da seção de tutoriais trocadas por tokens.

### Página inicial (`index.html`)
- Folha de estilos reorganizada em seções com tokens; estilos embutidos viraram classes.
- Barra do topo presa, que vira menu quando os links não cabem numa linha.
- Botões principais logo após o título; no celular, antes do texto longo.
- Tutoriais em trilho, números em 2 × 2 e cartões compactos com "Ver mais" no celular. A página ficou cerca de um terço mais curta no celular.
- Link para pular ao conteúdo, cópia de link com alternativa e estilos de impressão.

### Geral
- `site.webmanifest`, `icon-192.png` e `icon-512.png`: o programa pode ser adicionado à tela de início do celular.
- Brilho do botão dos vídeos dos alunos limitado a alguns ciclos.
- Versão 4.1 no selo, nos títulos e nos dados estruturados; `lastmod` do `sitemap.xml` atualizado.
- `LEIA-ME.txt` com as notas da versão e `CLAUDE.md` com as instruções de publicação.

## Decisões de design a conferir
- A faixa laranja "Versão para notebook (preferencial)" saiu do topo da página inicial; o mesmo aviso continua no herói.
- O selo "Novo na 4.0" da página inicial ficou translúcido, para sobrar um único botão amarelo de destaque.
- No celular, "Passo a passo" saiu da barra do fluxograma e foi para o menu.
- O manual em PDF, a `og-image.jpg` e os títulos dos vídeos continuam dizendo 4.0.

## Como foi verificado
- Simulador percorrido em navegador automatizado em 390 e 320 px (temas claro e escuro) e em 1100 e 1440 px: 37 verificações funcionais passaram, sem erros de JavaScript e sem rolagem horizontal.
- Página inicial conferida em 320, 390, 768, 1180, 1366 e 1440 px.
- As linhas de dados embutidos (bancos de compostos e imagens) não foram alteradas, exceto os atributos da imagem do herói.
- Não foi testado em aparelho real: a detecção de teclado e as áreas seguras do iPhone merecem uma conferida num celular.

body:
## Change

Step 4 of boat expeditions ([plan](https://claude.ai/artifact/61LciJHKi6eKEUsYMfFgwE)). Ships can now cross between worlds, the craft core's unbuilt phase 8. Code is in `code/modules/naval/ship_crossing.dm` and the docs are in `docs/ship-crossing.md`.

- **When the option appears.** The tiller offers **Leave these waters** when the hull is within 4 tiles of the map edge, at all stop, and not grappled. From any world it offers the EXPEDITION slots that hold a land (#5208); from such a land it offers the mainland. If no such land exists, the option does not appear, so the live group sees no change.
- **Packing.** The ship is packed as a record: floors (type, facing, health), masts (rigged), chests with their contents, and loose deck cargo. Items cross by the same travel kinds a traveller uses. Anything that cannot be rebuilt (an engine, a barrel, an animal, a body) keeps her in port, and the tiller names it.
- **Leaving.** She is taken off the water before anyone leaves, and the crew wait inside a hidden gate, so nothing can be picked up twice. Each crew member leaves as a normal region traveller. The first carries the record; payload extras `ship` and `voyage` are added, and the cap is 48 KB for that payload only. If nobody could leave, she is rebuilt where she lay.
- **Arriving.** The far side builds her on free deep water off its edge, coast side first, anchored with her papers. The rest of the crew arrive on her deck. If there is no water to anchor in, her cargo is put ashore. A refused crossing comes back to where she left. A replayed departure takes her off the water again.

author: behemothsecurity
body:
## What and why

Part of #1140. The usage errors were built to look like Python Click's. This PR removes that copy:

- **Click's usage line** (`usage.rs` `usage_line`: `[OPTIONS] … COMMAND [ARGS]...`, `{name}:<a|b>`) is replaced by clap's own `Command::render_usage()`, so the `usage:` note matches the usage line `--help` prints (`opentide validate [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]`, `opentide setup ci [OPTIONS] <ci_platform>`).
- **Click's error wording and its special case.** Click raised "requires an argument" and "does not take a value" before it chose a command, so those two errors had no command and no notes. Now every clap error goes through one path that sets the command and adds the notes. The wording is opentide's own, with values quoted by `{:?}`:
  - `Unknown command "x".` (was `No such command 'x'.`)
  - `Unknown option "--x".` (was `No such option: --x`)
  - `Unexpected argument "x".` (was `Got unexpected extra argument(s) (x)`)
  - `Invalid value "y" for --x: choose from a, b.` (was `… 'y' is not one of 'a', 'b'.`)
  - `… : expected an integer` and `… : expected a number`
  - `--file requires a value.` and `--json does not take a value.`
  - `did you mean "validate"?`
- **Click's `BadParameter` style:**
  - the `Invalid value:` prefix is gone from the validate, share and setup refusals and from `setup`'s `bad_parameter`
  - `Invalid value for '--x' / '-y':` becomes `--x: …`
  - the refusals name the flag that was typed (`--publish` or `--no-publish`, `--promotion` or `--no-promotion`) instead of the `--a/--no-a` pair
  - `new` quotes values with `{:?}`, and the completion shell refusal uses the same wording
- **Click's help text:** `HELP_FLAG_HELP` `Show this message and exit.` becomes `Print help`. This changes `commands --json` and `serve`'s `commands_digest`. The contract for the digest is its algorithm (sha256 of the sorted, compact document), not a fixed value. `tests/serve.rs` recomputes it, so no test pins it.

### Behaviour kept, and the tests that show it

- `failure.code` (`usage_unknown_command`, `usage_unknown_option`, `usage_invalid_choice`, `usage_invalid_value`, `usage_missing_option`, `usage_error`), `failure.argument`, `failure.suggestion` and exit `2` are unchanged. The `usage.rs` unit tests check code, argument and suggestion for each error kind, along with the new message and notes.
- Everything that was accepted or refused before still is; only the text changed. All `framework_usage_*` tests in `usage.rs` pass, and so do `tests/setup_ci.rs`, `tests/framework_binary.rs`, `validate_query.rs` and `generate_goldens.rs`.
- One deliberate change: a missing value (`validate --file`) or a value given to a flag (`--json=1`) now names its command (`command: "validate"` / `"info"`) and prints the `usage:`/`help:` notes. Before, it had an empty command and no notes. Covered by the new test `framework_usage_a_missing_or_unwanted_value_has_the_usual_notes` and by `app.rs`.
- New test `framework_a_share_option_its_subcommand_ignores_is_refused_by_its_flag`: the share refusal names `--publish` / `--no-publish`, keeps `usage_invalid_value`, and prints the usage note in plain mode.

## Verification

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p opentide-cli -p opentide --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask check-layers`
- [x] `cargo test -p opentide-cli`: the lib (541 tests) and every integration target except `tui_pty`, which was not run.
- [ ] `cargo test -p opentide --test cli` built but ran 0 tests (it probably needs a feature). Its one changed line matches `framework_binary.rs`, which passes.
- [ ] `bindings/node/test/cli.test.mjs`: the expected string is updated but the test was not run.
- [ ] `scripts/ci-local.sh --full`: not run, because the shared disk is short on space.

- [x] User-visible change: Changed entry under `## [Unreleased]` (At a terminal), and the earlier invalid-choice bullet updated
- [x] CLI surface change: `docs/cli/mcp.md` usage example updated
