author: cbeck88
body:
## Motivation

The upgrade tests need the latest consensus version of the PR binary and of the latest release.
`test_full_upgrade.sh` and `test_partial_upgrade.sh` each started one 4-validator devnet per binary to learn it.
Each devnet took 65–81 s, because the script waited for the consensus version to stop climbing.

Measured on a warm staging push, job `devnet (upgrade)`:

- The four probes took about 300 s of a 735 s job.
- The partial upgrade test spent 142 s on probes, then printed "Consensus version unchanged at 22. Skipping test".

This PR replaces the probe devnets with one REST request to a single node.

- The `/version` route serves `consensus_heights`, the consensus version schedule of the binary.
- A single client node answers it 2–3 s after it starts. It needs no peers.
- The latest release (v4.12.1) already has the route. Both binaries are asked the same way.

Design choices:

- **No cache, no new CLI flag.** A flag cannot reach a released binary. A cache next to `VERSION` would save about 3 s per script and add state that can go stale. Four queries cost about 12 s in total.
- **The version is the number of scheduled entries in `consensus_heights`.** That is the version a devnet on the default schedule settles on, which is what the probe measured. It equals `latest_consensus_version` today.
- **The node runs without `CONSENSUS_VERSION_HEIGHTS`**, as the probe devnets did.

One behaviour change, in the partial upgrade test only.
The test took a block height from the probe and named it the activation height. It was the height the probe devnet happened to be at when it stopped.
The test now gets the real activation height of the latest version (25 today) from the same schedule.
This path only runs when the two binaries differ in consensus version. They do not differ today, so this path did not run here. Please review that part with care.

Commit: read the consensus version from one node, and delete `probe_stable_consensus_version`, `stop_probe_nodes` and `PROBE_PIDS`.

## Test Plan

Local, PR binary built with `test_network` and the CI release profile, release binary v4.12.1 built by `download_and_build_latest_snarkos`:

- `query_default_consensus_version` returns `22 25` for both binaries on mainnet, testnet and canary, in 2–3 s. The probe gave 22 for both.
- The result is the same with a bogus `CONSENSUS_VERSION_HEIGHTS` in the environment.
- A binary that exits at once makes the function return 1 with a log line.
- `./.ci/test_full_upgrade.sh` passes. It derives the same 22-entry `CONSENSUS_VERSION_HEIGHTS` for both binaries and `EXPECTED_MAX_CONSENSUS_VERSION=22`. Both queries took 3 s in total.
- `./.ci/test_partial_upgrade.sh` logs `consensus_version=22, activation_height=25` and `consensus_version=22`, then skips. It took 5 s.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the three files.

Expected saving: about 290 s per `devnet (upgrade)` job.

## Documentation

None.

## Backwards compatibility

CI scripts only. No node code changes.

author: epicbagel
body:
## What this adds

Two things every host that shares a candidate ends up building for itself, as library components (0.26.0):

- **`CandidateSharedProfile`**: the content of the page someone opens from a link to a candidate.
- **`CandidateShareDialog`**: the dialog that makes that link.

Both are presentation only. The kit pin doesn't move: everything is built on primitives `@epicbagel/saas-kit` 1.16.0 already has.

## `CandidateSharedProfile`

Content only. It draws no header, brand, theme or shell, so the host wraps it in its own page and decides the width. It fetches nothing, navigates nowhere, stores nothing and holds no timer.

Every part is optional and shows only when its data is passed. A profile given a name alone is a heading.

| Prop | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `person` | `{ name, avatar, cover, title, company, location, yearsExperience, profileLink: { href, title, icon } }`, all optional |
| `anonymised` | Shows nobody (see below) |
| `eyebrow` | Above everything, such as the search the person was shared for |
| `people`, `personId`, `onPersonChange(id)`, `openingPersonId` | The people one link shares, and the switch between them |
| `archived` | A notice above a profile that dims |
| `voiceNote` | `{ src, transcript }` |
| `note` | `{ text, author }` |
| `fit` | `{ roleTitle, grade, summary, evidence }`; `grade` is `CandidateGradeBadge`'s own settings, `evidence` is `CandidateSummaryBullet[]` |
| `summary`, `experience`, `experienceOptions`, `education`, `skills`, `certifications`, `languages` | The profile itself; `experience` is `CareerHistoryItem[]` |
| `children` | The host's own sections, after the profile's |
| `decision`, `decisionReason`, `onDecide(decision, reason)` | The reader's Yes or No. No `onDecide`, no Yes or No |
| `reasonOptional`, `reasonSuggestions`, `reasonPrompt`, `reasonSheet` | How the reason is asked for: typed in a dialog, or voice first in the sheet |
| `clientNotes`, `onAddNote(text)`, `noteVoice`, `noteMaxLength` | The reader's own notes. No `onAddNote`, no note field |
| `readOnly` | Shows the answer and the notes and takes none |
| `credit` | A closing line, such as who shared it |
| `titleLevel` | The name's heading level; sections sit one under it |
| `renderAudio` | The host's own audio player |
| `labels`, `decisionLabels` | Wording, with generic defaults in `candidateSharedProfileLabels` |
| `id`, `className`, `style`, `data-*`, `aria-*` | The only things passed on to the root |

Promises drive the busy and error states as elsewhere in the library. While `onPersonChange`'s promise is pending (or the host names `openingPersonId`) the switcher says who is opening, and it, the Yes or No and the note field are held. If it rejects, a line under the switcher says so. The answer and a half-written note start afresh for each person.

The outline holds at any `titleLevel`: the name, then every section one level under it (the reader's answer and notes among them), then each role one under that.

### What it guarantees

- **Anonymised is enforced, not left to the host.** The name, the avatar, the cover and the profile link are never drawn, the switcher names nobody ("Candidate 2") and shows no faces, and the questions it asks say "this candidate", whatever `person` and `people` hold. What the host passes as an employer's name or a note is the host's to redact.
- **No prop takes a record.** A note is its words and who they are from. The grade and the fit are passed on field by field. Every root takes an id, a class, a style and `data-`/`aria-` attributes and drops anything else, so a field spread in off a view model is never written into the page as an HTML attribute. A test spreads a view model with extra fields and asserts none of them is in the page.
- **Print is a resume.** The profile loses its border, and the switcher, the archived notice, the profile link, the audio player, the answer, the notes, the credit and a career's "Show more" are left out. A spoken note prints as its transcript, and the fit's grade and sentiment dots print in colour.
- **Long words wrap.** A link pasted into a note wraps inside the profile and isn't cut off at its edge.

### Sections, each usable alone

| Export | Main props |
| --- | --- |
| `CandidateSharedProfileSwitcher` | `people`, `value`, `onChange(id)`, `opening`, `error`, `anonymised` |
| `CandidateSharedProfileHeader` | `person`, `anonymised`, `titleLevel`, `padding`, `eyebrow`, `status` |
| `CandidateSharedProfileVoiceNote` | `src`, `transcript`, `renderAudio`, `titleLevel` |

All take `labels` (`CandidateSharedProfileLabels`).

## `CandidateShareDialog`

Every part is optional. With none, it is a title and a button that makes the link.

| Prop | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `open`, `onOpenChange` | The host's |
| `candidateName` | For the title and the summary |
| `avatar`, `headline`, `reason` | The summary at the top, with the sharer's own reason |
| `audiences` | `{ id, label, description, fields, ready, live, liveDescription }[]`: who the link is for. `fields` is a slot whose values the host holds |
| `anonymisable` | Offers named or anonymised |
| `note`, `noteMaxLength` | A typed note for whoever opens the link |
| `recorder`, `defaultNoteFormat` | A slot for a spoken note, such as `CandidatePresentationRecorder`; with `note`, the two sit behind a switch that keeps both mounted |
| `choices`, `defaultChoices`, `onChoicesChange` | `{ audience, anonymised, note }`, held by the host or by the dialog |
| `onShare(choices)` | Makes the link. Returns the URL or a promise for it; resolving with nothing closes the dialog |
| `url` | The link, where the host already has one for these choices |
| `copyOnShare` | Copies in the click that makes the link |
| `waitingFor` | Holds the share button and says why, such as a recording still uploading |
| `error` | An error of the host's own |
| `labels` | Wording, with defaults in `candidateShareDialogLabels` |

Also exported: `candidateShareLinkText(url)`, the short form the link is shown in.

What the dialog holds for one opening (the choices, a share on its way, the link) is kept above the kit's responsive dialog, which swaps a dialog for a bottom sheet as the window narrows and remounts what it holds. A tablet turned mid-share loses nothing, each opening starts afresh, and a share that settles after the dialog has been opened again is dropped.

**Copying.** Copy calls the clipboard synchronously inside its own click, since some browsers take a write only from the gesture, then says "Copied" and announces it. Where the browser refuses, or has no clipboard, the whole link is put in a field, focused and selected, to copy by hand. `copyOnShare` asks the clipboard inside the create click for a link that arrives later (a `ClipboardItem` holding a promise), writes it once it is here in a browser that can't be asked ahead, and otherwise leaves the link with its Copy button and claims nothing.

body:
## Summary

States that **INDEPENDENT SET on graphs of thickness at most k (fixed k ≥ 1)** is NP-complete, as a `theorem_wanted` in
`WantedExt/Complexity/NPComplete/IndependentSetThicknessWanted.lean`, in the same form as the
existing statements there and the proved results in
`CSLibExt/Computability/Complexity/Karp`.

- Problem: Fix `k ≥ 1`. INSTANCE: a graph `G = (V, E)` of thickness at most `k` and a positive integer `K ≤ |V|`. QUESTION: does `G` contain an independent set of size `K` or more?
- Literature: Garey and Johnson (1979), [GT20] INDEPENDENT SET (problem, `K ≤ |V|`) and comment "Remains NP-complete for cubic planar graphs [Garey, Johnson, and Stockmeyer, 1976], [Garey and Johnson, 1977a], [Maier and Storer, 1977]"; M. R. Garey, D. S. Johnson and L. Stockmeyer, "Some simplified NP-complete graph problems", Theoretical Computer Science 1(3) (1976), 237-267, doi:10.1016/0304-3975(76)90059-1; D. S. Johnson, "The NP-completeness column: an ongoing guide", J. Algorithms 6(3) (1985), 434-451, doi:10.1016/0196-6774(85)90012-4, Table 1 thickness-k row, INDSET entry N [GJ]. Johnson's definition, Section 3: "Thickness-k Graphs. These are graphs G = (V,E) where E can be partitioned into sets E₁ through E_k such that Gᵢ = (V,Eᵢ) is planar, 1 ≤ i ≤ k." Johnson's thickness-`k` row is for a fixed `k`; the theorem is stated for every fixed `k ≥ 1` (the catalog record's "k ≥ 2 for hardness" note is not needed for this problem, which is already NP-complete on planar graphs, `k = 1`).
- Shipped definitions: `withThickness`, `WellFormed k` (simple edge list, thickness at most `k`, `0 < K ≤ n`), `independentSetThicknessDec k`, and `theorem_wanted independentSetThickness_npComplete (k) (_hk : 1 ≤ k)`; instance, graph and question reused from `TriangleFreeIndependentSetWanted` (as `IndependentSetK14FreeWanted` does; its triangle-freeness is not used).
- Campaign record: `W2.t16-thickness-k-indset` (NP-complete problems ledger).

## Clause map

| Source clause (verbatim) | Lean |
|---|---|
| "Graph G = (V, E)" [GT20] | `TriangleFreeIndependentSetInstance` = `(n, edges, K)`, `Graph i = edgeGraph n edges`; simple-edge-list conjunct of `WellFormed` |
| "graphs G = (V,E) where E can be partitioned into sets E₁ through E_k such that Gᵢ = (V,Eᵢ) is planar, 1 ≤ i ≤ k" (Johnson), "k fixed" | parameter `k : ℕ`; `GraphThickness.GraphThicknessFeasible (withThickness k i)` in `WellFormed`: `∃ f : Fin edges.length → Fin k, ∀ c, (edgeGraph n (edgeClass … f c)).IsPlanar` (the merged GRAPH THICKNESS question, edge classes `f⁻¹(c)`, each spanning all `n` vertices, shared `SimpleGraph.IsPlanar`) |
| "positive integer K ≤ \|V\|" [GT20] | `0 < i.2.2 ∧ i.2.2 ≤ i.1` |
| "Does G contain an independent set of size K or more, i.e., a subset V' ⊆ V such that \|V'\| ≥ K and such that no two vertices in V' are joined by an edge in E?" [GT20] | `TriangleFreeIndependentSetFeasible`: `∃ s : Finset (Fin n), K ≤ s.card ∧ (Graph i).IsIndepSet s` |
| "NP-complete" | `independentSetThicknessDec k ∈ NP ∧ ∀ L ∈ NP, Cslib.CookLevin.PolyManyOneRed L …` |

## Validation

- VMVM `lake build WantedExt.Complexity.NPComplete.IndependentSetThicknessWanted` (Lean 4.35.0,
  Lean Commons image, repository lakefile options): PASS, 17 closure modules for the batch build (the five new modules, their parents and the probes), build 125.2 s, peak 5.1 GiB of 8 GiB; no warnings in the log.
- Probes on the exact head (scratch file, not committed), compiled in the
  same VMVM build: yes (`k = 1`): path `0 - 1 - 2`, `K = 2`, `{0, 2}` (thickness via thick1 (all edges in class 0, `edgeClass` evaluated by `decide`) plus an explicit straight-line drawing (`fin_cases` + `linarith`)). No (`k = 1`): the triangle, `K = 2` (a planar graph that is not triangle-free, so the reused parent's own restriction is indeed dropped). Boundary: `k = 0` rejects a graph with an edge; `K = 0` and `K > n` rejected.
- Duplicate screen at `origin/main` 1b8d30b71: no `*Thickness*` INDEPENDENT SET module; planar variants (`IndependentSetCubicHamiltonianPlanarWanted`, `IndependentSetTwoConnectedCubicPlanarWanted`, `IndependentSetPlanarRegularHamiltonianWanted`) are subclasses; open PRs: title searches `thickness`, `dominating set`, `hamiltonian circuit`, `independent set`, `max cut`, `steiner tree`, `planar` (`is:pr is:open`): no thickness-restricted PR.
- API reuse: `TriangleFreeIndependentSetWanted` (instance, graph, question; reused the same way by `IndependentSetK14FreeWanted`); `GraphThicknessWanted` (`GraphThickness.GraphThicknessFeasible`, `edgeClass`, `GraphThicknessInstance`; the merged statement of Johnson's partition into `k` planar spanning subgraphs, also reused by `GraphThicknessTwoWanted` via a `withBound` helper, mirrored here as `withThickness`).
- `git diff --check` clean; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `opaque`,
  `native_decide`. `scripts/check.sh preflight`: exit 0 (about 97 s). The full
  `scripts/check.sh` runs in CI.

## Self-review

- [x] Self-review completed per REVIEWING.md on the exact head bytes (verdict line below)

Claim: for each fixed `k ≥ 1`, INDEPENDENT SET on graphs of thickness at most `k` is NP-complete. `WellFormed k`: simple edge list, thickness at most `k`, `0 < K ≤ n` (GJ's bound). A planar graph has thickness at most `1 ≤ k` (all edges in one class), so the planar hardness result transfers by the identity map to every fixed `k ≥ 1`. Membership: `V'` plus the edge partition. author: danielmillar
body:
## Problem

Staff couldn't listen to recordings in Discord. The WAV was attached through a file component inside the Components V2 alert card, and Discord shows that as a download link, not an audio player. Within one Components V2 message, attachments can only appear through components, so the clip can't sit outside the card in the same message.

## Fix

- The alert card is posted first, with no file attached.
- When `include-audio` is on, the recording follows as a second, plain webhook message: the WAV plus a small "Recording · <id>" line. Discord shows a player for an audio attachment on a plain message. The recording message doesn't ping the role again.
- Both messages are sent one after the other by VoiceWarden's single Discord consumer, so the recording sits directly under its alert. Retries and rate limits apply to each.
- If the recording fails (for example, it's too large for the server), the failure is logged and the alert still counts as delivered. If the card fails, no recording is sent.
- The `include-audio` comments in `config.yml` explain the separate message.

## Verification

- `./gradlew build` passes. `DiscordWebhookServiceTest` covers:
  - the card having no attachment or file component
  - the recording being a plain message with the byte-exact WAV and no role ping
  - the two messages arriving in order
  - a failed recording leaving the card counted, and a failed card sending no recording
  - the existing report and `/vw discordtest` flows
- Not yet checked against a real Discord channel. `/vw discordtest flag` posts a sample alert with a recording.

author: francescodoffizi
body:
## Summary

- Send an explicit empty JSON body (`{}` with `Content-Type: application/json`) on stream control `POST` requests in `app/src/main/assets/web/shared/stream.js` and `app/src/main/assets/web/local/live-view.html`.

## Root Cause

Following PR #688 (`fix(server): bound HTTP request heads and validate body framing`), `HttpRequestHead.java` rejects requests containing `Transfer-Encoding` with `400 Transfer-Encoding is unsupported` because the embedded HTTP/1 server does not implement chunked transfer decoding.

When accessing the web UI through reverse proxies such as Cloudflare Tunnel / Zrok, bodyless `fetch(..., { method: 'POST' })` requests (e.g., `/api/stream/enable`, `/api/stream/disable`, `/api/stream/quality/...`) can be forwarded by the proxy without `Content-Length` and with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, causing live video stream activation/quality changes to fail with HTTP `400`.

Adding `body: '{}'` forces browsers and reverse proxies to frame the request with a known `Content-Length: 2` instead of chunked transfer encoding.

## Changes

- `app/src/main/assets/web/shared/stream.js`: added `_postEmpty(url)` helper and updated all 4 bodyless stream `POST` calls (`/api/stream/disable`, `/api/stream/enable...`, and both `/api/stream/quality/...` calls).
- `app/src/main/assets/web/local/live-view.html`: updated the inline `POST /api/stream/quality/` call to send `Content-Type: application/json` and `body: '{}'`.

## Verification

- `node --check app/src/main/assets/web/shared/stream.js` passed.
- `./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug` succeeded (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).
- `./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest --tests "com.overdrive.app.server.*"` ran (all `com.overdrive.app.server.*` tests passed; 3 unrelated pre-existing failures in `HebrewLocaleSupportTest` and `RecordingIdApiContractTest`).

## Security
- **Next.js 16.0.3 / React 19.2.0 → 16.4.2 / 19.3.0.** The old versions are affected by [CVE-2025-66478](https://nextjs.org/blog/CVE-2025-66478) ("React2Shell", critical remote code execution) and later [denial-of-service advisories](https://nextjs.org/blog/security-update-2025-12-11).
- Every dependency pinned (many were `latest`).

## Bugs fixed
- **In any language other than English, every multiple-choice answer was marked wrong**: translated options were compared to the English answer. Grading now uses option position, and `tests/questions.test.ts` checks every question's translations line up.
- Competitive: rapid repeat submits scored twice and skipped questions; the timer ran side effects inside a state updater; the final confetti read a stale score; an unknown `?difficulty=` crashed the page.
- The sound toggle only logged to the console; it now plays short Web Audio tones.
- "Larger"/"largest" text sizes didn't match the settings type.
- Fonts were loaded but never applied (Comic Sans is missing on most non-Apple devices); now Nunito.
- Home headline read "Master The Matrix MATRIX" in every language; removed a third-party brand name from the competitive card.
- Lobby used `Math.random` during render (hydration mismatch).
- Corrupted Arabic and Hindi strings fixed; Arabic now lays out right to left, and the page language follows the setting.

## Cleanup
- TypeScript errors are no longer ignored at build time; added ESLint config.
- Removed 48 unused UI components, about 40 unused packages and v0 placeholder assets; added `.gitignore`, README and CI (lint, type check, tests, build).

author: kaizen403
body:
An active HTTP speech download could hit the startup cutoff before its first complete clip arrived. A fully downloaded WebAudio clip could also be abandoned while waiting for the user's playback gesture. Keep provider speech through these waits while preserving Pause, Stop, ownership and recorded replay bytes. Only growth in an actual audio JSON string extends startup recovery. Downloads share a 60-second / 24-MiB cumulative budget across retries and prefetch claims; whitespace, control traffic and malformed prefixes cannot keep extending the wait. Stalled downloads retain bounded fallback, and no path fabricates a speech start, alignment or measured duration. Register the synthetic historical-resume regression, with optional private narration replay. Replace stale intro command counts and silent-teaching assumptions with behavior checks; retain spoken-unit checks in teaching without requiring neutral figure intros to recite numerical planner roles. Align the billing cleanup and reservation fixtures with the current callback contracts. Validation: 87 real audio consumer groups; 30 startup scenarios; 41 diagram/audio scenarios; full `verify:speech`; synthetic and private historical resume replay; affected core/app typechecks and lint. Workspace and billing checks are also run on the integrated branch. Historical transport timing and physical device behavior remain unverified. Production validation is pending while the replacement host stays behind the recovery maintenance page; this PR does not assert closure of every historical speech issue.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The changes since the previous review appear safe to merge.

Summary

author: dribeiro0
body:
## What

A pure motion model for the island, asked for by David (relayed by Opus 2 on the board). **Two new files, nothing else touched, and nothing imports it yet**, so no behaviour changes from this PR alone.

- `client/src/motion.ts`
- `client/tests/motion.test.ts` (25 tests)

Based on `main`, not on `client/liquid-ui`: the module depends on neither #70's pill nor #76's island, so it can merge whichever surface @sysoutprntlne picks.

## How it moves

`stepIslandMotion(state, input, dt)` takes what Artemis is doing (`idle`, `listening`, `working`, `awaiting_approval`), the island's home point and an optional target point, and returns one frame: position, direction, stretch, scale, wobble energy, ring-to-droplet morph, trail points, a descriptive `phase`, and `settled`.

- **Leaving:** the ring collapses into a droplet over 0.55 s (ease-in-out cubic) and does not move until it has.
- **Travelling:** the droplet follows the target on a spring (stiffness 320, damping 30), so a moving target such as a text caret is followed smoothly. It stretches along its direction of travel, up to 1.3x at 2500 px/s, and leaves a trail with a point every 6 px that lasts 0.45 s.
- **Coming home:** when the work ends, an approval opens, or the target goes away, it flies back, lands with a squash and a wobble (size spring 180/12, wobble decaying at 1.4/s), then opens back into the ring.
- **Listening:** the ring stays home, quietly alive. No travel.

The constants are the GNOME prototype's (`client/prototypes/water-desktop/…/extension.js` in #80). From Opus 2's research on other products I took no numbers: the two ideas that mattered there are already the rules below (motion collapses to a still state under reduced motion, and state must never be visual only).

## Rules it keeps

- **Reduced motion or the motion setting off:** exactly one still frame, whatever Artemis is doing, including mid-flight.
- **Approvals:** while one is waiting, the droplet comes home and holds completely still, and a target offered then is ignored. Motion never shows or decides approval state.
- **Decoration only:** no window, canvas, focus, timer, React or Tauri in the module; no new permission. `phase` is descriptive: text and speech must keep coming from real state, never from this.
- **`settled`** tells the renderer it can stop its animation loop.
- **Frame-rate independent:** fixed 1/240 s physics steps; a stalled frame is clamped to 50 ms.

## Tested

`npm test`: 77 passed (8 files; 25 new). `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `npm run build`: OK. Windows 11, Node 24.

The new tests cover: rest and listening; morph timing and easing; arriving without overshoot; stretch capped at 1.3x and aligned with travel; following a moving target; trail spacing, order and lifetime; landing squash, overshoot and wobble for each way of coming home; stillness during an approval; wobble decay rate; the island being dragged or warped to another monitor; the still frame under reduced motion and with motion off; the same result at 60 and 144 fps; clamping and bad time steps. I also broke two constants on purpose (landing squash, trail lifetime) and confirmed the matching tests fail.

## Not verified, and not in this PR

- **Nobody has seen it move.** It is numbers only; how it looks depends on the renderer, and it has not been compared side by side with the GNOME prototype.
- **Not wired in.** `FlowWindow.tsx` on #76 has its own wander-and-return loop; replacing that with this model is for Jun, or for me if Jun asks.
- **No caret source.** Following the text caret of another app on Windows needs native code and a capability, which is Avery's review. The model only accepts a `target` point.
- **One difference from my posted plan:** a target that jumps far is flown to (stretch still capped), not snapped. Only the island's own home jumping is treated as a warp.
- **Not run on Linux or in CI yet.**

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `ec1bf0de-4944-47d8-b4aa-4ead82a41d26` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/labinius-fast-challenge at `cb78b114f0e4758c0fd2b82c16fede9298b17a7c`.

Current best score: 294.391692033969. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Grok 4.7
Harness: Cursor

# solution-arm: drop the paired-test clocks from the commitment sweep

## Summary

The promoted ARM record times every transform group and every sink with `cntvct` so it can print `ctxf` lines. Those reads stay on the official path. This submission deletes the four lines that take and store those stamps inside `sums2`. The table front stays on `lut_pass2`, the same dispatch as the record. No local wall-clock score is claimed.

## Why the previous send is not repeated

`f67d810e-db40-4a31-b5b1-1905d3d05261` changed `sums2` from `lut_pass2` to `lut_pass` and left the clocks in place. Official score 299.447951954789 against the record 294.391692. Rejection: score did not improve current best. That diff is reverted here. `sums2` calls `lut_pass2` again.

## Base

Parent `94a3b66b-7a4d-4d7c-9b9e-012c1a0d17d3`, source `cb78b114f0e4758c0fd2b82c16fede9298b17a7c`, official 294.391692 ms. That tree is the L1 scratch plus the table-front diagnostic. On the SVE build, `lut_pass2` alternates `pass_lut_asm` and `pass_lut_loop` and the sweep reads `cntvct_el0` twice per batch per sweep, once around the transforms and once around the sink.

## What changed

File: `solution-arm/proof_generate/src/ntt_sms.rs`, function `sums2` only. Four lines deleted:

- `let t0 = ctx::now();` before the transform loop
- `ctx::add([ctx::now() - t0, 0, 0, 0, (groups * LOCK) as u64]);` after it
- `let t1 = ctx::now();` before the sink
- `ctx::add([0, ctx::now() - t1, 0, 0, 0]);` after the sink

`ctx::now` is `mrs cntvct_el0`. `ctx::add` updates a thread-local pair of counters. Neither feeds the commitment. The transform loop is unchanged: `indices_asm`, `lut_pass2`, `pass_c_asm`, `pass_d_out`. The sink call is unchanged. `ctx::flip` at the start of `sums2` is unchanged, so the loop-versus-straight-line alternation is the record's. `ctx::report` still runs at the end of the worker and will print zeros, because nothing adds into the counters.

No other file changes. The generated assembly, the reduction set, `SINK`, `SWEEP`, `CHUNK`, and the modulus are the record's.

## Why the proof is the same

The deleted lines do not write the scratch buffer, the sweep buffer, the accumulators, or the proof bytes. They only sample a timer and add the delta into a thread-local array that `ctx::report` prints. `tests::sms_commit_matches_reference` compares the SMS commitment with the reference commitment. It passed after this deletion.

## Local check

From `solution-arm/proof_generate`, debug profile, offline:

```text
cargo test --offline --bin labinius-fast tests::sms_commit_matches_reference -- --exact
```

Result: `tests::sms_commit_matches_reference ... ok` (1 passed, about 34 seconds). The host is Apple Silicon, so this runs the NEON table front, not the SVE kernels. It checks that removing the stamps does not change the commitment bytes on that path. It is not a timing result. The SVE kernels are the same instructions as in the record; only the `mrs` and the counter update around them are gone.

An interval pass over the round-13 reductions, the same propagation as `lazy_lut_intervals`, found no extra level-5 skip and no extra dropped level-4 input reduction that stays inside `i16`. That lever was not edited.

## What this does not claim

No laptop milliseconds and no claimed score. Near-identical entries on this track spread by about 0.79 percent. `f67d810e` landed 1.72 percent above the record, so that particular dispatch was not a free redraw. This note does not predict where the clock removal will land. The official five-run median is the score.

The `ctxf` lines in the job log will not carry per-worker transform or sink times for `sums2`, because those counters are no longer updated. Workers still call `ctx::report`.

## Reproduce

```text
git checkout cb78b114f0e4758c0fd2b82c16fede9298b17a7c
# in sums2, delete the two ctx::now bindings and the two ctx::add calls
# leave lut_pass2 in place
cargo test --offline --bin labinius-fast tests::sms_commit_matches_reference -- --exact
```

Official evaluation is `bash .yukon/benchmark.sh --track arm` on the Graviton4 runner.

## Credit

The sweep, the table front, and the diagnostic harness are from `94a3b66b` and `ab6bce13`. `f67d810e` is the rejected `lut_pass` dispatch and is not in this tree. This submission only removes the `sums2` timer updates.

## What stays on the hot path

Each batch pair still runs `ctx::flip` once, so the record's side bit still selects `pass_lut_loop` or `pass_lut_asm` inside `lut_pass2`. Workers 0 and 4 remain controls. For every tile the order is still index packing, the table front, `pass_c_asm`, then `pass_d_out` into the sweep buffer, then `sink`. Chunk ends still use `chunk_row2`. The CRT tail and the five-byte wire stores are untouched.

The deleted counter update was also the only place that recorded how many transforms the worker had run (`groups * LOCK` in the fifth lane of the stamp). `ctx::report` divides by that count. With no updates the printed `ctxf` deltas are zero over a zero count, which the format clamps with `max(1)`. That print is diagnostic. It is not an input to the proof.

A reduction-skip search with the same signed intervals as `lazy_lut_intervals` rejected every extra level-5 node and every extra dropped level-4 input reduction. The skip list in `skip_lut5` is therefore the record's list of 27 nodes, and `gen/gen_pc.py` was not edited.

author: genshanxinli
body:
This is by an automated agent, not a human.

The NPU owns the live L2B ethertype table in the FE window at
`0x1fb50e00..0x1fb50f00`, but the driver has no read-only view of it:
`ppe/entries` walks the per-flow FOE table, and the only L2B state the
driver touches is the multicast bit in its own entry.

This adds `ppe/l2b`, a 0444 debugfs file implemented in
`airoha_ppe_debugfs.c` (as a new 7.3 patch), dumping the 256-byte window as
64 rows of `idx offset value`.  The read path uses `airoha_fe_rr()` on the FE
mapping only; it never reads the NPU's `0x1e900000..0x1ebfffff` window and
never writes a register.  The vendor-named ethertype enable mask and the
8-entry ethertype table are decoded; the rest of the window is printed raw.
The table is NPU-owned and can change between reads, so the dump is a
snapshot, not a lock-protected view.

This is for the bridge/NPU experiments; there is no behavioural change and no
write path.  Existing `entries`, `bind`, `usage`, `bind_rate` and `tb_regs`
output is untouched.

Testing:

- `patch -p1` applies the new 7.3 patch on top of the current airoha patch
  series (checked against a reconstructed 7.3 tree with the patches that
  touch `airoha_ppe_debugfs.c` applied).
- The modified `airoha_ppe_debugfs.c` compiles with the airoha target
  toolchain (`aarch64-openwrt-linux-musl-gcc`) and the 7.3 kernel build flags.
- No on-device run: the issue's booted-board check needs a rebuilt and
  flashed kernel, so the 64-row output has not been captured yet.
- GitHub Actions did not schedule checks on this branch.  The repository's
  workflows do not auto-trigger on push/pull_request here (only a manual
  `workflow_dispatch` has ever run), so `kernel.yml` still needs a manual run
  before merge.

body:
## Summary

The current documentation can direct work back toward path machinery that already exists, while obscuring the main remaining theorem: a successful occurrence-compatible BH escape from every required source.

This documentation-only PR targets `main` and aligns ten human and agent entrypoints around:

- Uniform entry into the explicit minus-Class-A zero-return predecessor set ([#452](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/issues/452)), with source coverage proved separately from selected escape.
- Reuse of existing occurrence decoding and coherent finite path lifting, plus the narrower original-transcript interface.
- Parallel residual A1′ work through the prescribed fixed-hub rays and common blocks at the same position.
- The separate C4 exclusion/extraction premises, ternary scope including nonunits, all-alphabet extension, and external spectral implication.

The new [BH escape roadmap](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/blob/42f20c2208f16e5656c407cded8f00c71c7a4839/docs/bh-escape-roadmap-2026-11-14.md) is the detailed source and acceptance reference. Older dated observations remain labelled as historical. The README, agent guide, proof ladder, research roadmap, direct-attack note, documentation index, state reconciliation, A1′ proximality note and side-findings ledger are synchronized.

## Work shown

### Assumptions and hypotheses

The universal completion target is ternary primitive irreducible Pisot substitutions, including nonunits. The proposed #452 increment is restricted to the declared minus-Class-A parameters and the required nonzero cyclic seed descendants. The full literal predecessor count is not a reachable-state count. Zero integral displacement allows unequal terminal letters.

This branch is based on `main@c9358c2d46d7b306853609e2c5a090328aff92c3`; it cites the unmerged #573 and #574 proof sources by full revision rather than incorporating their source files.

### Derivation / reduction

The classified target supplies the final edge to zero. Complete source coverage plus a selected escape into that target would establish the scoped hitting statement. Existing `packet_path_lift` composes valid finite steps; it does not supply universal escape existence. A finite maximum depth requires hitting coverage throughout the relevant seed graph, including transient sources.

A1′ requires the same block position in both fixed rays. The revised proximality note states that quantifier explicitly. Parameter-independent depth is not required; the known obstruction to such a depth across Class A comes from a separate plus-sign subfamily.

### Evidence and replay

- All 517 Markdown files pass `python3 tools/check_markdown_source.py`.
- All six claim-governance checks pass with `PYTHONPATH=tools python3 -m claim_governance.cli --root .`.
- Whitespace checks pass. The changed documents' 438 relative and pinned-source link destinations were checked against local files and the named Git trees.
- A separate source review checked the mathematical scopes and identified the plus-sign/minus-sign depth distinction.
- GitHub snapshot, November 14 at 15:43 EST: #573 source `6bf0b9704501eb763cbb4323c3fd1f939d6f11c8` passed family gate [43630544741](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/actions/runs/43630544741), full library [43630544688](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/actions/runs/43630544688), and original archive [43630544838](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/actions/runs/43630544838); broad checks remained running.
- #574 source `fd23a6681db651762e49c9c959a9aad682fb007f` passed its focused gate [43638030436](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/actions/runs/43638030436); its full-library workflow [43638030298](https://github.com/larsbx/pisot-substitution-conjecture-research/actions/runs/43638030298) remained running at that observation.

These are receipts for those proof revisions. This documentation change does not claim a new Lean or Mojo proof run.

### Negative controls

Retain productive cycles with unused successful exits; incomplete child covers; equal projected labels with different occurrence contexts; physical zero versus integral zero; original transcripts extending beyond production terminalization; and the non-Pisot productive but infinite-carrier example. Common factors at different positions do not establish proximality.

### Non-claims / remaining gaps

Universal BH, residual A1′, C4, G1 and PSC remain open. This PR changes no proof source, executable kernel, generated ledger or governed claim status. The family spectral implication still uses published results outside Lean. Source acceptance, integration and independent human review remain separate. No research PR is merged by this documentation update.

## Why
The old prod server (213.139.209.132) was lost in the Beget incident of Nov 1–2. Prod has been rebuilt on a new Beget VPS, **155.212.210.31**, running the same release as before (053760c). DNS for `crm.shabash-hub.ru` already points there, and HTTPS is set up.

## Changes
- `deploy.yml`: new `SSH_HOST` and the new server's pinned ed25519 host key.
- SSH config in the workflow: `ConnectionAttempts 10`, `ConnectTimeout 15` and keepalives. Beget currently drops part of inbound traffic from abroad, and GitHub runners are abroad, so a single lost connection shouldn't fail the deploy. The external health check also retries longer.
- `backend/pom.xml`: Testcontainers 1.19.x → 1.21.4. GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner now uses Ubuntu 26, whose Docker requires API ≥ 1.40, while 1.19 speaks 1.32. Every integration test failed before deploying anything ("client version 1.32 is too old"). Without this bump, any deploy fails at the test step.
- `backend/scripts/prod/SERVER_SETUP.md`: a runbook for rebuilding the server from scratch.

## Server side (already done)

## Summary

Step 2 of ADR-0044's rollout order (runbook, *The catalog's read-only role*), for **staging only**:

- staging's code server is pinned to the image built from main at 06355de (#80), whose jobs carry their own credentials in their `dagster-k8s/config` tags;
- the catalog owner's connection string, the R2 write token and the variables composed from them are removed from `dagster-staging/values.yaml`. The code server keeps the non-secret settings and `HEARTBEAT_URL`;
- ADR-0044 is marked Accepted, since the operator approved #80, along with the status lines that pointed at it.

Prod is unchanged. It still runs the image without tags, so its values must keep the credentials until staging's digest is promoted. That later pull request removes them from prod and adds prod to the test below.

- **What changes:** staging's Dagster runs the new image, and its code server stops holding the lake's write credentials. Each run now gets them from its own job instead.

- **How to undo it:** revert this PR. Argo CD puts back the old pin and the old values.

- Orchestration: `uv run pytest` 48 passed, `ruff check .` clean, CI's `mypy` invocation clean. A test loads the real staging values and merges them with the real tags through dagster-k8s's own launcher code. author: ajroetker
body:
When one item's output awaited ordered publication, it could occupy the same error slot used for provider retries. A later provider failure in that partition could therefore be returned as `ArtifactPublicationPending` instead of retaining its retry outcome and source identity.

Use one stack-only outcome aggregate for native reported batches, sequential fallback, document execution, and the transport-partition wrapper. It tracks publication progress separately from the first genuine provider retry. Control/fatal errors remain immediate; scheduling, concurrency, and payload ownership are unchanged.

Expand the existing Raft publication fixture with 35 new scenarios: multiple documents with held output, failures before/after pending items, six-document cohorts crossing the four-call execution boundary, native per-item text failures, and sequential text fallback. Each failed item is recovered independently; the tests verify its retry fingerprint, unaccepted-output invisibility, final per-source output, and no regeneration of accepted siblings. Document callback counters are atomic for concurrent execution.

Validation: all three focused mixed-cohort regressions passed (63 scenarios total, zero failures or leaks). `zig fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and full license-header checks passed. The repository watch build was stopped after success; `make gc` was run.

Follow-up to #1689, addressing the fresh static review's multi-document mixed-outcome coverage opportunity.

author: guetteman
body:
Implements #56, delivery 6 of the Calendar tools in #48: an agent can answer an invitation for one of the owner's accounts, as accepted, declined, or maybe. The account answers only for itself, so the tool must never answer as someone else or change anything else in the event. The accepted design and the observations on real accounts are in the comments of #56.

## What changes

- **A new tool, `respond_to_event`, in the group "Respond to invitations".** Like every tool, it starts at Not allowed. It is marked `irreversible`, because Google emails the organizer, so the connection page asks for confirmation before setting it to Allowed. With Ask first, no answer reaches Google before the owner approves.
- **It answers only in the account's primary calendar,** for the guest entry that Google marks `self`. It takes no `calendar`, because on another calendar Google's `self` marks that calendar's owner. Unlike the other tools that use `run`, it refuses extra fields, so an agent that sends `calendar` gets `invalid_arguments` instead of an answer in the primary calendar.
- **Refusals before any write.** An event the account organized, an event where it is not a guest, and an event that is not a regular event all get `invalid_arguments` naming `event`. "Not a guest" includes an invitation that reached the account only through a Google Group. A missing or cancelled event gets `not_found`.
- **The approval page** shows the event, its start, whether it is a single event, one occurrence, or a whole series, the organizer, the current and new answer, and the whole note. It also shows the earlier note whenever one exists, as removed or replaced. It says who can read the note.

## Decisions

- **The write names only the account's own entry.** It is an `events.patch` with `attendeesOmitted: true`, which Google documents as the way for a guest to update only their own response, and one attendee: the `self` entry's address as Google gave it, the answer, and `comment`. On the maintainer's accounts this changed only that entry, with `guestsCanModify` both off and on, and the entry kept `optional`, `displayName`, and `additionalGuests`.
- **`If-Match` ties the write to the read just before it.** A 412 returns `google_unavailable` with nothing changed and no retry, so the next call reads again and repeats every refusal. A read without an etag gets no write.
- **`sendUpdates=all`.** On the maintainer's accounts it was the only value that made Google email the organizer.
- **An answer without a note sends `comment: ""`.** Google erased the earlier note both with `""` and without the field, so the tool always sends it and the page always shows the note that goes.
- **The texts do not understate who reads the note.** Whether Google also emails other guests is not observed, because the test run had no second guest. The permission text and the tool description say that the organizer gets the answer and the note by email, that other guests who can see the guest list and people the organizer's calendar is shared with can read them, and that Google may email them to those guests. The approval page says the same, and names the people the calendar is shared with only when the call has a note.
- **The result never claims an answer Google did not confirm.** `my_response` comes from the `self` entry in Google's reply. When that entry is missing or holds another answer, the call reports an unknown outcome, as after a lost response, so the agent does not take the answer as given.
- **`onExcessProperty` in the tool registry.** The registry decided whether to refuse extra fields from `create`. It is now a field on the tool, with that same default, so the 16 existing account tools keep their schemas and decoding.

## How to review

Start with `src/google/respond.ts`. `invitation` holds every refusal, and both the approval view and the run go through it. `respondToEvent` sends the patch. Then the tool entry at the end of `src/mcp/tools.ts`, and the small schema additions in `src/google/events.ts` (`etag`, and `organizer` and `comment` on an attendee). The preview `/__pages/approval-respond-to-event` shows the approval page.

## What was tested

- `vp check`, `wrangler types --check`, `vp test run` (2,167 tests), and `vp build` pass on the final commit.
- `test/respond-to-event.test.ts` asserts the exact patch URL, headers, and body. `test/respond-to-event-view.test.ts` takes the tool through Ask first, approval, and `get_approval`.
- I broke the code on purpose six times and the suite failed each time: the address taken from `account` instead of the `self` entry, other guests in the body, no check of the attendee `organizer` flag, `my_response` taken from the request, no `If-Match`, and no `comment` when the agent gives no note.
- Not observed on real accounts: whether another guest's email arrives, an invitation through a Google Group, and `If-Match` on a guest's answer (Google returned 412 for a stale etag on the organizer's patch in #55's run).

## Not included

- The run reads the event again after approval, and nothing compares that read with what the owner approved. So a change to the event between the approval page's last read and the run's read would go unseen. The run still repeats every refusal, and the write still names only the account's own entry. #54 adds the fix to the approval mechanism: an approved run receives the approved view values. A small follow-up PR, after #54 merges, closes the window for `respond_to_event`. It builds the view and the write from one read, writes nothing when that view differs from the approved one, and sends that read's etag in `If-Match`.

## After merge

On the deploy, an agent in Claude Code and an agent in Claude on the web each accept a test invitation and decline one occurrence of a test series, and the maintainer approves one call from a phone with the tool at Ask first. This is the last check of #56, so leave #56 open until it is done.

author: deconstructo
body:
Fixes #371. Stacked on #374 (base branch `fix/370-jit-named-let-nontail`); merge that one first.

This is phase 0 of the bytecode-to-LLVM JIT plan: make it possible to see what the JIT does, and to test it, before changing how it compiles.

## What is added

- `(jit-compiled? proc)`: documented for a long time but never registered.
- `(jit-refusal-reason proc)`: a string saying why a closure is not compiled, or `#f`. The code generator's own message is kept (it used to be swallowed by `catch (...)`).
- `CURRY_JIT=on|off|force`. `force` compiles every accepted closure on its first call. `off` never compiles.
- `CURRY_JIT_LOG=1` prints a summary at exit (chunks compiled, chunks refused by reason). `=2` also prints one line per chunk.
- `jit_gate` in `src/runtime.c` is now the one place the refusal conditions are written. `maybe_jit_bcc`, `jit-compile!` and `curry-jit-call` each had their own copy.

## Behaviour changes

- `maybe_jit_bcc` now stores `V_FALSE` in `jit_val` for every refusal decided before code generation (it did so only for closures with upvalues). Every reader of `jit_val` treats `V_FALSE` and `V_VOID` the same, and the conditions cannot change after the closure exists.
- `curry_llvm_jit_compile` takes an error buffer.

## Testing

- `ctest`: 172/172, Release build with `BUILD_LLVM=ON`, `.scc` files cleared. 12 entries are new: `jit_force_*` runs 11 core suites with `CURRY_JIT=force`, `jit_off` runs the JIT tests with `CURRY_JIT=off`.
- The whole suite also passes with `CURRY_JIT=force` set for every test (172/172). The CI LLVM job now does this as a second pass.
- A build with `BUILD_LLVM=OFF` compiles and runs.
- Not tested: Linux / gcc (CI will), and a Debug build with LLVM.

## Review

Commits a90a414 and 5b32ad7 had an independent code review and a security review. Neither found a crash, a build break or a wrong result. The last commit applies their findings (UTF-8 cut in the error text, control characters in log lines, `off` not covering `curry-jit-call`/`curry-jit-eval`, a per-closure compare-and-swap, wording). The last commit itself was not reviewed again.

Known, not changed: if code generation leaves by `longjmp` instead of a C++ exception, the chunk stays uncompiled with no recorded reason, and `jit-refusal-reason` returns `#f`.

body:
Closes #110

## Summary

Adds the dispatch-only GKE suite `operator_diskfull` (test `operator_diskfull_refuses_then_recovers`). It fills the data volume of `tape-0` with `dd`, checks that appends are refused with `507 storage_full` while reads keep serving and `tape_storage_degraded` is 1, frees the space with `rm -f`, then checks that an append is accepted again, that `tape_storage_degraded` is 0, and that replay has the five acked ids followed by the new one. Refused ids are not in the replay.

This branch was redone from the default branch (`-r2`), so the workflow already contains `operator_partition`.

## Changes

- `crates/tape/tests/it/e2e/operator_diskfull.rs` (new): the suite and five unit tests (`is_storage_full_*`, `metric_value_*`, `workflow_lists_the_suite_and_keeps_it_out_of_all`).
- `crates/tape/tests/it/e2e/mod.rs`: `mod operator_diskfull;`.
- `k8s/gke-test-job/operator_diskfull/` (new): `job.yaml`, `kustomization.yaml`, `rbac.yaml`. The Role keeps only pods get/list/watch, pods/exec create/get, persistentvolumeclaims get/list and tapes get/list. No delete and no patch.
- `.github/workflows/gke-test.yml`: header line, `suite` option, the `case` branch and the error text for `operator_diskfull`. The `all` line is unchanged.
- `STATUS.md`: one sentence in the `gke-test-cluster-acceptance` row.

## Cluster run waits for approval

The cluster run is not started. One run uses the same single-pod CR as `operator_recovery` (one server node, one client node, Job deadline 70 min). The repository has no USD figure, so the owner approves the cost before running `gh workflow run gke-test.yml -f suite=operator_diskfull`.

author: 0z5a
body:
### What does this PR do?

Type of change: Bug fix

Fixes #3262

`create_sgpt_mask` ran the SparseGPT update on a copy of the weight and returned only the mask. `run_search` only calls `set_mask`. So `mode="sparsegpt"` kept the dense values of the unpruned weights, unlike what the docs say.

Changes in `weight_sparsity/sparsegpt.py`:

- The pruning loop moves into a private `_sgpt_prune()`, which returns the updated weight in its original shape. Pruned entries are zero.
- `create_sgpt_mask()` keeps its signature and returns `_sgpt_prune(...) != 0`, as before.
- `SparseGPTSearcher._compute_mask()` copies the updated weight into `module._parameters["weight"]` and returns the mask from the same tensor. It writes to the raw parameter because `module.weight` is the masked copy.

The mask does not change. The masks for a `Linear` and a `Conv2d` are identical before and after this change.

### Usage

```python
import modelopt.torch.sparsity as mts

model = mts.sparsify(model, "sparsegpt", config={"forward_loop": forward_loop})
# kept weights now include the SparseGPT update; the 2:4 mask is unchanged
```

### Testing

The runs below are on `main` at `86bd9b78`, before the rebase onto the current `main`; none of the code or test files this PR touches has changed since. All on CPU. `Linear(64, 32)` with correlated inputs (rank-8 signal plus noise), as in the issue.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp32: kept weights equal to dense weights | True | False |
| fp32: output MSE of sparsified model | 0.2491 | 0.0481 |
| fp32: output MSE of dense weights times the same mask | 0.2491 | 0.2491 |
| bf16: output MSE of sparsified model | 0.2537 | 0.0491 |
| 2:4 pattern holds (fp32, bf16, `Conv2d`) | yes | yes |
| Mask identical to main (`Linear`, `Conv2d`) | n/a | yes |
| New `test_sparsegpt_updates_weights` | FAIL (kept weights unchanged) | PASS (0.65 s) |
| `tests/unit/torch/sparsity/weight_sparsity/` | 109 passed | 110 passed |

```bash
pytest tests/unit/torch/sparsity/weight_sparsity/test_sparsify.py
```

The new test sparsifies and exports a small `Linear`. It checks three things:

- At most two nonzeros per group of four.
- The kept weights differ from the dense ones.
- The output MSE is below 0.9 times the MSE of the dense weights under the same mask.

### Before your PR is "*Ready for review*"

- Is this change backward compatible?: ✅ (the API is unchanged; SparseGPT-sparsified weights now differ from before, as documented)
- If you copied code from any other sources or added a new PIP dependency, did you follow guidance in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: N/A
- Did you write any new necessary tests?: ✅
- Did you update [Changelog](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.rst)?: ✅

### Additional Information

Not tested:

- FSDP2: the raw weight is a DTensor and the copy is not handled.
- Megatron tensor parallelism: each rank writes its own shard, updated with its local Hessian.
- Optimizers that already hold separate fp32 master weights, which do not see the write. Sparsify before building the optimizer.
- Shared (tied) weights: the write now reaches every module that shares the parameter. `*lm_head*` is excluded by the default rules, so tied embeddings are only affected if a user rule enables it.

This change was drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); the test results above are from the runs described.

- `apps/api/.../tracing.py`: `build_tracing` (None when off; OTLP/HTTP exporter when the endpoint is set; an injectable exporter for tests), FastAPI instrumentation, SQL spans, `trace_id` for logs.
- `packages/rag/.../tracing.py`: a small `Tracer` protocol with a no-op default, so the rag package names no tracing library (same pattern as `RetrievalObserver`).
- Manual spans: `embed_query`, `vector_search`, `lexical_search`, `fuse`, `rerank` (with `fallback`), `llm.stream` and its child `llm.first_token`; attributes book_id, k, candidate counts.

- JSON log lines carry `trace_id` inside a span (builds on #224).
- `compose.observability.yaml`: a `jaeger` service, ports on 127.0.0.1 only, no secrets. It is added to the existing #226 file (no second file).

author: aschelbert
body:
## What this does

Boards can now get small jobs done (a bulb on a high fixture, a wall rack, boxes to storage) by booking a TaskRabbit Tasker from inside an action, and follow the job there until it's paid.

**Where it shows up:** a new **Book a Tasker** button on the resident request's "Work order, letter or decision recorded on this action" checklist item. It also appears on repair items in common-area and preventive-maintenance actions.

**The lifecycle, all on the action:**
- **Book:** the form is prefilled from the action. It has the kind of job, task, what the Tasker sees, day and time window, how they get in, estimated time and a choice of Taskers, with ones the board rated well listed first.
- **Spending check:** up to the building's Tasker limit ($300 unless the board changes it) can be booked without a vote. Above that, the board records a vote on the action first. Anything over the bylaws spending limit is refused as a vendor project.
- **Asked → Accepted → On the way → Working → Done → Paid**, then rate the Tasker.
- **When it goes off track:** no reply (ask someone else), the Tasker cancels (rebook), the board cancels, more time or parts requested (approve or decline, a vote if it goes over the limit), and a problem with the work (payment held, free return visit or close without paying).
- **Licensed trades:** jobs that read like plumbing, wiring, roofing, gas or water damage are pointed to a vendor work order instead, with an override. A Tasker's completion note that mentions that kind of work prompts a vendor work order too.

**How it connects to existing records:**
- **Work orders:** when a Tasker accepts, a work order is opened on the action and approved, charged to Maintenance & Repairs. Changing the scope or the Tasker updates it; cancelling sets it to $0.
- **Payment:** confirming the work enters the final bill as the work order's invoice and pays it through the normal Funds accounting. It then ticks the checklist item, which completes the step.
- **Decision trail:** every update is recorded on the action.
- **Owner:** gets a comment on their request when the job is scheduled, and again if it's cancelled.

## The Tasker limit

The most one job may cost before the board votes. It's a building setting saved in `financial_settings`, so the whole board works to the same limit. It can be changed in two places:
- **Funds › Settings › Billing rules**, next to the other money rules.
- **Change** on the Tasker panel of an action (board and manager only). A change made there is recorded on that action's decision trail.

It must be a whole dollar amount from $0 to the bylaws spending limit, above which owners vote. $0 means every Tasker job needs a vote.

## Database

Both migrations are **applied to staging and production**.

- **`068_tasker_jobs.sql`** adds `tasker_jobs`: one row per job, keyed by building and job id, tied to its action and deleted with it. It names its work order by the app's id (`work_orders.local_id`). Status, checklist item and Tasker are columns; the full job is kept in `data`. Board members, the manager and the account owner read and write it; owners can't see it. Checked on both: row-level security on, policies and indexes present, no advisor findings, and an insert by a signed-in user with no board or manager role was refused.
- **`069_tasker_limit.sql`** adds `financial_settings.tasker_limit` (default $300, never negative). Existing buildings got the $300 default.

The app saves each job as it changes, one save at a time per job so a slow save can't overwrite a newer status. It loads the building's jobs on sign-in. Demo mode keeps jobs in the browser.

## Merges from `main`

- #181: the Tasker jobs load now sits in the new `loadTenantStores` helper.
- #182: it fixed the same date-dependent Home calendar test this branch had fixed, so `main`'s version is kept and this PR no longer changes that test.

## Not done yet

- **TaskRabbit is simulated.** `src/features/tasker/taskRabbit.ts` is a demo client, and the panel has demo buttons to play TaskRabbit's side. Going live means replacing it with real API calls (from a server function) and pointing TaskRabbit's status webhooks at `applyUpdate` in `lifecycle.ts`.
- **Guesses to check:** category names, fees, the time a Tasker has to accept and the late-cancellation rule are marked `VERIFY` in the code. I couldn't reach the partner documentation.
- **Not built:** lobby notices, telling the front desk, messaging the Tasker, real photos (only a count is stored) and a drafted reply to the owner at the last step.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run`: 71 files, 535 tests pass. New:
  - `src/__tests__/tasker.test.tsx`: the full lifecycle, the off-track cases, the spending check, licensed-trade detection, booking from the checklist item, and changing the limit (its bounds, the trail entry, and Change on the panel for the board but not for others).
  - `src/__tests__/taskerJobsDb.test.ts`: saving, save order and loading, against a fake Supabase client.
  - `src/__tests__/ux2/funds.test.tsx`: setting the limit under Funds › Settings › Billing rules.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
- Clicked through the whole lifecycle in the local demo app on a resident request action, from booking through paying and rating.
- Not tested: saving and loading a real job or the limit through the app against a real database.

author: photonpower
body:
## What

Two steps for the Path Tracer plugin (two commits):

1. **Coloured materials.** A material can have a spectrum (column *By wavelength*, e.g. `450:0.05, 550:0.1, 600:0.6, 650:0.8`): the reflectance of diffuse, mirror and glossy materials, the absorption of glass, at wavelengths in nm – straight lines between the values, the first / last value outside. It replaces the constant value. New default material `red paint`.
2. **Exact normals where rays hit curved faces.** Until now the normal at a hit was interpolated over the triangle; with coarse triangles a mirror or a lens sent the light on slightly wrong. Now the point where the ray meets the surface itself is found with Newton's method from the triangle's hit, and the normal and (u, v) are the surface's there. Flat faces keep their triangles' values; so do hits where the method does not arrive. The path's vertex stays on the triangle (within the mesh tolerance), so visibility and the weights are as before. Panel: *Exact normals on curved faces* (on).

## How

- `Materials.wavelengths()` sets tables [material, wavelength] of the reflectance and the absorption beside the index; `eval`, `sample` and the absorption inside glass take the paths' wavelengths – in the walks, at connections and when photons are gathered.
- `pt_nurbs.local_basis` / `Surface.at`: points one by one with only the basis functions that are not zero, so the cost per hit does not grow with the control net; `Mesh.shade_exact` uses it per face.

Only files of the plugin, its test and the changelog change.

## Tests

`tests/python/test_pathtracer.py`: a closed box whose paint reflects 0.2 at 450 nm and 0.6 at 650 nm against the series of each wavelength (light tracing, path tracing, bidirectional); the lit box seen by a camera (path tracing, photon mapping); glass that absorbs at one wavelength only against both closed forms; points one by one against the grid evaluation; normals at hits on a sphere patch of 45 triangles right to 1e-9 (interpolated: off by more than 1e-3); light paths off a coarse spherical mirror with and without.

Run locally: this test. Note: the CI Python has no numpy, so CI skips this test – it has only run locally.

author: kanylbullen
body:
Closes #228 (in-app feedback, 14 Nov: "rest timer time setting not synced to watch").

**Cause.** The default rest (Settings → Training, `rest_default_seconds`) is stored in each device's own DataStore and is not synced. The watch has no screen for it. In **companion** mode the phone times the rest with its own value, so that mode was already right. A **standalone** watch (linked to the account) used its own value, which was always 90 s.

**Fix (the owner chose the Data Layer over a synced setting):**
- `WatchWorkoutState.defaultRestSeconds` (core, additive and nullable: an older watch ignores it, an older phone leaves it out).
- `WatchStateSource` fills it from `restTimer.defaultSeconds`, so the phone's `WearStatePublisher` publishes it, and republishes when the setting changes.
- On the watch, `followPhoneDefaultRest` (`TungWearApp`, while the app is on screen) reads the phone's DataItem, even in standalone mode, and stores each new value with `setDefaultSeconds`.
- A watch without a paired phone (or an iPhone user) keeps its own value. A rest set per exercise was already synced and is unchanged.

Tests: `WearCommandHandlerTest.theStateCarriesTheDefaultRest` (the phone's state follows the setting) and `PhoneDefaultRestTest` (the watch stores each new value, and nothing when the field is missing). `WearCommandHandlerTest`, `LocalWatchCommandsTest` and `:core:jvmTest` pass, and `:data:compileKotlinIosArm64` compiles. Not tested on a real watch: that needs a dogfood build on the phone and the watch.

author: patrickfanella
body:
Lets Edda's GM use Claude Code skills (for example `run-rpg-sessions`, `fictional-worldbuilding` and `edit-fiction`) when it runs through `claude-bridge` on the owner's subscription.

- **Bridge:** `-skills` lets a request with `"skills": true` run `claude` with only the `Skill` tool and `--setting-sources user`, which is where `~/.claude/skills` loads from. Every other request keeps all tools off, as before.
- **Provider:** `llm.claudecode.skills` and a per-profile `skills` switch make the `claudecode` provider send `"skills": true`, and add one line to the system prompt telling the model to load the skill that fits before writing the turn.
- **README:** shows turning skills on for the GM-turn profile only.

Measured on Kvant with a GM-style turn on Sonnet 5.5 at high effort: without skills, about 8.5 s and about 4,700 input tokens. With the hint, the model loaded a skill, and the turn took about 11 s and about 10,000 input tokens. Without the hint, it loaded none. That cost is why skills go on the GM turn and not on state extraction or summaries.

Checks: `go test ./...` passes. The new tests cover the bridge (skills only when both allowed and asked), the provider (request flag and hint) and the roster (only the GM profile gets skills).

body:
## Co zmienia

Decyzja Bartosza z 14.11.2026 („mam dość zatwierdzania i nakładania etykiet”, potem „Tak, rób wszystko”): agenci sami scalają swoje PR, bez pytania go. Repo jest od dziś w organizacji FaktWay (`FaktWay/FaktWay`), gdzie działa kolejka scalania GitHuba. Kolejka sprawdza każdy PR razem z `main` i z PR przed nim, a przy konflikcie albo czerwonym teście wyrzuca go zamiast scalać.

Ustalenie z przeglądu ustawień: „Filtr: straż”, RLS i Mobile **nie były wymaganymi kontrolami**, więc automatyczne scalenie mogło wpuścić PR z czerwonym filtrem. Skrypt z tego PR je dopisuje.

## Zmiana

- **Workflowy** (`ci`, `security`, `filtr`, `mobile`, `filtr-straz`, `agent-guard`): `merge_group`, żeby wymagane kontrole zgłaszały się na commicie grupy z kolejki.
  - Straż i agent guard są tam pominięte. Ocena była na PR przed wejściem do kolejki, a pominięte zadanie GitHub liczy jako zaliczoną kontrolę.
  - Grupy `concurrency` dostają `|| github.ref`, żeby grupy kolejki nie anulowały się nawzajem.
  - `mobile.yml` bez filtra ścieżek przy PR (około 30 s). Wymagana kontrola z filtrem ścieżek nie zgłosiłaby się w PR bez zmian w `mobile/`.
- **`scripts/ops/kolejka-scalania.sh`** (nowy): ruleset „main - ochrona podstawowa”.
  - Dodaje regułę kolejki: merge, grupy po 5, CI do 60 min.
  - Dopisuje wymagane kontrole: Filtr: straż, Filtr: testy prawne, RLS isolation, Mobile.
  - Wyłącza „strict”, bo to robi kolejka.
  - Przed zapisem pokazuje stan przed i po, pyta i zapisuje kopię. Sprawdzone na sucho (odpowiedź „n”): przed 9 kontroli bez kolejki, po 13 kontroli z kolejką.
- **Zasady:**
  - `AGENTS.md`: niezmiennik 1 (agent wrzuca swój PR do kolejki `gh pr merge N --auto`; cudze tylko na polecenie Bartosza albo sesji, która je zrobiła; wdrożenie i migracje dalej na polecenie Bartosza), niezmiennik 2 i „Żelazny filtr”;
  - etykiety `zgoda:*` nadaje autor PR po ostatnim pushu i po drugim czytelniku bez otwartych uwag;
  - te same zasady w `docs/runbooks/scalanie-pr.md` (przepisany na kolejkę), `filtr.md`, `wdrozenie-produkcji.md`, skillu `/filtr`, szablonie PR i `mobile/AGENTS.md`.
- **`filtr/zgody.json`:** opis i `masloigor`, żeby sesje Codexa Igora też mogły nadać etykietę.

Nie zmienia: `.claude/settings.json`. Klasyfikator trybu auto odmówił agentowi dopisania `gh pr merge` i `gh pr edit` do dozwolonych poleceń („Undermining Oversight”), więc to zostaje decyzją Bartosza w jego ustawieniach.

## Najpierw test

Zmiana zasad i workflowów, bez kodu aplikacji.
- **Skrypt rulesetu:** uruchomiony na prawdziwym API w trybie bez zapisu, pokazał stan przed i po.
- **Workflowy:** sprawdzi je CI tego PR, a grupę kolejki pierwsze wejście do kolejki po uruchomieniu skryptu.

## Ponowienie od zera

n/d: CI i dokumenty. Skrypt jest idempotentny, bo kolejkę zastępuje, a kontrole łączy przez `unique_by(.context)`.

## Weryfikacja

| Sprawdzenie | Wynik |
|---|---|
| `vitest run tests/filtr/` | 36 plików, 353 zielone |
| `vitest related` zmienionych plików + testy czytające `AGENTS.md`, runbooki i `zgody.json` | 8 plików, 156 zielonych |
| `node --test scripts/ci/agent-guard.test.mjs` | 14/14 |
| `tests/unit/siec-blokada-testow`, `ci-rls`, `tests/filtr/straz` (czytają workflowy) | 71/71 |
| `kolejka-scalania.sh` na sucho | przed 9, po 13 kontroli i kolejka |

Poziom filtra: R0. Maszyneria (`.github/**`, `.claude/**`, `filtr/zgody.json`) potrzebuje `zgoda:zmiana-filtra`. Ostatni raz od Bartosza, bo zasady z tego PR działają dopiero z `main`.

## Migracje

Brak.

## Kolejność i po scaleniu

1. Najpierw #773 (obrazy GHCR), potem ten PR. Oba metodą merge, jeszcze bez kolejki.
2. Po scaleniu tego PR Bartosz uruchamia jedną linię: `./scripts/ops/kolejka-scalania.sh`. Od tej chwili agenci wrzucają PR do kolejki.
3. Pierwszy PR w kolejce: sprawdzić, że wszystkie wymagane kontrole zgłaszają się na commicie grupy (straż i agent guard jako pominięte).

body:
Fixes #909.

## Commits

1. `bb85b727` db: test that retiring an account's FTS rows keeps copies searchable (tests only, red on main)
2. `97e2f8a3` db: fill waiting copies before retiring an account's FTS rows (fix)

## The purge deleted the row a copy's search row waits for

A copy's `messages_fts_v2` row is staged with neither text nor vector (`restageFTS` for a COPY into another account, `stageFTS` for a delivery of a body another account has indexed), and the FTS worker fills it from a sibling row of the same body. `DeleteFTSRowsForAccount` (the purge's and the cleaner's FTS drain) deleted the source account's rows without looking at rows waiting on them. If the worker had not filled the copy yet, `resolveTextlessHashes` found no source and poisoned it with an empty vector. The message stays readable, but `BODY` search no longer finds it. The empty vector also spreads: `stageFTS` stages no text for a body whose sibling has a vector, so later deliveries of the same body copy the empty vector too. (The IMAP test's second subtest first failed for this reason, on a body the first subtest had poisoned. The test now gives each subtest a body of its own.)

Red on main. The IMAP test is the issue's reproduction (APPEND, COPY into another account's shared mailbox, `cleaner.PurgeAccount` of the source, then `UID SEARCH BODY` as the owner). The control, where the worker runs before the purge, passes:

```
--- FAIL: TestCrossAccountCopyStaysSearchableAfterSourcePurge
    --- FAIL: .../purge_before_the_worker
        Messages: the copy is still searchable by body
    --- PASS: .../worker_before_the_purge
--- FAIL: TestAccountFTSDrainKeepsCopiesSearchable/body_indexed
--- FAIL: TestAccountFTSDrainKeepsCopiesSearchable/text_still_pending
        Messages: message 32/1 of account 16 (hash 3bce2909…) is not searchable by body
```

Fix: before it deletes anything, `DeleteFTSRowsForAccount` gives the waiting rows of the batch's bodies what the worker would have given them: the body's vector, or its pending text when it has not been tokenised yet. This is `fillWaitingFTSRows`, which #923 added for the rekey. It moves to `fts.go`, takes a set of hashes, and looks up a source only for hashes that actually have a waiting row.

## Deliveries and copies in flight

A delivery or COPY that is staging a waiting row has not committed it yet, so the fill cannot see it. The drain now takes the orphan sweep's exclusive lock on each body of its batch, using `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` as the sweep does. Stagers take that lock shared. A body whose lock is held is left to a later batch. The try-lock never waits, so a COPY that takes several bodies' shared locks in another order cannot deadlock with the drain. At most `limit` locks are taken (`LIMIT` sits in the subquery), the same lock-table budget as the sweep. While holding them, the drain waits only for the FTS worker, and the worker never waits on anyone else's row or advisory locks.

```
--- FAIL: TestAccountFTSDrainWaitsForStagingInFlight
        Messages: message 40/1 of account 20 (hash b36322f4…) is not searchable by body
```

## The orphan sweep and the finalize

Two other deleters can take the same row:

- **Orphan sweep** (`DeleteMessagesFTSByKeyBatch`). Once the purge's S3 phase has deleted the source account's messages, its FTS rows are orphans, and the sweep on any node can delete them before the drain runs. The same applies whenever an account's last message with a body is removed while a copy it gave away still waits. The sweep already holds the exclusive locks, so it now fills before its delete.
- **Finalize** (`FinalizeAccountDeletions`). As a safety net, it deleted every FTS row the drain had left, with no locks and no fill. A drain error in the cleaner path, or a body skipped as above, led straight back to the bug. The finalize now keeps an account until its FTS rows are gone, and the next drain finishes it: the next purge pass (up to `purgeMaxPasses`) or the next cleaner cycle. Since `GetDanglingAccountsForFinalDeletion` does not check FTS rows, such an account keeps being listed and drained.

```
--- FAIL: TestOrphanSweepKeepsCopiesSearchable/body_indexed
--- FAIL: TestOrphanSweepKeepsCopiesSearchable/text_still_pending
--- FAIL: TestFinalizeKeepsFTSRowsTheDrainLeft
        Messages: message 36/1 of account 18 (hash d450b95c…) is not searchable by body
```

Mutation check: each of the four changes (fill in the drain, try-lock in the drain, fill in the sweep, FTS check in the finalize) was reverted one at a time, and each revert turned only its own tests red.

`TestFTSRecoverMessageContentsRepairsEmptyDestinations` used the purge to lose a destination's only vector, and it fails with this change (`queued`, `poisoned`, `legacy text without known vector`). It now deletes the source row directly, which is what the purge used to do.

Retention pruning (`PruneOldMessageVectors`) is not changed. A copy's row has the same `sent_date` as its source, so the prune removes both.

## Not in this PR

Rows that production has already poisoned this way cannot be repaired by #861's `fts_recover_message_contents.sql`, because these bodies have no `message_contents` row. Their vectors could only be rebuilt from S3.

Merges cleanly with #787. In a trial merge only the `Makefile` conflicts, and that conflict is between #787 and main.

## Tests run

```
export GOFLAGS=-trimpath SORA_TEST_DB_NAME=sora_is_909
go build ./... && go vet ./db ./server/cleaner && go vet -tags=integration ./integration_tests/imap
go test ./db/ -count=1 -run 'TestAccountFTSDrain|TestFinalizeKeepsFTSRows|TestOrphanSweep|TestAccountFinalize|TestFTSDrainKeepsRowsOfAccountNotFinalizable|TestDeleteMessagesFTSByHashBatchRevalidatesReferences|TestRestageFTS|TestGetUnusedFTSKeys|TestRekey|TestFTS|TestLegacyFinalizeLeavesALiveLease|TestAccountIsNotFinalizedUnderALiveLease|TestAddressStaysTakenWhileAnUploadIsInFlight|TestDeliveryStagesFTSV2|TestSameAccountMoveCopyTakeNoFTSLocks|TestCrossAccountMoveCopyStageDestinationFTSRow|TestHardDeleteAccountStep|TestCopyMessages|TestMoveMessages|TestProcessFTS'
go test -race ./db/ -count=1 -timeout 30m -run 'TestAccountFTSDrain|TestFinalizeKeepsFTSRows|TestOrphanSweep|TestRekeyWaitsForCopiesInFlight|TestRekeyKeepsCopiesSearchable'
go test ./server/cleaner/ -count=1
go test -tags=integration ./integration_tests/imap/ -count=1 -run 'TestCrossAccountCopyStaysSearchableAfterSourcePurge|TestCrossAccountCopyMove_|TestSharedMailboxOwnership_|TestCrossAccountCopyOfSourceRekeyed|TestCrossAccountMoveOfSourceRekeyed|TestCrossAccountCopyHoldsDestObjectLockUntilCommit|TestCrossAccountMoveHoldsDestObjectLockUntilCommit|TestCrossAccountCopyWaitsForCleaner|TestCrossAccountMoveWaitsForCleaner'
go test -tags=integration ./integration_tests/adminapi/ -count=1 -run 'TestPurgeWorker_|TestAdminAPI_PurgeRequest_|TestHardDelete_LeavesAnUploadInFlightAlone|TestRestore_KeepsTheUploadInFlight|TestAdminAPI_DeleteAccount_'
go test -tags=integration ./cmd/sora-admin/ -count=1 -run 'TestAccountPurge|TestDomainPurge'
```

All pass, and the integration runs report PASS, not SKIP (imap 17, adminapi 19, sora-admin 13).
